<a id="section-5-3"></a>

## 5.3. Permission management

<a id="section-5-3-1"></a>

### 5.3.1. Role permissions

<a id="section-5-3-1-1"></a>

#### 5.3.1.1. Overview

A role is a collection of access permissions. In the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, role types include preset roles, custom roles, RAM role-based authorization, and RAM-based authorization.

**Role types**

**Preset role**

A preset role is a collection of preset permissions for specific operations. To implement privilege separation, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides preset roles based on the general use cases in cloud platforms. After a RAM user is assigned a preset role, the user has the corresponding operation permissions. During authentication, the system determines whether the user has the permissions to perform the corresponding operations based on the permissions that belong to the preset role assigned to the user. For more information, see Preset roles.

**Custom role**

You can create a custom role to combine and set permission policies based on your business requirements. You can configure the sharing scope and permissions on resources, applications, and menus for the custom role, and configure custom permission policies to flexibly specify the services that can be accessed by the role, the operations that can be performed by the role, and the resources that can be managed by the role. Compared with preset roles, custom roles are more flexible and can be customized.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e7f43de83c8448eb786708ab812a066a.jpeg)

> **Note**
>
> Custom roles are commonly used to manage the permissions of users who log on to cloud service consoles. In addition, third-party independent software vendors (ISVs) can create custom roles when they require AccessKey pairs with limited permission scope to call cloud service APIs for application development.

**RAM role-based authorization**

RAM role-based authorization is the process of associating a RAM role with RAM users, other Apsara Stack tenant accounts, or Apsara Stack services. An authorized entity can directly assume a RAM role to obtain the collection of permissions that belong to the role without the need to grant permission policies to the entity.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9d22ab323444bed65d8e9cb489d64bc1.jpeg)

> **Note**
>
> RAM role-based authorization can be divided into the role of Apsara Stack tenant accounts and the role of Apsara Stack services based on the types of trust entities.
>
> - Role of Apsara Stack tenant accounts: the role that can be assumed by RAM users. RAM users who assume this type of role can belong to the own Apsara Stack tenant accounts or other Apsara Stack tenant accounts. The roles of this type are used for cross-account access or temporarily authorized access.
>
> - Role of Apsara Stack services: the role that can be assumed by cloud services. The roles of this type are used for access across Apsara Stack services.

**RAM-based authorization**

Each RAM user is a user entity with a unique identity. You can assign custom policies to RAM users by using user groups. This way, the RAM users always have these permissions regardless of whether they assume a role.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6235afbb1eb38da681ffa35d48128b3c.jpeg)

> **Note**
>
> - RAM-based authorization is performed based on RAM user groups other than RAM roles.
>
> - RAM-based authorization is used to enhance the fine-grained permission control of custom roles that are created on a GUI. After you create a custom role, you can use RAM-based authorization to attach a RAM policy to RAM users if some permissions cannot be granted by using the custom role.
>
> - RAM-based authorization must be used together with user groups.

<a id="section-5-3-1-2"></a>

#### 5.3.1.2. RAM policies

This topic describes the elements, structure, and syntax of RAM policies that are used to define the scope of permissions for custom roles, RAM authorization and RAM role-based authorization.

**Structure**

RAM policies are in the JSON format, containing two parts:

- Version: the version number of the policy.

- Statements: the statements that specify the permissions. The elements of statements include Effect, Action, Resource, Condition, and Principal.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ad4107bdc281b376d523361cd811f9e9.png)

**Elements in statements**

The elements of statements include Effect, Action, Resource, Condition, and Principal.

**Effect (Required)**

Specifies whether a statement result is an explicit allow or an explicit deny. Valid values: Allow and Deny.

> **Note**
>
> Precedence of Deny: Deny statements take precedence when a user is assigned multiple policies that contain Allow and Deny statements, and when a single policy contains both Allow and Deny statements.

**Example**

```text
"Effect": "Allow"
```

**Action (Required)**

The specific API operations involved in the statement.

The Action element is in the following format:  `<ram-code>:<action-name>` .

- `<ram-code>` : the product code.

- `<action-name>` : the API operation of the product involved in the policy.

> **Note**
>
> The values of the Action element are case-insensitive. However, to ensure consistency, we recommend that you follow the standard capitalization of the product code and API
>
> ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1bbf1dd1af2d0f06f970c5fc1d3ef56e.png)
>
> operation names.

**Example**

```text
"Action": [
  "oss:ListBuckets",
  "ecs:Describe*",
  "rds:Describe*"
]
```

> **Note**
>
> You can use the asterisk (\*) as a wildcard character. For example, in the preceding example,  `ecs:Describe*`  indicates that all the API operations of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) whose names start with Describe are involved in the policy.

**Resource (Required)**

The resources of cloud services involved in the statement, which are indicated by their Aliyun Resource Names (ARNs)

Resource elements are in the following format:  `acs:<ram-code>:<region>:<account-id>: <relative-id>` .

- `acs` : the prefix of ARNs. It stands for Alibaba Cloud Service.

- `<ram-code>` : the product code.

- `<region>` : the region ID of the resource. You can use the asterisk (\*) as a wildcard character to indicate regionless resources or resources in all regions.

- `<account-id>` : the user ID of the level-1 organization. This is used to specify the resources that belong to a specific level-1 organization.

- `<relative-id>` : the description of the specific resources. Its syntax is product-specific. For example, the relative-id for an OSS object is a path of that object, such as mybucket/dir1/object1.jpg.

**Example**

```text
"Resource": [
 "acs:ecs:*:*:instance/inst-001",
 "acs:ecs:*:*:instance/inst-002",
 "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket",
 "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket/*"
]
```

**Condition (Optional)**

The conditions that are required for the policy to take effect. A Condition element, or a condition block, contains one or multiple conditions. Each condition consists of an operator, a condition key, and a condition value.

Condition keys are case-sensitive. The case-sensitivity of the condition values is determined by the operator. For example, assume that a condition key of the string type is specified. if the StringEquals operator is used, the system performs a case-sensitive match. If the StringEqualsIgnoreCase operator is used, the system performs a case-insensitive match.

Description:

- Evaluation logic

  - You can specify one or more values for a condition key. If the value in a request matches one of the values, the condition is met.

  - A condition can have multiple keys that are attached to a single conditional operator. The condition of this type is met only if all requirements for the keys are met.

  - A condition block is met only if all of its conditions are met.

- Operators

  Operators are classified into the following types: string, number, data and time, Boolean, and IP address.

  | Category | Operator |
  | --- | --- |
  | String | • StringEquals<br>• StringNotEquals<br>• StringEqualsIgnoreCase<br>• StringNotEqualsIgnoreCase<br>• StringLike<br>• StringNotLike |
  | Number | • NumericEquals<br>• NumericNotEquals<br>• NumericLessThan<br>• NumericLessThanEquals<br>• NumericGreaterThan<br>• NumericGreaterThanEquals |
  | Date and time | • DateEquals<br>• DateNotEquals<br>• DateLessThan<br>• DateLessThanEquals<br>• DateGreaterThan<br>• DateGreaterThanEquals |
  | Boolean | Bool |
  | IP address | • IpAddress<br>• NotIpAddress |

- Condition keys

  - General condition keys are in the following format:  `acs:<condition-key>` .

    | General condition key | Type | Description |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | acs:CurrentTime | Date and time | The time when the server receives the request.Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard, for example, 2012-11-11T23:59:59Z. |
    | acs:SecureTransport | Boolean | Specifies whether a secure channel is used to send a request. For example, a request can be sent over HTTPS. |
    | acs:SourceIp | IP address | The IP address of the client that sends the request It can be a single IP address or a CIDR block. If the value is a single IP address, you must specify the specific IP address rather than a CIDR block. For example, you must specify 10.0.0.1 rather than 10.0.0.1/32. |
    | acs:MFAPresent | Boolean | Specifies whether multi-factor authentication (MFA) is used when the user who sends the request logged on. |
    | acs:PrincipalARN | String | The identity of the requester. This operator is only used in trust policies of RAM roles. |

  - Service-specific condition keys are in the following format:  `<ram-code>:<condition-key>` .

    | Service-specific condition key | Cloud service | Type | Description |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | ecs:tag/&lt;tag-key&gt; | Elastic Compute Service (ECS) | String | The condition key for tags of ECS resources, which are customizable. |
    | rds:ResourceTag/&lt;t ag-key&gt; | ApsaraDB RDS | String | The condition key for tags of ApsaraDB RDS resources, which are customizable. |
    | oss:Delimiter | Objective Storage Service (OSS) | String | The delimiter used by OSS to categorize object names. |
    | oss:Prefix | OSS | String | The prefix of an OSS object name. |

**Principal**

The entity that is allowed or denied to call the related API operations. This element is available only for resource-based policies. For example, in a trust policy attached to a RAM role, you can specify the resources that are allowed to assume the role in the Principle element. The Principal element is required in resource-based policies.

> **Note**
>
> You cannot specify the Principal element in identity-based policies. Identity-based policies are attached to RAM identities. The RAM identities to which identity-based policies are attached are the principals.

You can specify multiple types of principals for the Principal element in a policy. You can also specify multiple principals of the same type for the Principal element in a policy. If you specify multiple types of principals, separate the types with commas (,). If you specify multiple principals of the same type, separate the principals with commas (,) and enclose the principals with brackets ([]). Multiple principals are associated with each other by the OR operator, meaning that the policy is attached to all principals in the policy.

**Example**

```text
"Principal": {
 "RAM": [
 "acs:ram::123456789012****:root",
 "acs:ram::987654321098****:root"
 ],
 "Service": "ecs.aliyuncs.com"
}
```

Principals are authenticated RAM entities, which are divided into the following types:

- Organization account

  Set the Principal element to the account of the level-1 organization. When you configure the trust policy of a RAM role-based authorization, the account ARN of the selected trust organization will be added to the policy as the principal, such as  `acs:ram::165399189392****:root` .

- Cloud service

  Set the Principal element to a cloud service. When you configure the trust policy of a RAM role-based authorization, the identifier of the selected trust service will be added to the policy as the principal, such as  `ecs.aliyuncs.com` .

**Policy syntax**

A RAM policy consists of the version_block and statement_block components.

```text
policy = {
 <version_block>,
 <statement_block>
}
```

**version_block**

The version of the policy. By default, the value is 1.

```xml
<version_block> = "Version" : ("1")
```

**statement_block**

The statements. A RAM policy can contain multiple statements.

```xml
<statement_block> = "Statement" : [ <statement>, <statement>, ... ]
```

- Each statement consists of the effect_block, action_block, resource_block, and condition_block elements. condition_block is an optional element.

  ```xml
  <statement> = { 
   <effect_block>,
   <action_block>,
   <resource_block>,
   <condition_block?>
  }
  ```

  - Valid values of an effect_block element are  `Allow`  and  `Deny` .

    ```xml
    <effect_block> = "Effect" : ("Allow" | "Deny") 
    ```

  - Multiple action_block and resource_block elements can be specified in each statement.

    ```xml
    <action_block> = "Action" : 
     ("*" | [<action_string>, <action_string>, ...])
    <resource_block> = "Resource" : 
     ("*" | [<resource_string>, <resource_string>, ...])
    ```

  - Each condition_block element can contain multiple operators and

    ```xml
    <condition_block> = "Condition" : <condition_map>

    <condition_map> = {
      <condition_type_string> : { 
          <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
          <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
          ...
      },
      <condition_type_string> : {
          <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
          <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
          ...
      }, ...
    }  
    ```

**Valid values of elements**

- If an element value is a string, number, date, time, Boolean value, or an IP address, the value must be enclosed in double quotation marks ("").

- If an element value is a string, you can use asterisks (\*) and question marks (?) as wildcard characters.

  - An asterisk (\*) indicates 0 or multiple letters. For example,  `ecs:Describe*`  indicates all the API operations of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) whose names start with Describe.

  - A question mark (?) indicates a single letter.

**Policy syntax check**

RAM policies follow the JSON format. When you create or update a RAM policy, the system automatically checks the validity of the JSON format. We recommend that you use JSON validators or formatters to help you ensure the validity of the policy. For more information about JSON syntax standards, see RFC 7159.

<a id="section-5-3-1-3"></a>

#### 5.3.1.3. Manage preset roles

Preset roles support viewing, authorization, disabling, activation, and replication. Only platform administrator users can operate the Operations Administrator role.

**View preset roles**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Permissions** **> Role Permission**.

4. Optional: Switch to the Central Cloud Role tab.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The multi-cloud role tabs for Central Cloud and connected subordinate clouds appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only Central Cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. In the role list, view the following information for preset roles: **Role Name/ID**, **Role Type**, **Security Level**, **Role Description**, **Authorization Object**, **Sharing Scope**, and **Status**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - At the top of the list, you can filter roles by selecting a role type or entering a role name for quick search.
   >
   > - The numbers following users and user groups in the Authorization Object column indicate the count of authorized users and user groups. Click to navigate to the Authorized Personnel tab to view detailed lists.
   >
   > - The Security Level column appears only when security policies enable Security Level-Based Access.

6. Click the role name of a preset role or click **View** in the **Actions** column.

7. On the preset role details page, view basic information, management permissions, application permissions, and authorized personnel information for the role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/732d1c4111bff5fec8b1b750545892a7.jpeg)

   | Display item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Basic informatio n | Displays role type, description, sharing scope, management permissions, permission statistics, and authorized personnel. |
   | Managem ent permission s | On the Management Permissions tab, select <strong>View only authorized</strong> to view the management permissions granted to this role. |
   | Applicatio n permission s | On the Application Permissions tab, select <strong>View only authorized products</strong> to view the cloud services and their permissions granted to this role. |
   | Menu permission s | On the Menu Permissions tab, select <strong>View only authorized</strong> to view the menus granted to this role. |
   | Authorized personnel | On the Authorized Personnel tab, view information about authorized users and user groups for this role. |

**Authorize users and user groups with preset roles**

**Procedure**

- Method 1:

  <ol type="i">

  <li>

  Click **Authorize** in the **Actions** column for the preset role.

  </li>

  <li>

  In the **Authorize** dialog box, on the **Users** and **User Groups** tabs, select the users and

  </li>

  </ol>

  user groups to authorize.

  > **Note**
  >
  > Above the lists on the Users and User Groups tabs, you can quickly find target users and user groups by selecting an organization and role, then entering a user or user group name.

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8d6f8c5cef8eaba7923d30cfe6ff8824.jpeg)

  <ol type="i" start="3">

  <li>

  Click **OK**.

  </li>

  </ol>

- Method 2:

  <ol type="i">

  <li>

  Click the role name of the preset role or click **View** in the **Actions** column.

  </li>

  <li>

  Switch to the **Authorized Personnel** tab.

  </li>

  </ol>

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/646edb01dba31b7b6a58fc38d97e9873.jpeg)

  <ol type="i" start="3">

  <li>

  Authorize users and user groups as needed.

  </li>

  </ol>

  | Action | Description |
  | --- | --- |
  | Authorize users | a. In the <strong>Authorize User</strong> section, click <strong>Authorize</strong>.<br>b. In the <strong>Authorize User</strong> dialog box, select the users to authorize.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fbfcb692bd8f7734da8083d6f899d11b.jpeg)<br>c. Click <strong>Confirm authorization</strong>. |
  | Authorize user groups | a. In the <strong>Authorize User Group</strong> section, click <strong>Authorize</strong>.<br>b. In the <strong>Authorize User Group</strong> dialog box, select the user groups to authorize.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cb0258c74f7add0f6927ec3ef653deed.jpeg)<br>c. Click <strong>Confirm authorization</strong>. |

**Remove authorized users and user groups from preset roles**

**Procedure**

1. Click the role name of the preset role or click **Actions** column’s **View**.

2. Switch to the **Authorized Personnel** tab.

3. Remove authorized users and authorized user groups as needed.

   | Action | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Remove authorized users | i. In the <strong>Authorized User</strong> section, click <strong>Actions</strong> column’s <strong>Remove</strong>.<br>ii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. If you unbind authorization, this user will also be automatically unbound from any resource sets joined through the current role. Proceed with caution. |
   | Remove authorized user groups | i. In the <strong>Authorized User Group</strong> section, click <strong>Actions</strong> column’s <strong>Remove</strong>.<br>ii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. If you unbind authorization, this user group will also be automatically unbound from any resource sets joined through the current role. Proceed with caution. |

**Disable a preset role**

**Prerequisites**

The status of the preset role is **Effective**.

**Procedure**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column of the preset role, then select **Disable**.

2. Click **Confirm**. After you disable this role, all users bound to it cannot log in. Proceed with caution.

**Activate a preset role**

**Prerequisites**

The status of the preset role is **Disabled**.

**Procedure**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column of the preset role, then select **Activate**.

2. Click **Confirm**. After you activate this role, users previously bound to it regain the permissions included in the role.

**Copy a preset role**

**Procedure**

1. Click **Copy** in the **Actions** column of the preset role. <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt="">

2. On the Create Custom Role page, follow the instructions to complete the configuration for Basic Configuration, Management Permission, Application Permission, and Menu Permission.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Copying a role quickly creates a new role with identical permissions. You can adjust permissions as needed. If you make no changes, the copied role has the same sharing scope, management permission, application permission, and menu permission as the original role.
   >
   > - You must define a new role name. It cannot be the same as the name of the role being copied.

<a id="section-5-3-1-4"></a>

#### 5.3.1.4. Manage custom roles

Custom roles support the following operations: create, view, edit, update permissions, authorize, disable, activate, copy, and delete.

**Create a custom role Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** **> Role Permissions**.

4. (Optional) Switch to the central cloud role tab.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The multi-cloud scenario displays tabs for both central cloud and connected subordinate clouds. In a single-cloud scenario, only the central cloud exists by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. Above the role list, click **Create Custom Role,** to go to the **Create Custom Role** page.

6. Configure **Basic Configurations** and click **Next**.

   **Operations administrator creates a custom role**

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4beb6b50e3ffddc113647e61e190e1d0.jpeg)

   **Organization administrator creates a custom role**

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/eeaa62cc43d708397b8039aeece2f1c1.jpeg)

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Role Name | The name of the role. |
   | Description | (Optional) The description of the role. |
   | Applicable Organization | Select the organization to which the role applies. The operations administrator can select the root organization. |
   | Sharing Scope | The visibility scope of the role when you authorize user. If the operations administrator creates a custom role and selects the root organization as the applicable organization, the sharing scope supports only <strong>Global</strong>.<br>• <strong>Global</strong>: The role is visible across all organizations.<br>• <strong>Current Organization</strong>: The role is is visible only within the current organization.<br>• Shared within the Current Organization and Its Subordinate <strong>Organizations</strong>: The role is visible within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |
   | Management Scope | The resource scope that the role can manage. Combined with the organization of the authorized user, the role can manage resources within the corresponding scope. If the organization administrator creates a custom role, only <strong>Specified Organization and Subordinate Organizations</strong> and <strong>Resource Sets</strong> are available.<br>• <strong>All Organizations</strong>: The role can manage cloud service resources in all organizations.<br>• <strong>Specified Organization and Subordinate Organizations</strong>: The role can manage cloud resources in the specified organization and its cascading subordinate organizations.<br>• <strong>Resource Sets</strong>: The role can manage only cloud resources within a specific resource set. For constraints on resource set scope permissions, see Limits on roles. |
   | Custom Policy | You can enable or disable Custom Policy.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3ec933c28754130c646f539f25323d46.png" width="24" alt="">: Disabled. After you disable this option, you cannot define custom<br>policies.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7a59d59abdef30d0755e934ef079161e.png" width="24" alt="">: Enabled. After you enable this option, you can define custom policies. |
   | Security Level-Based Access | Configure security level for roles whose management scope is resource set.<br>Note<br>• Enable this if Security Level-Based Access is activated in security policies and the <strong>Management Scope</strong> is set to Resource Sets.<br>• The security level of your current role determines the maximum security level you can assign to new roles. You can assign only levels equal to or lower than your own. |

7. Configure **Management Permissions**. Select the management permissions that you want to authorize in the permission list, and then click **Next**. Management permissions define console-related operation permissions for the role, such as authorizing operations on organizations, users, and resource sets.

   > **Important**
   >
   > If you selected Resource Sets in the basic configuration of the custom role, only read-only permissions take effect in this step. Write permissions do not take effect.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8d281f994f2c41bacb1c7863fa0263e0.jpeg)

8. Configure **Application Permissions**. Select the cloud service permissions that you want to authorize in the permission list, and then click **Next**. Application permissions define which operations a user can perform on specific cloud services. For example, if you only need to grant users the permission to view Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances, select only the view instance permission under ECS.

   > **Important**
   >
   > - The system automatically selects dependent permissions. Removing dependencies may restrict operations. Proceed with caution.
   >
   > - Resource sharing permissions:
   >
   >   - Resource sharing permissions do not affect normal role authorization. They supplement management permissions specifically for shared resource states.
   >
   >   - When a shareable resource is shared to a target organization or resource set, and the target user's management scope does not cover that resource, management must occur via resource sharing permissions.
   >
   > - On the right side of each cloud service, click **Read/Write** or **Read-Only** to quickly authorize the role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f378183e3d322b937e4c4849f22989dc.jpeg)

9. Configure **Menu Permissions**. Select the menu entries that you want to authorize from the list, and then click **Next** or **Create**. Menu permissions control which menu items a role can view, enabling entry hiding.

   > **Important**
   >
   > - For console users, if platform operation permissions and cloud service permissions are granted via management and application permissions, corresponding menu permissions must also be assigned to ensure users can access those entries.
   >
   > - If you enabled Custom Policy, click **Next** to configure the custom policy content. If you did not enable custom policies, click **Create** to complete the creation of the custom role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2c10231c6cc2c6f1143e4e4ef3258c63.jpeg)

0. (Optional) Configure the **Custom Policy**. Define applied RAM actions, and then click **Create**.

   > **Important**
   >
   > You can configure custom policies only after you enable Custom Policy in the Basic Configurations step.

   Custom policies precisely describe authorized resources and permitted operations by defining RAM Actions. RAM Actions include Allow and Deny statements: Allow permits operations, Deny rejects them. If both exist, Deny takes precedence.

   The RAM Action format is &lt;ram-code>:&lt;action-name>. Separate multiple actions with commas (,).

   - &lt;ram-code> represents the RAM code of the cloud service, which is typically the service code.

   - &lt;action-name> represents the name of the OpenAPI operation for the cloud service.

   For example, if you set  `oss:ListBuckets,ecs:Describe*,rds:Describe*`  in Allow, the role has the permission to list all Object Storage Service (OSS) buckets, call all ECS APIs starting with Describe, and call all ApsaraDB RDS APIs starting with Describe.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e10f739d0f3dcd4706d3f280082e2f5c.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > Click **Preview** to view the added actions in the preview dialog box. In the **Preview** dialog box, click **Delete** in the **Operation** column to remove an added action. Click **Close** at the bottom of the **Preview** dialog box to close the preview.

1. After the role is created, click **Complete** in the **Create Custom Role** dialog box.

   Alternatively, click **Authorize Now** in the dialog box to go to the **Authorize Personnel** page and assign the role to users and user groups.

   | Custom Policy | On the Custom Policy tab, view the custom policies defined for the role.<br>Note<br>The Custom Policy tab appears only when you enable Custom Policy and configure the policy content during custom role creation. |

You can add or delete policies as needed.<br>Note<br>The Custom Policy tab appears only if you enabled Custom Policy and configured the policy content when you created the custom role.<br>• Add a policy<br>a. **Batch dd authorization to roles**

In some upgrade scenarios, due to product evolution, certain products require new permission points to be added in the new version. When a specific type of role needs multiple new authorizations added at once, you can use batch role authorization to improve efficiency for subsequent permission additions.

> **Important**
>
> Batch adding authorization to selected roles means supplementing permission points for roles without reducing or overwriting existing role permissions.
>
> - If the original role does not have the selected new permission points, the system adds them.
>
> - If the original role already has them, they remain unaffected.

**Procedure**

1. On the **Role Permissions** page, select **Custom Role** from the **Role Type** drop-down list.

2. Select multiple custom roles that require batch authorization.

3. Click **Add Permissions** below the list, and then click **OK**.

4. Follow the wizard to add permission points to the roles.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   **Select Roles**: Confirm the selected custom roles.

   - To add more roles, click **Add Role**.

   - To remove a selected role, click **Remove** in the **Actions** column of the target role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6e575c8976345486d9afd5ff615485e4.jpeg)

   </li>

   <li>

   **Add Management Permissions**: Select the permission points to add for the selected roles.

   </li>

   <li>

   **Add Application Permissions**: Select the product operation permissions to add for the selected roles.

   </li>

   <li>

   **Add Menu Permissions**: Select the menu permissions to add for the selected roles.

   </li>

   </ol>

5. (Optional) After the creation,go to the task list to check the execution status of the batch role authorization task.

**Disable a custom role**

**Prerequisites**

The custom role is in the **Enabled** state.

**Procedure**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column of the custom role, and select **Disable**.

2. Click **OK**. After you disable the role, all users with this role cannot log in. Proceed with caution.

**Enable a custom role**

**Prerequisites**

The custom role is in the **Disabled** state.

**Procedure**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column of the custom role, and select **Enable**.

2. Click **OK**. After you enable the role, the system restores the role permissions to users who previously had this role.

**Copy a custom role**

**Procedure**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column of the custom role, and select **Copy**.

2. On the Create Custom Role page, follow the instructions to configure the basic configurations, management permissions, application permissions, menu permissions, and custom policies.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Copying a role quickly creates a new role with identical permissions. You can adjust permissions as needed. If you make no modifications, the copied role has the same sharing scope, management permissions, application permissions, menu permissions, and custom policies as the original role.
   >
   > - The system displays custom policies only if the original role supports them.
   >
   > - You must specify a new name for the role, and the name cannot be the same as the name of the original role.

**Delete a custom role**

**Prerequisites**

Before you delete a custom role, you must unbind it from users and user groups.

**Procedure**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column of the custom role, and select **Delete**.

2. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-5-3-1-5"></a>

#### 5.3.1.5. Manage RAM role authorization

Resource Access Management (RAM) role authorization supports creating, viewing, editing, managing permission policies, updating trust policies, managing RAM roles, and deleting.

**Create RAM role authorization**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** **> Role Permissions**.

4. (Optional) Switch to the Central Cloud Role tab.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The multi-cloud role tabs for Central Cloud and connected subordinate clouds appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only Central Cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. Click **Create Custom Role,** to go to the **Create Custom Role** page.

6. On the **Create Custom Role** page, expand **Advanced Creation** at the bottom of the page, and click **Create RAM Role & Attach Policy**.

7. Configure **Basic Configurations**, and click **Next**.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Role Name | Enter a custom name. |
   | Description | (Optional) Enter a description for the role. |
   | Applicable Organization | Select the organization to which the role applies. Operations administrators can select the root organization. |
   | Sharing Scope | Specifies the visibility scope of this role. If an operations administrator creates a role and selects the root organization as the applicable organization, the sharing scope supports only <strong>Global</strong>.<br>• <strong>Global</strong>: The role is visible to all organizations.<br>• <strong>Current Organization</strong>: The role is visible only to the current organization.<br>• Shared within the Current Organization and Its Subordinate <strong>Organizations</strong>: The role is visible to the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |

8. On the **Configure Custom Policy** page, select policies, and click **Next**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can select up to five policies for each role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4fb00b54d25b8101c5c1c8d4db25c61e.jpeg)

   - **View policy content:** Click **Policy Content** in the **Action** column to view the JSON-formatted policy content.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7e5eba90bd3fb73731fa94f7beec3e68.jpeg)

   - **Create policy**: If no suitable policy exists, create a custom policy.

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Click **Create Policy** in the upper-right corner of the policy list.

     </li>

     <li>

     In the **Create Policy** dialog box, enter a policy name, select an applicable organization, specify the sharing scope, add remarks, enter the policy content, and select the sharing scope.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     Click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

9. On the **Configure Trust Policy** page, select the **Trust Organization** and **Trust Cloud Service**, and click **Next**. The trust policy defines the entities that can assume the RAM role. You can specify level-1 organizations (Alibaba Cloud accounts) and cloud services to assume the RAM role.

   > **Note**
   >
   > After you enable the OIDC feature, you can also select a trusted OIDC provider to assume the RAM role and configure restriction conditions.

   - **Trust Organization**: Specify one or more level-1 organizations (Alibaba Cloud accounts) to assume the RAM role.

   - **Trust Cloud Service**: Specify one or more cloud services to assume the RAM role.

   - **Trust Policy**: The system generates JSON-format policy content based on the selected trust organizations and trust cloud services.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8be6ffd7c9cd16e8d8cf888b36db1c22.jpeg)

   As shown in the preceding figure, the policy grants the asr.aliyuncs.com service and specific root users the permission to assume this role. Based on this policy, the system allows the asr.aliyuncs.com service or specific root users to assume the role.

   - "Version": The policy version number. The value here is "1".

   - "Statement": The permission statement list. This field defines one permission statement.

     - "Action": The allowed action. The value here is "sts:AssumeRole", which allows the AssumeRole action.

     - "Effect": Specifies whether to allow or deny the action. The value here is "Allow", which allows the action.

     - "Principal": The entity allowed to assume the role. This can be a service (Service) or a RAM resource (RAM).

       - "Service": The service allowed to assume the role. The value here is "asr.aliyuncs.com", which allows the asr.aliyuncs.com service to assume the role.

       - "RAM": The RAM resource allowed to assume the role. The value here is "acs:ram::125279671240\*\*\*\*:root", which allows all RAM users and RAM roles under the Alibaba Cloud account to assume the role.

         > **Note**
         >
         > Alibaba Cloud account ARN syntax: `acs:ram::<account-id>:root` . This format represents the RAM users and RAM roles under the Alibaba Cloud account.
         >
         > RAM user ARN syntax:  `acs:ram::<account-id>:user/<user-name>` . This format represents a RAM user under the Alibaba Cloud account.
         >
         > RAM role ARN syntax:  `acs:ram::<account-id>:role/<role-name>` . This format represents a RAM role under the Alibaba Cloud account.
         >
         > &lt;account-id>: the Alibaba Cloud account ID

0. On the **Policy Preview** page, review the selected policies and trust policy content. After confirmation, click **Create** to complete the RAM role authorization.

   | RAM role | On the RAM Role tab, view the RAM role instances under this RAM role authorization.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5f22b12521583872fc1b47781079de09.jpeg) |

4. (Optional) Manage the policy list.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Operation</td>
       <td>Description</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>View the policy list</td>
       <td>Click <strong>Policies</strong> above the list to expand the <strong>Policies</strong> panel, where you can view all policies within your permission scope.<br>Note<br>Enter a policy name above the list to quickly find a policy.<br>• Click a policy name to expand its details and view basic information, policy content, and reference records.<br>Note<br>• Basic information: displays the policy name, remarks, sharing scope, and creation time. Click <strong>Modify</strong> to update the policy name and remarks.<br>• Policy content: displays the policy content in JSON format. Click <strong>Modify Policy content</strong> to update the policy content.<br>• Reference records: displays roles that reference this policy. Select a role type (RAM Role Authorization and RAM Authorization) and enter a role name to quickly find a role. Click <strong>Remove</strong> <strong>authorization</strong> in the <strong>Action</strong> column to remove the role and unbind the policy from the role.<br>• Click the number in the <strong>Reference Count</strong> column to go to the reference records tab of the policy details page and view the roles that reference this policy.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Create a policy</td>
       <td>i. In the <strong>Policies</strong> panel, click <strong>Create Policy</strong>.<br>ii. In the <strong>Create Policy</strong> dialog box, set <strong>Policy Name</strong>, <strong>Applicable Organization</strong>, <strong>Sharing Scope</strong>, <strong>Remarks</strong>, and <strong>Policy Content</strong>.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Modify a policy</td>
       <td>i. In the <strong>Policies</strong> panel, click <strong>Modify</strong> in the <strong>Action</strong> column for the target policy.<br>ii. In the <strong>Modify Permission Policy</strong> dialog box, update the policy name and remarks.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Modify policy content</td>
       <td>i. In the <strong>Policies</strong> panel, click the policy name.<br>ii. On the <strong>Policy Details</strong> page, go to the <strong>Policy Content</strong> tab and click <strong>Modify</strong> <strong>Policy content</strong>.<br>iii. After updating the policy content, click <strong>Save</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Delete a policy</td>
       <td>Important<br>Before you delete a policy, unbind it from any roles that reference it.<br>i. In the <strong>Policies</strong> panel, click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Action</strong> column for the target policy.<br>ii. Click <strong>Delete</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

**Update the trust policy of a RAM role authorization**

1. Click the role name of the RAM role authorization or **View** in the **Actions** column.

2. On the RAM Role Authorization details page, click the **Trust Policy** tab.

4. Set **Trust Organization** and **Trust Cloud Service** as needed. The system generates the policy content in JSON format based on your selections for trusted organization and trusted cloud service.

**Procedure**

1. Click the role name of the RAM role authorization or **View** in the **Actions** column.

2. On the RAM Role Authorization details page, click the **RAM Role** tab.

3. Perform the following operations to manage RAM roles as needed.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Operation</td>
       <td>Description</td>

In the <strong>Create</strong> dialog box, select the organization where you want to create the RAM Role.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ea0a24191324c1d7279e66e0910d58d2.jpeg" alt=""><br>iii. **Delete a RAM role authorization**

**Prerequisites**

Before you delete a RAM role authorization, you must remove all RAM roles under this authorization.

**Procedure**

1. In the **Actions** column of the RAM role authorization, click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c266cf685bb43a5383d1f321e8e2788f.png" width="14" alt=""> and select **Delete**.

2. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-5-3-1-6"></a>

#### 5.3.1.6. Manage RAM authorization

Resource Access Management (RAM) authorization is similar to a RAM role. You can use RAM authorization when a product does not support RAM role authorization. You can create, view, edit, and delete RAM authorizations, and manage authorizations and permission policies.

**Create RAM authorization**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** **> Role Permissions**.

4. (Optional) Switch to the Central Cloud Role tab.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The multi-cloud role tabs for Central Cloud and connected subordinate clouds appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only Central Cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. Click **Create Custom Role,** and go to the **Create Custom Role** page.

6. On the **Create Custom Role** page, expand **Advanced Creation** at the bottom of the page and click **Create RAM Authorization**.

7. Configure **Basic Information**.

   | Paramete r | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Role Name | The name of the role. |
   | Descripti on | (Optional) The description of the role. |
   | Applicabl e Organizat ion | Select the organization to which the role applies. Operations administrators can select the root organization. |
   | Sharing Scope | The visibility scope of the role. When an operations administrator creates a role and selects the root organization as the applicable organization, the sharing scope supports only <strong>Global</strong>.<br>• <strong>Global</strong>: The role is visible to all organizations.<br>• <strong>Current Organization</strong>: The role is visible only to the current organization.<br>• <strong>Sharing within Current and Subordinate Organizations</strong>: The role is visible within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |

8. Click **Create and Configure RAM Authorization**. On the **Role Authorization** page, configure role authorization.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | User group managemen t | Define user groups to which permission policies apply. You can add or remove user groups.<br>• Add a user group<br>a. Click the <strong>User Group Management</strong> tab.<br>b. Click <strong>Add User Group</strong>. In the <strong>Add User Group</strong> dialog box, select the target user group and click <strong>Confirm</strong>.<br>• Remove a user group<br>a. Click the <strong>User Group Management</strong> tab.<br>b. Click <strong>Remove</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column of the user group. |
   | Permission managemen t | Define access permissions for resources. You can add or remove permission policies. For detailed descriptions of permission policies, see "Manage permission policies" in Manage RAM role authorization.<br>• Add a permission policy<br>a. Click the <strong>Permission Management</strong> tab.<br>b. Click <strong>Add Policy</strong>. In the <strong>Add Policy</strong> dialog box, select a policy and click <strong>Confirm</strong>. If the existing policies do not meet your requirements, you can also create a custom permission<strong> </strong>policy.<br>• Remove a permission policy<br>a. Click <strong>Remove permissions</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column of the permission<strong> </strong>policy.<br>b. Click <strong>Confirm</strong>. |

9. After you complete the configuration, click **Confirm**.

**View a RAM authorization**

**Procedure**

1. In the role list, view the **Role Name/ID**, **Role Type**, **Role Description**, **Authorization Object**, **Applicable Organization**, **Sharing Scope**, and **Status** of the RAM authorization.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Above the list, you can select a role type or enter a role name to quickly find a role.
   >
   > - The numbers following users and user groups in the Authorization Object column indicate the number of users and user groups authorized for this role. Click to go to the Authorization Management tab to view detailed authorized users and user groups.

2. In the role list, click the role name of the RAM authorization or click **View** in the **Actions** column.

3. On the RAM Authorization Details page, view the basic information, authorization management, and permission policies of the RAM authorization.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e82e9392c5c1459da92973e9aefc81e6.jpeg)

   | Item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Basic information | Displays the role type, applicable organization, sharing scope, and description. |
   | Authorization management | On the Authorization Management tab, view the specific authorized users and user groups of the role.<br>Note<br>The system displays only the users and user groups within the management permission scope of the current user. |
   | Permission policy management | On the Permission Policy Management tab, view the specific permission policies added to the role. |

**Edit the basic information of a RAM authorization**

**Procedure**

1. In the role list, click the role name of the RAM authorization or click **View** in the **Actions** column.

2. On the RAM Authorization Details page, click **Edit Basic Information** in the upper-right corner.

3. In the **Modify** dialog box, update **Role name** and **Description** of the RAM authorization.

4. Click **OK**.

**Authorize users and user groups**

  <ol type="i">

  In the role list, click **Authorize** in the **Actions** column of the RAM authorization.

  </li>

  In the **Authorize** dialog box, select the users and user groups that you want to authorize

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8d6f8c5cef8eaba7923d30cfe6ff8824.jpeg)

  <ol type="i" start="3">

  <li>

  Click **OK**.

  </li>

  <ol type="i">

In the <strong>Authorize User</strong> dialog box, select the users that you want to authorize.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fbfcb692bd8f7734da8083d6f899d11b.jpeg)<br>c. Click <strong>Confirm Authorization</strong>. |

In the <strong>Authorize User Group</strong> dialog box, select the user groups that you want to authorize.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cb0258c74f7add0f6927ec3ef653deed.jpeg)<br>c. Click <strong>Confirm Authorization</strong>. |

**Remove authorized users and user groups**

**Procedure**

1. In the role list, click the role name of the RAM authorization or click **View** in the **Actions** column.

   | Operation | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Remove authorized users | i. In the <strong>Authorized User</strong> section, click <strong>Remove</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column for the authorized user.<br>ii. Click <strong>Confirm</strong>. If you unbind the authorization, the user is automatically unbound from the resource set joined through the current role. Proceed with caution. |

In the <strong>Authorized User Group</strong> section, click <strong>Remove</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column for the authorized user group.<br>ii. Click <strong>Confirm</strong>. If you unbind the authorization, the user group is automatically unbound from the resource set joined through the current role.Proceed with caution. |

**Manage permission policies**

**Procedure**

1. In the role list, click the role name of the RAM authorization or click **View** in the **Actions** column.

2. Go to the **Policies** tab.

3. Add or remove permission policies as needed. For more information about the permission policy list, see "Manage permission policies" in Manage RAM role authorization.

   | Operation | Description |
