<a id="section-5-3-1-7"></a>

#### 5.3.1.7. Manage multi-cloud roles

In multi-cloud scenarios, the role authorization page displays multi-cloud roles from connected clouds. You can manage these multi-cloud roles according to your business requirements.

**Managed Apsara Stack resource pools**

**Create a role of a managed Apsara Stack resource pool**

**Prerequisites**

- The platform administrator has connected the managed Apsara Stack under **Configurations** > **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Multi-Cloud Management**.

- You have used the operations administrator to bind the organization of the managed Apsara Stack.

- You are an operations administrator (bound to the operations administrator role of the managed Apsara Stack) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to the organization administrator role of the managed Apsara Stack).

**Procedure**

1. On the **Role Authorization** page, switch to the managed Apsara Stack role tab.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The center cloud and connected managed multi-cloud role tabs appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only the center cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

2. On the managed Apsara Stack role tab, click **Create Custom Role**.

3. On the **Role Authorization** page, complete the **Basic Configuration**, **Management Permission**, **Application Permissions**, and **Menu Permissions** for the custom role.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   **Basic Configurations**: Set the basic information for the custom role, then click **Next**.

   **Operations administrator creates a custom role**

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ad90ad9fb233c173e4d2297cec57d706.jpeg)

   **Organization administrator creates a custom role**

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/500ee948f59c683f624834c5de296eeb.jpeg)

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Role Name | The name of the role. |
   | Description | (Optional) The description of the role. |
   | Sharing Scope | The visibility scope of the role when you authorize users on behalf of this role.When an operations administrator creates a custom role, only <strong>Global</strong> is available.<br>• <strong>Global</strong>: The role is shared across all organizations.<br>• <strong>Current Organization</strong>: The role is shared within the current organization.<br>• <strong>Subordinate Organization</strong>: The role is shared with the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |
   | Management Scope | The resource management scope of the role. Combined with the organization of the authorized user, it determines which resources the role can manage.When you create a role for the managed Apsara Stack, only the <strong>Resource</strong> <strong>Set</strong> management scope is supported.<br>• <strong>All Organizations</strong>: The role can manage cloud resources in all organizations.<br>• <strong>Current Organization and Cascade Subordinate Organizations</strong>: The role can manage cloud resources in the current organization and its cascade subordinate organizations.<br>• <strong>Resource Set</strong>: The role can manage cloud resources only within a specific resource set. |

   </li>

   <li>

   **Management Permission**: Select the required management permissions in the permission list, then click **Next step**. Management permissions define console-related operation permissions for the role. You can select permissions based on the resource set scope.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6b6ea65fd2f0a2f4b641a9ce56730157.jpeg)

   </li>

   <li>

   **Application Permissions**: Select the required cloud service permissions in the permission list, then click **Next**. Application permissions define which operations a user can perform on which cloud services. For example, if you need to grant only the permission to view ECS instances, select only the View Instance permission under Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

   > **Important**
   >
   > - The system automatically selects other dependent operation permissions. Removing dependent permissions may restrict operations. Proceed with caution.
   >
   > - Resource sharing permissions:
   >
   >   - Resource sharing permissions do not affect normal role authorization. They supplement management permissions only when resources are in a shared state.
   >
   >   - When a shareable resource is shared with a target organization or resource set, if the management scope of the target organization’s user does not cover the resource, the user can manage the resource only through resource sharing permissions.
   >
   > - On the right side of a cloud service, click **Read/Write** or **Read-only** to quickly authorize the role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6c3e9d76f3fb55a921e381536beb15c3.jpeg)

   </li>

   <li>

   **Menu Permissions**: Select the required menu entries in the list, then click **Create**. Menu permissions control which menus the role can view, enabling menu entry hiding.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a66b1e27bf633b5aad5a1739be8dc240.jpeg)

   </li>

   </ol>

4. The role is created successfully. Click **Complete**. You can view the role in the role list under the corresponding resource pool, or select it when authorizing a user with a multi-cloud role in User Management.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d6cba8ea2ec593778f779843f6e4b7c5.jpeg)

**View managed Apsara Stack roles**

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator (bound to the operations administrator role of the managed Apsara Stack) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to the organization administrator role of the managed Apsara Stack).

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** **> Role Permission**.

4. Switch to the managed Apsara Stack role tab.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The center cloud and connected managed multi-cloud role tabs appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only the center cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. On the managed Apsara Stack role tab, view the list of roles for the managed Apsara Stack.

   > **Note**
   >
   > After the managed Apsara Stack is connected, the role list displays all roles within the resource set management scope of the managed Apsara Stack.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/51ef4b90bb0ae63695f6ee0cea34d41c.jpeg)

**Managed public cloud**

**Create a RAM role for the managed public cloud**

**Prerequisites**

- The platform administrator has accessed the managed public cloud under **Configuration** > **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Multi-Cloud Management**.

- The operations administrator has already bound the managedpublic cloud.

- The operating user is either an operations administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level).

**Procedure**

1. On the **Role authorization** page, switch to the managed public cloud role tab.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The center-cloud and connected managed multi-cloud role tabs appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only the center cloud exists by default, and no tabs appear.

2. On the managed public cloud role tab, click **Create RAM Role**.

3. In the **Create RAM Role** dialog box, enter basic information and policies for the RAM role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/68dae8b719c6e45cbde8aa6f4071df8d.jpeg)

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Role name | Enter a name for the RAM role in the managed public cloud. The name can be up to 64 characters long and may contain letters, digits, periods (.), and hyphens (-).The first character must be a letter or digit. Example: ecs-readonly-role. |
   | Organization | Select an organization that has already bound the managed public cloud from the drop-down list. |
   | Bind user | Select a user from the organization bound to the managed public cloud from the drop-down list. This action grants the RAM role to the selected user. |
   | Description | Enter a description for the RAM role. |
   | Permission scope selection | Select <strong>Resource group scope</strong> or <strong>Alibaba Cloud account scope</strong>. When binding a role to a user and selecting Alibaba Cloud account scope, you do not need to add the user to a public cloud resource group. |
   | Policy | Select one or more RAM role permission policies. You can choose system policies or custom policies. Policies appear only after you select the user’s organization.<br>The AdministratorAccess and AliyunRAMFullAccess policies carry high risk. We recommend choosing more granular permission policies instead. If you select the AdministratorAccess policy, the <strong>High-risk Authorization Reminder</strong> dialog box appears. You can choose <strong>Replace with PowerUserAccess</strong> or <strong>Continue using</strong> <strong>AdministratorAccess</strong>.<br><strong>Replace with PowerUserAccess</strong>: We recommend using this policy.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/aa8a78c696c33cbc5880ceb3e44fcd85.jpeg)<br><strong>Continue using AdministratorAccess</strong>: To continue using Administrator Access, manually select the checkbox below labeled <strong>I understand the risks.</strong>for secondary confirmation. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6cacb610bf88cfb0f556f377e876520a.jpeg)

4. Click OK.

5. Select menu and resource type permissions.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - When configuring menu and resource type permissions, you can view the permission policies selected in the basic information and policy section, including policy name, policy type, and description.
   >
   > - Menu permissions: Configure entry permissions for product menus.
   >
   > - Resource type permissions: Configure permissions to view resources on the resource retrieval page.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/afb0c250f70a4365aaf9eb3c5aa71418.jpeg)

6. Click **Confirm and Modify Role**.

7. In the **Role Authorization** dialog box, click **Cancel** or **Associate Multi-Cloud Resource Set**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Binding a multi-cloud resource set navigates you to the current user details page, where you can bind a multi-cloud resource set to the user.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f2bedcc6801e9800693b2819d3488a1e.jpeg)

**View RAM roles for the managed public cloud**

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is either an operations administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level).

**Procedure**

1. On the managed public cloud role tab, view the list of RAM roles. The list includes **Role Name**, **Authorization Object**, **Description**, and **Creation Time**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Enter a role name above the list to quickly find a role.

2. Click **View** in the **Actions** column of the RAM role.

3. In the expanded **View RAM Roles** panel, view the policies bound to this RAM role.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1a8b6f7bc26664390328f1c0e5d3c3c9.jpeg)

**Update RAM roles for the managed public cloud**

**Prerequisites**

- The authorization object of the RAM role is a user who does not have the operations administrator role.

- The operating user is either an operations administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level).

**Procedure**

1. On the managed public cloud role tab, click **Update** in the **Actions** column of the RAM role.

2. In the **Edit RAM Role** dialog box, update the **Description** and **Permission Policy** of the RAM role.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When you update a RAM role, you cannot modify the **Role Name**, **Organization**, or **Bind User**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/11d59b90ec7fd5a11562163d383fce1f.jpeg)

3. Click **Confirm and Modify Role**.

4. Update permissions for menus and resource types.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/afb0c250f70a4365aaf9eb3c5aa71418.jpeg)

5. Click **Confirm and Modify Role**.

**Delete RAM roles for the managed public cloud**

**Prerequisites**

- The authorization object of the RAM role is a user who does not have the operations administrator role.

- The operating user is either an operations administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level).

**Procedure**

1. On the managed public cloud role tab, click **Delete** in the **Actions** column of the RAM role.

2. Click **OK**. After you delete the RAM role, the system unbinds all users from this role.

<a id="section-5-3-1-8"></a>

#### 5.3.1.8. Limits on roles

**Limits on the management scope of resource sets**

If you select Resource Sets for Management Permissions when you create a custom role, the role has permissions on the resource sets of the associated user by default. This role is mainly used to manage resources. The permissions described in the following table are beyond the management scope of resource sets and do not take effect even if you select them.

| Management permission | Description |
| --- | --- |
| User management | Create, delete, enable, disable, lock, unlock, and manage users. |
| Role management | Create, delete, lock, unlock, and manage roles. |
| User group management | View, create, delete, and manage user groups. |
| Organization management | Create, delete, and manage organizations. |
| Resource set management | Create and delete resource sets. |
| AccessKey management | View the AccessKey pairs of organizations and users, create AccessKey pairs for organizations, delete, enable, and disable the AccessKey pairs of organizations, and view AccessKey logs. |
| Access policy | Create, delete, and manage access policies. |
| Change management | Change resource sets, resources, or users. |
| Bill management | View the bills of cloud services, organizations, and resource sets, and export and modify bills. |
| Service-linked role | Create service-linked roles. |
| Process management | View organization applications. |
| Multi-cloud management platform hosting | Configure multi-cloud management platform hosting. |
| Announcement | Manage announcements. |

<a id="section-5-3-1-9"></a>

#### 5.3.1.9. Examples

<a id="section-5-3-1-9-1"></a>

##### 5.3.1.9.1. Example: Create a role with read-only permissions for ECS (custom role)

**Background information**

CompanyA (Level-1 Organization) needs to assign dedicated O&M responsibilities. The organization must grant Xiao Zhuan, the ECS administrator, view-only permissions for all ECS resources within the company.

**Planning approach**

Xiao Zhuan, as an O&M personnel for ECS resources, needs to view all ECS resources under this company. Therefore, you can create a custom role. Set the role’s management scope to the current organization and its subordinate organizations. Grant only view permissions for ECS resources in application permissions. Then, enable the ECS resource entry in menu permissions.

**Procedure**

By default, orgA is the Level-1 Organization Administrator of CompanyA. The following steps use orgA as the example operator.

1. orgA logs in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Permissions** **> Role** Permission.

4. On the **Role Authorization** page, click **Create Custom Role**.

5. Fill in the basic configuration information, then click **Next**.

   - **Role Name**: ECS Read-Only Administrator

   - **Description**: View permissions for ECS resources

   - **Applicable Organizations**: Select applicable organization

   - **Sharing Scope**: Share within current organization

   - **Management Scope**: Current organization and cascading subordinate organizations

6. **Management Permissions** define console-related operational permissions (such as organization or resource set dimensions). For this ECS read-only role, no authorization is needed. Click **Next** directly.

7. On the **Application Permissions** page, locate the cloud service **Elastic Compute Service (ECS)**. Select view permissions for corresponding resources, or click **Read-Only** in the upper-right corner to add read-only permissions for ECS to this role. Then, click **Next**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f9d55883b5dc49cb16ed91c357648711.jpeg)

8. On the **Menu Permissions** page, add the ECS cloud service entry for the ECS read-only administrator. Otherwise, users cannot access the ECS service after logging in.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cb4e3989de6111d89a0635336fa348aa.jpeg)

9. After adding the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) entry, click **Create**. The ECS read-only administrator role is now created.

   After creation, assign this role to user Xiao Zhuan. Xiao Zhuan can then view all ECS resources of CompanyA.

<a id="section-5-3-1-9-2"></a>

##### 5.3.1.9.2. Example: Modify the ECS Read-Only Administrator Role (Custom Role)

**Background information**

Due to changes in Company A’s business, Xiao Zhuan needs permission to view all ECS resources and also all VPC resources. The ECS read-only administrator role for Xiao Zhuan is already created. For details, see Example: Create a role with read-only permissions for ECS (custom role).

**Planning approach**

Add read-only permissions for VPC to the existing ECS read-only administrator role.

**Procedure**

By default, orgA is the level-1 organization administrator of CompanyA. The following steps use orgA as the operating user.

1. orgA logs in to the Apsara Uni-manager management console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Permission Management** **>**  **Role Authorization**.

4. On the **Role Authorization** page, find the existing ECS read-only administrator role.

5. Click **View** in the **Actions** column for the role.

6. On the role details page, modify the basic role information and add read-only permissions for VPC resources.

   - Edit basic information: Since the user also needs to view VPC resources, update the **Role Name** and **Description** to “ECS and VPC Read-Only Administrator” and “Permissions to view ECS and VPC resources,” respectively. Click **Modify Basic Information** in the upper-right corner to make these changes.

   - Add read-only permissions for VPC resources: Click the **Application Permissions** tab, locate the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) service, then select the view permission or click **Read-Only** in the upper-right corner.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2d5db014bcb18acbf61ceddf214744f7.jpeg)

7. On the **Menu Authorization** page, select the entry point for Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) resources to grant this role access to VPC operations.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/14eb4a255a59a4b03670f3c753ce489c.jpeg)

8. Click **Update** to complete the modification of the ECS read-only administrator role. View the updated role in the role list.

<a id="section-5-3-1-9-3"></a>

##### 5.3.1.9.3. Example: Grant a user permission to restart ECS instances by using a RAM role (RAM Role Authorization)

**Background information**

Grant Xiao Zhuan, a dedicated operations engineer under CompanyA (Level-1 Organization), permission to restart all ECS instances.

**Planning approach**

Configure a permission policy in RAM Role Authorization to allow rebooting all ECS instances. Define Xiao Zhuan as the authorized user in the trust policy.

**Procedure**

Assume that OrgA is the Level-1 Organization Administrator for CompanyA. The following steps demonstrate actions performed by OrgA.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as OrgA.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Permissions** **> Role Permission**.

4. On the **Role Permission** page, click **Create Custom Role**.

5. Expand **Advanced Settings**, and then click **Create RAM Role & Attach Policy**.

6. In **Basic Configurations**, enter basic information for the RAM role, and then click **Next**.

   - **Role Name**: RebootECSRebootInstancesRamRole

   - **Description**: Users can restart ECS instances by assuming this RAM role.

   - **Applicable Organizations**: Select applicable organization.

   - **Sharing Scope**: Share within current organization.

7. In **Configure Custom Policy**, click **Create Policy** to create a policy that grants permission to restart all ECS instances.

   - **Policy Name**: RebootECSInstancesoPolicy

   - **Applicable Organizations**: Select applicable organization.

   - **Sharing Scope**: Share within current organization.

   - **Remarks**: Policy for restarting ECS instances.

   - **Policy Content**:

     ```json
     {
       "Version": "1",
       "Statement": [
         {
           "Action": "ecs:RebootInstance",
           "Resource": "*",
           "Effect": "Allow"
         }
       ]
     }
     ```

8. In the policy list, select the policy you created, and then click **Next Step**.

9. In **Configure Trust Policy**, specify Xiao Zhuan (username: xiaozhuan) as the authorized user who can assume this role.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   First, select the trusted organization CompanyA. This authorizes all RAM users and RAM roles under this Alibaba Cloud account. The system automatically populates the ARN of the cloud account, such as  `acs:ram::139900176770****:root` .

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Alibaba Cloud Account ARN syntax: `acs:ram::<account-id>:root` . This represents RAM users and RAM roles under the Alibaba Cloud account.
   >
   > - RAM User ARN syntax:  `acs:ram::<account-id>:user/<user-name>` . This represents a RAM user under the Alibaba Cloud account.
   >
   > - RAM Role ARN syntax:  `acs:ram::<account-id>:role/<role-name>` . This represents a RAM role under the Alibaba Cloud account.
   >
   > - &lt;account-id>: Represents the Alibaba Cloud account ID.

   </li>

   <li>

   Since only Xiao Zhuan requires authorization, modify the ARN in the trust policy to  `acs:ram::139900176770****:user/xiaozhuan` .

   </li>

   </ol>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d841a88e0a407bd9fa2551a0f4d9689f.jpeg)

0. In the policy preview, confirm the permission policy and trust policy details, and then click **Create**.

   After successful creation, the RAM role template is complete.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/56d57d22a88dd9367ba26863f01ce1d8.jpeg)

1. In the role list, click the role name to go to its details page.

2. On the **RAM Role** tab of the role details page, click **Create**. In the **Organization** drop-down list, select companyA. This creates the RAM role instance under the companyA cloud account. After creation, the authorized user Xiao Zhuan can assume the RAM role to restart ECS instances within the companyA organization.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/bce924e1176c590de3e8faf421bedeab.jpeg)

<a id="section-5-3-1-9-4"></a>

##### 5.3.1.9.4. Example: Use RAM authorization to grant users permissions to view and delete VPC-connected instances (RAM Authorization)

**Background information**

Use RAM authorization to grant users in the VPC-Group user group under CompanyA (Level-1 Organization) permissions to view and delete VPC-connected instances.

**Planning ideas**

Define permissions for viewing and deleting all VPC-connected instances in RAM authorization. Then bind the user group to the permission policy and grant the policy to users in the user group.

**Procedure**

By default, orgA is the Level-1 Organization administrator of CompanyA. The following procedure uses operations performed by orgA as an example.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console as orgA.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** **> Role Permission**.

4. On the **Role Permission** page, click **Create Custom Role**.

5. Expand **Advanced Settings**, and then click **Create RAM Authorization**.

6. In **Basic Information**, enter the RAM authorization information and click **Create and Configure RAM Authorization**.

   - **Role Name**: Grant permissions to view and delete VPC-connected instances

   - **Description**: Use RAM authorization to grant users permissions to view and delete VPC-connected instances

   - **Applicable Organizations**: Select applicable organizations

   - **Sharing Scope**: Share within current organization

7. On the **Role Authorization** page, click the **Permission Management** tab, and then click **Add Policy**.

8. In the **Add Policy** dialog box, click **Create Policy**.

   - **Policy Name**: DescribeAndDeleteVpcsPolicy

   - **Applicable Organizations**: Select applicable organizations

   - **Sharing Scope**: Share within current organization

   - **Remarks**: Policy for viewing and deleting VPC-connected instances

   - **Policy Content**:

     ```json
     {
       "Version": "1",
       "Statement": [
         {
           "Action": [
             "vpc:DescribeVpcs",
             "vpc:DeleteVpc"
           ],
           "Effect": "Allow",
           "Resource": [
             "*"
           ]
         }
       ]
     }
     ```

9. After you create the permission policy, select the policy and click **OK** to add the policy to the RAM authorization.

0. On the **Role Authorization** page, click the **User Groups** tab, and then click **Add User Group**.

1. In the **Add User Group** dialog box, select the VPC-Group user group and click **OK** to bind the user group to the DescribeAndDeleteVpcsPolicy permission policy.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5745f4d7c7bc9aebb0be23a4c764e005.jpeg)

2. On the **Role Authorization** page, click **OK**. After you create the RAM authorization, users in the user group have permissions to view and delete VPC-connected instances.

### 5.3.2. Data permissions

On the Data Permissions page, you can authorize specific users to access specific cloud service instances. You can also view and change all data permissions granted to specific users.

**Background information**

In the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can view and manage the management permissions, application permissions, and menu permissions granted to users. The preceding permissions allow users to manage resource sets or organizations. However, the scopes of the preceding permissions are still not fine-grained enough to meet the business requirements of customers in specific scenarios. Therefore, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console allows you to grant data permissions to a user on a specific resource instance. This way, you can not only control access to resource sets or resources, but also manage the operations of a specific user on a specific resource instance.

To simplify and optimize data permissions on instances, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides an intuitive and easy-to-use data permission feature. This way, you can grant permissions on cloud service instances to users on the Data Permissions page.

Alternatively, you can create policies to grant permissions to users. In this case, you can grant data permissions to users on cloud services that include the cloud services displayed on the Data Permissions page.

**Cloud services that are displayed on the Data Permissions page**

You can grant data permissions on the instances of the following cloud services to users on the Data Permissions page: ApsaraMQ, Object Storage Service (OSS), Simple Log Service (SLS), DataHub, Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK), Key Management Service (KMS), and Tablestore.

**Use cases**

To grant operation permissions on resource instances to users in the console, you can perform the following steps to create a custom role and grant data permissions to the role:

1. Create a custom role to define access permissions on services of resource sets or organizations. For more information, see the "Create a custom role" section of the Manage custom roles topic.

2. Grant access and operation data permissions on specific resource instances. For more information, see the Grant data permissions on specific instances on the Data Permissions page section of this topic.

For example, you can perform the following authorization to grant the view permissions on all ApsaraMQ instances of resource sets and operation permissions on topics or groups in a specific ApsaraMQ instance.

- **First authorization**: You can create a custom role to grant the view permissions on ApsaraMQ instances of resource sets. This way, users can only view all the ApsaraMQ instances of resource sets in the console.

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b59b0c2d3944d505659881def7aab6e9.jpeg)

- **Second authorization**: You can grant operation permissions on a specific ApsaraMQ instance or a specific topic or group in an ApsaraMQ instance on the Data Permissions page.

**Perform authorization in the ACK console**

> **Note**
>
> You can configure fine-grained role-based access control (RBAC) for Resource Access Management (RAM) users or RAM roles in the ACK console. This way, you can grant access or operation permissions on resources in clusters. For example, you can authorize RAM users or RAM roles to manage resources only in the specified namespace in a cluster.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Computing** > **Container Service for Kubernetes**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authorizations**.

4. On the **RAM Users** or RAM Roles tab, find the RAM user or RAM role that you want to manage and click **Modify Permissions**.

5. In the **Configure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** step, click **Add Permissions**. Select all clusters or a cluster from the Cluster drop-down list. If you select a cluster, you also need to select one or more namespaces of the cluster. Select the preset role or custom role that you want to manage and click **Next Step**.

   The following table describes the permissions that roles have on clusters and namespaces.

   | Role | RBAC permissions on cluster resources |
   | --- | --- |
   | Administrator | This role has the read and write permissions on all resources in all namespaces of the corresponding cluster. |
   | O&amp;M engineer | This role has the read and write permissions on resources in all namespaces and read-only permissions on nodes, persistent volumes (PVs), namespaces, and service quotas of the corresponding cluster. |
   | Developer | This role has the read and write permissions on resources in a specific namespace or all namespaces. |
   | Restricted user | This role has the read-only permissions on resources in a specific namespace or all namespaces. |
   | Custom role | The permissions of a custom role are determined by the ClusterRole that you select. Before you select a ClusterRole, check the permissions of the ClusterRole to ensure that you grant only the required permissions to the RAM user. |

<a id="section-5-3-3"></a>

### 5.3.3. Access control

<a id="section-5-3-3-1"></a>

#### 5.3.3.1. Create an access policy

To improve the security of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can create access policies as an administrator to control logon access based on the logon time and IP addresses of users.

**Background information**

Access policies are used to control the time periods and IP addresses valid for user logon. After a user is associated with an access policy, user logons are limited based on the logon time and IP addresses specified in the policy.

The default policy generated by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console does not have limits on the time and IP addresses valid for user logon. This policy cannot be deleted.

**Limits**

- The platform administrator (the username is super) can only create access policies that are shared within the current organization, and these policies can only be configured for custom operations administrators.

- Operations administrators can only create globally shared access policies.

- If you use a custom role whose permissions are shared by all organizations, you can create globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations.

- If you use a role whose permissions are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations, you can only create access policies that are shared within the current organization and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations.

- If you use a custom role whose permissions are shared by resource sets, you cannot create access policies even if you are granted the required permissions.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Access Control**.

4. On the page that appears, click **Create Access Policy** in the upper-left corner.

5. In the **Create Access Policy** dialog box, configure the **Name**, **Description**, **Sharing Scope**, **Policy Property**, **Logon Time**, and **IP Address** parameters.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f91aa316cde21670b0b54c08e4f89214.jpeg)

   **Parameters for creating an access policy**

   | Paramet er | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Name | The name of the access policy. The name must be 2 to 50 characters in length and can contain only letters and digits. The name must be unique in the system. |
   | Descript ion | The description of the access policy. |
   | Sharing Scope | The scope in which the policy is available. Valid values:<br>• <strong>Global</strong>: The policy is available in all organizations.<br>• <strong>Current Organization</strong>: The policy is available only in the current organization and is unavailable in its subordinate organizations.<br>• <strong>Subordinate Organization</strong>: The policy is available in the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |
   | Policy Propert y | The authentication method of the access policy.<br>Important<br>The authentication method takes effect in combination with the <strong>Login Time</strong> and <strong>IP</strong> <strong>Address</strong> parameters.<br>• <strong>Whitelist</strong>: Logins are allowed for users whose logins match the settings of both the Login Time and IP Address parameters.<br>• <strong>Blacklist</strong>: Logins are not allowed for users whose logins match the settings of both the Login Time and IP Address parameters. |
   | Login Time | The login time period. Valid values: <strong>By Period</strong>, <strong>Every Day</strong>, and <strong>Every Week</strong>. You can click <strong>Add Time Period</strong> to add a login time period.<br>• <strong>By Period</strong>: You must specify a start date, an end date, and a specific login period.<br>• <strong>Every Day</strong>: You need to only specify a specific login period.<br>• <strong>Every Week</strong>: You need to select one or more days of the week (from Monday to Sunday) and specify a specific login period.<br>Note<br>• The start time of the login period must be earlier than the end time of the login period.<br>• You can click <strong>Select All Day</strong> to quickly set the login period to 00:00 -23:59. |
   | IP Address | The IP address for logins. You can click <strong>Add IP Address</strong> to add an IP address. IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported.<br>• An example of IPv4 CIDR blocks: 192.168.1.0/24. If the subnet mask of a login IP address is 32 bits in length, only this IP address is allowed to log in.<br>• An example of IPv6 CIDR blocks: 2001:db8:1234:abcd::/64.<br>• The CIDR block cannot be empty or duplicated. |

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-5-3-3-2"></a>

#### 5.3.3.2. Manage access policies

After you create an access policy, you can view, modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policy.

**Limits**

- The default policy of the system is globally shared and is in the Enabled state. You cannot modify, disable, or delete the default policy.

- If you are the platform administrator, you can view the default policy of the system and the access policies that you created. You can also modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policies that you created.

- If you use a role whose permissions are shared by all organizations, you can view globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. You can also modify, disable, enable, or delete all available access policies except the default policy.

- If you use a role whose permissions are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations, you can view globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. You can also modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policies that are available within the management scope.

- If you use a custom role whose permissions are shared by resource sets, you can view globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. You cannot modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policies even if you are granted the required permissions.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Access Control**.

4. Perform operations on access policies as needed.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9def938c0096e496e220a78b2842df2c.jpeg)

   | Operation | Procedure |
   | --- | --- |
   | View access policies | i. In the access policy list, view the information displayed in the following columns: <strong>Policy Name/ID</strong>, <strong>Policy Property</strong>, <strong>Status</strong>, <strong>Sharing Scope</strong>, <strong>Users</strong>, <strong>Access</strong> <strong>Time</strong>, <strong>Endpoint</strong>, <strong>Description</strong>, <strong>Created At</strong>, <strong>Created By</strong>, <strong>Modified At</strong>, and <strong>Last Updated By</strong>.<br>Note<br>You can click the icon next to <strong>Policy Property</strong>, <strong>Status</strong>, and <strong>Sharing</strong><br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/913c3d8a3808a6e9dfaed50fe87de8b9.png" width="11" alt=""><br><strong>Scope</strong>, and specify filter conditions to search for an access policy.<br>ii. Find an access policy and click the number in the <strong>Users</strong> column. In the <strong>Access</strong> <strong>User</strong> panel, view the users who are configured with this access policy. Only the users that can be viewed by the current user are displayed.<br>Note<br>In the <strong>Access User</strong> panel, you can find a user and click <strong>Replace Policy</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column to change the logon policy for the user. |
   | Modify an access policy | i. Find an access policy and click <strong>Modify</strong> in the Actions column.<br>ii. In the <strong>Modify an access policy</strong> dialog box, modify the parameters such as <strong>Name</strong>, <strong>Description</strong>, <strong>Policy Property</strong>, <strong>Logon Time</strong>, and <strong>IP Address</strong>. For more information about the parameters, see Create an access policy.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Disable an access policy | You can disable an access policy if you do not need it at the moment.<br>Important<br>After an access policy is disabled, users that are associated with the policy cannot log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.<br>i. Find an access policy that is in the <strong>Enabled</strong> state and click <strong>Disable</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Enable an access policy | Find an access policy that is in the <strong>Disabled</strong> state and click <strong>Enable</strong> in the Actions column. |
   | Delete an access policy | Important<br>Before you delete an access policy, make sure that it is not associated with any users.<br>i. Find an access policy and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the Actions column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |

<a id="section-5-3-4"></a>

### 5.3.4. Permission boundary

<a id="section-5-3-4-1"></a>

#### 5.3.4.1. Service boundary management

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console leverages the API control capabilities of the core gateway of Apsara Stack to provide the service boundary feature. You can create service boundaries to implement fine-grained control on API operations based on organizations, usage methods, and time periods.

<a id="section-5-3-4-1-1"></a>

##### 5.3.4.1.1. Create a service boundary

You can associate API control policies with service boundaries to implement fine-grained control on API operations.

**Background information**

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console allows you to control operations by organizations, time, and operation methods through setting service boundaries. You can also use service boundaries to trigger approval processes when cloud operations are performed.

Service boundaries take effect on operations performed through all methods, including cloud accounts, RAM users, and STS tokens. Specially, they also take effect on operations performed on the console. This is because when users perform operations on the console, the system is calling API operations under the hood.

> **Important**
>
> API operations performed across cloud services (such as when Resource Orchestration Service calls an Elastic Compute Service operation to manage the resources) are also controlled by service boundaries. Therefore, inappropriate configurations may interrupt the normal usage of cloud services. You need to add the ARNs of relevant resources to the whitelist of the service boundaries and make sure that you are aware of the impact of the service boundaries before you enable them.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Service Boundary**.

3. On the **Service Boundary Management** page, click **Create Service Boundary**. On the page that appears, configure the parameters.

   **Section**

   **Parameter**

   **Description**

   Service

   The name of the service boundary.

   Boundary Name

   Basic

   Description

   The description of the service boundary.

   Information

   The organizations for which the service boundary takes effect. Valid values: **Global** and **Specified Organization**. When you

   Management

   select Specified Organization, you need to select one or more

   Scope

   organizations from the **Authorize Organization** drop-down list.

   Manageme nt Scope

   The API control policies with which the service boundary is

   Associate API

   associated. You can select one or more API control policies. In an

   Control Policy

   API control policy, you can specify conditions based on the parameter values of specific API operations.

   The action on an operation that hits the control policy. Valid values:

   - **Reject**: rejects the operation.

   Console Calls

   - **Process Approval**: initiates a preconfigured approval process for the operation. If you select this option, you must configure

   Control

   the **Process** parameter in the **Configure Resource**

   Mode

   **Application Process** dialog box. You can select an existing process or create a new process

   The action on an API call that hits the control policy. The value is

   API Calls

   set to **Reject** and cannot be changed.

   The periods of time during which the service boundary takes effect. Valid values:

   - **By Period**: If you select this option, you must configure the **Start and End Time** parameter.

   Period

   - **Every Day**: If you select this option, you must configure the

   Effective Period

   Settings

   **Start and End Time** and **Effective Time per Day** parameters.

   - **Every Week**: If you select this option, you must configure the **Start and End Time**, **Effective Days per Week**, and **Effective Time per Day** parameters.

   The status the service boundary enters immediately when it is created. Valid values:

   - **Enable**

   - **Disable**

   Status

   > **Important**
   >
   > We recommend that you disable the service boundary first, and enable it after you have comprehensive knowledge about its influence.

   Settings

   The resources (RAM authorizations), RAM users, and RAM roles that are exempt from the service boundary. Specify the entities by ARNs. You can perform a fuzzy search and select existing ARNs from the drop-down list, or specify a custom ARN by following the format.

   Whitelist

   > **Note**
   >
   > Up to 10 ARNs can be specified in the whitelist of a service boundary.

4. Click **Submit**.

<a id="section-5-3-4-1-2"></a>

##### 5.3.4.1.2. Manage service boundaries

You can view, modify, enable, disable, and delete service boundaries and manage their whitelists in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Service Boundary**.

3. On the Service Boundary page, click **Advanced Filter** and configure the following parameters: **Service Boundary ID**, **Service Boundary Name**, **Management Scope**, **Authorize Organization**, **Associated Policy ID**, **Console Calls**, **Status**, and **Created At**. Then, click **Search**.

4. Perform the following operations as needed.

   | Operation | Procedure |
   | --- | --- |
   | View the details of a service boundary | Find the service boundary that you want to view and click its ID. On the <strong>Service Boundary Details</strong> page, you can view the details of the service boundary, including its basic information, associated API control policies, approval processes, and whitelists. |
   | Modify a service boundary | • Modify the configurations of a service boundary: Find the service boundary that you want to modify and click <strong>Edit</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column. On the page that appears, you can modify the basic information, management scope, control mode, and effective period of the service boundary.<br>• Modify the API control policies associated with a service boundary: Find the service boundary that you want to modify and click <strong>Modify</strong> <strong>Policy</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column. On the <strong>Associated Policy</strong> tab of the page that appears, click <strong>Add API Control Policy</strong> to associate control policies. You can also find an API control policy and click <strong>Remove</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column to disassociate the control policy. |
   | Enable or disable a service boundary | Find the service boundary that you want to enable or disable and click <strong>Enabled</strong> or <strong>Disable</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column. |
   | Manage whitelists | Find the service boundary that you want to manage, move the pointer over the <strong>More</strong> icon in the <strong>Actions</strong> column, and then select <strong>Manage</strong> <strong>Whitelist</strong>. On the <strong>Whitelist</strong> tab of the page that appears, you can click <strong>Add</strong> or <strong>Edit</strong> to add or modify the Alibaba Cloud Resource Names (ARNs) that are exempt from the service boundary. |
   | Delete a service boundary | Find the service boundary that you want to delete, move the pointer over the More icon in the <strong>Actions</strong> column, and then select <strong>Delete</strong>. In the message that appears, click OK. |

<a id="section-5-3-4-2"></a>

#### 5.3.4.2. Control policy management

API control policies are associated with service boundaries to implement fine-grained access control. In an API control policy, you can specify conditions based on parameter values of specific API operations. After it is associated with a service boundary, actions will be taken when the conditions in the API control policy are met. For example, you can define a control policy that enables service boundaries to take actions when users query details of instances whose names contain a specific string.

**Supported services**

The following table lists the cloud services and their API versions that are supported by API control policies.

> **Note**
>
> The services and API versions listed in the console prevail. We recommend that you refer to relevant API documentation to learn about the operations and their parameters.

**Content of control policies**

The content of a control policy consists of a coordinate and parameters. The policies are stored as a JSON file that can be modified on the control policy details page.

| Element | Description |
| --- | --- |
| coordinate | The coordinate of the API operation. Format: <code> ${popCode}:${version}:${action} </code>. popCode indicates the product code; version indicates the API version; action indicates the API operation. You can use an asterisk (\*) as a wildcard character to replace ${version} so that all API versions are included. |
| parameters | An array that contains details about the rule, including the name of the parameter (key), logical expression (condition), and specified value (value). |
| ﹂condition | The logical relationship between the actual value of the parameter and the specified value. |
| ﹂value | The specified value.<br>Note<br>The value can be left empty only if condition is set to NotNull or IsNull. |
| ﹂key | The name of the controlled API operation. |

**Example**

```json
[
 {
  "coordinate": "CloudAPI:2016-02-01:AbolishApi",
  "parameters": [
   {
    "condition": "IsNull",
    "value": "",
    "key": "AccessKeyId"
   }
  ]
 }
]
```

<a id="section-5-3-4-2-1"></a>

##### 5.3.4.2.1. Create an API control policy

In the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can create API control policies to control API operations on cloud resources based on values of the request parameters.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Control Policies**.

3. On the **API control policy management** page, click **Create an API control policy**.

4. On the **Create Control Policy** page, specify the name and description of the policy and click **Create** in the Control Content section. In the dialog box that appears, configure the following parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Cloud Services | The cloud services whose API operations are to be controlled. |
   | Version | The API version. Some cloud services may have multiple API versions. We recommend that you select All Versions for this parameter. |
   | API | The API operation that is controlled.<br>Note<br>Each rule is set for a single operation. If you want to specify rules for multiple operations in a single policy, you can click <strong>Add Rule</strong>. The rules in a policy are in <strong>OR</strong> logical relations. This means that when the policy is attached to a service boundary, the policy takes effect as long as one of the rules is met. |
   | Field | The request parameter to be controlled, a specified value, and the logical relation between the values in actual requests and the specified value.<br>The logical relations vary with the types of the selected request parameters. Valid values include <strong>Similar To</strong>, <strong>Equal to String</strong>, <strong>Equal to</strong> <strong>(case-insensitive)</strong>, <strong>Empty</strong>, <strong>Not Empty</strong>.<br>Note<br>You can click <strong>Add Field</strong> to specify multiple conditions. The conditions in a rule are in <strong>AND</strong> logical relations. This means that the rule takes effect only if all conditions are met.<br><strong>Example</strong>: The following figure shows how to configure the Field parameter for a rule that is created to control the action of creating a VPC named "test".<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f2f96876fb046c17d74d4491a7385b4c.jpeg) |

5. Click **Create**. Then, you can attach the API control policy to service boundaries.

<a id="section-5-3-4-2-2"></a>

##### 5.3.4.2.2. Manage API control policies

You can view the details of existing API control policies, including their content and association with service boundaries. You can also modify and delete the policies.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Control Policies**.

3. On the page that appears, the existing policies are listed, and you can perform operations on them.

   | Operation | Procedure |
   | --- | --- |
   | View details of an API control policy | Click the ID of an API control policy. On the <strong>Policy Details</strong> tab of the page that appears, you can view the basic information and control content of the policy. On the <strong>Reference Information</strong> tab, you can view information of the service boundaries with which the policy is associated. You can click <strong>Disassociate</strong> in the Actions column corresponding to a service boundary to cancel the association. |
   | Modify an API control policy | • Click <strong>Modify</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column corresponding to a policy. In the dialog box that appears, you can modify its name and description.<br>• Click <strong>Modify Control Content</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column corresponding to a policy. On the policy details page that appears, you can modify or delete the existing rules in the policy, or create new rules.<br>Note<br>• When you modify a rule, you cannot change the cloud service, API version, or the API operation involved.<br>• After you delete a rule, service boundaries with which the policy is associated will be affected. Proceed with caution.<br>If you are familiar with the format of control policies, you can click <strong>Custom Edit</strong> to modify the JSON file of the policy. This way, you can modify the cloud service, API version, and the API operation involved.You need to make sure that the modifications comply with the JSON format and that you are aware of the modifications' impact on relevant service boundaries. |
   | Delete an API control policy | Click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column corresponding to a policy.<br>Note<br>Policies that are associated with service boundaries cannot be deleted. |

<a id="section-5-3-5"></a>

### 5.3.5. AccessKey log

This topic describes how to view and export the logs of AccessKey pair calls to understand the usage of AccessKey pairs. This helps you enhance the security of AccessKey pairs.

> **Important**
>
> The AccessKey logs are for reference only. Data collection may miss records or experience delays. Do not use this data to disable AccessKeys.

<a id="section-5-4"></a>

## 5.4. Operation audit

<a id="section-5-4-1"></a>

### 5.4.1. Overview

The Overview page consists of the Basic Data, Event Count Trend, Getting Started, and Unusual IP Address Events sections to help you quickly learn about the overall situation of operation audit.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned one of the following roles: operations administrator, resource auditor, organization resource auditor, security auditor, global organization security auditor, platform security auditor, organization security administrator, global organization security administrator, security system configuration administrator, platform security administrator, or platform security configuration administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Overview**.

4. View the information.

   - **Basic Data**: displays the following metrics: **Total Events (Yesterday)**, **Notifications (Yesterday)**, **Total Sensitive Events (Yesterday)**, and **Effective Organizations**.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4cff4ba58f0b14a2e7e30832659ae481.jpeg)

   - **Event Count Trend**: displays the number of resource events within a specific period of time in a column chart. You can select a service and a resource type from the Product Type and Resource Type drop-down lists and select a 7-day, 15-day, or 30-day period. You can move the pointer over a column in the chart to view the specific quantity.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2672e8613ec9a1e903d84f5a3c76c6b8.jpeg)

   - **Getting Started**: displays the features of operation audit and the procedure for using operation audit to quickly get started.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/804db646537187cde153bcadc98cf4b2.jpeg)

   - **Unusual IP Address Events**: records events of access from unusual IP addresses. You can specify a time range to view the information about unusual IP address events within the time range.

     > **Important**
     >
     > Before you use this feature, you must specify common IP addresses.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/822c89871dc9998a321b482b717006f0.jpeg)

     - **Configure common IP addresses:**

       <ol type="a">

       <li>

       In the **Unusual IP Address Events** section, click **Common IP Settings**.

       </li>

       <li>

       In the **Common IP Settings** dialog box, specify common IP addresses.

       - You can specify up to 20 common IP addresses.

         ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e6a90b2ec79bf8a8ff9c559b89c19b18.jpeg)

         - **Add IP addresses**: Click **Add IP Address**. In the IP address field, enter a common IP address.

           > **Note**
           >
           > IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported.
           >
           > - An example of IPv4 CIDR blocks: 192.168.1.0/24. If the subnet mask of a login IP address is 32 bits in length, only this IP address is allowed to log in.
           >
           > - An example of IPv6 CIDR blocks: 2001:db8:1234:abcd::/64.
           >
           > - The CIDR block cannot be duplicated.

         - **Remove IP addresses**: Click **Delete** next to an IP address.

       - **View Historical IP addresses**: Click **View Historical IP Addresses**. Then, the right-side **Historical IP Addresses** panel displays the historical IP addresses. The IP addresses are sorted in descending order of visits. You can enter an IP address into the search box above the list to search for an IP address.

         ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/860fc1f8a46cbb41a385399cf523e2bf.jpeg)

       </li>

       </ol>

       <ol type="i" start="100">

       <li>

       Click **OK**.

       </li>

       </ol>

     - **View event details**:

       You can click **Details** in the **Actions** column of the event list in the Unusual IP Address Events sector to view detailed information in the Event Details panel, including the basic information of the event and API call details.

       ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/77cf0500f6719a75c25d0db9a1125a65.jpeg)

<a id="section-5-4-2"></a>

### 5.4.2. Operation logs

This topic describes how to view operation logs.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, an organization administrator, a resource set administrator, or a resource user. Custom roles have the permissions to view operation logs and choose Operation Audit > Operation Log in the left-side navigation pane.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Operation Log**.

4. Click **Advanced Filter** and configure the following parameters: **Organization**, **Product Type**, **Resource Type**, **Event Type**, **Resource ID**, **Source IP**, **Event ID**, and **Start/End Time**. Then, click **Search** to search for operation logs that meet the specified filter conditions.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Before you configure the **Resource Type** and **Event Type** parameters, configure the **Product Type** parameter.

5. View the operation log list.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/613a42028e6e6e492a3b11b6222aa163.jpeg)

6. Find the operation log that you want to view and click **View** in the **Details** column.

7. In the **Operation Details** panel, view the details of the operation log.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2c8c318c264f9f5d18842163bac830df.jpeg)

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is one of the following: Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Organization Resource Auditor, Security Auditor, Global Organization Security Auditor, Platform Security Auditor, Organization Security Administrator, Global Organization Security Administrator, Security System Configuration Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, or Platform Security Configuration Administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Operation Audit** > **Advanced Query**.

4. Select a query type. You can perform default queries, queries by custom template, or queries by system template.

   - **Default query**: When you enter Advanced Query, the system defaults to the **Default Query** tab.

   - **Query by custom template**: On the left side of the **Advanced Query** page, in the template repository, click your target custom template to expand its query tab.

     > **Note**
     >
     > - Custom templates are query templates saved via the **Save As** operation.
     >
     > - You can edit or delete custom templates.
     >
     >   - **Edit template**: Hover over the target template
     >
     >     , select **Edit**
     >
     >     <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/09e1014c3f0c546d37a97e872f6e4152.png" width="10" alt="">
     >
     >     **Template**, enter the template name in the dialog box, and click **Confirm**.
     >
     >   - **Delete template**: Hover over the target template
     >
     >     , select **Delete**
     >
     >     <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/09e1014c3f0c546d37a97e872f6e4152.png" width="10" alt="">
     >
     >     **Template**, and click **Confirm**.

   - **Query by system template:** On the left side of the **Advanced Query** page, in the template repository, click your target system template to expand its query tab.

     > **Note**
     >
     > System templates are preset by the system and cannot be edited or deleted.

5. Set filter conditions such as **Username**, **Organization**, **Product Type**, **Resource Type**, **Event Type**, **Operation Name**, **Resource ID**, **Source IP**, and **Event ID**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The organization condition is required.
   >
   > - The event type automatically updates based on the selected product type and resource type.
   >
   > - On the Default Query tab, select query conditions according to your needs.
   >
   > - On the custom template query tab, the system automatically links the query conditions configured for that template. You can flexibly modify or add query conditions as needed.
   >
   > - On the system template query tab, the system automatically links the preset query conditions of that template. You can flexibly modify or add query conditions and save them as a custom template.

6. Select a time period as needed. You can choose **1 hour**, **12 hours**, **1 day**, **7 days**, **30 days**, or a **custom** time range.

7. Click **Run** to view target events in the list.

   | Field | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Time | The time when the target event operation completed. |
   | Username | Displays the username, user ID, role ID, or associated organization UID of the operator, depending on the calling method. |
   | Product Type | The cloud service corresponding to the target event. |
   | Resource Type | The resource type corresponding to the target event. |
   | Source IP | The IP address of the operator who triggered the target event. |
   | Operation Name | The specific operation name of the target event. |
   | Status | The current status of the target event. |
   | Call Source | The source from which the target event originated. |
   | Organization | The organization where the target event occurred. |
   | Resource Set | The resource set where the target event occurred. |
   | Event ID | The ID of the target event. |

   | Details | Click <strong>View</strong> to expand the operation details panel and review <strong>Basic Information</strong> and <strong>Instance Details</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/529b43fbf0c26e1bd0eb99fa5b1864cb.jpeg) |
   | --- | --- |

8. Perform other related operations as needed.

   | Operation | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Create a custom template | i. On the Default Query or System Template Query tab, set your query conditions and click <strong>Save As</strong>.<br>ii. In the <strong>Create Template</strong> dialog box, enter a template name.<br>iii. Click <strong>Confirm</strong> to create the custom template. |
   | Update a custom template | i. On the Custom Template Query tab, update the query conditions.<br>ii. Click <strong>Save</strong> to update the custom template. |
   | Create an event export task | Transfer operation logs of Apsara Stack products to an OSS bucket for long-term storage. Create an asynchronous dump task to export specific operation logs to OSS.<br>i. Click <strong>Export Event</strong>.<br>ii. In the <strong>Export Event</strong> dialog box, define the scope of operation logs to export.<br>• Basic report information<br>• <strong>Task name</strong>: Enter a name for the dump task.<br>• Export objects<br>• <strong>Organization</strong>: Select the organization to which the operation logs belong.<br>• <strong>Filter condition name</strong>: Set filter conditions for cloud service resources to narrow the log scope. You can select either product name or resource type. Multiple selections are not supported.<br>• <strong>Start and end time</strong>: Select the time range during which the operations occurred.<br>• <strong>Username</strong>: Enter the username of the operator. Only one username is allowed.<br>• <strong>Resource ID</strong>: Enter the resource instance ID associated with the operation. Only one resource ID is allowed.<br>• <strong>Source IP</strong>: Enter the IP address of the operator. Only one source IP is allowed.<br>iii. Click <strong>Confirm</strong>. After successful creation, you can view the task on the Export Records page. |
   | Create a notification | Click <strong>Create Notification</strong> to go to the Audit Notification page where you can create a new notification.You can specify notification recipients based on rule names, check frequency, and trigger conditions. For more information, see Audit notifications. |

<a id="section-5-4-4"></a>

### 5.4.4. Export history

After an event export task is created, you can view the status of the task on the Export History page. After the task is complete, you can save the **.xlsx** log file to your computer for backup.

**Prerequisites Prerequisites**

- An event export task is created on the Advanced Query page.

- You are assigned one of the following roles: operations administrator, resource auditor, organization resource auditor, security auditor, global organization security auditor, platform security auditor, organization security administrator, global organization security administrator, security system configuration administrator, platform security administrator, or platform security configuration administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Export History**.

4. Optional. Click Advanced Filter and configure the following parameters: **Task Name**, **Creator**, **Status**, and **Time Range**. Then, click **Search**.

5. View the information about Object Storage Service (OSS) delivery tasks in the task list.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/aaac47a6c4050b59f90f49669fc46df6.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > A task is in one of the following states:
   >
   > - **In Progress**: The task is being executed.
   >
   > - **Downloading**: The task is downloading data.
   >
   > - **Completed**: The task is complete. You can click **Download Report** in the **Actions** column to download the operation log report from the OSS bucket to your computer.
   >
   > - **Failed**: The task failed. You can click **Retry** in the **Actions** column to execute the task again.
   >
   > - **Expired**: The task has expired. The default validity period is four days.

### 5.4.5. Audit notifications

By configuring audit notifications, you can detect in real time and quickly respond to potential security threats and abnormal behaviors to ensure system stability and data integrity.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned one of the following roles: operations administrator, resource auditor, organization resource auditor, security auditor, global organization security auditor, platform security auditor, organization security administrator, global organization security administrator, security system configuration administrator, platform security administrator, or platform security configuration administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Audit Notifications**.

4. Click **Create Notification**.

5. In the Create Notification dialog box, configure the parameters.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/461b1950dd44cb33b56eb8280a43a974.jpeg)

   | Paramete r | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Rule Name | The name of the audit notification rule. You can click <strong>Select Template</strong> to specify a rule template, such as User AccessKey Pair Deletion Event. |
   | Check Frequen cy | The check frequency. Valid values:<br>• <strong>Fixed Interval</strong>: Operations are checked against the rule at a fixed interval, such as 5 minutes, 2 hours, or 1 day.<br>• <strong>Cron</strong>: Operations are checked against the rule based on a CRON expression. A CRON expression is a string used to schedule tasks. You can use a CRON expression to specify when to perform tasks in a more fine-grained manner. For more information, see the CRON expressions section of this topic. |
   | Trigger Conditio ns | The conditions under which notifications are triggered. You can add multiple trigger conditions and combine them by using AND or OR. If the conditions are combined by using AND, a notification is triggered only when all conditions are met. If the conditions are combined by using OR, a notification is triggered when one of the conditions is met. |
   | Notificat ion Title | The notification title. |
   | Notificat ion Content | The notification content. |
   | Notificat ion Object | One or more users to whom notifications are sent. |
   | Status | Specifies whether to enable the audit notification rule.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fab20422d5853fc54e7f953195d9d1da.png)<br>: enables the audit notification rule.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5b665a21269fe6b9182df9a5535f7d36.png)<br>: disables the audit notification rule. |

6. Click **OK**. The audit notification rule is created.

7. Perform the following operations as needed.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Operation</td>
       <td>Description</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>View the details of the audit notification rule</td>

In the rule list, view the information about the audit notification rule in the following columns: <strong>Rule Name</strong>, <strong>Check Frequency</strong>, <strong>Trigger</strong> <strong>Conditions</strong>, <strong>Status</strong>, <strong>Notification Object</strong>, and <strong>Created At</strong>.<br>Note<br>You can move the pointer over the value in the Notification Object column to view the specific users.<br>ii. Click <strong>Details</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>iii. In the panel that appears, view the details of the audit notification rule.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2d2342336017630a5665803ef1f5725e.jpeg" alt=""></td>
     </tr>

     </tr>

       <td>Enable the audit notification rule</td>
       <td>Click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/61de85f2927f2e37de321ccde8af1b3f.png" width="17" alt="">icon in the <strong>Actions</strong> column and select <strong>Enabled</strong>.<br>Note<br>You can enable an audit notification rule only if it is in the <strong>Disabled</strong> state.</td>

Click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/61de85f2927f2e37de321ccde8af1b3f.png" width="17" alt="">icon in the <strong>Actions</strong> column and select <strong>Disable</strong>.<br>Note<br>You can disable an audit notification rule only if it is in the <strong>Enabled</strong> state.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
