       <td>i. Move the pointer over the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/61de85f2927f2e37de321ccde8af1b3f.png" width="17" alt="">icon in the <strong>Actions</strong> column and select<br><strong>Delete</strong>.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

**CRON expressions**

A CRON expression is a string of six or seven fields that are separated with five or six spaces. Each field describes an individual detail of the schedule.

Specify the CRON expression in one of the following formats:

- &lt;Seconds> &lt;Minutes> &lt;Hours> &lt;Day of month> &lt;Months> &lt;Day of week> &lt;Years>

- &lt;Seconds> &lt;Minutes> &lt;Hours> &lt;Day of month> &lt;Months> &lt;Day of week>

**Valid values of fields**

| Field | Valid value | Supported special character | Remarks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Seconds | 0–59 | - \* / | None |
| Minutes | 0–59 | - \* / | None |
| Hours | 0–23 | - \* / | None |
| Day of month | 1–31 | - \* ? / L W C | None |
| Months | 1–12 | JAN-DEC - \* / | None |
| Day of week | 1–7 | SUN-SAT - \* ? / L C # | A value of 1 indicates Sunday, a value of 2 indicates Monday, and so on. |
| Years (optional) | 1970–2099 | , - \* / | The value of this field is automatically generated. |

**Special characters**

| Character | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| \* | All values of a field. | Set the Minutes field to an asterisk (\*) to run a task every minute. |
| ? | Any value of a field. However, this character can be used only in the Day of month and Day of week fields. For the two fields, using ? in one field allows you to specify a value in the other without creating a conflict. | To run a task on the twentieth day of every month, regardless of the day of the week, use the following CRON expression: <code> 13 13 15 20 * ? </code>. Because the Day of month field is set to 20, the Day of week field must be <code> ? </code>, instead of <code> * </code>.Using <code> * </code> for the Day of week field means every day of the week. This conflicts with the twentieth-day requirement and results in an invalid CRON expression. |
| - | A range of values. | Set the Minutes field to 5-20 to run a task every minute from the fifth minute to the twentieth minute of an hour. |
| / | Separates the start time and interval. | Set the Minutes field to 5/20 to run a task at the fifth, twenty-fifth, and forty-fifth minutes of an hour. |
| , | Separates multiple values. | Set the Minutes field to 5,20 to run a task at the fifth and twentieth minutes of an hour. |
| L | The last day of the month or the last specified day of the week in a month. | Set the Day of week field to 5L to run a task on the last Thursday of a month. |
| C | The specified date (calendar day). If no date is specified, C indicates any day. This character can be used only in the Day of month and Day of week fields. | Set the Day of month field to 5C to run a task on the first day after the fifth day of a month. Set the Day of week field to 1C to run a task on the first day after Sunday. |
| W | The nearest weekday (Monday through Friday) to the specified day of the month.You can use this character only in the Day of month field. | Set the Day of month field to 5W. If the fifth day of a month is a Saturday, the task runs on the fourth day, which is a Friday. If the fifth day of a month is a Sunday, the task runs on the sixth day of the month, which is a Monday. If the fifth day of a month is a weekday, the task runs on that day. The nearest weekday search does not cross month boundaries. |
| LW | The last weekday of a month. | None. |
| # | The N-th occurrence of a day of the week in a month. This character can be used only in the Day of week field. | Set the Day of week field to 4#2 to run a task on the second Wednesday of a month. 4 indicates Wednesday and 2 indicates the second. |

**Examples**

- `*/5 * * * * ?` : Run a task every 5 seconds.

- `0 */1 * * * ?` : Run a task at an interval of 1 minute.

- `0 0 2 1 * ?` : Run a task at 02:00 on the first day of every month.

- `0 15 10 ? * MON-FRI` : Run a task at 10:15 every day from Monday to Friday.

- `0 0 1 ? * L` : Run a task at 01:00 every Sunday.

- `0 15 10 ? * 6#3` : Run a task at 10:15 on the third Friday of every month.

### 5.4.6. Event fields

This topic describes the key fields in operation events.

**Key fields**

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| acsRegion | The region ID. |
| additionalEventData | The additional information about the event. |
| apiVersion | The API version information. |
| eventId | The event ID. |
| eventApi | The operation that was called in the event. |
| eventName | The name of the event, if any. |
| eventRW | The read/write type of the event. Valid values:<br>• Write<br>• Read |
| eventTime | The time when the event occurred. |
| eventVersion | The format version of the user-initiated event. The current version is 1. |
| errorCode | The error code that is returned when an error occurred during the processing of the API request. |
| errorMessage | The error message that is returned when an error occurred during the processing of the API request. |
| requestId | The request ID. |
| requestParameterJson | The JSON-formatted representation of the requestParameters parameter. |
| resourceName | The name of the event-associated resource. The name is the unique identifier of the resource. |
| resourceType | The type of the event-associated resource. |
| responseElements | The response in the JSON format. |
| referencedResources | The resources that are associated with the event. |
| serviceName | The name of the Apsara Stack service for which the user-initiated event is generated. |
| sourceIpAddress | The IP address from which the user-initiated event is generated. |
| userAgent | The user agent that sends the API request. |
| userIdentity | The identity information about the requester. For more information, see the Fields included in userIdentity section of this topic. |

**Fields included in userIdentity**

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| type | The type of the identity. Valid values:<br>• root-account: an Apsara Stack account.<br>• ram-user: a Resource Access Management (RAM) user.<br>• assumed-role: a RAM role. |
| userName | The username of the account used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. |
| accountId | The primary key (PK) of the account of the requester. |
| principalId | The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the RAM role. |
| accessKeyId | The AccessKey ID that is used by the requester.<br>• If the requester sends an API request by using an SDK, this field is recorded.<br>• If the requester performs an operation in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, this field is not recorded.<br>• If the requester sends an API request by using a Security Token Service (STS) token, this field is set to the temporary AccessKey ID. |
| orgId | The organization ID of the current user. |
| sysUid | The UID of the account used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. |
| resourceSetId | The resource set ID of the current user. |

### 5.4.7. Examples

<a id="section-5-4-7-1"></a>

#### 5.4.7.1. Use operation audit to monitor AccessKey pair deletion events

This topic describes how to use the audit notification feature of operation audit to monitor AccessKey pair deletion events and send notifications by using internal messages.

**Background information**

An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret, which are used to identify a user and verify the key of the user. Malicious or accidental deletion of AccessKey pairs may cause service interruption and bring serious losses to enterprises or individuals.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned one of the following roles: Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Organization Resource Auditor, Security Auditor, Global Organization Security Auditor, Platform Security Auditor, Organizational Security Administrator, Global Organization Security Administrator, Security System Configuration Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Configuration Administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Audit Notifications**.

4. Click **Create Notification**.

5. In the Create Notification dialog box, configure the parameters.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f89bdad418dfcf0b9932d1fa675494e8.jpeg)

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Rule Name | The name of the rule. Click <strong>Select Template</strong>. In the Select Template panel, find the <strong>User AccessKey Pair Deletion Event</strong> template and click Set. |
   | Check Frequency | The check frequency of the rule. In this example, a fixed interval of 15 minutes is configured. |
   | Trigger Conditions | The trigger conditions of the rule. In this example, <strong>Operation Name</strong> = <strong>DeleteUserAccessKey</strong> is configured. |
   | Notification Title | The title of the notification. In this example, User AccessKey Pair Deletion Event Notification is used. |
   | Notification Content | The content of the notification. In this example, the following content is used: A user AccessKey pair deletion event occurred in the account in the past 15 minutes. |
   | Notification Object | The recipient of the notification. In this example, <strong>admin</strong> is selected. |
   | Status | The status of the rule. In this example, the switch is turned on. |

**Verify the feature**

> **Note**
>
> In this example, the following operations are performed by the admin user.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the upper-right corner of the page, click the profile picture and select **User Information**.

3. In the AccessKey Pair section, find an AccessKey pair and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6041d04f62ed5c8301c258c48fdce6c2.jpeg)

4. In the dialog box that appears, select the checkbox and click **Delete**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/985681b6fd362e1b60e26a69a1d6e747.jpeg)

5. Click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/aac04f3c9f79ad45bd471c4d56451551.png" width="18" alt=""> icon in the upper-right corner. In the Message window, click More to view

   internal messages. The following figure shows an example.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f36405994aeafeefabd1b689e325f4b9.jpeg)

6. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Advanced Query**. On the Advanced Query page, select DeleteUserAccessKey from the Operation Name drop-down list and click Run to view the corresponding logs.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/12954ea9482f985a0dac3c0c7b384ef1.jpeg)

## 5.5. Alibaba Cloud platform management configurations

This directory includes topics related to resource synchronization configurations and resource ownership configurations for Alibaba Cloud platforms.

<a id="section-5-5-1"></a>

### 5.5.1. Configure resource synchronization for an Alibaba Cloud platform

You can enable or disable resource synchronization based on your business requirements. If you enable the resource synchronization feature for a cloud platform, the status of instances in the cloud platform is synchronized in real time. If you disable the resource synchronization feature for the cloud platform, you can no longer obtain information about instances in the cloud platform in real time. As a result, the instance information in the resource list is updated with a delay.

**Prerequisites**

- You have connected an Alibaba Cloud platform to the central cloud platform as a platform administrator. To connect an Alibaba Cloud platform to the central cloud platform, log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Multi-cloud Management**.

- You are the operations administrator of the managed Alibaba Cloud platform. The operations administrator is assigned a Resource Access Management (RAM) role to which the AdministratorAccess policy of the Alibaba Cloud account is attached.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Public Cloud Management Configurations**.

4. On the Public Cloud Management Configurations page, find the Alibaba Cloud platform that you want to manage and click **Resource Synchronization** in the **Actions** column.

5. In the **Resource Synchronization Configurations** dialog box, turn on or off **Enable Incremental Synchronization for Resources** and configure parameters.

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f51da453cd170b9dee66798993d5a11e.png" width="30" alt=""> : The resource synchronization feature is disabled.

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a35cdf68a1a87ee1a42f3cefc9e08745.png" width="30" alt=""> : The resource synchronization feature is enabled.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <th colspan="2">Parameter or section</th>
       <th>Description</th>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="2">Synchr onize Cloud Servic e Config uratio ns</td>
       <td>Activate Cloud Service</td>
       <td>Select the cloud service that you want to synchronize from the drop-down list.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Cloud Service Region</td>
       <td>Select the region to which the cloud service that you want to synchronize belongs from the drop-down list.<br>Note<br>The regions that are associated with the Alibaba Cloud platform are displayed in the Cloud Service Region drop-down list.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="2">Cloud Config Config uratio ns</td>
       <td>Activate Cloud Service</td>
       <td>Select Cloud Config from the drop-down list.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Cloud Service Region</td>
       <td>Select the region in which Cloud Config resides from the drop-down list.<br>Note<br>The regions that are associated with the Alibaba Cloud platform are displayed in the Cloud Service Region drop-down list.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

6. Click **OK**.

### 5.5.2. Configure resource ownership

You can move resources in the default resource set in an Alibaba Cloud platform to other resource sets. This allows you to manage resources in the Alibaba Cloud platform by resource set.

**Prerequisites**

- You have connected an Alibaba Cloud platform to the central cloud platform as a platform administrator. To connect an Alibaba Cloud platform to the central cloud platform, log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Multi-cloud Management**.

- You are the operations administrator of the managed Alibaba Cloud platform. The operations administrator is assigned a Resource Access Management (RAM) role to which the AdministratorAccess policy is attached.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Public Cloud Management Configurations**.

4. On the Public Cloud Management Configurations page, find the Alibaba Cloud platform that you want to manage and click **Resource Ownership** in the **Actions** column.

5. On the **Resource Ownership** page, configure the **Product Type** and **Resource Type** parameters.

6. Find the resource instance that you want to manage and click **Change Ownership** in the **Actions** column.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can search for a resource instance by ID or name in the search boxes above the resource instance list.

7. In the **Change Resource Set Ownership** dialog box, select the organization and resource set to which you want to move the resource instance.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <th colspan="2">Parameter or section</th>
       <th>Description</th>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="3">Selected Instance Information</td>
       <td>Selected Instance</td>
       <td>The ID of the selected instance.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Organization</td>
       <td>Select an organization to which you want to move the resource instance from the drop-down list.<br>Note<br>The organizations that are associated with the Alibaba Cloud platform are displayed in the Organization drop-down list.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Change Resource Set To</td>
       <td>Select a resource set to which you want to move the resource instance from the drop-down list.<br>Note<br>The resource sets that are associated with the Alibaba Cloud platform are displayed in the Change Resource Set To drop-down list.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

8. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-5-6"></a>

## 5.6. Asynchronous task

You can view the progress and results of asynchronous tasks on the Asynchronous Task page.

**Background information**

On the Asynchronous Task page, you can view the information about each asynchronous task, including the task name, task type, status, creator, and creation time. The system updates the execution situation of each task in real time. This way, users can know whether the task is running as expected at any time.

Asynchronous tasks are classified into the following types: batch creation of organizations and users and batch authorization of roles.

**View the information about a task**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Asynchronous Task**.

4. On the **Asynchronous Task** page, specify the **Start Date**, **End Date**, **Task Type**, and **Task Name** parameters to search for the desired task.

5. View the task information in the task list.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/05fe7f1e94e8d36fe47d5b4e24bff3ca.jpeg)

6. Find the desired task and click the task name or click **View Task** in the **Actions** column. The **Task Details** panel appears.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/56f52334f0f52b45335cd2eb4a84e6be.jpeg)

**Delete a task**

1. On the **Asynchronous Task** page, find the desired task and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b64c0149349823e0a01eb45383764a2b.jpeg)

2. In the **Delete** message, click **OK**.

   > **Important**
   >
   > After a task is deleted, the information about the task cannot be queried. Exercise caution when you delete a task. The information about task deletion is recorded in an operation log.

# 6.Configurations

<a id="section-6-1"></a>

## 6.1. Resource pool configuration

You can manage the logical inventory of cloud resources to control the maximum usage of resources.

<a id="section-6-1-1"></a>

### 6.1.1. Service resources

<a id="section-6-1-1-1"></a>

#### 6.1.1.1. Configure quota items

This topic describes how to configure quota items on the Resource Pool Configuration page.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Limits**

- You can add a subitem of a group quota item without adding the group quota item. When you select a group quota item, all of its subitems are selected. For more information, see Cloud services that support group quota configuration.

- When you add a subitem of a category quota item, the category quota item is also added. For more information, see Cloud services that support category quota configuration.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.

4. Select the **Product Resources** tab.

5. In the upper part of the page, select a resource pool, a region, and a zone.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The resource pool drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments.
   >
   > - If you select All Zones, you can manage quotas in the region. If you select the corresponding zone, you can manage quotas in the zone, and the Resource Pool Configuration page displays the services only in the zone.

6. (Optional) In the upper-right corner of the page, select **Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts** to display only the cloud services that trigger alerts.

7. Click the target cloud product to open the **Resource Pool Details** panel. Using Elastic Compute Service (ECS) as an example, view configuration details displayed in the following columns: **Resource Item**, **Logical Inventory**, **Physical Inventory**, and **Total Activated Resources**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5ba6358a91438ffce1a7fc5ab329a5fe.jpeg)

8. In the **Resource Pool Details** panel, click **Configure Quota Items** at the bottom.

9. In the **Configure Quota Items** dialog box, add or remove quota items.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When you configure quota items for a specific zone, you can use the **Synchronize Quota Items to Other Zones** switch to control quota items in other zones.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e40dfe8ee407bd5f47304e6a83c9967f.jpeg)

   - **Add quota items**: In the **Available Quota Items** list on the left side, select the quota

     items that you want to add and click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4e99c1b8ecc78274822b98a049fc748a.png" width="17" alt=""> to add them to the **Added Quota Items** list on

     the right side.

   - **Remove quota items**: In the **Added Quota Items** list on the right side, select the

     quota items that you want to remove and click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c24dd017bf4a098ad8553ce74229c8dc.png" width="18" alt=""> to remove them.

0. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-6-1-1-2"></a>

#### 6.1.1.2. Create or modify a logical inventory

After configuring quota items, you can set a logical inventory for them to limit the total resource usage.

**Background information**

Resources in a resource pool are limited. You must limit the resource quotas for each organization based on its scope of responsibilities in the resource pool to ensure that each department receives a fare share of resources.

The quota configuration process in a resource pool is as follows:

1. The platform administrator sets the maximum total usage of each cloud service resource for the entire resource pool.

2. The operations administrator allocates quotas of each cloud service resource to each level-1 organization based on the logical inventory set by the platform administrator.

3. Each organization administrator allocates quotas to subordinate organizations or resource sets sequentially.

When you activate, change configurations of, delete, or transfer ownership of a cloud service, the system directly uses the corresponding quota to validate resources and update consumption calculations for organizations and resource sets with configured quotas configured. For organizations and resource sets without configured quotas, the system traverses up the hierarchy to find the quota of a parent organization that has an ownership relationship with the current organization or resource set for validation and calculation.

**Prerequisites**

- Quota items are configured.

- The default operator is the platform administrator.

**Limits**

- When the physical inventory is unlimited, the logical inventory must not be less than the allocated inventory.

- When the physical inventory is limited, the default logical inventory must not be less than the used inventory and must not exceed the physical inventory.

  > **Important**
  >
  > - When the logical inventory falls below the used inventory, the system restricts resource creation, leading to resource creation failure.
  >
  > - If you need to set the logical inventory to a value greater than the physical inventory, contact technical support to disable logical inventory validation and remove the physical inventory limit.

- When you configure the logical inventory of a group quota for the first time, it defaults to the sum of the logical inventory of all child items. After manual configuration, your specified value takes precedence. The sum of the logical inventory of all child items cannot exceed the logical inventory of the parent item.

  > **Note**
  >
  > Child items of a group quota item may share the same resource pool. Therefore, the physical inventory of a group quota item may be less than the sum of the physical inventory of its child items. This is normal.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.

4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.

5. In the upper part of the page, select a resource pool, a region, and an availability zone.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The resource pool is displayed only in multi-cloud scenarios.
   >
   > - When you select **All Zones**, the system enforces quota management at the region level. When you select a specific availability zone, the system enforces quota management at the availability zone level, and displays only the services in that availability zone.

6. (Optional) In the upper-right corner of the page, select **Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts** to quickly filter cloud services that have triggered alerts.

7. Click the target cloud service to open the **Resource Pool Details** panel. Using Elastic Compute Service (ECS) as an example, view the **Resource Item**, **Logical Inventory**, **Physical Inventory**, and **Total Activated Resources** of the cloud service.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5ba6358a91438ffce1a7fc5ab329a5fe.jpeg)

8. In the **Resource Pool Details** panel, click **Create Inventory** or **Modify Inventory** at the bottom of the page.

9. Enter inventory quotas in the **Logical Inventory** column to limit the maximum usage of resources.

   > **Note**
   >
   > If you do not specify a quota for a resource item, the system does not limit the resource consumption for the corresponding item.

0. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-6-1-1-3"></a>

#### 6.1.1.3. Cancel quotas

The resource pool configuration feature allows you to cancel configured quotas.

**Prerequisites**

- You have created an inventory.

- The default operator is the platform administrator.

> **Note**
>
> - When the requested resource quantity plus the total provisioned resource quantity exceeds the physical inventory, you can cancel the quota to clear the quota data for the service. After you clear the quota data, the console no longer validates resources for the service during resource creation, which enables overselling.
>
> - Canceling a quota resets the organization and logical inventory capacity data for the service to the unset status and disables quota validation. Proceed with caution.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.

4. Select the **Product Resources** tab.

5. At the top of the page, select a resource pool, a region, and an availability zone.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.
   >
   > - When you select **All Zones**, the system manages quotas at the region level. When you select a specific availability zone, the system manages quotas at the availability zone level, and displays only the services in that availability zone.

6. (Optional) In the upper-right corner of the page, select **Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts** to filter services that have triggered alerts.

7. Click the target cloud service to open the **Resource Pool Details** panel. Using Elastic Compute Service (ECS) as an example, check the **Resource Item**, **Logical Inventory**, **Physical Inventory**, and **Total Activated Resources** of the cloud service.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5ba6358a91438ffce1a7fc5ab329a5fe.jpeg)

8. In the **Resource Pool Details** panel, click **Cancel Quota** at the bottom.

9. In the **Cancel Quota** dialog box, select **I am aware of the risks and want to perform this operation**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When you cancel the quota for a specific availability zone, you can use the **Synchronize Quota Cancellation to Other Availability Zones** switch to control quotas in other availability zones.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/758c66bed74a67a6fd63ba2eebf5201e.jpeg)

0. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-6-1-1-4"></a>

#### 6.1.1.4. Configure physical inventory change notifications

After you configure physical inventory change notifications, the system sends SMS, email, or in-app notifications to the specified recipients at the configured time whenever the physical inventory quantity changes.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the platform administrator.

**Limits**

Connected public cloud resource pools do not support physical inventory change notifications.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top menu bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.

4. Select the **Product Resources** tab.

5. At the top of the page, select a resource pool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The system displays resource pools only in multi-cloud scenarios, and you can configure physical inventory change notifications only for the central cloud and secondary Apsara Stack.

6. Click **Inventory Change Notification** in the upper-right corner of the page.

7. In the **Inventory Change Notification** dialog box, select **Contact** and set **Notification Time**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fec9e782b78c717fdd037e2898b99ab3.jpeg)

8. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-6-1-2"></a>

### 6.1.2. AI service tokens

<a id="section-6-1-2-1"></a>

#### 6.1.2.1. Set quotas

You can set token quotas for AI services on a monthly basis. The used quota will automatically reset to the initial limit on the 1st of each calendar month.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the platform administrator.

> **Note**
>
> The current quota control mode is soft control. That is, when consumption exceeds the configured quota, the platform sends an alert notification but does not restrict further usage.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.

4. Select the **AI Service Token** tab.

5. In the upper part of the page, select a region and zone.

6. Click **Set Quota**.

7. Set the **Total Monthly Quota** and the **Quota** for each product.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/76ec9fe5124b88ee7092cef3d0180c34.jpeg)

8. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-6-2"></a>

## 6.2. Native hybrid cloud

<a id="section-6-2-1"></a>

### 6.2.1. Multi-Cloud Management

The Multi-Cloud Management page displays a list of integrated resource pools. The system manages cloud resources from multiple Apsara Stack Enterprise Editions and Alibaba Cloud Public Cloud in a unified manner.

**Prerequisites**

- Turn on the multi-cloud switch.

- The operating user defaults to the platform administrator.

**Constraints**

- When you integrate an Apsara Stack, the system currently supports only Apsara Stack Enterprise Edition v3.18.3 and earlier versions, and Enterprise Edition v3.18.6.

- Add a custom resource pool:

  - Create and enable a custom cloud platform type. For more information, see Cloud platform type management.

  - You can add a custom resource pool only when products exist under the custom cloud platform type.

  - You can add only one custom resource pool for each custom cloud platform type.

**Basic information**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configuration**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Multi-Cloud Management**.

4. On the **Multi-Cloud Management** page, view information such as central cloud name, central cloud code, creation time, update time, number of integrated resource pools, and remaining integrable quantity.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fc2815ddfed9e132d2517a6614748ed8.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > Total supported integration quantity equals the sum of integrated resource pools and remaining integrable quantity. The total supported integration quantity depends on the Multi-Cloud Management license of the current cloud.

5. Hover over the central cloud name and click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/47e3ede47e614733c277d1f1de2d86b5.png" width="11" alt=""> .

6. Enter the central cloud name in the text box and click **Confirm**. The system successfully modifies the central cloud name.

**Cloud service category**

**Descriptions of strong control, weak control, and SSO**

- Strong control: The Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console hosts the creation page and list page for products. It redirects to the cloud console for product detail pages.

- Weak control: The Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console hosts only the list page for products. It redirects to the cloud console for both the creation page and the detail page.

- SSO: Redirect to the corresponding product page on the subordinate cloud by using SSO to perform resource operations. When you switch the resource pool to a subordinate cloud from the product header in the central cloud, a prompt appears to redirect you to the product page of the selected resource pool.

### 6.2.2. Cloud platform type management

Configure and manage cloud platform types in Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console. The system presets two cloud platform types: Public Cloud and Apsara Stack. You can also define custom cloud platform types.

**Prerequisites**

- You have turned on the multi-cloud switch and deployed the COMS service.

- The operator is the platform administrator by default.

**Limits**

You cannot operate the preset cloud platform types.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Operations Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configuration**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Cloud Platform Type Management**.

4. Click **Add Type**.

5. In the **Add Type** dialog box, configure the cloud platform type.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fdff733be53844c72db1cd88582ac174.jpeg)

   | Configurati on item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Type Name | Enter a name for the cloud platform type. The name can contain only letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-). It cannot start with a digit. The name must be 2 to 30 characters in length. |
   | Code | Enter an encoding for the cloud platform type. The encoding can be up to 15 characters in length. |
   | Description | Enter a description for the cloud platform type. The description can be 1 to 150 characters in length. |
   | Type | The system sets the type of the new cloud platform to <strong>Custom</strong>. |

6. Click OK.

7. Perform other related operations.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/bd309a7b045fdc0ab0b47029f213433d.jpeg)

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Operation</td>
       <td>Description</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Edit cloud platform type</td>
       <td>i. Click <strong>Edit</strong> in the <strong>Action</strong> column of the cloud platform type.<br>ii. In the <strong>Modify Type</strong> dialog box, update the name and description of the cloud platform type.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/56da5055a1f5d0a6aad47aaca5ec15c1.jpeg" alt=""><br>iii. Click <strong>Confirm</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Disable cloud platform type</td>
       <td>i. Click <strong>Disable</strong> in the <strong>Action</strong> column of the cloud platform type.<br>Note<br>• You cannot disable a cloud platform type if products exist under it.<br>• You can disable a cloud platform type only when its status is Enabled. After you disable it, its status changes to Disabled.<br>• After you disable a cloud platform type, resource pools and products under the corresponding cloud platform no longer appear.<br>ii. Click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Enable cloud platform type</td>
       <td>i. Click <strong>Enable</strong> in the <strong>Action</strong> column of the cloud platform type.<br>Note<br>You can enable a cloud platform type only when its status is Disabled.After you enable it, its status changes to Enabled.</td>

In the dialog box, click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

**Impact on other features**

- **Multi-cloud management:** The multi-cloud management page displays items by cloud platform type. For more information, see Multi-Cloud Management.

- **Product management:** For more information, see Product management.

  - When you create a product, you can select a cloud platform type.

  - The classification tree on the product list displays the newly added cloud platform types. Each cloud platform type is a root node. You cannot edit root nodes in product management.

<a id="section-6-2-3"></a>

### 6.2.3. Export local cloud data

The configurations of the current cloud platform can be exported and used for multi-cloud configuration on another Apsara Stack platform. This way, the current cloud platform is managed by the Apsara Stack platform.

**Prerequisites**

- Native Hybrid Cloud and Local Cloud Data are selected by a platform administrator. To do so, click **Configurations** in the top navigation bar. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Menu Settings** > **Main Menu Configuration**. On the Main Menu Configuration page, click the **Single-cloud Menu** tab. On this tab, click **Configurations** and select Native Hybrid Cloud and Local Cloud Data.

- You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Local Cloud Data**.

4. On the Local Cloud Data page, click **Export Local Cloud Data** to export the data of the current Apsara Stack platform as a JSON file.

<a id="section-6-3"></a>

## 6.3. Security policies

You can configure login password policies, login control settings, and resource security levels.

<a id="section-6-3-1"></a>

### 6.3.1. Set a password policy

This topic describes how to set a password policy.

**Prerequisites**

The operator is the platform administrator by default.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Security Policy**.

4. On the **Password Policy** tab, configure **Basic settings**, **Log in settings**, and **Password change settings**.

5. Click **Save**.

   Click **Reset** to restore default settings.

**Basic settings**

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/236a12cadca84a07bc0eec29fe794399.jpeg)

| Configuration item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Password Length | Set the minimum password length. Valid values: 8 to 32 characters. |
| Required Character Types in Password | Select one or more required character types for passwords.<br>• Lowercase Letters<br>• Uppercase Letters<br>• Digits<br>• Special Characters |
| Password Validity Period (Days) | Specify the password validity period in <strong>Days</strong>. The system prompts that the password has expired when the validity period exceeds the specified value. Valid values: 0 to 1095 days.<br>Note<br>• 0 indicates that the password never expires.<br>• The password validity period also applies to preset accounts. |

**Log in settings**

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/283ed198a245c609f2bff2110d989ba1.jpeg)

| Configuration item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Login Disabled After Password Expires | Supports <strong>Yes</strong> or <strong>No</strong>.<br>• <strong>Yes</strong>: After the password expires, the system prevents users from logging in to the console. In the drop-down list, select <strong>Allow Users to</strong> <strong>Change Password</strong> or <strong>Do Not Allow Users to Change Password</strong>.<br>• <strong>Allow Users to Change Password</strong>: After the password expires, allow users to change their passwords on the log in page. They can log in after changing their passwords.<br>• <strong>Do Not Allow Users to Change Password</strong>: After the password expires, users cannot change their passwords on the log in page.Only an administrator can change the password for the user to regain access.<br>• <strong>No</strong>: After the password expires, allow users to continue logging in to the console.<br>Important<br>To avoid security risks that may arise from password leakage, we recommend that users change their passwords as soon as possible. They can change passwords on the log in page or notify administrators to perform the change. |
| Password Attempts | Set the maximum number of failed log in attempts allowed within one hour. The account locks temporarily when this limit is reached. Valid values: 0 to 32 attempts.<br>Note<br>0 indicates the system does not enforce password retry constraints. |
| Temporary Account Lock Duration (Minutes) | Set the temporary account lock duration in <strong>Minutes</strong>. If the number of incorrect password attempts exceeds the limit, the account enters a temporary lockout period during which log in is not allowed. Valid values: 0 to 1440 minutes.<br>Note<br>0 indicates the system does not enable temporary account locking. |
| Password History Check | The system ensures the new password does not match any of the previous passwords. Valid values: 0 to 24 passwords.<br>Note<br>0 indicates the system does not enable password history checking.<br>For example, if you set this value to 3, the current password cannot match any of the last three passwords used. |

**Password change settings**

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fcc6c096c80b04b45c3c784a8ef3e95a.jpeg)

| Configuration item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Password Expiration Notification | Specifies whether to send a notification when the password expires.<br>• Reminder<br>• No Notification |
| Notification Method | Specifies how to send password expiration notifications. You can select multiple methods.<br>• Email<br>• DingTalk<br>• SMS<br>Note<br>You must configure this parameter only if you enable password expiration notifications. |
| Notification Template | Select a template for password expiration notifications. For information about how to edit templates, see Message Gateway.<br>Note<br>You must configure this parameter only if you enable password expiration notifications. |
| Notification Time | Specifies the number of days before password expiration to send a reminder. Valid values: 1 to 30 days.<br>Note<br>You must configure this parameter only if you enable password expiration notifications. |

<a id="section-6-3-2"></a>

### 6.3.2. Configure login control

This topic describes how to configure login control settings.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is the platform administrator by default.

**Important notes**

> **Important**
>
> For Internet-accessible sites, the system sets session control to single-session mode by default and forces logout after 23 hours and 55 minutes.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configuration**.

3. On the **Security Policy** page, click the **Login Control** tab.

4. Configure login control settings according to your business requirements.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/42b35e80385d0e96b720c31d55d10c22.jpeg)

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Session Control | Select a session mode.<br>• Single session: A user can log in from only one client at a time.<br>• Multi-session: A user can log in from multiple clients simultaneously.<br>• Region-based setting: Restrict users to single or multi-session mode based on their region. |
   | Global MFA verification | Enable or disable <strong>global MFA verification</strong>.<br>• Enabled: All user accounts in the platform must use MFA for login authentication.<br>After enabling global MFA verification, select the scope of user accounts to which it applies.<br>• Exclude system preset users (such as admin)<br>• All users<br>• Disabled: User accounts in the platform are not required to use MFA for login authentication. |
   | MFA Binding Instructions | Configure the instructions displayed on the binding page. You can configure content in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. |
   | SSO User Login | Enable or disable SSO user login.<br>• Enabled: SSO users can log in to this platform.<br>• Disabled: SSO users cannot log in directly to this platform and must log in through SSO.<br>Note<br>Platform administrator accounts are not subject to this login restriction. |
   | Login Duration During Which No Actions Occur | Set the idle timeout duration. Valid values: 5 minutes to 24 hours.<br>If no button interaction occurs within the specified duration, the system automatically logs you out and requires you to log in again. |
   | Login Duration Before Forced Logout | Set the forced logout duration. Within this time frame, the system forcibly reminds users to log out and requires re-authentication.<br>Important<br>The forced logout duration must be greater than or equal to the idle timeout duration. Setting both minutes and hours to zero disables this feature. |

5. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-6-3-3"></a>

### 6.3.3. Configure security level-based authorization

This topic describes how to configure security level-based authorization for a resource.

**Usage notes**

> **Important**
>
> - On the Security Level Based Access tab, you can enable security level-based authorization and configure security levels for resource sets and roles. If you enable security level-based authorization, you must configure security levels for resource sets and roles. When you add an account to a resource set, the security level of the role assumed by the account must be higher than or equal to the security level of the resource set.
>
> - After you enable security level-based authorization, you cannot disable it in the console. If you want to disable security level-based authorization, contact technical support.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Security Policies**. On the Security Policies page, click the **Security Level Based Access** tab.

4. Configure the parameters that are described in the following table based on your business requirements.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6e783ec04354febf372662adea2c4396.jpeg)

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Enable Security Level Based Authorization | Specifies whether to enable security level-based authorization.<br>After you enable security level-based authorization, a resource set is assigned the lowest security level by default. Preset roles, except for resource set administrators and resource users, are assigned the lowest security level. Other preset roles are assigned the highest security level.The management scope of a role cannot be changed. |
   | Security Level (from Low to High) | The security levels from top to bottom in ascending order of priority. A maximum of 10 security levels are supported.<br>• <strong>Add a security level</strong>:<br>a. In the lower part of the Security Level Based Access tab, enter a defined security level in the text box.<br>b. Click the square boxes next to <strong>Text Color</strong> and <strong>Text Background</strong> <strong>Color</strong>. Then, select a color from a color picker or enter a color code.<br>c. Click <strong>Add</strong>.<br>• <strong>Delete a security level</strong>: Find the security level that you want to delete and click <strong>Delete</strong>.<br>• <strong>Change the colors of a security level</strong>: Click the square boxes next to <strong>Text Color</strong> and <strong>Text Background Color</strong>. Then, select a color from a color picker or enter a color code. |

5. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-6-4"></a>

## 6.4. Authentication modes

<a id="section-6-4-1"></a>

### 6.4.1. Authentication modes

This topic describes the authentication modes. Authentication modes are classified into the token mode and the hybrid mode. You can configure an authentication mode based on your business requirements.

**Token mode**

In token mode, Resource Access Management (RAM) and Security Token Service (STS) are required. Temporary STS tokens are issued to users and cloud services to assist in permission management.

- In token mode, all cloud services use STS tokens to authenticate users. Cloud services that do not support STS may be affected. For example, only operations administrators and level-1 organization administrators can log on to the console of a cloud service.

  > **Note**
  >
  > On the **Authentication Mode** page, you can view the cloud services that support the token mode.

- After you enable the token mode, authentication of northbound APIs may be affected.

  For example, if you use the AccessKey pair of a RAM user to call an API operation to add, delete, modify, or query specified resources in a specified organization and resource set, and the required RAM policies are not attached to the RAM user, an error may be returned.

  > **Warning**
  >
  > Before you enable the token mode, we recommend that you contact Alibaba Cloud to evaluate the situation. If an error occurs when you call an API operation, disable the token mode.

**Hybrid mode**

In hybrid mode, cloud services that support RAM and STS can still authenticate users based on STS tokens. For cloud services that do not support STS, permissions are managed based on the authentication logic of Apsara Stack tenant accounts and RAM users. In hybrid mode, if you select one or more cloud services, the cloud services use STS tokens to authenticate users. Cloud services that are not selected still authenticate users in hybrid mode.

<a id="section-6-4-2"></a>

### 6.4.2. Configure an authentication mode

You can configure an authentication mode based on the scenario.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication Mode**.

4. Select **Token Mode** or **Hybrid** based on the scenario.

   If you select **Hybrid**, you can control the authentication model of a cloud service by selecting or clearing the cloud service. If you select a cloud service, Security Token Service (STS)-based authentication is enabled for the cloud service.

   > **Important**
   >
   > After token-based authentication is enabled, the authentication mode of northbound API operations is affected. We recommend that you contact the Alibaba Cloud service team for evaluation before you enable token-based authentication. If an error occurs when an API operation is called, roll back and disable token-based authentication for the service.

5. In the lower part of the page, click **Save**.
