### 6.5.2. Create or synchronize specifications

You can create or synchronize specifications of cloud resources.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.

4. On the Specifications page, select a cloud service from the **Resource Specification Settings** drop-down list.

5. Click the **Resource Specifications** tab.

   - **Create specifications**

     > **Note**
     >
     > You can create specifications for the following cloud services: NAT Gateway, Server Load Balancer (SLB), IPv6 Gateway, ApsaraDB RDS, Tair (Redis OSS-compatible), PolarDB-X 1.0, PolarDB-X 2.0, ApsaraDB for MongoDB, and PolarDB.

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Click **Create Specifications**.

     </li>

     <li>

     In the Create Specifications dialog box, configure the parameters. For more information about the specification parameters, see Specifications.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     Click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Synchronize specifications**

     > **Note**
     >
     > The specifications of cloud services are synchronized to the current system by calling API operations. You can manually synchronize the specifications of Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Click **Synchronize Specifications**.

     </li>

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-6-5-3"></a>

### 6.5.3. Manage specifications

You can enable or disable specifications of different cloud resources. This way, only enabled specifications can be configured when resources are created.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   On the Specifications page, configure the **Specification Synchronization Settings** parameter to specify the specification synchronization mechanism.

   > **Important**
   >
   > New specifications may be released after cloud services are updated. You can configure the specification synchronization mechanism to make sure the specifications are up-to-date.

   <ol type="a">

   <li>

   Click **Edit**. Select **Maintain Current Specifications** or **Synchronize Specifications**.

   - **Maintain Current Specifications**: New specifications are not synchronized after version updates.

     > **Note**
     >
     > Select this option if you want to retain the existing configurations after version updates.

   - **Synchronize Specifications**: New specifications are synchronized after version updates.

     > **Note**
     >
     > We recommend that you select this option to make sure that specifications are up-to-date.

   </li>

   <li>

   Click **Save**.

   </li>

   </ol>

   </li>

   <li>

   Select a cloud service from the **Resource Specification Settings** drop-down list.

   </li>

   </ol>

   | Operation | Procedure |
   | --- | --- |
   | View specification s | • Click the <strong>Resource Specifications</strong> tab to view the information about resource specifications, such as the status.<br>• Click the <strong>Specifications History</strong> tab to view the information about historical specifications.<br>• Click the <strong>Existing Specifications</strong> tab to view the used specifications and the number of resources that use the specifications. |
   | Disable a specification | You can disable an enabled specification. The disabled specification is unavailable when users create the corresponding resources.<br>a. Click the <strong>Resource Specifications</strong> tab.<br>b. Find the resource specification that you want to disable and click <strong>Disable</strong> in the Actions column.<br>c. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Enable a specification | You can enable disabled specifications.<br>a. Click the <strong>Resource Specifications</strong> tab.<br>b. Find the resource type that you want to enable and click <strong>Enable</strong> in the Actions column.<br>c. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Export specification s | You can export the specification information to your computer for backup.<br>a. Click the <strong>Resource Specifications</strong> tab.<br>b. Click <strong>Export</strong> above the specification list.<br>c. Configure the storage path, enter a file name, and then click <strong>Download</strong> to export specifications of the cloud service as a .csv file to your computer. |

<a id="section-6-5-4"></a>

### 6.5.4. Examples

<a id="section-6-5-4-1"></a>

#### 6.5.4.1. Create an ApsaraDB RDS instance specification

**Background information**

Company A uses ApsaraDB RDS to deploy and manage database instances. The company needs to create a new ApsaraDB RDS instance specification to meet the requirements of different departments and applications.

**Planning**

Company A analyzes the specific requirements of departments and applications and poses the following requirements on the specification: The vCPU performance must be high and content resources must be extensive to support large-scale database operations. The storage capacity and the maximum number of connections can be expanded based on business requirements. SSD storage is required. High-speed read and write performance and a low failure rate are required. Company A then plans specification configurations based on these requirements. Example:

vCPU: 8 cores

Memory: 16 GB

Storage: 500 GB SSD

Maximum number of connections: 1,000

Database engine: MySQL 8.0

> **Important**
>
> Before you create specifications, check with cloud service technical support to make sure that the specifications are available.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.

4. On the **Specifications** page, choose **Database Services** > **ApsaraDB RDS** from the **Resource Specification Settings** drop-down list.

5. On the **Resource Specifications** tab, click **Create Specifications**.

6. In the **Create Specifications** dialog box, configure the parameters.

   - Database Engine: MySQL

   - Minimum Storage: 500

   - Maximum Storage: 3000

   - Instance Type: rds.mysql.A

   - Chip Type: intel

   - Engine Version: 8.0

   - cpu: 8

   - Connections: 1,000

   - Memory: 16

   - Edition: dual_ha

   - Storage Type: cloud_ssd

7. Click **OK**. View the specification you created in the specification list.

**Subsequent impact**

The administrator named orgA of the level-1 organization of Company A can select the created specification when orgA creates an ApsaraDB RDS instance.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/09949d02726a0d6ef330fb15df6e289b.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-5-4-2"></a>

#### 6.5.4.2. Disable an ApsaraDB RDS instance specification

**Background information**

Due to changes in business, Company A needs to disable the ApsaraDB RDS instance specification rds.mysql.A. After this specification is disabled, the related departments and applications can no longer use the specification. For more information about how to create the specification rds.mysql.A, see Create an ApsaraDB RDS instance specification.

**Planning**

After the specification rds.mysql.A is disabled, it is unavailable when users create ApsaraDB RDS instances.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as the super administrator.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.

4. On the **Specifications** page, choose **Database Services** > **ApsaraDB RDS** from the **Resource Specification Settings** drop-down list.

5. On the **Resource Specifications** tab, find the specification rds.mysql.A and click **Disable** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4f330814c2f7a96e602bd01dbed82074.jpeg)

6. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the specification is disabled, the value in the **Status** column of the specification changes to **Disabled**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6515c884529c5635000a9f730b6e0c98.jpeg)

**Subsequent impact**

The specification rds.mysql.A is unavailable when the level-1 organization administrator orgA of Company A creates an ApsaraDB RDS instance.

<a id="section-6-6"></a>

## 6.6. Menu management

<a id="section-6-6-1"></a>

### 6.6.1. Configure menus

This topic describes how to configure menus to manage and control access to services and operations.

**Background information**

You can add external links to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for centralized management and easy access. This greatly simplifies operations, prevents frequent switching between different platforms, and improves work efficiency.

In addition, to implement personalized and categorized management, you can group and name menu items that you create. This also facilitates management and search. The highly flexible and user-friendly configuration method allows you to create, edit, and organize various submenu items based on your requirements. You can categorize features into different groups so that users can quickly and accurately locate the required features. This allows the menus to better meet the requirements of different scenarios.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Menu item parameters**

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Title | The display name of the menu item. |
| URL | The URL of the menu item. |
| Console Type | The type of the console. Different consoles have different domain names. Valid values: oneconsole and other.<br>• <strong>oneconsole</strong>: You need to only enter the path in the URL field. The domain name is automatically matched. The URL starts with one.console.<br>• <strong>other</strong>: You must enter the domain name in the URL field. |
| Identifier | The unique identifier of the menu item in the system. This identifier can be used to indicate whether the menu item is selected in the navigation bar. The identifier cannot be changed. |
| Sort | The display order among the same-level menu items. The larger the value, the lower it is displayed. |
| Parent Level | The parent menu item to which the menu item belongs. |
| Level-1 Group | The level-1 group to which the menu item belongs. This parameter is available and required if the Parent Level parameter is set to <strong>Products</strong>. |
| Level-2 Group | Optional. The level-2 group to which the menu item belongs. |
| Open With | The method to open the page of the menu item. Valid values: <strong>Default</strong> and <strong>New</strong> <strong>Window</strong>.<br>• <strong>Default</strong>: opens the page in the current tab.<br>• <strong>New Window</strong>: opens the page in a new tab. |
| Description | The description of the menu item. |

**Create a menu item**

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Menu Settings** > **Main Menu Configuration**.

4. On the **Main Menu Configuration** page, click the **Single-cloud Menu** tab.

5. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, click **Create**.

6. In the **Create** dialog box, configure the parameters. For more information, see the Menu item parameters section of this topic.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/686509204412a88bbd037fa966c633d1.jpeg)

7. Click **OK**.

**Modify a menu item**

You can modify a menu item as needed.

**Limits**

The default menu items cannot be modified.

**Procedure**

1. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, find the menu item that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fdc95856bb6c407bbe6aba1362faae25.jpeg)

2. In the **Edit** dialog box, modify the menu item information and click **OK**.

**Delete a menu item**

You can delete a menu item if you no longer need it.

**Limits**

The default menu items cannot be deleted.

**Procedure**

1. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, find the menu item that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/368f883a326279b669355fe42e5c3fce.jpeg)

2. In the **Delete** message, click **OK**.

**Show or hide a menu item**

**Procedure**

1. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, find the required menu item and select or clear the check box in the **Display** column.

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/16d90e907914f7f79ad8968226cde890.png" width="14" alt=""> : The menu item is displayed in the console.

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7dd406266a0b3d294e34e070346479f6.png" width="14" alt=""> : The menu item is not displayed in the console.

<a id="section-6-6-2"></a>

### 6.6.2. Creation page configuration

To let users customize the product creation page experience according to their needs, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides a creation page configuration feature. This feature allows administrators to globally adjust parameters and layout for multiple product creation pages.

**Background information**

With the creation page configuration feature, users can freely choose and set whether various elements appear or remain hidden, and whether they are required or optional. For example, during the creation of a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), if a customer wants to emphasize the “Description” field, they can configure it as a required field through this feature, ensuring detailed descriptions accompany every VPC creation.

Creation page configuration supports setting required fields, hidden fields, and options on product creation pages.

- Configure required fields: Set fields that users must fill out when creating a product.

- Configure hidden fields: Hide specific fields so users cannot see them on the product creation page.

- Configure options: Show or hide specific options within fields, make selections visible to users, and reorder options based on user habits.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user defaults to the platform administrator.

**Configure required fields**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Menu Settings** > **Creation Page Configuration**.

4. On the **Creation Page Configuration** page, locate the target product form.

   You can quickly find it by using the **Product** drop-down list and **dataId** above the list.

5. Click **Required Settings** in the **Actions** column for the target form.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/93117c218c460b5328f3208a609f3c78.jpeg)

6. In the **Required Settings** dialog box, select the fields you want to mark as required. For example, after selecting the **Description** field, it becomes mandatory during product creation.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Fields without checkboxes do not support configuration.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7a3b036f048b7f823a22231199fbde3d.jpeg)

7. Click **Confirm**.

**Configure hidden fields**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cfe97e14285ad9a1b9525702da7af69c.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column for the target form, then select **Hidden Item Settings**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8b7238a3d9a7a57eae5842eef11418b9.jpeg)

2. In the **Hidden Item Settings** dialog box, select the fields you want to hide. For example, after selecting **IPv6 CIDR Block**, users will not see this field on the creation page when creating a product.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Fields without checkboxes do not support configuration.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1060c321470bcb5dc49a149205c2ef19.jpeg)

3. Click **Confirm**.

**Configure options**

1. Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cfe97e14285ad9a1b9525702da7af69c.png" width="14" alt=""> in the **Actions** column for the target form, then select **Option Settings**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3d9d0606350c35ace34aa02e8efe69c3.jpeg)

2. In the **Options** dialog box, select the field whose options you want to configure, then click **Next Step**. For example, select the **Sharing Scope** field.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Fields without checkboxes do not support configuration.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6128e6949ec4eefd3207f3eb48fda53f.jpeg)

3. Set whether each option is **Hide**, and adjust the order of options.

   > **Note**
   >
   > : Indicates that option hiding is enabled. The option remains invisible to
   >
   > ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/eba5cd5cb4fbb22cd357fe7258f7e7c8.png)
   >
   > users on the creation page.
   >
   > : Indicates that option hiding is disabled. The option appears visible to users
   >
   > ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d28d2f4cb8b36f1fc02b4d6b2cdd0a8e.png)
   >
   > on the creation page.
   >
   > - Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ee6390046621270f5314d59367251dc2.png" width="15" alt=""> to the right of **Option**, then select **Move Up** or **Move Down** to adjust
   >
   >   the option order.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d7ea4d403985ca20dfd8fa3daf9c545a.jpeg)

4. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-6-6-3"></a>

### 6.6.3. Redirection page configuration

You can turn on or off the switch to remove the product redirection page based on your requirements.

**Prerequisites**

The operator must be a platform administrator by default.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configuration**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Menu Management** > **Redirection Page Configuration**.

4. Configure the authorization sequence and the redirection page removal setting.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/287f969e32b856ed835f2a9c409d3085.jpeg)

   - To configure the authorization sequence: Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/dd57462e2a908a4fbc8bf9fc7038cb81.png" width="12" alt=""> in the **Authorization Sequence**

     column. Drag <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5887ab7fe5869a1fbf200343f2c0ee1b.png" width="10" alt=""> in front of each access mode to adjust the authorization priority.

   - To configure redirection page removal: In the **Remove Redirection Page Configuration** column, turn on or off the switch.

     <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cf7d4d1bb4ff8c661539d7d9184b5be3.png" width="31" alt=""> indicates that the redirection page removal switch is turned on. When the switch

     is turned on, the redirection page does not appear when you enter the product console. The floating menu in the product console displays account switching options. You can switch accounts in the floating menu.

     > **Important**
     >
     > When the redirection page removal switch is turned on, the system accesses the product based on the priority configured in the authorization sequence.
     >
     > - If the configured priority does not exist, the system uses the second configured priority by default.
     >
     > - If you set a default access mode in the account switching menu, the system ignores the priority configured in the authorization sequence.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/50e7cb9f5193c08cf4da1576ac2648ba.jpeg)

     <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/bf713bd14299fba5d35fb95c335b9da0.png" width="30" alt=""> indicates that the redirection page removal switch is turned off. When the switch

     is turned off, the redirection page appears before you enter the product console. You must select an organization, region, and access mode on the redirection page to proceed. The floating menu in the product console displays account switching options. You can switch accounts in the floating menu.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/40480da0b29c030954626edbdd895bc9.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-7"></a>

## 6.7. Configure the billing feature on the Billing Switch page

Billing switches control whether billing is enabled to generate resource usage bills and display cost information.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Billing Switch**.

4. In the lower part of the page, click **Edit**.

5. Configure the billing feature based on your business requirements.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Currency | The billing currency. Select a currency from the drop-down list. After you specify the currency, the currency in the system will be changed to the latest currency. If you change the currency, the amount of the generated bill will not change. |
   | Monthly Billing Start Date | The start date of the monthly bill. |
   | Pricing Mode | The pricing mode. Valid values: <strong>Service Metering</strong> and <strong>Cost Rate</strong>. This parameter is displayed only if you deploy multi-cloud management services.Cost-plus pricing is supported for all Alibaba Cloud services. Usage-based pricing is supported only for Alibaba Cloud services with metering data and billing rules.<br>• <strong>Service Metering</strong>: In usage-based pricing mode, prices are determined based on billing rules and pricing factors for metering data. The resale amount of Alibaba Cloud services is calculated based on the billing rules and metering data of Alibaba Cloud services.<br>• <strong>Cost Rate</strong>: In cost-plus pricing mode, the resale amount of Alibaba Cloud services is calculated based on the following formula: Resale amount of Alibaba Cloud services = Cost in the bills of Alibaba Cloud services × Price multiplier. If you set this parameter to <strong>Cost Rate</strong>, enter a price multiplier in the field next to Cost Rate. Valid values: (0,10000\]. Unit: %.<br>Important<br>After the pricing mode is switched, it takes effect in the next billing cycle. |
   | Price Inquiry Switch | Specifies whether to enable price inquiry.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3f5669baa43f25642dd95c13f8703fe0.png)<br>: enables price inquiry.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2519ccf2feb586a025a333e102f483c6.png)<br>: disables price inquiry. |
   | Fee Deduction Switch | Specifies whether to enable fee deduction.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3f5669baa43f25642dd95c13f8703fe0.png)<br>: enables fee deduction.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2519ccf2feb586a025a333e102f483c6.png)<br>: disables fee deduction. |
   | Refund Ratio | The refund ratio. The refund amount is calculated based on the refund policy for switching the billing method from subscription to pay-as-you-go, refund policy for unsubscribing from subscription instances, or refund policy for downgrading subscription instances. The usage duration is accurate to the day.The part that is less than one day is counted as one day.<br>• Refund amount = (Original order amount - Consumed amount) × Refund ratio<br>• Consumed amount = Average daily unit price × Usage duration<br>• Usage duration = Unsubscription initiation time - Order start time |
   | Per-second Billing | Specifies whether to enable per-second billing for cloud services. If you enable per-second billing for a cloud service, the resource usage data is collected at the second level and bills are generated based on the second-level metering data.<br>Important<br>By default, the per-second billing feature is disabled. If you enable the feature for a cloud service, bills are generated based on the second-level metering data. After the per-second billing feature is enabled for a cloud service, the feature cannot be disabled. Exercise caution when you enable this feature. |

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Monthly Billing Start Date:
   >
   >   - Billing starts at 00:00:00 on the selected day and ends at 00:00:00 on the same day in the following calendar month. If you set the start date to the 15th day of the month or a day before the 15th day, the billing cycle starts in the current month and ends in the following month. If you set the start date to a day after the 15th day of the month, the billing cycle starts in the previous month and ends in the current month. If you change the billing cycle, the change takes effect in the following month.
   >
   >     Examples:
   >
   >     - If you set the start date to the 10th day of the month, the billing cycle for February starts at 00:00:00 on February 10 and ends at 00:00:00 on March 10.
   >
   >     - If you set the start date to the 18th day of the month, the billing cycle for February starts at 00:00:00 on January 18 and ends at 00:00:00 on February 18.
   >
   >   - If the date that you selected does not exist in a calendar month, the system uses the last day of the calendar month as the start date. For example, if you set the start date to the 31st day of the month, the system uses the last day of February and other 30-day months as the start date of the billing cycle. Examples:
   >
   >     - Billing cycle for January: 00:00:00 on December 31 to 00:00:00 on January 31
   >
   >     - Billing cycle for February: 00:00:00 on January 31 to 00:00:00 on February 28
   >
   >     - Billing cycle for March: 00:00:00 on February 28 to 00:00:00 on March 31
   >
   >     - Billing cycle for April: 00:00:00 on March 31 to 00:00:00 on April 30
   >
   >     - Billing cycle for May: 00:00:00 on April 30 to 00:00:00 on May 31
   >
   > - Price Inquiry Switch: After you enable price inquiry, you can view the fees that are generated when you create (activate) services, change the configurations of (scale out) services, release (delete) services, renew services, add services to Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ), or place orders. After you disable price inquiry, fees are not displayed. If you use resources that are billed on a monthly basis and you disable price inquiry, fees cannot be calculated when you unsubscribe from the resources or change the configurations of the resources.
   >
   > - Fee Deduction Switch: After you enable fee deduction, fees are deducted from the budget based on the bill. After you disable fee deduction, no fee is deducted from the budget.
   >
   > - If you enable price inquiry and disable fee deduction, only bills are generated and no fee is deducted from the budget. If you enable both price inquiry and fee deduction, fees are deducted from the budget. Fees are deducted only after the fee deduction switch is turned on. Historical fees are not deducted from the budget. If historical bills are regenerated, the historical fees are deducted.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/03e0e6fbdb96aa113706e58b5abf4bb9.jpeg)

6. Click **Save**.

7. Optional. In the lower part of the Billing Switch page, click **History** to view the historical modification records.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7569f885930554226052f04a1fd24924.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-8"></a>

## 6.8. Manage announcements

You can create announcements on the platform to inform users about events such as O&M, updates, and daily operations.

**Background information**

- After an announcement is published, users can view the announcement in the Announcement section of the homepage.

  > **Important**
  >
  > - The announcements that a user can view vary based on the role of the user:
  >
  >   - If the user assumes a global role, the user can view all published announcements.
  >
  >   - If the user assumes a non-global role, the user can view the published announcements of the organization to which the user belongs and the published announcements of which the Visible for Organization parameter is set to All.
  >
  > - The announcements are displayed in descending order based on the publish time.

- The announcement management feature allows you to create, modify, view, edit, and delete announcements. Tenant isolation is also implemented to ensure that announcements are separately managed for each tenant.

  > **Important**
  >
  > - When a platform administrator creates or edits an announcement, the platform administrator can set the Visible for Organization parameter to All or SystemDefaultOrganization. However, only All is a valid value. If the Visible for Organization parameter is set to SystemDefaultOrganization, an error is reported when the announcement is saved.
  >
  > - Global roles can view and manage announcements of all organizations.
  >
  > - Non-global roles can view only the announcements of the level-1 organization to which the current account belongs. If you create or edit an announcement by assuming a non-global role, you can select only All or the corresponding level-1 organization from the Visible for Organization drop-down list.

  - You can limit the visibility of announcements to specified organizations.

  - Announcement content supports rich text. You can adjust the content style and insert images or links based on your business requirements.

  - Announcements are automatically published or unpublished based on the specified publish or unpublish time.

  - You can delete an announcement if you no longer need it. After the announcement is deleted, it cannot be restored.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator or operations administrator.

**Create an announcement**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Announcement Management**.

4. On the **Announcement Management** page, click **Create Announcement**.

5. On the **Create Announcement** page, configure the parameters described in the following table.

   | Section and parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Title | The title of the announcement. The title must be 2 to 120 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, and the following characters: periods (.), commas (,), semicolons (;), colons (:), single quotation marks ('), double quotation marks (''), question marks (?), angle brackets (&lt;&gt;), exclamation points (!), and spaces. |
   | Type | The type of the announcement. Valid values: <strong>Upgrade Announcement</strong>, <strong>O&amp;M Notifications</strong>, <strong>Security Notifications</strong>, <strong>Urgent Events</strong>, and <strong>Daily</strong> <strong>Announcement</strong>. |
   | Visible for Organization | The organizations to which the announcement is visible. By default, <strong>All</strong> is selected. In this case, users in all organizations can view the announcement.You can also select a level-1 organization from the drop-down list. In this case, only the users in the selected level-1 organization can view the announcement.<br>Note<br>• If you use a platform administrator account, the displayed values of the Visible for Organization parameter are All and SystemDefaultOrganization. To create the announcement, you must select All for the Visible for Organization parameter.Otherwise, the configuration is invalid.<br>• If you use an operations administrator account, you can view all level-1 organizations in the drop-down list. You can select All or a specific level-1 organization to create the announcement.<br>• If you use a custom Resource Access Management (RAM) role that has the permissions to manage announcements, take note of the following items:<br>• If you use a global RAM role, you can view all level-1 organizations in the drop-down list. You can select All or a specific level-1 organization to create the announcement.<br>• If you use a non-global RAM role, you can view only the level-1 organization to which the current account belongs in the drop-down list. You can select All or the corresponding level-1 organization to create the announcement. |
   | Publish -Unpublish Time | The time that you want to publish and unpublish the announcement. The time is accurate to seconds. Announcements are automatically published or unpublished based on the specified publish or unpublish time.<br>The publish time must be later than the current time, and the unpublish time must be later than the publish time. |
   | Announcement content | Announcement content supports rich text. You can adjust the content style and insert images or links based on your business requirements. |

6. Click **Create**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - After an announcement is created and automatically published, the announcement is displayed in the Announcement section of the **homepage**. Only the users in the specified organizations can view the announcement.
   >
   > - Automatic publishing and unpublishing of announcements may be delayed by 1 to 5 seconds.

**View the announcement list and details of an announcement**

After an announcement is created, you can view the created announcement in the announcement list.

1. Optional. On the **Announcements** page, enter an announcement name in the search box to search for the announcement.

2. View the information about the announcement displayed in the following columns: **Announcement Type**, **Announcement Name**, **Status**, **Visible Organization**, **Modified At**, **Created At**, **Published At**, and **Unpublished At**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/051a6f0b073028d0bbb5ef6f1f0a1b77.png" width="12" alt=""> icon next to the **Status** column to filter announcements by status.
   >
   >   Valid values of the Status column: **Pending**, **Published**, and **Unpublished**.
   >
   > - Click the
   >
   >   icon next to the **Modified At**, **Created At**, **Published At**, or
   >
   >   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/48bcc2f28e2bfd6cadb3815945de4096.png" width="12" alt="">
   >
   >   **Unpublished At** column to sort announcements in ascending or descending order based on the corresponding time.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/79fcd129b9bb4c814e921f6a6b45ea53.jpeg)

3. Click the name of the announcement to go to the announcement details page and view the announcement details.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can go to the details pages of only announcements in the **Published** state.

**Modify an announcement**

You can modify an announcement to reflect information changes.

1. On the **Announcement Management** page, find the announcement that you want to modify and click **Modify** in the Actions column.

2. On the **Modify Announcement** page, modify the title, type, organizations to which the announcement is visible, publish and unpublish time, and content based on your business requirements.

3. Click **Modify**.

**Delete an announcement**

You can delete an announcement if it is no longer needed.

1. On the **Announcement Management** page, find the announcement that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the Actions column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fdea795b23e94beeef75c6fbdba5c236.jpeg)

2. In the **Confirm** message, click **OK**.

<a id="section-6-9"></a>

## 6.9. Privacy documents

<a id="section-6-9-1"></a>

### 6.9.1. Create a privacy document

This topic describes how to create a privacy document that contains the platform privacy policy and legal terms.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Privacy Document**.

4. On the **Privacy Document** page, click **Create Document**.

5. On the **Create Document** page, select a document type and language, and enter the document title and content.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The document types include **User Agreement**, **Privacy Policy**, and **Terms of Service**. You can create only one document of each type. If one document of a type already exists, you cannot select this document type.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/de56635fced1c4985bddaa118df745cf.jpeg)

6. Click **Create**.

<a id="section-6-9-2"></a>

### 6.9.2. View a privacy document

After a privacy document is created, you can view the created privacy document on the Privacy Document page. This topic describes how to view a privacy document.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Privacy Document**.

4. On the **Privacy Document** page, find the privacy document that you want to view and view its information, including the document ID, type, status, creation time, and last modification time.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a06790466fc2a747981dc06774fc68b4.jpeg)

5. Click the document ID in the **Document ID** column to view the details of the privacy document.

<a id="section-6-9-3"></a>

### 6.9.3. Modify a privacy document

This topic describes how to modify a privacy document.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Limits**

To modify a published privacy document, you must unpublish it first.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Privacy Document**.

4. On the **Privacy Document** page, find the privacy document that you want to modify and click **Modify** in the **Actions** column.

5. On the **Edit Document** page, update the content of the document in different languages.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You cannot modify the type of a privacy document.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/be45840be724fecf049c0c3155881baa.jpeg)

6. Click **Modify**.

<a id="section-6-9-4"></a>

### 6.9.4. Publish a privacy document

After you publish a privacy document, users must select the privacy document and agree to its terms before they can log in to the platform. This topic describes how to publish a privacy document.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Privacy Document**.

4. On the **Privacy Document** page, find the privacy document that you want to publish and click **Publish** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a06790466fc2a747981dc06774fc68b4.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Impact**

After you publish the privacy document, users must select the privacy document and agree to its terms before they can log in to the platform. The document title is displayed in the hyperlink on the login page, as shown in the following figure.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d3d83246bf2b2128529ee30d17069e4e.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-9-5"></a>

### 6.9.5. Unpublish a privacy document

After you unpublish a published privacy document, the privacy document no longer appears on the login page. If all privacy documents of the three types are unpublished, the check boxes for selecting the privacy documents no longer appear on the login page. This topic describes how to unpublish a privacy document.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Privacy Document**.

4. On the **Privacy Document** page, find the privacy document that you want to unpublish and click **Unpublish** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a06790466fc2a747981dc06774fc68b4.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-6-9-6"></a>

### 6.9.6. View the versions of a privacy document

This topic describes how to view the historical versions of a privacy document.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Privacy Document**.

4. On the **Privacy Document** page, find the privacy document that you want to view and click **View History** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a06790466fc2a747981dc06774fc68b4.jpeg)

5. On the **View Historical Version** page, select the version that you want to view and view the details of the version.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/aa184058736ee142738a6da229116629.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-10"></a>

## 6.10. Custom settings

<a id="section-6-10-1"></a>

### 6.10.1. Platform settings

You can customize the logon page, platform logo, and other platform configurations on the platform based on your requirements.

**Background information**

- Multiple languages are supported, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. You can select a default language for the platform.

- You can select a dark or light mode. You can also change the theme color of the console.

- You can enable and customize the page watermark.

- You can configure multi-language brand information in the console (including the browser ICO image, platform logo, platform name, and information displayed on the logon page).

- You can restore the page to factory settings. The restoration is irreversible.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Custom Configurations** > **Platform Settings**.

4. Modify the platform settings as needed. To restore factory settings, click **Restore Factory Settings** at the bottom of the page. The configurations take effect the next time you log in to the console.

<a id="section-6-11"></a>

## 6.11. Third-party authentication

You can configure third-party authentication to implement single sign-on (SSO) in which the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console serves as a service provider (SP) and the system that is developed by a customer serves as an identity provider (IdP). This way, users can access the resources provided by the SP without additional authentication after they pass the authentication of the IdP.

**Terms**

- SSO: allows users to log in to multiple systems with a single action of login without the need to re-enter the username and password for authentication.

- Single logout (SLO): allows users to log off from multiple systems with a single action of logoff.

- IdP: provides identity management services.

- SP: provide users with specific services by using the identity management services provided by IdPs.

- Security Assertion Markup Language 2.0 (SAML 2.0): a protocol that is designed for enterprise-level user identity authentication. SAML 2.0 is used for communication between SPs and IdPs by exchanging authentication and authorization data within security domains.

- Open Authorization (OAuth) 2.0: an authorization protocol that specifies the following grant types for different scenarios: authorization code, client credentials, resource owner password credentials, and implicit. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console uses the authorization code grant type.

<a id="section-6-11-1"></a>

### 6.11.1. User-based SSO

<a id="section-6-11-1-1"></a>

#### 6.11.1.1. Configure a global IdP

This topic describes how to configure a global identity provider (IdP).

**Usage notes**

> **Important**
>
> - The following section describes how to configure a global IdP, which is an enterprise system, when the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console serves as a service provider (SP). In one cloud with multiple regions scenarios, users from all regions must be authenticated by the global IdP.
>
> - When a global IdP is configured for the cloud platform, users are authenticated by the global IdP after they click the button for authorized login on the login page of the platform.
>
> - If a global IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a local IdP. You must clear the global IdP before you configure a local IdP.
>
> - If a local IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a global IdP. You must clear the local IdP before you configure a global IdP.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**. The User-based SSO tab appears.

4. On the **Global IdP Settings** tab, click **Edit** and configure the parameters in the **Global IdP Settings**, **Obtain Verified User Information**, and **Global Authorization Redirect** sections.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The Obtain Verified User Information section is displayed only if you set the Protocol Type parameter to OAuth 2.0.
   >
   > - The parameters in the Obtain Verified User Information section are not required in OAuth 2.0. Configure the parameters based on your business requirements.

5. After you complete the configurations, click **Save**.

   > **Important**
   >
   > If you click **Restore Factory Settings**, the global IdP settings are cleared. Users are not authenticated by the global IdP when they log in to the platform. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

**Global IdP Settings**

**Protocol type: SAML 2.0**

<a id="section-6-11-1-2"></a>

#### 6.11.1.2. Configure a local IdP

This topic describes how to configure a local identity provider (IdP).

**Usage notes**

> **Important**
>
> - If a local IdP is created and bound to a level-1 organization, the button for authentication is unavailable on the login page of the platform for the users of the level-1 organization and subordinate organizations. The users are navigated to the platform only after they log in from the local IdP.
>
> - After you create a local IdP, you can bind the IdP to a level-1 organization to implement IdP authentication at the organization level. Each level-1 organization can be bound to only one IdP including a global IdP.
>
>   - If a global IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a local IdP. You must clear the global IdP before you configure a local IdP.
>
>   - If a local IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a global IdP. You must clear the local IdP before you configure a global IdP.
>
>   - If a level-1 organization is bound to a local IdP, you can still configure local IdPs for other level-1 organizations.
>
> - Before you delete a local IdP, you must unbind the local IdP from bound organizations.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**. The User-based SSO tab appears by default.

4. On the **Local IdP Settings** tab, click **Create Local IdP**.

5. In the **Create Local IdP** dialog box, configure parameters in the IdP Settings and Obtain Verified User Information sections.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The Obtain Verified User Information section appears only if you set the Protocol Type parameter to OAuth 2.0.
   >
   > - The parameters in the Obtain Verified User Information section are not required in OAuth 2.0. Configure the parameters based on your business requirements.

6. Click **OK**.

7. Manage local IdPs.

  <tr>
    <td>Obtain Path for Parsing Verified Username</td>
    <td>The parsing path for the verified username. The objects returned from the service must be JSON objects.<br>Note<br>Use periods (.) to indicate the level of the username in the object. For example, <code> user </code> indicates that the username is at the root level, and <code> ascm.user </code> indicates that the username is at the second level.</td>
  </tr>
</table>

**Request type: POST**

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/540e86801f01d5a997f9d9b364ee2710.jpeg)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Service Address for Obtaining Verified User | The URL for user authentication. Format: <code> http://URL </code> or <code> https://URL </code>.<br>Note<br>Click <strong>Test</strong> to test whether the service address can be connected as expected. |
| Request Type | The request type. Select <strong>POST</strong>. |
| Content-Type | Valid values: <strong>application/json; charset=utf-8</strong> and <strong>application/x-www-form-</strong><strong>urlencoded</strong>.<br>Note<br>The value of the Content-Type parameter depends on the requirements of the local IdP. Forms and JSON data are supported.<br>• If the local IdP accepts requests in forms, set the <strong>Content-Type</strong> parameter to <strong>application/x-www-form-urlencoded</strong>.<br>• If the local IdP accepts requests in JSON, set the <strong>Content-Type</strong> parameter to <strong>application/json; charset=utf-8</strong>. |
| Access Token Request Header Template | Default value: <code> [{ "key": "access_token", "value": "{{access_token}}" </code><code>}] </code>.<br>Note<br>• {{access_token}} will be replaced with the obtained access token information and is a required parameter.<br>• The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console will add the key and value in the template to the header of the requests sent to the user authentication URL. |
| Access Token Request Body Template | • If the <strong>Content-Type</strong> parameter is set to <strong>application/json; charset=utf-8</strong>, the default value of the Access Token Request Body Template parameter is <code> { </code><code>"access_token": "{{access_token}}" } </code>.<br>• If the <strong>Content-Type</strong> parameter is set to <strong>application/x-www-form-</strong><strong>urlencoded</strong>, the default value of the Access Token Request Body Template parameter is <code> [{ "key": "access_token", "value": "{{access_token}}" </code><code>}] </code>.<br>Note<br>• {{access_token}} will be replaced with the obtained access token information and is a required parameter.<br>• The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console will add the key and value in the template to the body of the requests sent to the user authentication URL. |
| Obtain Path for Parsing Verified Username | The parsing path for the verified username. The objects returned from the service must be JSON objects.<br>Note<br>Use periods (.) to indicate the level of the username in the object. For example, <code> user </code> indicates that the username is at the root level, and <code> ascm.user </code> indicates that the username is at the second level. |

<a id="section-6-11-1-3"></a>

#### 6.11.1.3. Configure a multi-cloud IdP

If a cloud platform is managed by another cloud platform, the other cloud platform acts as an identity provider (IdP) to provide unified identity authentication and this cloud platform acts as a service provider (SP) to accept identity assertion of the other cloud platform. This enables users to access resources without repeated logins. The Multi-cloud IdP Settings tab displays the configuration information about a multi-cloud IdP.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**. The User-based SSO tab appears by default.

4. On the **Multi-cloud IdP Settings** tab, view the details of a multi-cloud IdP. If the cloud platform is not connected, the parameters on the tab are left empty.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | IdP Service Name | The service name of the multi-cloud IdP. |
   | Protocol Type | The protocol type. Default value: <strong>SAML 2.0</strong>.<br>Note<br>When you configure single sign-on (SSO) on the IdP side, use the metadata provided by the Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) service provider of Apsara Stack. |
   | IdP Authenticatio n Address | The URL for multi-cloud IdP authentication. Format: <code> http://URL </code> or <code> https://URL </code>. |
   | IdP Certificate | The Base64-encoded third-party certificate. |
   | SLO Endpoint | The URL for single logout (SLO). Format: <code> http://URL </code> or <code> https://URL </code>.<br>Note<br>The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console accesses this endpoint when it responds to an SLO request from the IdP. |
   | SLO Request Method | The SLO request method. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5455b1e1c4c78459b9450dbdc68a01e9.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-11-2"></a>

### 6.11.2. Manage OIDC IdPs

This topic describes how to view and delete OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers (IdPs).

**Usage notes**

> **Important**
>
> - OIDC is an authentication protocol based on OAuth 2.0. Applications can use OIDC for authentication based on the relationship between external IdPs and Apsara Stack Resource Access Management (RAM).
>
> - You can use the OIDC authentication feature to control API permissions on different pods that are deployed in a Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) cluster. This enables fine-grained permission control on pods and reduces security risks.
>
> - Only ACK supports the OIDC authentication feature. You can view OIDC IdPs created by ACK clusters in the OIDC IdP list. You cannot directly create an OIDC IdP. You must contact technical support to enable the OIDC authentication feature for ACK clusters.
>
> - After ACK clusters create OIDC IdPs, the platform administrator can view and delete the OIDC IdPs on the OIDC Authentication tab.
>
> - After an OIDC IdP is deleted, RAM roles that reference the OIDC IdP become unavailable. This may affect cloud service authentication and cause business risks. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**View OIDC IdPs**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**.

4. On the **Authentication by Third Party** page, click the **OIDC Authentication** tab.

5. In the OIDC IdP list, view information about existing OIDC IdPs in the following columns: **IdP Name**, **arn**, **Issuer URL**, **Client ID**, **Description**, and **Created At**.

   - **IdP Name**: the name of the OIDC IdP.

   - **arn**: the Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the OIDC IdP.

   - **Issuer URL**: the URL of the OIDC IdP. The URL is used by the client to authenticate the source of the ID token.

   - **Client ID**: the ID that the OIDC IdP uses to authenticate an application.

   - **Description**: the description of the OIDC IdP.

   - **Created At**: the time when the OIDC IdP was created.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ffd8ad498bf5e0bd8f47b2ef57fc5a3c.jpeg)

**Delete an OIDC IdP**

**Procedure**

1. In the OIDC IdP list, find the OIDC IdP that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the Actions column.

2. In the dialog box that appears, select **I am aware of the risks and want to delete the OIDC provider**.

3. Click **OK**.

## 6.12. Message Gateway

The system sends messages to users through email, SMS, and DingTalk. You must complete the relevant configuration for each method before you send messages.

**Background information**

The system supports configuration of the email gateway, SMS gateway, DingTalk settings, Webhook, and message templates.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is the platform administrator.

**Configure the email gateway**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Message Gateway**.

4. Click the **Mail Gateway** tab.

5. Fill in the email gateway configuration items.

   <table>

       <td>Configuration item</td>
       <td>Description</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Sender email</td>
       <td>Enter the sender email address. The system sends emails through this address.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Enable SMTP AUTH</td>
       <td>Enable or disable SMTP AUTH.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4fcf466199ef95ae58a6291e9d86c282.png" alt=""><br>: indicates enabled.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/36ddb570e8daae170a0aaadbeea9fe08.png" alt=""><br>: indicates disabled.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Sender email password</td>
       <td>Enter the password for the sender email account. You must enter the <strong>sender</strong> <strong>email password</strong> if you enable SMTP AUTH.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>SMTP Server Address</td>
       <td>This is the outgoing mail server. It is usually smtp.<em>xxx</em>.com.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Port</td>
       <td>Enter the SMTP server port.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Encryption</td>
       <td>Select from three options: <strong>Not Encrypted</strong>, <strong>SSL</strong>, or <strong>TLS</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Enable</td>
       <td>Select <strong>Enable</strong> or <strong>Disabled</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Email attachment</td>
       <td>Select <strong>Enable</strong> or <strong>Disabled</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7dce92b56790183ea20f8a8a31594e27.jpeg)

6. Click **Submit** to complete the email configuration.

   Click **Reset** to clear the email gateway configuration and reconfigure it.

   Click **Test email**, enter the destination email address, and test whether the email can be sent successfully.

**Configure the SMS gateway**

**Procedure**

1. On the **Message Gateway** page, click the **SMS gateway** tab.

2. Fill in the SMS gateway configuration items.

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | SMS gateway address | Enter the API URL of the SMS gateway. |
   | Receive number parameter name | Enter the parameter name that represents the recipient phone number in the SMS gateway. |
   | SMS content parameter name | Enter the parameter name that represents the SMS content in the SMS gateway. |
   | Request header parameters | Enter the header parameters for the request to the SMS gateway. Click <strong>Add</strong> to add a new request header parameter. Enter the parameter name in the first column and the parameter value in the second column. |
   | Request body parameters | Click <strong>Add</strong> to add a new request body parameter. When the transfer mode is POST, both the recipient number parameter and the SMS content parameter are placed in the request body. |
   | Content encoding | Select <strong>UTF-8</strong> or <strong>GBK.</strong> |
   | Transfer mode | Select <strong>GET</strong> or <strong>POST</strong>.<br>• When the transfer mode is GET, ignore the request body parameters.Append both the phone number and content using the GET method.<br>• When the transfer mode is POST, append the request body parameters, recipient number parameter, and content parameter to the request body. |
   | Enable | Select <strong>Enable</strong> or <strong>Disabled</strong>. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4126c52679e7ddbc530046891c94d381.jpeg)

3. Click **Submit** to complete the SMS configuration.

Create a new DingTalk group chat.<br>ii. Add an intelligent group assistant and select Custom Robot.<br>iii. In the security settings of the robot, select <strong>Add Signature</strong> and obtain the secret key. |

1. On the **Message Gateway** page, click the **Webhook** tab.

2. Fill in the Webhook configuration items.

   | Configuration item | Description |

Example:<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d913cf2f57d43a3c236ed8bfc33caae0.jpeg) |

## 6.13. Manage service-linked roles

You can create a Resource Access Management (RAM) role to authorize cloud services in a level-1 organization to view and manage other resources in the organization.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an operations administrator, organization administrator, global organization security administrator, or organization security administrator.

**Create a service-linked role**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Service-linked Roles**.

4. On the **Service-Linked Roles** page, click **Create Service-linked Role**.

5. On the page that appears, select a service from the **Service Name** drop-down list and select one or more organizations from the **Authorized Organization Name** drop-down list.

   - After you select a service, the permissions of the service-linked role are displayed.

   - You can select multiple organizations.

6. Click **OK**.

**View the details of a service-linked role**

1. On the **Service-linked Roles** page, configure the **Role Name**, **Organization Name**, and **Service Name** parameters to filter RAM roles.

2. Find the RAM role that you want to manage and click **View Details** in the **Actions** column to go to the details page of the RAM role.

3. On the **role details** page, view the details and policy of the RAM role.

   - Click the **Role Details** tab to view the name, creation time, description, and trust policy of the RAM role.

   - Click the **Role Policy** tab to view the policy information, including the policy name, policy type, default version, description, and time when the policy is attached to the RAM role.

     > **Note**
     >
     > You can click **View Details** in the **Actions** column to view the policy details.

## 6.14. Configure risky operation settings

This topic describes how to configure different identity authentication and notification methods for different risky operations. This reduces unexpected operations and ensures service security.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

- If text message-based authentication and email or text message notifications are required, you must configure text message and email gateways on the platform. The valid mobile number and email address must be saved in the personal information of the user who performs risky operations.

- If multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled, you must bind a virtual MFA device to the user who performs risky operations and enable MFA when the user logs in to the platform.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Risky Operation Settings**.

4. Optional. Select a cloud service from the Product drop-down list.

5. Find the operation that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.

6. In the **Edit Risky Operation Configurations** dialog box, configure the identity authentication and notification methods.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Identity Authentica tion | The identity authentication method. Valid values: <strong>None</strong>, <strong>MFA</strong>, and <strong>Text Message</strong>.You can select only one value. |
   | Notificatio n Settings | The notification method. Valid values: <strong>Email</strong> and <strong>Text Message</strong>. You can select multiple values. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/96f88ea33f9771cea814617fd25d7993.jpeg)

7. Click **Save**.

## 6.15. Configure log storage settings

You can configure a storage mode for the operation logs and AccessKey logs of cloud services. This way, security administrators can query logs to check the resource usage and component status in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Security administrators can also export operation logs as a file and download the file to a local device.

**Background information**

- The log storage settings apply to the storage of operation logs and AccessKey logs of cloud services.

- By default, logs are stored in the underlying storage of Simple Log Service. If no Logstore exists in the sales cloud, logs are stored in the Logstore of the Apsara Infrastructure Management cluster. By default, logs are retained for seven days.

- The capacity required for log storage is calculated based on the following formula: 5,000,000 × Log retention period × Number of organizations/1,024/1,024/1,024.

  For example, if the number of organizations is 300 and the log retention period is 180 days, approximately 251.46 GB of capacity is required for log storage.

  > **Note**
  >
  > - 5,000,000 is the estimated amount of log data generated in one day, measured in bytes. The log data includes the data generated by using Apsara Stack consoles, calling API operations, and using developer tools.
  >
  > - The storage capacity is measured in GB.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

   > **Note**
   >
   > We recommend that you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as the preset operations administrator. This ensures the security of created Simple Log Service projects and Logstores and prevents accidental deletion.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Log Storage Settings**.

4. In the lower-left part of the Log Storage Settings page, click **Edit**.

   The following log storage modes are available: **Default**, **Log Storage for All Organizations**, and **Log Storage for Specified Organization**.

   | Storage Mode | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Default | The operation logs of the users of all organizations are stored in the system Logstore for seven days.<br>Only <strong>All Events</strong> is available for the <strong>Event Type</strong> parameter. |
   | Log Storage for All Organizatio ns | The operation logs of the users of all organizations are stored in the configured Logstore. You need to purchase Simple Log Service in advance.<br>• You can set the <strong>Storage Duration</strong> parameter to 30 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days, 180 Days, 360 Days, or 720 Days. The maximum storage duration is 720 days.<br>• You can set the <strong>Event Type</strong> parameter to <strong>All Events</strong>, <strong>Write Event</strong>, or <strong>Read</strong> <strong>Event</strong>. |
   | Log Storage for Specified Organizatio n | The operation logs of the users of the specified organizations are stored in the configured Logstore. You need to purchase Simple Log Service in advance.<br>• You can set the <strong>Storage Duration</strong> parameter to 30 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days, 180 Days, 360 Days, or 720 Days. The maximum storage duration is 720 days.<br>• You can set the <strong>Event Type</strong> parameter to <strong>All Events</strong>, <strong>Write Event</strong>, or <strong>Read</strong> <strong>Event</strong>.<br>• In the <strong>Settings</strong> section, configure the parameters in the <strong>Organization</strong> and <strong>Log</strong> <strong>Service Configuration</strong> sections. In the Log Service Configuration section, the <strong>Log Service Region</strong>, <strong>Project Name</strong>, and <strong>Logstore Name</strong> parameters are<br>required. You can click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b885fe06b3c09a0b82253ce15298c489.png" width="13" alt="">icon to add more organization configurations.<br>Important<br>The organizations must belong to different level-1 organizations. |

5. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-6-16"></a>

## 6.16. Billing and Order Dump Configuration

Configure the storage mode for orders and billing records.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the Operations Administrator.

**Constraints**

You cannot modify the dump mode after you set the archive mode for historical billing and order data.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Log Storage Settings**.

4. Click **Edit**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/677058c7a57fbe3d8a2f62c8c0729ab9.jpeg)

5. Configure the log transfer mode. The system supports **Default** and **Archive Historical Data** modes.

   - **Default**: The system stores all orders and billing records in the default database permanently.

   - **Archive Historical Data**: The system archives historical data older than five years to another storage location. You cannot query archived data. In addition, the time range available for filtering and querying orders, billing records, and data analysis is limited to the most recent five years.

     - **ossBucket**: Select a storage product. Configure this parameter only when you select Archive Historical Data as the dump mode.

     - **path**: Enter the storage address. Configure this parameter only when you select Archive Historical Data as the dump mode.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2398187de5398a2125c5e922d1427520.jpeg)

6. Click **Save**.

   If you select the **Archive Historical Data** mode and click Save, the system displays the **Confirm Authorization** dialog box. You must confirm authorization.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/538130da30899ee291312a9851bc1385.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-17"></a>

## 6.17. Event notifications

<a id="section-6-17-1"></a>

### 6.17.1. View events

The Events page displays the change events that can be associated with resources.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Event Notification** > **Events**.

4. Optional. On the **Events** page, enter an event ID and select a cloud service to search for an event.

5. In the event list, view event information in the following columns: **Event ID**, **Service**, **Event Name**, and **Event Version**. For more information about supported events, see Supported change events.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a4faa5640b05fa691518706b5cb828dd.jpeg)

6. Find the event that you want to view and click **Details** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/abfc9ca228f51798a3de639dd70fbbf3.jpeg)

<a id="section-6-17-2"></a>

### 6.17.2. Configure event push

The event push feature allows you to push the events in the event list to event receivers. This way, data can be efficiently communicated and forwarded.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Event Notification** > **Event Push**.

4. On the **Event Push** page, click **Create Configuration**.

5. In the **Create Configuration** dialog box, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4dea5028abcc6032fc71dbd0698d78e2.jpeg)

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Name | The name of the event push configuration. The name must be 2 to 64 characters in length. |
   | Description | The description of the event push configuration. |
   | Acceptor URL | The API endpoint of the receiver. Enter a valid URL that consists of the HTTP or HTTPS protocol, domain name, and path. |
   | Acceptor Parameter Name | The name of the parameter used by the receiver to receive resource changes. |
   | Organization | The effective scope of event push. When a user in the selected organization performs an operation included in the event list, the event is pushed based on the configuration. |
   | Request Header Parameters | The header names and values in the requests sent to the receiver API endpoint.The specified request headers must ensure the security, integrity, and accuracy of communication.<br>Click <strong>Add</strong> to add more request headers. Click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5622a8a2343237be55cf978a0043b0d3.png" width="12" alt="">icon to remove added<br>request headers. |
   | Request Body Parameters | The parameter names and values in the body of HTTP POST requests sent from a client to a server. |
   | Content Code | The encoding type of the content. Valid values: <strong>UTF-8</strong> and <strong>GBK</strong>. |
   | Passing Method | The HTTP request method. Valid values: <strong>GET</strong> and <strong>POST</strong>.<br>Important<br>• If this parameter is set to GET, the request body parameters are ignored and the receiver parameter is concatenated in GET mode.<br>• If this parameter is set to POST, the request body parameters and the receiver parameter are concatenated in the request body. |
   | Enable | Specifies whether to enable the event push configuration. |

6. Click **OK**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can click **Cancel** to discard the event push configuration. You can also click **Test** to test the connectivity of the event push configuration.

7. Perform the following operations as needed.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Operation</td>
       <td>Description</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>View event push configurations</td>
       <td>i. Optional. On the <strong>Event Push</strong> page, enter a configuration name and select an organization to search for the event push configuration that you want to view.<br>ii. In the event push configuration list, view the information about event push configurations in the following columns: <strong>Name</strong>, <strong>Enabling Status</strong>, <strong>Acceptor URL</strong>, <strong>Acceptor Parameter Name</strong>, <strong>Effective Organization</strong>, <strong>Request Header Parameters</strong>, <strong>Request Body Parameters</strong>, <strong>Content</strong> <strong>Code</strong>, <strong>Passing Method</strong>, <strong>Description</strong>, and <strong>Created At</strong>.<br>Note<br>You can click the icon next to <strong>Enabling Status</strong> to filter event push<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5023e339267bc4129725d2919336aa11.png" width="11" alt=""><br>configurations and display the configurations in the <strong>Enabled</strong> or <strong>Disabled</strong> state.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e6bc27c073d26f1d02b619377d60da0b.jpeg" alt=""></td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Modify an event push configuration</td>
       <td>i. On the <strong>Event Push</strong> page, find the configuration that you want to modify and click <strong>Modify</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the <strong>Modify Configuration</strong> dialog box, modify the parameters. You cannot modify the configuration name.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Enable an event push configuration</td>
       <td>Note<br>Only event push configurations in the <strong>Disabled</strong> state can be enabled.<br>i. On the <strong>Event Push</strong> page, find the configuration that you want to enable and click <strong>Enable</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Disable an event push configuration</td>
       <td>Note<br>Only event push configurations in the <strong>Enabled</strong> state can be disabled.<br>i. On the <strong>Event Push</strong> page, find the configuration that you want to disable and click <strong>Disable</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Delete an event push configuration</td>
       <td>i. On the <strong>Event Push</strong> page, find the configuration that you want to delete and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>Delete</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>
