<a id="section-7"></a>

# 7.Operations

<a id="section-7-1"></a>

## 7.1. Resource operations

<a id="section-7-1-1"></a>

### 7.1.1. Application forms

The Application Forms page displays service-related application forms submitted on the platform, including the application forms submitted by using a service catalog.

<a id="section-7-1-1-1"></a>

#### 7.1.1.1. View application forms

The Application Forms page displays a list of application forms categorized as My Application Forms, To Be Approved, Participated, Handled, and All Application Forms.

**Background information**

- My Application Forms: all application forms that you created

- To Be Approved: application forms that require your approval

- Participated: application forms you have participated in, including those copied to you and all approvals automatically passed

- Handled: application forms that you processed, including all approval forms that you processed, transferred, or co-signed

- All Application Forms: all application forms within your visibility scope, including application forms that you created, processed, or participated in, as well as other application forms within your visibility scope

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Forms**.

4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **My Application Forms**, **To Be Approved**, **Participated**, **Handled**, or **All Application Forms** tab.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b43a93838e73061c6df706f3adfda4fe.jpeg)

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the filter conditions, and then click **Search**.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Tab</td>
       <td>Supported filter conditions</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   | My Application Forms | <strong>Application Form No.</strong>, <strong>Process Name</strong>, <strong>Scenario</strong>, <strong>Application Form</strong> <strong>Status</strong>, and <strong>Submission Time</strong>. For <strong>Scenario</strong>, you can select <strong>Management</strong> <strong>Operations</strong>, <strong>Cloud Service Operations</strong>, <strong>Service Catalog</strong>, <strong>Service</strong> <strong>Boundary</strong>, or <strong>Custom</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/298bef8cc5d69929129d1318ba5e0e21.jpeg) |
   | --- | --- |
   | To Be <strong>Approved</strong>/<strong>Partici</strong> <strong>pated</strong>/<strong>Handled</strong> | <strong>Application Form No.</strong>, <strong>Process Name</strong>, <strong>Scenario</strong>, <strong>Query Type</strong>, <strong>Applicant</strong> <strong>Organization</strong>/<strong>Applicant</strong>, <strong>Include Subordinate Organizations</strong>, and <strong>Submission Time</strong>. For <strong>Scenario</strong>, you can select <strong>Management Operations</strong>, <strong>Cloud Service Operations</strong>, <strong>Service Catalog</strong>, <strong>Service Boundary</strong>, or <strong>Custom</strong>. For <strong>Query Type</strong>, you can select <strong>Query by Applicant</strong> <strong>Organization</strong> or <strong>Query by Applicant</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/da6fb8d1d092c74606a5460ed1606e4e.jpeg) |
   | All Application Forms | <strong>Application Form No.</strong>, <strong>Process Name</strong>, <strong>Scenario</strong>, <strong>Application Form</strong> <strong>Status</strong>, <strong>Query Type</strong>, <strong>Applicant Organization</strong>/<strong>Applicant</strong>, <strong>Include</strong> <strong>Subordinate Organizations</strong>, and <strong>Submission Time</strong>. For <strong>Scenario</strong>, you can select <strong>Management Operations</strong>, <strong>Cloud Service Operations</strong>, <strong>Service</strong> <strong>Catalog</strong>, <strong>Service Boundary</strong>, or <strong>Custom</strong>. For <strong>Query Type</strong>, you can select <strong>Query by Applicant Organization</strong> or <strong>Query by Applicant</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/43c7fde3cebda35826facf34202aa03a.jpeg) |

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Scenario**: includes **Management Operations**, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
   >
   > - **Management Operations**: The system displays this option when you select **Management Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service Operations**: The system displays this option when you select **Cloud Service Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Service Catalog**: The system displays this option when you select **Service Catalog** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service**: The system displays this option when you select **Service Boundary** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Query Type**: includes **Query by Applicant Organization** and **Query by Applicant**.
   >
   > - **Applicant Organization** and **Include Subordinate Organizations**: The system displays these options when you select **Query by Applicant Organization** for **Query Type**.
   >
   > - **Applicant**: The system displays this option when you select **Query by Applicant** for **Query Type**.
   >
   > - **Submission Time**: Set the submission time of the application form.

6. View the application form list.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/599d163685b72186abb4a1f7dcb34ca1.jpeg)

7. Click the application No. to go to the **Details** page.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The application form requirement details vary based on the scenario.
   >
   >   - For the Service Catalog scenario, approvers can modify the configuration. Click **Modify Configuration** in the Actions column to update the applicationform configuration. For more information, see Modify the configuration of an application form.
   >
   >   - Click **Detailed Parameters** in the **Actions** column to view the call parameter information in the **Detailed Parameters** panel.
   >
   > - To view the application progress, click **View All** next to Approval Progress of Application Form.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ed007003af1dcf625f0b29ec84d3f009.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-1-1-2"></a>

#### 7.1.1.2. Withdraw an application form

The application form page allows you to withdraw an application form pending approval.

**Prerequisites**

The application form is in the **Pending Approval** status.

**Limits**

You can withdraw only the application forms created by yourself.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Application Forms**.

4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **My Application Forms** tab.

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, specify the **Application Form No.**, **Process Name**, **Scenario**, **Management Operations**/**Cloud Service Operations**/**Service Catalog**/**Cloud Service**, **Application Form Status**, and **Submission Time** conditions, and then click **Search**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/298bef8cc5d69929129d1318ba5e0e21.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Scenario**: Supports **Management Operations**, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
   >
   > - **Management Operation**: Appears when you select **Management Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service Operations**: Appears when you select **Cloud Service Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Service Catalog**: Appears when you select **Service Catalog** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service**: Appears when you select **Service Boundary** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Submission Time**: Specifies the submission time of the application form.

6. In the application form list, click **Withdraw** in the **Actions** column of the target application form.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/56fc00604aeedd08393f6814835f42fa.jpeg)

7. In the dialog box, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-1-3"></a>

#### 7.1.1.3. Modify the configuration of an application form

When an approver modifies the configuration of an application form, the approver must ensure that the product operation is connected to a service and that the relevant system preset services are listed before proceeding with configuration changes.

**Prerequisites**

- The workflow bound to this application form must allow approvers to modify configurations. Approvers can successfully change configurations only if their management scope exceeds that of the initiator.

- The application form is in the **Under approval** state.

- The **Scenario** of the application form is Service Catalog.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Application Forms**.

4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **To Be Approved** tab.

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure **Application Form NO.**, **Process Name**, **Scenario**, **Management Operation**/**Cloud Product Operation**/**Service Catalog**/**Cloud Service**, **Query Type**, **Applicant Organization**/**Applicant**, **Include Subordinate Organizations**, and **Submission Time**, and then click **Search**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/da6fb8d1d092c74606a5460ed1606e4e.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Scenario**: includes **Management Operation**s, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
   >
   > - **Management Operations**: appears when you select **Management Operations** for Scenario.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service Operations**: appears when you select **Cloud Service Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Service Catalog**: appears when you select **Service Catalog** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service**: appears when you select **Service Boundary** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Query Type**: includes **Query by Applicant Organization** and **Query by Applicant**.
   >
   > - **Applicant Organization** and **Include Subordinate Organizations**: appear when you select **Query by Applicant Organization** for **Query Type**.
   >
   > - **Applicant**: appears when you select **Query by Applicant** for **Query Type**.
   >
   > - **Submission Time**: specifies the submission time of the application form.

6. In the application form list, click the No. of the application form.

7. On the application form details page, click **Modify Configuration**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ace3fe1a37ef0484db5b225eddc24509.jpeg)

8. On the product console page, update the configuration.

9. In the **Reason for modifying the configuration** dialog box, enter the reason.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/afc6ceadb674a386d04ed03435f4effd.jpeg)

0. Return to the application form details page and view the configuration modification history.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ed007003af1dcf625f0b29ec84d3f009.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-1-1-4"></a>

#### 7.1.1.4. Approve an application form

Approve an application form pending your approval.

**Background information**

When an application form requires your approval, the system sends notifications using DingTalk, in-system messages, and emails. If the applicant is also the approver of the current approval node, the system automatically approves the application form. For countersigns involving multiple approvers, the remaining approvers must approve the application form as usual.

**Prerequisites**

The application form is in the **Pending Approving** status.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Appliction Forms**.

4. On the **Appliction Forms** page, click the **To Be Approved** tab.

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Application Form No.**, **Process Name**, **Scenario**, **Management Operation**s/**Cloud Service Operations**/**Service Catalog**/**Cloud Service**, **Query Type**, **Applicant Organization**/**Applicant**, **Include Subordinate Organizations**, and **Submission Time** conditions, and then click **Search**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/da6fb8d1d092c74606a5460ed1606e4e.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Scenario**: Supports **Management Operations**, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
   >
   > - **Management Operations**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Management Operations**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service Operations**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Cloud Service Operations**.
   >
   > - **Service Catalog**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Service Catalog**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Service Boundary**.
   >
   > - **Query Type**: Supports **Query by Applicant Organization** and **Query by Applicant**.
   >
   > - **Applicant Organization** and **Include Subordinate Organizations**: Appear when you set **Query Type** to **Query by Applicant Organization**.
   >
   > - **Applicant**: Appears when you set **Query Type** to **Query by Applicant**.
   >
   > - **Submission Time**: Specifies the submission time of the application form.

6. Approve a single application form or approve application forms in batches.

   - **Approve a single application form**:

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     In the application form list, click **Review** in the **Actions** column of the target application form.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8f09ad3acb5bdf79956d659dafb0ed01.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li>

     In the **Review** dialog box, select comments, enter a review description, and upload attachments.

     > **Note**
     >
     > - You can set the comments to **Approve** or **Reject**.
     >
     > - Click **Approval Analysis** to open Apsara Copilot, which analyzes the application form and provides approval suggestions. The approval analysis feature appears only after an operations administrator enables the intelligent assistant in **Configurations** > **Apsara Copilot** > **Custom Configuration**.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1495b5768f6d316f0318e9cf45e05d71.jpeg)

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     Click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Approve multiple application forms in batches**:

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     In the application form list, select multiple application forms that require approval.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a5d0c11a1ffacc4d31786c05ae624fb5.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Batch Approve** below the list.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the **Batch Approve** dialog box, select comments, enter an approval description, and upload attachments.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c150ffeaa8d3dd6d5d9aab1be4239015.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li value="500">

     Click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-7-1-1-5"></a>

#### 7.1.1.5. Transfer an application form

The current approver can transfer an application form to another approver for processing.

**Prerequisites**

The application form is in the **Pending Approving** status.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Application Forms**.

4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **To Be Approved** tab.

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, set the **Application Form No.**, **Process Name**, **Scenario**, **Management Operations**/**Cloud Service Operation**s/**Service Catalog**/**Cloud Service**, **Query Type**, **Applicant Organization**/**Applicant**, **Include Subordinate Organizations**, and **Submission Time** conditions, and then click **Search**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/da6fb8d1d092c74606a5460ed1606e4e.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Scenario**: Supports **Management Operations**, **Cloud Service Operation**s, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
   >
   > - **Management Operations**: Appears when you select **Management Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service Operations**: Appears when you select **Cloud Service Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Service Catalog**: Appears when you select **Service Catalog** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service**: Appears when you select **Service Boundary** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Query Type**: Supports **Query by Applicant Organization** and **Query by Applicant**.
   >
   > - **Applicant Organization** and **Include Subordinate Organizations**: Appear when you select **Query by Applicant Organization** for **Query Type**.
   >
   > - **Applicant**: Appears when you select **Query by Applicant** for **Query Type**.
   >
   > - **Submission Time**: Specifies the submission time of the application form.

6. In the application form list, click the No. of the application form.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8f09ad3acb5bdf79956d659dafb0ed01.jpeg)

7. On the **Details** page, click **Transfer** in the upper-right corner.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/abe6947768f069601509fe9a6177192f.jpeg)

The current approver add approvers to insert a new approval node before the current approval node. This feature allows you to add specific personnel to the approval process to meet actual business requirements or additional review requirements in special situations.

4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **To Be Approved** tab.

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Application Form No.**, **Process Name**, **Scenario**, **Management Operation**s/**Cloud Service Operations**/**Service Catalog**/**Cloud Service**, **Query Type**, **Applicant Organization**/**Applicant**, **Include Subordinate Organizations**, and **Submission Time** conditions, and then click **Search**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/da6fb8d1d092c74606a5460ed1606e4e.jpeg)

   > **Note**

   > - **Management Operation**s: Appears when you select **Management Operations** for **Scenario**.
   >
   > - **Cloud Service Operations**: Appears when you select **Cloud Service Operations** for **Scenario**.

   >

6. In the application form list, click the application form No..

7. On the **Details** page, click **Add Signature** in the upper-right corner.

<a id="section-7-1-2"></a>

### 7.1.2. Process management

<a id="section-7-1-2-1"></a>

#### 7.1.2.1. Manage processes

You can create process definitions to define approval processes for different organizations and services based on the approval requirements. You can configure custom approval processes for resource applications based on existing approval processes. You can dynamically add user nodes in an approval process and specify system users as approvers. You can configure sequential signature and parallel signature approval methods, add multiple approval nodes, and specify multiple approvers. The system provides preset Start and End nodes.

**Background information**

You can manage approval processes at the operation control layer of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to allow or reject operations that users want to perform. This way, user operations can be approved in a fine-grained manner. The process management feature is used to approve operations that users want to perform, such as creating resources. Users may perform high-risk operations in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Before users perform high-risk operations, a role with higher or centralized permissions must approve the operations. This prevents accidental operations or unauthorized access and ensures the security, stability, and compliance of the system.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Process Management** > **Process Management**.

4. On the **Process Management** page, click **Create Process**.

5. In the Create Process wizard, configure the parameters in the **Basic Information** and **Process Configuration** steps.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Configure the parameters in the Basic Information step and click **Next**. The following table describes the parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Process Name | The name of the process. |
   | Process Description | The description of the process. |
   | Applicable Personnel | The organization with which the process can be associated. Valid values: <strong>All</strong> <strong>Organizations</strong> and <strong>Select Organization</strong>.<br>• <strong>All Organizations</strong>: The process can be associated with all organizations.<br>• <strong>Select Organization</strong>: The process can be associated only with the selected organization. |
   | Select Organization | The organization with which the process can be associated. This parameter is displayed only if the <strong>Applicable Personnel</strong> parameter is set to <strong>Select</strong> <strong>Organization</strong>.<br>Select an organization from the <strong>Select Organization</strong> drop-down list. You can select only one organization within a tenant. The process can be associated only with the selected organization. |
   | Bind Sub-organization | Specifies whether the process can be associated with the subordinate organizations of the selected organization. This parameter is displayed only if the <strong>Applicable Personnel</strong> parameter is set to <strong>Select Organization</strong>.<br>If a subordinate organization is associated with another process, the current process cannot be associated with the subordinate organization.<br>After you select an organization from the <strong>Select Organization</strong> drop-down list, you can turn on or off the switch.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/00f50aae605f23e0c56a8e77f6dd6203.png" width="27" alt="">: The process can be associated with the subordinate organizations<br>of the selected organization.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b20024a0a33222e35c29d30284bd7231.png" width="28" alt="">: The process cannot be associated with the subordinate<br>organizations of the selected organization. |

All users who assume the selected roles can initiate the process. |

If you clear the check box, all users assigned the selected role in the level-1 organization can approve the process.<br>• If you set the <strong>Type</strong> parameter to <strong>Supervisor</strong>, select a value from the <strong>Initiator</strong> drop-down list to specify the supervisor level. Only supervisors of the selected level can approve the process. Valid values of the Initiator parameter include <strong>Direct Supervisor</strong>, <strong>Second Level Supervisor</strong>, <strong>Third Level Supervisor</strong>, <strong>Fourth Level Supervisor</strong>, and <strong>Fifth Level Supervisor</strong>. You can select only one supervisor level.<br>Note<br>• Supervisors are the organization administrators of organizations of each level. The process is approved in turn by supervisors from the lowest level to the highest level. Supervisors of multiple levels may be involved as the approvers of the approval node. If you select Second Level Supervisor, the final approver is the organization administrator of the parent organization to which the initiator belongs. You can select a supervisor of up to the fifth level.<br>• If no supervisor can be found, the process is automatically approved. If you clear the check box, the approver is not allowed to modify the configurations.<br>Note<br>This parameter is suitable for creating products or services and changing configurations. If the permission scope of the approver is higher than that of the applicant, the approver can change configurations as expected. If the approver has no permission to view data during the configuration change, the application is rejected. In this case, the applicant must resubmit the application. |

**Configure the External Process Integration node**

To transfer application forms from the process system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to a third-party approval node, you must complete the following connection configurations to notify the third-party process system and start the approval process in the third-party process system. After you complete the configurations, click **Connectivity Test** to check the connectivity between the two parties.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4304f0490d89ab1144f7f859e5f22a8d.jpeg)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Request Method | The request method. Default value: <strong>POST</strong>. |
| Request URL | The request URL of the notification operation provided by the third-party process system.<br>Important<br>The request URL must be an external cloud URL. To enable access to the URL, contact Apsara Stack technical support. The involved server role is unimanager-workflow.flow#. |
| Access Token | The access token of the notification operation. Access tokens are a security mechanism used for identity authentication and authorization. When a request is made, an access token is inserted into headers in the format of {"Authorization": " bearer &lt;Access token&gt;"} to prove the identity of the requester and obtain access permissions. |
| Process Access Configuratio n | The custom parameters to be included in the request. You can click <strong>Add One Row</strong> to add a custom parameter. You can add at most 20 parameters, one per row. For more information, see the Request parameters section of this topic.<br>In each parameter row, enter the parameter name in the Request Parameter Name field and the parameter value in the Field Name field.<br>When the third-party notification operation is called, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console generates a set of key-value pairs based on the specified parameters, encapsulates them into a JSONObject, and then passes the JSONObject to the third-party process system. |

**Request parameters**

The parameters to be included in requests from the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to the third-party notification operation are defined as paramJson. paramJson consists of required data and custom data.

- **Required data**

  For more information, see lines 35 to 37 in the Pseudocode for constructing request parameters section of this topic.

  Required data is passed by default. You do not need to add required data in the **Process Access Configuration** section. The following table describes the required data.

  > **Important**
  >
  > If you add a parameter with the same name as a required parameter in the **Process Access Configuration** section, the added parameter does not take effect.

  | Parameter | Type | Description |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | callbackParams | Map&lt;String, Object&gt; | The parameters required for callbacks.<br>After the third-party process system completes the approval, it notifies the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console with the parameters. |

- **Custom data**

  In each parameter row in the **Process Access Configuration** section, the parameter name is defined as paramKey and the parameter value is defined as paramValue. Parameter values support preset and non-preset values.

  - **Preset values**

    For more information, see lines 24 to 27 in the Pseudocode for constructing request parameters section of this topic.

    If the value of a custom parameter is a preset value, the console dynamically obtains the corresponding information of the application form based on the definition of the preset value, and encapsulates the parameter name and dynamic information as a new key-value pair into paramJson.

    The following table describes the preset values.

    | Key (including $, {, and }) | Description | Type | Example |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_UUID} | The ID of the application form. | String | pi-2501231508290001 |
    | ${SHOW_INFO} | The content of the application form. | List&lt;List&lt; JSONObje ct&gt;&gt; | \[ \[ { "label": "SLB instance ID", "value": "lb-insId1" }, { "label": "Organization", "value": "coms-001" } \], \[ { "label": "SLB instance ID", "value": "lb-insId2"}, { "label": "Organization", "value": "coms-002" } \] \] |
    | ${ASCM_FLOW_ID} | The ID of the process associated with the application form in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. | Integer | 74 |
    | ${ASCM_FLOW_NAME} | The name of the process associated with the application form in the<br>Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. | String | Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Process 74 |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_GMT_C REATED} | The time when the application form was created. | Date | 2025-01-23T07:08:30.000+0000 |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_GMT_M ODIFIED} | The time when the application form was modified. | Date | 2025-01-23T07:11:22.000+0000 |
    | ${SERVICE_TYPE} | The business scenario of the application form. | String | Valid values:<br>• ascm_management<br>• product_operation<br>• workflow<br>• permission_boundary |
    | ${SERVICE_TYPE_MDS} | The description of the business scenario of the application form. | String | Examples:<br>• ascm_management: Management Operations<br>• product_operation: Cloud Service Operations<br>• workflow: Service Catalog<br>• permission_boundary: Service Boundary |
    | ${SERVICE_OPERATIO N_DETAIL} | The business operation of the application form and its classification information. | List&lt;JSON Objectt&gt; | Each JSONObject contains the following elements:<br>{ "serviceOperationSortMds": "Classification information about the business operation of the application form", "serviceOperation": "Business scenario code", "serviceOperationMds": "Business scenario description", "opType": "Operation type", "opTypeMds": "Operation type description" }<br>Valid values of serviceOperationSortMds:<br>• ascm_management and product_operation: the classification information about the operation.Example: SLB - Instance.<br>• workflow: the service and category.Example: ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ -ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ 4.0.<br>• permission_boundary: the POP code of the service. Example: Rds.<br>Valid values of serviceOperation:<br>• ascm_management and product_operation: the code of the operation. Example: PRIG_SLB_INSTANCE_DEL.<br>• workflow: the service catalog ID.Example: CS000186.<br>• permission_boundary: the API operation. Example: CreateDBInstance.<br>Valid values of serviceOperationMds:<br>• ascm_management and product_operation: the description of the operation. Example: Delete an SLB instance.<br>• workflow: the name of the service catalog. Example: MQ Service Catalog.<br>• permission_boundary: same as the value of permission_boundary in serviceOperation.<br>Valid values of opType:<br>• ascm_management and product_operation: null.<br>• workflow: the operation type. Valid values: create, modify, and release.<br>• permission_boundary: The value is permissions-boundary.<br>Valid values of opTypeMds:<br>• ascm_management and product_operation: null.<br>• workflow: the description of the operation type. Examples:<br>• create: Activate Resources.<br>• modify: Change Configurations.<br>• release: Release Resources.<br>• permission_boundary: the description of the service boundary.Example: Service Boundary. |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_APPLY_INFO} | The application reason. | String | Example: To create an ApsaraDB RDS instance. |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_ASCM_USER_ID} | The UID of the applicant in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. | String | 5003 |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_ASCM_USER_NAME} | The username of the applicant in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. | String | admin |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_ASCM_ORG_ID} | The ID of the organization to which the applicant belongs in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. | String | 4 |
    | ${FLOW_FORM_ASCM_ORG_NAME} | The name of the organization to which the applicant belongs in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. | String | iaas_test |

  - **Non-preset values**

    For more information, see lines 29 to 32 in the Pseudocode for constructing request parameters section of this topic.

    The console directly encapsulates the name and value of a parameter as a constant key-value pair in paramJson.

    If more than one process exists in the third-party process system, you can add a custom parameter to specify the ID of the third-party process that applies.

**Pseudocode for constructing request parameters**

The following pseudocode is provided to help you better understand how parameters are constructed.

```text
// The preset values.
private static final List<String> preSetInfoList = Arrays.asList("See the preset value table", "Omitted in the pseudocode");

// Each element corresponds to a parameter row that you specify.
List<List<String>> userDefineParamKeyAndValueList = new ArrayList<>();
userDefineParamKeyAndValueList.add(Arrays.asList("paramKey1", "paramValue1"));
userDefineParamKeyAndValueList.add(Arrays.asList("paramKey2", "paramValue2"));
...


public JSONObject getParamJsonFromUserDefineParamKeyAndValueList 
                        (List<List<String>> userDefineParamKeyAndValueList) {

    // Define the parameters included in the requests from the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for calling the third-party notification operation as paramJson. 
    JSONObject paramJson = new JSONObject();
    
    // Traverse the parameter rows that you specify.
    for (List<String> paramKeyAndValuePair : userDefineParamKeyAndValueList) {
        
        // Define the value in the Request Parameter Name field as paramKey and the value in the Field Name field as paramValue in each parameter row. 
        String paramKey =  paramKeyAndValuePair.get(0);   
        String paramValue =  paramKeyAndValuePair.get(1);   
    
        // If a paramValue is a preset value, the console dynamically obtains the corresponding information of the application form based on the definition of the preset value and passes it to the third-party process system.
        if (preSetInfoList.containsKey(paramValue)) {
            paramJson.put(paramKey, "Dynamic data of the application form obtained 
based on paramValue");
        }
        
        // If a paramValue is not a preset value, it is regarded as a constant and is directly encapsulated into paramJson and passed to the third-party process system.
        else {
            paramJson.put(paramKey, paramValue);
        }
    }
    
    // Required parameters on the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console side, which areused to distinguish application forms and approval nodes.
    // When the third-party process is complete, the third-party process system calls the notification operation of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and returns callbackParams.
    paramJson.put("callbackParams", "Callback parameters");

    return paramJson;
    
}
```

#### 7.1.2.2. Workflow binding

Configure the association between workflows and business operations to meet configuration requirements for multiple scenarios. The system supports dynamically binding resource application methods with approval processes. Multiple types of resources can share the same workflow.

**Background information**

- Establish a binding relationship between workflows and business operations. The system intercepts the requester’s operation based on specific business requirements and workflow settings. The system executes the related operation only after approval. This approach provides better control over workflow execution and ensures compliance and accuracy of business activities.

- Create, modify, and delete workflow binding relationships.

**Prerequisites**

- Before you create a workflow binding relationship, make sure that you have created the workflow and that the workflow is in the **Published** state.

- By default, the operating user is the operations administrator.

**Limits**

A single workflow can have only one binding relationship with a business scenario. If the selected workflow already has a binding relationship, the corresponding business scenario becomes grayed out and cannot be bound again.

**Create a workflow binding relationship**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operation** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Process Management** > **Bind Process**.

4. At the top of the page, click **Bind Process**.

5. On the **Bind Process** page, complete the following binding configuration.

   | Configuratio n item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Process name | From the process name drop-down list, select the workflow to bind. You can only select workflows with the status <strong>Published</strong>. |
   | Business scenario | The workflow supports binding to one of the following business scenarios: <strong>Management Operations</strong>, <strong>Cloud Service Operations</strong>, or <strong>Service Catalog</strong>.Single selection only. |
   | Managemen t Operations | <strong>Business scenario</strong> is set to <strong>Management Operations</strong>. Configure this item. You can select multiple management operations.<br>When you perform the selected management operations, the system requires workflow approval. Examples include managing organizations and managing resource sets.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0ed96e4ad4b05e72bd7b69725dca7583.jpeg) |

   <table>
     <tr>

       <td><strong>Business scenario</strong> is set to <strong>Cloud Service Operations</strong>. Configure this item. You can select multiple cloud resources and their operations.<br>When you perform the selected cloud service operations, the system requires workflow approval. Examples include starting or stopping an ECS instance under Elastic Compute Service (ECS), or creating, modifying, or deleting a VPC under Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).<br>Note<br>In multi-cloud scenarios, a unified approval process is supported. For public cloud services, permission points are limited to those cloud services already integrated into the service catalog. Currently supported public cloud services include ECS, VPC, Server Load Balancer (SLB), and Elastic IP Address (EIP).<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2246ac8d91609b35e23e310924e8d808.jpeg" alt=""></td>

<a id="section-7-1-3"></a>

### 7.1.3. Quota management

<a id="section-7-1-3-1"></a>

#### 7.1.3.1. Products that support resource quotas

Organization administrators and users can create resources within the quota limits of each product in their organization. When the quota for a product is exhausted, they cannot create additional resources for that product. To continue creating resources, they must first increase the product quota in the organization. If no quota is configured, the system does not limit resource creation.

> **Note**
>
> For disk, memory, and capacity quotas, the minimum calculation unit is **GB**. The system rounds decimal values to the nearest integer. For example, when calculating the quota, the system rounds 0.8 GB up to 1 GB and 0.2 GB down to 0 GB.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-1"></a>

##### 7.1.3.1.1. Elastic computing

###### 7.1.3.1.1.1. ECS

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for Elastic Compute Service (ECS), calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

<table>
  <tr>
    <th colspan="2">Quota</th>
    <th>Description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>

  </tr>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td rowspan="4">Disk Quota (GiB)</td>
    <td>SSD (GiB)</td>

  </tr>
  <tr>

    <td>The number of instances that can be created for an instance type.</td>
  </tr>
</table>

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

The usage of CPU cores, memory, GPUs, and disk capacity of a single ECS instance is calculated based on the following formulas:

- CPU core usage = instanceTypeId.cpu

- Memory usage = instanceTypeId.mem

- GPU usage = instanceTypeId.gpu

- Disk capacity usage= ∑ (System disks and attached disks)

- Instance type usage = Number of created instances of the instance type

> **Note**
>
> - The usage of CPU cores, memory, and GPUs of a single ECS instance is obtained the information defined in the instance type.
>
>   - instanceTypeId.cpu indicates the number of CPU cores defined in the selected instance type.
>
>   - instanceTypeId.mem indicates the memory size defined in the selected instance type.
>
>   - instanceTypeId.gpu indicates the number of GPUs defined in the selected instance type.
>
> - The disk capacity usage of an instance is calculated by accumulating the size of the system disks and the size of the attached disks.

The usage of security groups, custom images, and ENIs is calculated based on the following formulas:

- Security group usage = Number of created security groups

- Custom image usage = Number of created custom images

- ENI usage = Number of created ENIs

> **Note**
>
> The usage of security groups, custom images, and ENIs is the number of created resource instances.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Important**
>
> Some Elastic Block Storage (EBS) clusters can share disks of multiple types. When you configure logical inventories, make sure that the sum of the logical inventories of the disk quota items does not exceed the physical inventory. For example, if an IO15 cluster has a physical inventory of 1,000 GiB and can share premium performance disks and standard SSDs, the physical inventory of both premium performance disks and standard SSDs is increased by 1,000 GiB. When you configure logical inventories, you need to check whether disk sharing is enabled for the EBS cluster and make sure that logical inventories do not exceed 1,000 GiB.

**Calculation method of quota usage**

The quota usage of a single cluster is calculated based on the following formulas:

- CPU core usage = Cluster.CpuCount = sum(Node.CpuCount)

- Memory usage = Cluster.MemCount = sum(Node.MemCount)

- Computing power usage = Cluster.FlopsCount = sum(Node.FlopsCount)

- GPU memory usage = Cluster.VideoMemCount = sum(Node.VideoMemCount)

> **Note**
>
> - Cluster.CpuCount indicates the number of CPU cores of the selected cluster.
>
> - Node.CpuCount indicates the number of CPU cores of a node in the selected cluster.
>
> - Cluster.MemCount indicates the memory of the selected cluster.
>
> - Node.MemCount indicates the memory of a node in the selected cluster.
>
> - Cluster.FlopsCount indicates the computing power of the selected cluster.
>
> - Node.FlopsCount indicates the computing power of a node in the selected cluster.
>
> - Cluster.VideoMemCount indicates the GPU memory of the selected cluster.
>
> - Node.VideoMemCount indicates the GPU memory of a node in the selected cluster.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Important**
>
> Bare metal clusters and container clusters share the physical inventory. When you configure logical inventories, make sure that the sum of the logical inventories of a quota item of the two types of clusters cannot be exceed the physical inventory. For example, if the physical CPU inventory of both bare metal clusters and container clusters is five cores, the sum of the logical CPU inventories of bare metal clusters and container clusters must be equal to or smaller than five cores.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-1-9"></a>

##### 7.1.3.1.2. Storage

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-2-1"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.2.1. File Storage NAS

This topic describes the configurable quota items for File Storage NAS, how the system calculates quota usage, and the source of inventory.

**Quota items**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| NAS capacity threshold (GiB) | The total storage capacity of the File Storage NAS service. |
| NAS used capacity (GiB) | This item performs weak validation and sets an upper limit for used capacity. When the actual NAS usage exceeds this quota, the system prevents creation of new instances but does not restrict usage of existing instances. |

**How the system calculates quota usage**

Usage of a single NAS instance = The usage of the selected NAS instance.

> **Note**
>
> - The system obtains the pre-allocated space limit from the current instance’s capacity storage. This value becomes the capacity threshold for the current instance.
>
> - The system measures the actual usage of a NAS instance under the NAS used capacity quota item.

**Inventory source**

Capacity management in the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

| Capacity-type capacity (GiB) | The capacity-type capacity of the CPFS file system. |

**How the system calculates quota usage**

The usage of a single CPFS instance equals the usage of the selected CPFS instance.

Capacity management in the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

###### 7.1.3.1.2.3. OSS

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Bucket Capacity Threshold (GiB) | The total capacity of OSS buckets. |
| Bucket Usage (GiB) | This quota is of the weak verification type. You can configure this quota to specify the maximum storage capacity of OSS that can be used.<br>If the actual used storage capacity of OSS exceeds the value that you specify for this quota, you cannot create new OSS buckets. However, the existing OSS buckets are not affected. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

Capacity quota of a single bucket = Capacity of the selected bucket

> **Note**
>
> - The total capacity of a bucket is equal to the maximum capacity that can be pre-allocated to the bucket.
>
> - The resource usage details of a bucket are included in the Bucket Usage quota.
>
> - The total capacity of an OSS bucket whose capacity is unlimited is calculated as 0.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4"></a>

##### 7.1.3.1.4. Database services

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-1"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.4.1. AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL, calculation method of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL. |

**Calculation method of quota usage**

- **Integrated storage mode**

  - CPU quota usage = cpuCore × DBInstanceGroupCount

  - Memory quota usage = memory × DBInstanceGroupCount

  - Disk quota usage = disk × DBInstanceGroupCount × Number of replicas

  > **Note**
  >
  > The quota usage of AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL instances of the integrated storage mode is calculated based on the instance type, the number of compute nodes, and the number of replicas.
  >
  > - cpuCore indicates the number of CPU cores of the selected instance type.
  >
  > - DBInstanceGroupCount indicates the number of compute nodes.
  >
  > - memory indicates the memory capacity of the selected instance type.
  >
  > - disk indicates the disk size of the selected instance type.
  >
  > - By default, the number of replicas is 2.

- **Reserved storage mode**

  - CPU quota usage = cpuCore × (SegNum + MasterNum + Number of replicas)

  - Memory quota usage = memory × (SegNum + MasterNum + Number of replicas)

  - Disk quota usage = disk × (SegNum × 2 + MasterNum + Number of replicas)

  > **Note**
  >
  > The quota usage of AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL instances of the reserved storage mode is calculated based on the instance type, the number of compute nodes, the number of master nodes, and the number of replicas. The fixed ratio of CPU cores, memory capacity, and disk capacity of an instance is 1:8:80.
  >
  > - cpuCore indicates the number of CPU cores of the selected instance type.
  >
  > - memory indicates the memory capacity of the selected instance type.
  >
  > - disk indicates the disk size of the selected instance type.
  >
  > - SegNum indicates the number of compute nodes.
  >
  > - MasterNum indicates the number of master nodes.
  >
  > - By default, the number of replicas is 1.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note**
>
> Shared AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL instances share physical resources with each other without being limited by the physical inventory. The shared physical resources include the memory capacity and CPU cores. Therefore, the physical inventory of the memory capacity and CPU cores may not indicate the saleable memory capacity and CPU cores. The saleable memory capacity and CPU cores may be greater than the physical inventory.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-2"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.4.2. ApsaraDB for MongoDB

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

- **Replica set instance**

  - CPU quota usage = DBInstanceClass.cpu × Number of primary and secondary nodes

  - Memory quota usage = DBInstanceClass.mem × Number of primary and secondary nodes

  - Disk quota usage = DBInstanceStorage × Number of primary and secondary nodes

  > **Note**
  >
  > The quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications and the number of primary and secondary nodes.
  >
  > - DBInstanceClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  > - DBInstanceClass.mem: the memory capacity of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  > - DBInstanceStorage: the storage capacity of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  > - By default, the number of primary and secondary nodes is 3.

- **Sharded cluster instance**

  - CPU quota usage = mongosSpec.cpu × mongosCount + shardSpec.cpu × shardCount × Number of replicas + configserverSpec.cpu × configserverCount × Number of replicas

  - Memory quota usage = mongosSpec.mem × mongosCount + shardSpec.mem × shardCount × Number of replicas + configserverSpec.mem × configserverCount × Number of replicas

  - Disk quota usage = shardStorage × shardCount × Number of replicas + configserverStorage × configserverCount × Number of replicas

  > **Note**
  >
  > The quota usage of mongos nodes, shard nodes, and Configserver nodes is calculated.
  >
  > - The quota usage of mongos nodes is calculated based on the node specifications and the number of mongos nodes.
  >
  >   - mongosSpec.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected mongos node specifications.
  >
  >   - mongosCount: the number of mongos nodes.
  >
  > - The quota usage of shard nodes is calculated based on the node specifications, number of shard nodes, and number of replicas.
  >
  >   - shardSpec.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected shard node specifications.
  >
  >   - shardSpec.mem: the memory capacity of the selected shard node specifications.
  >
  >   - shardStorage: the storage capacity of the selected shard node specifications.
  >
  >   - shardCount: the number of shard nodes.
  >
  >   - By default, the number of replicas is 3.
  >
  > - The quota usage of Configserver nodes is calculated based on the node specifications, number of Configserver nodes, and number of replicas.
  >
  >   - configserverSpec.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected Configserver node specifications.
  >
  >   - configserverSpec.mem: the memory capacity of the selected Configserver node specifications.
  >
  >   - configserverStorage: the storage capacity of the selected Configserver node specifications.
  >
  >   - configserverCount: the number of Configserver nodes.
  >
  >   - By default, the number of replicas is 3.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note**
>
> Shared ApsaraDB for MongoDB instances share physical resources with each other without being limited by the physical inventory. The shared physical resources include the memory capacity and CPU cores. Therefore, the physical inventory of the memory capacity and CPU cores may not indicate the saleable memory capacity and CPU cores. The saleable memory capacity and CPU cores may be greater than the physical inventory.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-3"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.4.3. PolarDB-X 2.0

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for PolarDB-X 2.0, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total amount of memory that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total disk capacity that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |
| License Core Quota (Core) | The total number of License cores that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

- **CPU**

  - Standard Edition:

    CPU usage = CPU specification of a data node + CPU specification of a data node + 2

  - Enterprise Edition:

    - CPU usage of compute nodes = Number of compute nodes × CPU specification of a compute node

    - CPU usage of data nodes = Number of data nodes × (CPU specification of a data node + CPU specification of a data node + 2)

    - CPU usage of Global Meta Service (GMS) nodes = CPU specification of a data node + CPU specification of a data node + 2

    - CPU usage of Change Data Capture (CDC) nodes = 2 × 4

    - Total CPU usage = CPU usage of compute nodes + CPU usage of data nodes + CPU usage of GMS nodes + CPU usage of CDC nodes

- **Memory**

  - Standard Edition:

    Memory usage = Memory specification of a data node + Memory specification of a data node + 4

  - Enterprise Edition:

    - Memory usage of compute nodes = Number of compute nodes × Memory specification of a compute node

    - Memory usage of data nodes = Number of data nodes × (Memory specification of a data node + Memory specification of a data node + 4)

    - Memory usage of GMS nodes = Memory specification of a data node + Memory specification of a data node + 4

    - Memory usage of CDC nodes = 2 × 16

    - Total memory usage = Memory usage of compute nodes + Memory usage of data nodes + Memory usage of GMS nodes + Memory usage of CDC nodes

- **Disk**

  - Standard Edition:

    Disk usage = User-specified capacity × 2

  - Enterprise Edition:

    - Disk usage of compute nodes = Number of compute nodes × 300

    - Disk usage of data nodes = Number of data nodes × 2 × User-specified capacity

    - Disk usage of GMS nodes = 2 × 50

    - Disk usage of CDC nodes = 200

    - Total disk usage = Disk usage of compute nodes + Disk usage of data nodes + Disk usage of GMS nodes + Disk usage of CDC nodes

- **License core**

  - Standard Edition:

    - Dedicated: License core usage = CPU usage

    - General-purpose: License core usage = CPU usage/2

  - Enterprise Edition:

    - Dedicated: License core usage = Total CPU usage

    - General-purpose: License core usage = Total CPU usage/2

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-4"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.4.4. ApsaraDB RDS

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Database engines**

ApsaraDB RDS supports the following database engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, PolarDB, and SQL Server. You can configure quotas for different database engines.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

- **High-availability Edition**

  - CPU quota usage = dbInstanceClass.cpu × Number of nodes

  - Memory quota usage = dbInstanceClass.mem × Number of nodes

  - Disk quota usage = DBInstanceStorage × Number of nodes

  > **Note**
  >
  > The quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications and the number of nodes.
  >
  > - dbInstanceClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  > - dbInstanceClass.mem: the memory capacity of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  > - DBInstanceStorage: the storage capacity of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  > - By default, the number of nodes is 2.

- **Enterprise Edition**

  - CPU quota usage = dbInstanceClass.cpu × Number of regular nodes + Fixed CPU overhead of replica nodes

  - Memory quota usage = dbInstanceClass.mem × Number of regular nodes + Fixed memory overhead of replica nodes

  - Disk quota usage = DBInstanceStorage × Number of regular nodes + Fixed storage overhead of replica nodes

  > **Note**
  >
  > - The CPU quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications, the number of regular nodes, and the fixed resource overhead of replica nodes.
  >
  >   - dbInstanceClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  >   - By default, the number of regular nodes is 2.
  >
  >   - The CPU overhead of replica nodes is fixed to 2 GiB.
  >
  > - The memory quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications, number of regular nodes, and fixed resource overhead of replica nodes.
  >
  >   - dbInstanceClass.mem: the memory capacity of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  >   - By default, the number of regular nodes is 2.
  >
  >   - The memory overhead of replica nodes is fixed to 4 GiB.
  >
  > - The disk quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications, number of regular nodes, and fixed resource overhead of replica nodes.
  >
  >   - DBInstanceStorage: the storage capacity of the selected instance specifications.
  >
  >   - By default, the number of regular nodes is 2.
  >
  >   - The storage overhead of replica nodes is fixed to 50 GiB.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note**
>
> - ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instances and PolarDB for MySQL clusters that use local disks share the inventory.
>
> - Shared ApsaraDB RDS instances share physical resources with each other without being limited by the physical inventory. The shared physical resources include the memory capacity and CPU cores. Therefore, the physical inventory of the memory capacity and CPU cores may not indicate the saleable memory capacity and CPU cores. The saleable memory capacity and CPU cores may be greater than the physical inventory.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-5"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.4.5. Tair (Redis OSS-compatible)

This topic describes the quota that you can configure for Tair (Redis OSS-compatible), calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quota**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that can be configured for Tair (Redis OSS-compatible). |

**Calculation method of quota usage**

- **Standard Edition (Master-replica)**

  Memory usage = instanceClass.mem × Number of replicas

  > **Note**
  >
  > The preceding formula is used to calculate the memory usage of a standard instance.
  >
  > - instanceClass.mem indicates the memory size that is defined in the instance type.
  >
  > - The number of replicas is fixed to 2.

- **Cluster Edition**

  Memory usage = instanceClass.mem × Number of replicas + Proxy node overhead + CS node overhead

  > **Note**
  >
  > The preceding formula is used to calculate the memory usage of a cluster instance.
  >
  > - instanceClass.mem indicates the memory size that is defined in the instance type.
  >
  > - The number of replicas is fixed to 2.
  >
  > - You can calculate the corresponding proxy node overhead based on the number of proxy nodes. You can obtain the number of proxy nodes by checking the number before "proxy" in the InstanceClass field. For example, if an instance is of the redis.logic.sharding.8g.8db.0rodb.8proxy.default class, the number of proxy nodes of the instance is 8.
  >
  > - The CS node overhead is fixed to 1 GiB.

- **Read/write Splitting**

  Memory usage = instanceClass.mem × (2 + Number of read-only nodes) + Proxy node overhead + CS node overhead

  > **Note**
  >
  > The preceding formula is used to calculate the memory usage of a read/write splitting instance.
  >
  > - instanceClass.mem indicates the memory size that is defined in the instance type.
  >
  > - You can select one or three read-only nodes when you select a node type.
  >
  > - You can calculate the corresponding proxy node overhead based on the number of proxy nodes. You can obtain the number of proxy nodes by checking the number before "proxy" in the InstanceClass field. For example, if an instance is of the redis.logic.sharding.8g.8db.0rodb.8proxy.default class, the number of proxy nodes of the instance is 8.
  >
  > - The CS node overhead is fixed to 1 GiB.

The following table describes the relationships between the number of proxy nodes and the proxy node overhead.

| Number of proxy nodes | Proxy node overhead |
| --- | --- |
| 4 | 20 GiB |
| 6 | 30 GiB |
| 8 | 40 GiB |
| 12 | 40 GiB |
| 16 | 60 GiB |
| 24 | 80 GiB |
| 32 | 120 GiB |
| 48 | 180 GiB |
| 64 | 240 GiB |
| 96 | 320 GiB |
| 128 | 480 GiB |
| 192 | 480 GiB |
| 256 | 480 GiB |
| 384 | 960 GiB |
| 512 | 1,280 GiB |
| 768 | 1,920 GiB |
| 1024 | 2,560 GiB |

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note**
>
> The memory of a shared Tair (Redis OSS-compatible) instance can be shared. The shared Tair (Redis OSS-compatible) instance shares physical resources with other shared Tair (Redis OSS-compatible) instances without being limited by the physical inventory. Therefore, the physical inventory data of the memory size may not indicate the saleable memory size. The saleable memory size may be greater than the physical inventory.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-6"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.4.6. PolarDB

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for PolarDB, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that can be configured for PolarDB. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total size of memory that can be configured for PolarDB. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that can be configured for PolarDB. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

- CPU quota usage = DBNodeClass.cpu × DBNodeNum + CPU overhead of hot standby storage clusters + CPU overhead of PolarProxy

- Memory quota usage = DBNodeClass.mem × DBNodeNum + Memory overhead of hot standby storage clusters + Memory overhead of PolarProxy

- Disk quota usage = StorageSpace + Disk overhead of hot standby storage clusters

> **Note**
>
> - DBNodeClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores defined in the selected node specifications.
>
> - DBNodeNum: the number of selected nodes. If you select **1 Read/Write + 1 Read-only**, the number of nodes is 2. If you select **1 Read/Write**, the number of nodes is 1.
>
> - DBNodeClass.mem: the memory size defined in the selected node specifications.
>
> - StorageSpace: the size of the selected storage space.
>
> - CPU overhead of hot standby storage clusters: You can enable or disable the hot standby storage cluster feature.
>
>   - If the hot standby storage cluster feature is disabled, the CPU overhead of hot standby storage clusters is 0.
>
>   - If the hot standby storage cluster feature is enabled, the CPU overhead is equal to the number of CPU cores defined in the selected node specifications.
>
> - CPU overhead of PolarProxy: You can enable or disable the PolarProxy feature.
>
>   - If the PolarProxy feature is disabled, the CPU overhead of PolarProxy is 0.
>
>   - If the PolarProxy feature is enabled, the CPU overhead is calculated based on the following formulas:
>
>     - MySQL and PostgreSQL: CPU overhead of PolarProxy = Number of CPU cores defined in the selected cluster specifications.
>
>     - Oracle: CPU overhead of PolarProxy = Number of CPU cores defined in the selected cluster specifications × 2. By default, two replicas are used.
>
> - Memory overhead of hot standby storage clusters: You can enable or disable the hot standby storage cluster feature.
>
>   - If the hot standby storage cluster feature is disabled, the memory overhead of hot standby storage clusters is 0.
>
>   - If the hot standby storage cluster feature is enabled, the memory overhead is equal to the memory size defined in the selected node specifications.
>
> - Memory overhead of PolarProxy: You can enable or disable the PolarProxy feature.
>
>   - If the PolarProxy feature is disabled, the memory overhead of PolarProxy is 0.
>
>   - If the PolarProxy feature is enabled, the memory overhead is calculated based on the following formulas:
>
>     - MySQL and PostgreSQL: Memory overhead of PolarProxy = 4 GiB. This is a fixed value.
>
>     - Oracle: Memory overhead of PolarProxy = Memory size defined in the selected cluster specifications × 2. By default, two replicas are used.
>
> - Disk overhead of hot standby storage clusters: You can enable or disable the hot standby storage cluster feature.
>
>   - If the hot standby storage cluster feature is disabled, the disk overhead of hot standby storage clusters is 0.
>
>   - If the hot standby storage cluster feature is enabled, the disk overhead is equal to the size of the selected storage space.

**Inventory source**

No inventory is involved. By default, the inventory is unlimited.

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-7"></a>

| Synchronization Tasks(Units) | The total number of synchronization tasks that can be created for DTS. |
| Subscription Tasks(Units) | The total number of change tracking tasks that can be created for DTS. |

**Calculation method of quota usage**

- Migration task usage = Number of migration tasks that are created for DTS

- Synchronization task usage = Number of synchronization tasks that are created for DTS

- Change tracking task usage = Number of change tracking tasks that are created for DTS

> **Note**

**Inventory source**

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-4-8"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.4.8. Lindorm

This topic describes the quota that you can configure for Lindorm, the calculation method of quota usage, and the inventory source.

**Quota**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total disk capacity that can be configured for Lindorm. |

**Calculation method of quota usage**

Disk usage = (Number of replicas × Disk capacity × Number of disks × Capacity threshold)/3

> **Note**
>
> The default capacity threshold is 0.9.

**Inventory source**

No inventory is involved. By default, the inventory is unlimited.

| --- | --- |

| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total capacity of disks that can be configured for MaxCompute. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

- CU quota usage = Number of CUs that are configured for the current instance

- Disk quota usage = Used disk capacity of the current instance

> **Note**
>
> - The CU quota usage of the current instance is equal to the number of CUs that are configured for the current instance.
>

**Inventory source**

<a id="section-7-1-3-1-5-2"></a>

###### 7.1.3.1.5.2. Elasticsearch on Kubernetes

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that can be configured for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total size of memory that can be configured for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that can be configured for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

Elasticsearch on Kubernetes includes the following types of nodes: data node, Kibana node, dedicated master node, and client node. The CPU and memory quota usage is calculated based on the number of nodes and specification-based overhead. The disk quota usage is calculated based on the number of nodes and the storage capacity of nodes.

- CPU or memory quota usage = nodeSpec.spec × nodeAmount + kibanaConfiguration.spec × kibanaConfiguration.amount + masterConfiguration.spec × masterConfiguration.amount + clientNodeConfiguration.spec × clientNodeConfiguration.amout

- Disk quota usage = nodeSpec.disk × nodeAmount + kibanaConfiguration.disk × kibanaConfiguration.amount + masterConfiguration.disk × masterConfiguration.amount + clientNodeConfiguration.disk × clientNodeConfiguration.amout

> **Note**
>
> - The specifications of a node include the number of CPU cores and the memory size. The number of CPU cores is used to calculate the CPU quota usage and the memory size is used to calculate the memory quota usage.
>
> - nodeSpec.spec: the selected data node specifications.
>
> - nodeAmount: the number of data nodes.
>
> - kibanaConfiguration.spec: the selected Kibana node specifications.
>
> - kibanaConfiguration.amount: the number of Kibana nodes.
>
> - masterConfiguration.spec: the selected dedicated master node specifications.
>
> - masterConfiguration.amount: the number of dedicated master nodes.
>
> - clientNodeConfiguration.spec: the selected client node specifications.
>
> - clientNodeConfiguration.amout: the number of client nodes.
>
> - nodeSpec.disk: the storage capacity of the selected data node specifications.
>
> - kibanaConfiguration.disk: the storage capacity of the selected Kibana node specifications.
>
> - masterConfiguration.disk: the storage capacity of the selected dedicated master node specifications.
>
> - clientNodeConfiguration.disk: the storage capacity of the selected client node specifications.

**Inventory source**

No inventory is involved. By default, the inventory is unlimited.

#### 7.1.3.3. Manage quotas

##### 7.1.3.3.1. Service resources

<a id="section-7-1-3-3-1-1"></a>

###### 7.1.3.3.1.1. Cloud services supported by multi-cloud quotas

In a multi-cloud scenario, operations managers can manage resource quotas for subordinate clouds from the central cloud.

> **Important**
>
> - When you set quotas by resource pool in the central cloud console, you can only configure quotas for bound level-1 organizations in the subordinate cloud. After setting subordinate cloud quotas, the system updates them to the subordinate cloud. To manage resource set quotas for the subordinate cloud, you must configure them in the subordinate cloud console.
>
> - When you set quotas in the subordinate cloud console, it includes quotas for managed level-1 organizations. After the subordinate cloud updates level-1 organization quotas, the central cloud displays them in real time.

**Cloud services with quota support in Apsara Stack**

When the subordinate cloud is Apsara Stack, the supported cloud services for quota configuration include all cloud services that support quotas in that Apsara Stack.

**Cloud services with quota support in Alibaba Public Cloud**

When the subordinate cloud is Alibaba Public Cloud, the supported cloud services for quota configuration are as follows.

> **Note**
>
> The quota usage for instance count is calculated based on the actual number of instances used. The quota usage for CPU, memory, disk, and other resources is calculated by summing the corresponding fields returned by the API.

**Compute**

| Cloud service | Quota item |
| --- | --- |
| Elastic Compute Service (ECS) | Disk quota, basic disk, ultra disk, shared ultra disk, shared SSD, cloud SSD, I/O-intensive local disk, throughput-intensive local disk, local disk, local SSD, ESSD, high-performance disk, standard performance disk, ESSD AutoPL, ESSD Entry, elastic ephemeral disk - standard edition, custom image quota, CPU quota, security group quota, GPU quota, elastic network interface quota, memory quota |

**Containers**

| Cloud service | Quota item |
| --- | --- |
| Container Registry | Instance count |
| Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) | Cluster |

**Storage**

| --- | --- |
| File Storage NAS | Instance count |
| Tablestore | Instance count |
| Object Storage Service (OSS) | Instance count |

**Network**

| --- | --- |
| Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) | VPC quota |
| Server Load Balancer (SLB) | Server certificate, public IP address quota, internal IP quota - VPC network, SLB instance count |
| Elastic IP Address (EIP) | EIP bandwidth, EIP quota |
| NAT Gateway | Instance count |
| Private Line Gateway | Instance count |
| Application Load Balancer (ALB) | ALB instance |
| Alibaba Cloud DNS | Instance count |

| ApsaraMQ for Kafka | Disk quota, instance count |

| Realtime Compute for Apache Flink | Memory quota, CPU quota |
| Hologres | CPU quota |

**Development tools**

| Cloud service | Quota item |
| --- | --- |
| API Gateway (legacy) | Instance count |

<a id="section-7-1-3-3-1-2"></a>

###### 7.1.3.3.1.2. Cloud services that support group quota configuration

This topic describes the rules for group quota configuration and the cloud services that support group quota configuration.

**Configuration rules**

Group quotas are configured top-down. A parent organization must have a quota configured before you can configure quotas for its subordinate organizations.

- A group quota must be configured before individual quotas can be configured within that group.

- You can configure a group quota for a subordinate organization only after the parent organization has its group quota configured.

- You can configure individual quotas within a group for a subordinate organization only after the parent organization has its corresponding group quota and individual quotas configured.

- A group quota must be greater than or equal to the sum of its configured individual quotas.

This example demonstrates disk quota configuration for Elastic Compute Service (ECS). In this example, Organization B is subordinate to Organization A.

- If no disk quota is configured for Organization A, you cannot configure individual quotas for SSDs, ultra disks, premium performance disks, or standard performance disks in Organization A.

- If no disk quota is configured for Organization A, you cannot configure a disk quota for Organization B.

- If no individual disk quotas are configured for SSDs, ultra disks, premium performance disks, or standard performance disks in Organization A, you cannot configure corresponding quotas in Organization B.

- When you configure individual disk quotas in Organization A, the sum of the quotas for SSDs, ultra disks, premium performance disks, and standard performance disks cannot exceed the total configured disk quota of Organization A.

**Supported cloud services**

Only ECS supports group quotas, specifically for disks.

    <th>Parent resource item</th>
    <th>Child resource item</th>
  </tr>

  </tr>
