<a id="section-7-1-3-3-1-3"></a>

###### 7.1.3.3.1.3. Cloud services that support category quota configuration

This topic describes the rules for category quota configuration and the cloud services that support category quota configuration.

**Configuration rules**

Category quotas are configured top-down. A parent organization must have a quota configured before you can configure quotas for its subordinate organizations. You can configure individual quotas within a category for a subordinate organization only after the parent organization has its corresponding category quota and individual quotas configured.

This example demonstrates category quota configuration for Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP). In this example, Organization B is subordinate to Organization A. If no quotas are configured for basic intelligent computing clusters such as machineA and machineB in Organization A, you cannot configure quotas for the corresponding clusters in Organization B.

**Supported cloud services**

Only Elastic Compute Service (ECS) and BMCP support category quota configuration.

**ECS**

| Parent resource item | Child resource item |
| --- | --- |
| Instance type | Specifications supported by the instance type. Example: ecs.sn2ne.xlarge. |

**BMCP**

| Parent resource item | Child resource item |
| --- | --- |
| High-performance Network Cluster | Specifications supported for a high-performance network cluster. |
| Managed Cluster | Specifications supported for a managed cluster. |
| High-performance Computing Network Cluster | Specifications supported for a high-performance computing network cluster. |
| Basic Cluster | Specifications supported for a basic cluster. |

<a id="section-7-1-3-3-1-4"></a>

###### 7.1.3.3.1.4. Cloud services that support zone-level resource quotas

This topic describes the cloud services that support zone-level resource quotas.

When you configure a resource quota, you can select a zone. If you select all zones, you can configure resource quotas at the region level. If you select a zone, you can configure resource quotas for the zone, and the console displays only cloud services in the current zone.

**Supported cloud services**

Currently, cloud services that support zone-level resource quotas include Elastic Compute Service (ECS) and File Storage NAS (NAS).

| Cloud service | Resource item |
| --- | --- |
| ECS | Disk quota, SSD, ultra disk, premium performance disk, standard performance disk, memory quota, CPU quota, GPU quota, Elastic Network Interface (ENI) quota, and specification quota. |
| NAS | NAS usage, performance disk capacity, capacity disk capacity, and NAS quota. |

<a id="section-7-1-3-3-1-5"></a>

###### 7.1.3.3.1.5. Set or modify quotas for a single cloud service

Resources in a resource pool are limited. You must restrict the number of resources for each organization based on its scope of responsibilities. Quota management allows you to set or modify quotas for each cloud service in organizations and resource sets.

**Prerequisites**

- Before setting quotas, ensure that the platform administrator (super) has completed the resource pool configuration. For more information, see Resource pool configuration.

- By default, the operations administrator and organization administrator can perform this operation. Users with custom roles require the Operate Quotas permission under Quota Management, as well as the Quota Management > Quota Management menu permission.

**Limits**

- You must set the quota of the parent organization before setting the quota of a subordinate organization. Quotas must be allocated level by level. Skipping levels is not allowed.

- Quotas support two settings: limited and unlimited. If a quota is not explicitly set, it defaults to unlimited, allowing an organization to use all available quota from its parent organization. Resource sets and subordinate organizations under the same organization share the quota of that organization.

- When you set group quotas, the general rule is that you cannot set a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is set. For the specific cloud services that support group quotas, see Cloud services that support group quota configuration.

  - You can set quota items within a group only after the group quota item is set.

  - You can set the group quota item of a subordinate organization only after the group quota item of the parent organization is set.

  - You can set quota items within a group of a subordinate organization only after the quota items within the group of the parent organization are set.

  - The group quota value must be greater than or equal to the sum of the configured values of quota items within the group.

- When setting category quotas, the general rule is that you cannot set a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is set. You can set category quota items of a subordinate organization only after the category quota items of the parent organization are set. For the specific cloud services that support category quotas, see Cloud services that support category quota configuration.

- The operations administrator can set quotas for all organizations and resource sets.

- The organization administrator can set quotas for subordinate organizations, including resource set quotas. Setting a quota for the current organization is treated as a quota application to the parent organization. The application takes effect after approval.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top menu bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quotas**.

4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.

5. Above the organization structure on the left side of the page, select a resource pool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

6. Above the product list on the right side, set the region and zone, and select Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - If you select All Zones, you can configure quotas at the region level. If you select a zone, you can configure quotas for the zone, and the console displays only cloud services in the current zone.
   >
   > - If you select **View Only Cloud Services That Have Triggered Alerts**, only the cloud services that trigger alerts are displayed.

7. In the left-side organization structure of the Quotas page, select the organization or resource set whose resources you want to manage.

8. Click the target service (ECS in this example) to open the Quota Details panel. For more information about the resource quotas of each cloud service, see Products that support resource quotas.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7a76c0827ab67abb8169605fe4d92923.jpeg)

9. In the Quota Details panel, configure the quotas.

   - To set quotas for a subordinate organization or resource set, click **Set Quota** or **Modify Quota**.

   - To set a quota for the current organization, click **Apply for Quota**.

0. In the **Quota** column, set the quotas for the resource items related to the cloud service.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Quota**: If you do not enter a quota in the column that corresponds to a resource item, the quota of the resource item is unlimited.
   >
   > - **Existing Quota**: This column displays the existing quotas of resource items.
   >
   > - **Quota Change**: This column displays the difference between the configured quota and the original quota.
   >
   > - Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ef973f531e2a5b3234fafdcc7a2a1e65.png" width="8" alt=""> before a resource item to display the child resource items of the resource
   >
   >   item.
   >

The system does not limit the overhead of the corresponding resources in the current organization or resource set. The quotas of the parent organization to which the current organization or resource set belongs are used for verification and calculation.

###### 7.1.3.3.1.6. Set quotas in batches

The quota management feature allows you to set quotas for multiple cloud services in batches.

**Prerequisites**

- Before you set quotas, make sure that the platform administrator (super) has configured the resource pool. For more information, see the **Resource pool configuration** section.

- By default, only operations administrators and organization administrators can perform this operation. Users with custom roles must have the Operate Quotas permission under Quota Management and the Quotas > Quotas menu permission.

**Limits**

- You must set the quotas for a parent organization first before configuring quotas for its subordinate organizations. You can allocate quotas only hierarchically and cannot skip levels.

- Quotas support two modes: limited and unlimited. If you do not set a quota, the quota is unlimited, and the organization can consume all available quotas of its parent organization. Resource sets and subordinate organizations under the same organization share the quota of that organization.

- When you configure group quotas, the general rule is that you cannot configure a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is configured. For the specific cloud services that support group quotas, see Cloud services that support group quota configuration.

  - You can configure quota items within a group only after configuring the group quota item.

  - You can configure a subordinate group quota item only after configuring the parent group quota item.

  - You can configure a subordinate quota item within a group only after configuring the parent quota item within the group.

  - The group quota value must be greater than or equal to the sum of all quota item values within the group.

- When you configure category quotas, the general rule is that you cannot configure a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is configured. You can configure a subordinate quota item within a category only after configuring the parent quota item within the category. For the specific cloud services that support category quotas, see Cloud services that support category quota configuration.

- Operations administrators can set quotas for all organizations and resource sets.

- Organization administrators can set quotas for subordinate organizations, including resource set quotas. Setting a quota for the current organization is equivalent to applying for a quota from the parent organization. The application succeeds after approval.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Quotas** > **Quotas**.

4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.

5. Above the organization hierarchy on the left, select a resource pool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

6. Above the product list on the right, set the region, available zone, and the option to only view cloud services that trigger alerts.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - If you select **All Zones**, the system applies quota management at the region level. If you select a specific available zone, the system applies quota management at the available zone level and displays only the products in that zone.
   >
   > - Select **Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts** to quickly filter cloud services that have triggered alerts.

7. In the organization hierarchy on the left, click the target organization or resource set.

8. Set quotas in batches.

   - To set quotas for a subordinate organization or resource set, click **Configure Quotas**.

   - To set quotas for the current organization, click **Apply for Quotas in Batches**.

9. In the **Configure Quotas**/**Apply for Quotas in Batches** panel, click **Add Service**.

###### 7.1.3.3.1.7. View quotas

The quota management feature allows you to view quotas.

**Prerequisites**

By default, operations administrators, resource auditors, organization administrators, organization resource auditors, and resource set administrators can perform this operation. Users with custom roles require the View Quotas permission under Quota Mangement and the Quotas > Quotas menu permission.

**Limits**

- Operations administrators and resource auditors can view the quotas of all organizations and resource sets.

- Organization administrators and organization resource auditors can view the quotas of their own organizations and subordinate organizations, including resource set quotas.

- Resource set administrators can view only the quotas of their own resource sets.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Quotas** > **Quotas**.

4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.

5. Above the organization hierarchy on the left, select a resource pool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

6. Above the products on the right, set the region, availability zone, and the option to only view cloud services that trigger alerts.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - When you select **All Zones**, the system applies quota management at the region level. When you select a specific availability zone, the system applies quota management at the availability zone level and displays only the products in that zone.
   >
   > - Select **Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts** to quickly filter cloud services that have triggered alerts.

7. In the organization hierarchy on the left, click the target organization or resource set.

8. Click the target product, such as Elastic Compute Service, to open the quota details panel and view the quota details of the cloud service for the organization or resource set.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/68b1792d61b2c2c35dff47dbc9f6bb28.jpeg)

###### 7.1.3.3.1.8. Clear quotas

After clearing quotas, the system stops validating resource quotas for cloud services in the current organization or resource set. However, it still traverses up the hierarchy to find quotas of the parent organization that has an affiliation with the current organization or resource set for validation.

**Prerequisites**

- Before you clear quotas, make sure that no quotas exist for any subordinate organizations or resource sets under the target organization.

- By default, only operations administrators and organization administrators can perform this operation. Users with custom roles must have the Operate Quotas permission under Quota Management and the Quotas > Quotas menu permission.

**Limits**

- Operations administrators can clear quotas for all organizations and resource sets.

- Organization administrators can clear quotas only for subordinate organizations, including resource sets.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Quotas** > **Quotas**.

4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.

5. Above the organization hierarchy on the left, select a resource pool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

6. Above the product list on the right, set the region, availability zone, and the option to view only cloud services that have triggered alerts.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - If you select **All Zones**, the system applies quota management at the region level. If you select a specific availability zone, the system applies quota management at the availability zone level and displays only the products in that availability zone.
   >
   > - Select **View Only Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts** to quickly filter cloud services that have triggered alerts.

7. In the organization hierarchy on the left, click the target organization or resource set.

8. Click the target service, such as Elastic Compute Service (ECS), to open the quota details panel and view the quota details of the cloud service for the organization or resource set.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/68b1792d61b2c2c35dff47dbc9f6bb28.jpeg)

9. In the quota details panel, click **Clear Quota** at the bottom.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When clearing quotas for a specific availability zone, you can use the **Synchronously Clear Quotas in Other Zones** switch to control quotas in other availability zones.

0. In the **Reset Quota** dialog box, click **OK**.

- An organization administrator can create alert rules only for the organization that is managed by the organization administrator and its subordinate organizations, including alert rules for quotas of resource sets.

<a id="section-7-1-3-3-1-10"></a>

###### 7.1.3.3.1.10. Configure a quota template

This topic describes how to configure a quota template for the root organization or level-1 organizations. After a quota template is configured, subordinate organizations and resource sets can use the quota template to apply various quota configurations.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator or level-1 organization administrator role. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to configure quota templates and access the Quotas page in the Quotas module.

**Limits**

- An operations administrator can configure quota templates in the root organization and all level-1 organizations.

- A level-1 organization administrator can configure quota templates only in the current level-1 organization.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quotas**.

4. Click the **Service Resources** tab.

5. Above the organization structure on the left side of the page, select a resource pool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The resource pool drop-down list appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

6. In the upper-right corner of the Quotas page, configure the region and zone, and select Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - If you select All Zones, you can configure resource quotas at the region level. If you select a zone, you can configure resource quotas for the zone, and the console displays only cloud services in the current zone.
   >
   > - If you select **Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts**, only the cloud services that trigger alerts are displayed.

7. In the left-side organization structure, click the root organization or a level-1 organization.

8. In the upper-right corner of the **Quotas** page, click **Quota Template Settings**.

9. In the **Quota Template Settings** panel, click **Create Template**.

0. In the **Create Template** dialog box, configure the **Cloud Service**, **Template Name**, and **Configuration Method** parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |

   | Template Name | The name of the template. |
   | Configurati on Method | The resource items of the selected cloud service are displayed. You can configure the resource items.<br>• <strong>Resource Type</strong>: displays the resource items of the selected cloud service.<br>• <strong>Type</strong>: Select <strong>Percentage</strong>, <strong>Number</strong>, or <strong>No</strong>.<br>Note<br>• If you set Type to Percentage, the quota of the resource item is set to a percentage of the remaining allocatable quota of the parent organization.<br>• If you set Type to Number, the quota of the resource item is set to the value in the template. If the quota is insufficient, it is automatically changed to the maximum allocatable quota.<br>• If you set Type to No, the resource item is not configured.<br>• <strong>Numerical Value</strong>: Specify a value based on the setting of the Type parameter.<br>• If you set Type to <strong>Percentage</strong>, specify a percentage in the <strong>Numerical Value</strong> column. Valid values: 0 to 100<br>• If you set Type to <strong>Number</strong>, specify a value in the <strong>Numerical Value</strong> column.The value must be greater than or equal to 0.<br>• If you set Type to <strong>No</strong>, <strong>No data found</strong> is displayed in the <strong>Numerical Value</strong> column by default. |

<a id="section-7-1-3-3-2"></a>

##### 7.1.3.3.2. AI service tokens

<a id="section-7-1-3-3-2-1"></a>

###### 7.1.3.3.2.1. Set quotas

On the AI Service Token tab, set quotas for organizations, resource sets, and services.

**Prerequisites**

- Before setting quotas, ensure that the platform administrator (super) has completed the resource pool configuration. For more information, see Resource pool configuration.

- By default, the operations administrator and organization administrator can perform this operation. Users with custom roles require the Operate Quotas permission under Quota Management, as well as the Quota Management > Quota Management menu permission.

**Limits**

- You must set the quota of a parent organization before setting the quota of a subordinate organization. Quotas must be allocated level by level. Skipping levels is not allowed.

- Quotas support two modes: limited and unlimited. If a quota is not explicitly set, it defaults to unlimited, allowing the organization to use all available quota from its parent organization. Resource sets and subordinate organizations under the same organization share the quota of that organization.

- Operations administrators can set quotas for all organizations and resource sets.

- Organization administrators can set quotas for subordinate organizations, including resource set quotas. When an organization administrator sets a quota for the current organization, the system treats this action as a quota application to the parent organization. The application takes effect after approval.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quotas**.

4. Click the **AI Service Token** tab.

5. In the upper part of the page, select a region and a zone.

6. Set the organization or resource set quota.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   In the organization structure on the left side, select an organization or a resource set.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When an operations administrator selects the root organization, the system displays the quota information of all organizations.

   </li>

   <li>

   Click **Set Quota** or **Modify Quota**.

   </li>

   <li>

   In the **Total Quota** field, enter the quota value.

   </li>

   </ol>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a499612315be8585398da809704861ff.jpeg)

   <ol type="i" start="4">

   <li>

   Click **Save**.

   </li>

   </ol>

7. Set service quotas and API key quotas.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   In the **Quota of Each Product** section, click a service card.

   </li>

   <li>

   Click **Set Quota** or **Modify Quota**.

   </li>

   </ol>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5e9610469e72a52f94b731450e184179.jpeg)

   <ol type="i" start="3">

   <li>

   In the row that contains the quota below the product, set the product quota.

   </li>

   <li>

   In the API Key Quota section, set quotas at the API key level.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can set API key quotas only when you select a resource set to configure quotas.

   </li>

   <li>

   Click **Save**.

   </li>

   </ol>

<a id="section-7-1-3-4"></a>

#### 7.1.3.4. Quota alert management

<a id="section-7-1-3-4-1"></a>

##### 7.1.3.4.1. Create a quota alert rule

The system provides a default alert rule for each product service. The rule is named after the product code, applies to all organizations and resource sets, and belongs to the root organization. You can create a new alert rule when the preset alert rule does not meet your requirements. Quota alerts support notifications. When the quota of an organization or resource set reaches the preset threshold, the system notifies the organization administrator or resource set administrator. The system sends the notification once a day upon the first trigger of each day.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the operations administrator or organization administrator.

**Limits**

- You cannot create a new alert rule for the current organization or resource set if an enabled alert rule already exists.

- A newly created alert rule takes effect immediately and disables all other alert rules within its effective scope.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the menu bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Quotas** > **Quota Alerts**.

4. On the **Quota Alerts** page, click **Create Alert Rule**.

5. In the **Create Alert Rule** dialog box, complete the configuration.

   **Configuration item**

   **Description**

   Select the resource pool where the current quota alert rule takes effect.

   **Resource**

   > **Note**

   **Pool**

   > The resource pool drop-down list appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

   **Rule Type**

   Select **Product Resources** or **AI Service Token**.

   **Organizatio**

   Select the organization or resource set where the current quota

   **n/Resource**

   alert rule takes effect.

   **Set**

   **Alert Rule Informatio**

   Enable or disable the option to include subordinate organizations.

   **n**

   When enabled, the effective scope of the alert rule covers the current organization and all subordinate organizations, as well as all resource sets within the scope. This option appears only when

   **Include**

   you select an organization for **Organization/Resource Set**.

   **Child Organizatio**

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/311770f555337aad46441b3426f7e219.png" width="30" alt=""> : Include subordinate organizations.

   **ns**

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c6a40de28b0f15d437aecb3b50b30787.png" width="29" alt=""> : Do not include subordinate organizations.

   **Region**

   Select the region where the current quota alert rule takes effect.

   Select the cloud service for which you want to create the alert rule.

   **Cloud**

   > **Important**

   **Service**

   > You can select only cloud services that have quotas in the current organization or resource set.

   **Alert Rule**

   Enter a name for the current quota alert rule.

   **Name**

   - **Used Amount**: The system triggers an alert when the used quota exceeds the configured alert threshold.

   **Alert Type**

   - **Remaining Available Quota**: The system triggers an alert when the remaining quota falls below the configured alert threshold.

   **Alert Informatio**

   - **Resource Type**: The default value is the resource item that

   **n**

   has a configured quota for the selected cloud service.

   - **Used Amount/Quota**: The default values are the used quota and the quota of the cloud service in the selected organization and resource set.

   **Alert**

   - **Threshold**: You can select **No**, **Percentage**, or **Number**.

   **Threshold**

   - **Alert Threshold**: Set the alert threshold value. The system generates an alert when the used quota exceeds the alert threshold or the remaining quota falls below the alert threshold. When you set **Threshold** to **No**, the default value for this item is **No Alerts**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7eee2d7ad644bd5685edffa8179e2c05.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-3-4-2"></a>

##### 7.1.3.4.2. Manage quota alert rules

If the quotas of cloud services are changed in an organization or a resource set, you can manage existing quota alert rules. Generated alerts are recorded. Operations staff can analyze the alert history to learn about the resource usage of organizations. This way, they can optimize the quota allocation and create quota alert rules.

**Limits**

- Preset quota alert rules cannot be modified or deleted.

- Only one quota alert rule can be enabled for a cloud service. If a quota alert rule is enabled for a cloud service, you must disable this rule before you can enable another quota alert rule for this cloud service.

- The quota alert rules that you can view in an organization or a resource set include all quota alert rules in the current organization or resource set and all quota alert rules with Include Child Organization enabled in the parent organization.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quota Alerts**.

4. Optional. Click **Advanced Filter**, configure filter conditions such as **Alert Rule Name**, **Cloud Platform**, **Organization/Resource Set**, **Region**, and **Cloud Service**, and then click **Search**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The Cloud Platform parameter is displayed only in multi-cloud environments.

5. Perform the operations that are described in the following table to manage quota alert rules.

   | Operation | Procedure |

   | Modify a quota alert rule | i. Find the quota alert rule that you want to modify and click <strong>Edit</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the <strong>Modify Quota Alert Rule</strong> dialog box, modify the configurations of the quota alert rule. The <strong>Cloud Platform</strong>, <strong>Organization/Resource Set</strong>, <strong>Region</strong>, and <strong>Cloud Service</strong> parameters cannot be modified.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |

You are navigated to the <strong>Quota</strong> <strong>Alert History</strong> page.<br>ii. On the <strong>Quota Alert History</strong> page, view the history of the quota alert rule.<br>Note<br>The quota alert history is updated every two hours. |
   | Enable a quota alert rule | i. Find a quota alert rule whose value in the <strong>Status</strong> column is <strong>Disable</strong>, move<br>the pointer over the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ba2a0fb5deb13c898e5101327b3cb122.png" width="21" alt="">icon in the <strong>Actions</strong> column, and then select<br><strong>Enable</strong>.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Disable a quota alert rule | i. Find a quota alert rule whose value in the <strong>Status</strong> column is <strong>Enable</strong>, move<br>the pointer over the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ba2a0fb5deb13c898e5101327b3cb122.png" width="21" alt="">icon in the <strong>Actions</strong> column, and then select<br><strong>Disable</strong>.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Delete a quota alert rule | i. Find the quota alert rule that you want to delete and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |

<a id="section-7-1-3-5"></a>

#### 7.1.3.5. View the quota alert history

If a quota reaches the specified alert threshold, alerts are generated. You can view the alerts to understand the resource quota usage and identify exceptions at the earliest opportunity.

   > **Note**
   >

6. Find the quota alert rule that you want to manage and click **Change Quota** in the **Actions** column.

8. Click **Save**.

You can configure the specification quotas for an instance to restrict the specifications that can be enabled or configured for the instance.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

> **Important**

### 7.1.4. Tag management

<a id="section-7-1-4-1"></a>

#### 7.1.4.1. Manage tags

Tags are used to classify and manage resources from different dimensions. You can add tags to cloud resources to manage the resources in a finer-grained and more intelligent manner.

**Background information**

- Each tag consists of a tag key and a tag value.

  - A tag key is the core identification part of a tag. It is used to define the resource category or describe resource attributes. In most cases, the tag key is a short and descriptive string. Each tag key added to a resource must be unique.

  - A tag value refers to the content that is associated with a tag key and provides more details of a resource.

- Administrators can define various types of tags based on business requirements and add multiple tag keys and corresponding tag values to cloud resources. This way, you can classify and retrieve resources from different dimensions. This helps you quickly find the resources that you require from a large amount of resources and facilitates cloud resource management.

**Limits**

- You can create at most 20 tags at a time and add the tags to resources.

- You can select at most 50 resource instances at a time when you add tags to resources.

**Create or select tags and add the tags to resources**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Tag**.

4. On the **Tag** page, click **Create or Select Tags and Add Them to Resources**.

5. In the **Create or Select Tags and Add Them to Resources** dialog box, configure parameters in the following steps as prompted.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   **Create or Select Tags**

   Select an existing tag key or create a tag key, enter a tag value in the **Tag Value** field, and then click **Next**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c667eb58fcb1a72d089ffe95ca77beee.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > In the Create or Select Tags step, you can create multiple tags at a time.
   >
   > - You can click **Add** to create or select more tags.
   >
   > - You can click the
   >
   >   icon that corresponds to a tag to delete or remove the tag.
   >
   >   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/36af23476a05b24b534d449f43592581.png" width="13" alt="">

   </li>

   <li>

   **Select a Resource**

   Select the organization and resource set to which the resources belong, region, and cloud services, and click **Next**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/63de7ef166e463388fb926d76d0e5231.jpeg)

   </li>

   <li>

   **Confirmation Information**

   Confirm the information about the tags and resources and click **Confirm**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c7d34815a4fa1a12524b020dd91eb2c8.jpeg)

   </li>

   </ol>

**View resources to which tags are added**

**Procedure**

1. In the left-side **Tag Key** pane of the **Tag** page, find the tag key that you want to view.

   You can click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/73968fccd35e2280a6caef89bd97c5e9.png" width="12" alt=""> icon next to Tag Key to specify filter conditions in the **Filter**

   **Conditions** dialog box. The filter conditions include the organization and resource set to which resources belong, the region in which resources reside, and keyword.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The number next to Tag Key indicates the total number of tag keys.
   >
   > - In the tag key list, the number next to each tag key indicates the number of tag values that correspond to the tag key.

2. Click the tag key that you want to view. In the right-side Tag Key section, view the tag values that correspond to the tag key and the cloud services to which the tag is added.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - In the right-side Tag Key section, you can click **Add Tag Value** to add one or more tag values to the tag key.
   >
   > - In the tag value list, you can view the number of cloud services to which each tag is added.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/25f9a922edeb1bd697e167841d13bcf6.jpeg)

3. View the resources to which a tag is added.

   Find the tag value that you want to view and click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b75e58997cc4665386ba55db1edc76e7.png" width="10" alt=""> icon next to the tag value to view

   the cloud services to which the tag is added.

   </li>

   to view the resources to which the tag is added. Alternatively, click **View Resources** in the **Actions** column of the tag value. In the panel that appears, select a cloud service to view the resources to which the tag is added.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can select multiple resource instances and click **Unbind Current Tags** or **Bind Multiple Tags** below the resource instance list to unbind the current tags from or bind other tags to the resource instances at a time.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/742384e3528ddf4634fd2a8183f87654.jpeg)

4. Optional. In the tag value list, find the tag value that you want to manage and click **Bind Resources** in the **Actions** column. In the panel that appears, select the resources to which you want to add the tag and click **Submit**.

<a id="section-7-1-4-2"></a>

#### 7.1.4.2. Policy library

A tag policy defines standardized tag rules to ensure that all tags added to resources meet unified requirements. The tag policy can be applied to organizations, resource sets, cloud services, or instances. It can define the valid tag keys and tag values.

<a id="section-7-1-4-2-1"></a>

##### 7.1.4.2.1. Create a tag policy

When creating a tag policy, you can restrict the effective scope of the policy by resource type, resource set, excluded resource ID, region, and tag scope.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operations administrator and organization administrator can perform this operation. Users with custom organization-scoped roles must have the Create Tag Policy permission under Tag Management and the Tag Management > Policy Library menu permission.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Tags** > **Policy Library**.

4. Click **Create Tag Policy**.

5. On the **Create Tag Policy** page, configure the tag policy.

     </tr>
   </table>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/49d75b24ce8ce493f00e615cbb6ecefd.jpeg)

6. Click **Create**.

<a id="section-7-1-4-2-2"></a>

##### 7.1.4.2.2. View tag policies

On the Policy Library page, you can view tag policies and the details of each tag policy.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a resource auditor, an organization administrator, or an organization resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to view tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.

4. View information about existing tag policies. You can quickly search for tag policies by organization, policy ID, policy name, and tag key.

5. Find the tag policy that you want to view and click its name or **Details** in the **Actions** column to go to the policy details page. Then, view the details of the tag policy.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/36909d86d13c5aa1a7c8f99deeee3aa5.jpeg)

6. Optional. Click **View Effective Policy and Check Tasks** on the details page of the tag policy to go to the details page of the effective policy. You can perform this step if the tag policy is enabled. For more information, see Effective policies.

<a id="section-7-1-4-2-3"></a>

##### 7.1.4.2.3. Edit a tag policy

You can modify a tag policy when the policy changes.

**Prerequisites**

- The tag policy is in the **Disabled** status.

- By default, only the operations administrators and organization administrators can perform this operation. Users with custom organization-scoped roles require the Edit and Delete Tag Policies permission under Tag Management and the Tags > Policy Library menu permission.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Tags** > **Policy Library**.

4. In the list, click **Modify** in the **Actions** column of the target policy.

5. On the **Modify Tag Policy** page, update the policy configuration. For more information on the configuration items, see Create a tag policy.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5f4c55c3631c282aac566ee82db5abc1.jpeg)

6. Click **Modify**.

<a id="section-7-1-4-2-4"></a>

##### 7.1.4.2.4. Enable a tag policy

After a disabled tag policy is enabled, the system checks the compliance of resource tags and automatically executes related rules based on the tag policy. When you enable a tag policy, the effective policy with the same policy type and tag key as the tag policy is updated. If no such effective policy exists in the current organization, a new effective policy is created.

**Prerequisites**

- The tag policy is in the **Paused** state.

- You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to modify and delete tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.

4. On the Policy Library page, find the tag policy that you want to enable and click **Enable** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9a855942ecc7772f3e27d7bf8a28ed62.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > After you enable a tag policy, the tag policy applies to resources within the specified scope.
   >
   > - The tag configured in the tag policy is automatically added to new resources after they are created.
   >
   > - The tag configured in the tag policy is automatically added to existing resources.

<a id="section-7-1-4-2-5"></a>

##### 7.1.4.2.5. Disable a tag policy

After an enabled tag policy is disabled, the system no longer checks the compliance of resource tags or automatically executes related rules based on the tag policy. When you disable a tag policy, the effective policy with the same policy type and tag key as the tag policy is updated. If the tag policy is the only one associated with the effective policy, the effective policy is deleted after the tag policy is disabled.

**Prerequisites**

- The tag policy is in the **Enabled** state.

- You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to modify and delete tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.

4. On the Policy Library page, find the tag policy that you want to disable and click **Disable** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9a855942ecc7772f3e27d7bf8a28ed62.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-4-2-6"></a>

##### 7.1.4.2.6. Delete a tag policy

You can delete tag policies that you no longer require.

**Prerequisites**

- The tag policy is in the **Paused** state.

- You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to modify and delete tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.

4. On the Policy Library page, find the tag policy that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9a855942ecc7772f3e27d7bf8a28ed62.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-4-3"></a>

#### 7.1.4.3. Effective policies

An effective policy is obtained by aggregating multiple tag policies.

<a id="section-7-1-4-3-1"></a>

##### 7.1.4.3.1. View effective policies

After tag policies are enabled, they are aggregated by tag key and policy type and displayed on the Effective Policy page. If multiple tag policies of the same policy type share a tag key, the effective scope of the effective policy depends on the order in which the tag policies are enabled. If the effective scopes of the tag policies conflict, the effective scope of the earliest enabled tag policy prevails.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a resource auditor, an organization administrator, or an organization resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to view effective policies and access the Effective Policy page in the Tags module.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Effective Policy**.

4. View effective policies on the Effective Policy page. You can quickly search for effective policies by tag key and policy type.

5. Find the effective policy that you want to view and click **Details** in the **Actions** column to go to the details page of the effective policy. Then, view the details of the effective policy.

   - **Basic Information**: View the basic information about the tag policy whose binding order is 1.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/573642983cd1cdcda30628d6cb65cfa3.jpeg)

   - **Relevant Policies**: On the **Relevant Policies** tab, view the information about the tag policies that are associated with the effective policy in the following columns: **Policy ID**, **Policy Name**, **Binding Order**, and **Bound At**.

     > **Note**
     >
     > - You can find the tag policy that you want to view and click its ID or **Details** in the **Actions** column to go to the details page of the tag policy.
     >
     > - You can find the tag policy that you want to modify and click **Modify** in the **Actions** column to go to the **Modify Tag Policy** page. On the Modify Tag Policy page, you can update the tag policy.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/87cb65d948e2d19d365da84200cf5bde.jpeg)

   - **Detection Results**: On the **Detection Results** tab, view the detection results and fix tags of non-compliant resources. You can view the detection results in the following sections: **Detected Resources**, **Compliant Resources**, **Non-compliant Resources**, **Inapplicable Resources**, and **Non-compliant Resources/Percentage**.

     > **Note**
     >
     > - **Compliant**: The specified tag keys are added to the resources and resource sets to which the resources belong.
     >
     > - **Non-compliant**: The specified tag keys are not added to the resources. Tags of non-compliant resources can be manually fixed. For more information, see Manage effective policies.
     >
     > - **Inapplicable**: The specified tag keys are not added to the resource sets to which the resources belong. For example, the specified tags are removed from a resource set.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f3048354ffc1d8dd069d5c0e3c8f65a0.jpeg)

   - **Fix Records**: On the **Fix Records** tab, view the details of the automatic fix records.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0c06729b3e598aa37ec6e0a94a59c3f5.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-1-4-3-2"></a>

##### 7.1.4.3.2. Manage effective policies

You can manually fix the tags of non-compliant resources.

**Prerequisites**

- Resources are in the **Non-compliance** state.

- You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to manage effective policies and access the Effective Policy page in the Tags module.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Effective Policy**.

4. On the Effective Policy page, find the effective policy that you want to manage and click **Details** in the **Actions** column.

5. On the details page of the effective policy, click the **Detection Results** tab. On the Detection Results tab, manually fix non-compliant resources in the **Fix Non-compliant Resources** section. You can select **Non-compliance** from the Compliance Status drop-down list to search for non-compliant resources.

   | Operat ion | Procedure |
   | --- | --- |
   | Fix the tags of a single non-compli ant resour ce | i. Find the non-compliant resource whose tags you want to fix and click <strong>Fix</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the <strong>Fix Tags</strong> dialog box, enter a new tag value in the tag value field and click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f93c3c67be145fda4eb55a82f7b652c5.jpeg)<br>iii. After the resource tags are fixed, click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c24eb8114425c6330ca87b09bbe924de.jpeg) |
   | Fix the tags of multipl e resour ces at a time | i. In the resource list, select multiple non-compliant resources.<br>ii. Click <strong>Batch Fix</strong> below the resource list.<br>iii. In the <strong>Fix Tags</strong> dialog box, enter a new tag value in the tag value field and click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/be9cb7a3b2c46dd9fb785b6bda74286e.jpeg)<br>iv. After the resource tags are fixed, click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c69b2de331d914920c9cc08400673dc6.jpeg) |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f3048354ffc1d8dd069d5c0e3c8f65a0.jpeg)

### 7.1.5. Metering management

<a id="section-7-1-5-1"></a>

#### 7.1.5.1. Metering configuration management

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-1"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.1. Create a metering table

This topic describes how to create a metering table for a cloud service. You can customize metering rules and metering fields in a metering table to generate new metering data in order to meet operations needs.

**Prerequisites**

- The switch controlling metering table creation is turned on. Contact O&M personnel if you need to turn on this switch.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Then, click the card of the resource to go to metering configuration details page.

6. On the **Metering table** tab, click **Create Metering Table**.

7. In the **Create Metering Table** panel, configure the metering parameters.

The type of the metering field. Valid values: **Value** or **Text**.

Specify whether the metering field is required. Valid values: **Optional** and **Required**. This parameter is set to Required for all predefined

**Required**

metering fields. This parameter is set to Optional for custom metering fields and cannot be changed.

This parameter is required when you set the Type parameter to **Value**.

You can choose the following metering units: vCPU, CU, LCU, KB, MB,

**Metering**

GB, GiB, TB, Kbps, Mbps, tps, qps, Topic, Token, Cores, GPUs, GPU-

**Informati**

**Unit**

hours, GB-hours, and Sets.

**on**

The type of source parameters of the metering rule. Valid values: **Value** and **Text**.

**Source**

- If the Type parameter is set to **Value**, you can set the Source

**Parameter**

Parameter Type parameter to **Value** or **Text**.

**Type**

- If the Type parameter is set to **Text**, you can set the Source Parameter Type parameter only to **Text**.

- When the Source Parameter Type parameter is set to **Value**:

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0ad99253ee1dff6eefa39b4a8ce79acd.jpeg)

**Metering Rule**

- **Rules**: Select a rule from the drop-down list. You can select **Maximum Value (max)**, **Minimum Value (min)**, **Average Value (avg)**, or **Sum (sum)**.

  You can click**Add Condition** to add a condition, which functions as a counting rule. The condition consists of the parameter, calculation method, and value.

  - Parameter: You can select only numeric parameters.

  - Calculation method: You can select **Add**, **Minus**, **Multiply**, **Divide**, **Floor Division**, or **Ceiling Division**.

  - Value: The value field is displayed only after you select a calculation method. You can enter only numbers. Decimals are supported.

- **Expression**: An expression is generated based on the counting

**Rules**

rule. The expression consists of a function and the counting rule.

- **Value Rule**: You can select **Maximum Value (max)**, **Minimum Value (min)**, **Average Value (avg)**, **Sum (sum)**, **Use First (first)**, or **Use Last (last)**.

- When the Source Parameter Type parameter is set to **Text**:

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c73af14b612badc6999d771dd4fd4890.jpeg)

  - **Rules**: The drop-down list displays the text fields of cloud resources.

  - **Value Rule**:

    - When the Type parameter is set to **Value** and the Source Parameter Type parameter is set to **Text**, valid values are **Count** and **Count after Deduplication (distinct)**.

    - When the Type parameter is set to **Text** and the Source Parameter Type parameter is set to **Text**, valid values are **Use First (first)** and **Use Last (last)**.

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-2"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.2. Modify a metering table

This topic describes how to modify the basic information and metering fields of a metering table.

**Prerequisites**

- You have logged in to the console as an operations administrator.

- The status of the custom metering table to be modified is **Draft**.

**Limits**

You can modify only custom metering tables.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Then, click the card of the resource to go to metering configuration details page.

6. On the **Draft** tab of the **Metering Table** page, click **Configure** in the **Operations** column of a custom metering table.

7. In the **Modify Metering Table** panel, modify the basic information and metering fields of the metering table.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3be5573966f849ec342459ae87bc2ce9.jpeg)

8. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-3"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.3. View metering tables

View preset or custom metering tables for product metering resources. Metering tables created by third-party products in product management also appear here.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user defaults to the Operations Administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the menu, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Metering** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, from the **Resource** drop-down list, select a cloud service resource.

5. Click a resource card to enter its metering configuration details.

6. Under **Metering Table**, on the **Published** or **Draft** tab, click **View** in the **Actions** column.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The Published tab displays published metering tables. Preset metering tables are **Enabled** by default and appear under the **Published** tab.
   >
   > - The Draft tab displays draft metering tables.

7. In the **Meter Details** panel, view the detailed information of this metering table.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a6538b75bb006d8018a215690bcaf0a9.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-4"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.4. Enable a metering table

After you enable a metering table in the Draft state, the enabled metering table generates corresponding metering tasks based on the metering cycle.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- The custom-type metering table is in the **Draft** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

- Only custom-type metering tables can be enabled.

- Under the same product metering resource, only one custom-type metering table can be enabled.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.

6. On the **Published** or **Draft** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to manage and click **Enable** in the **Operations** column.

7. In the dialog box that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-5"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.5. Disable a metering table

You can disable an enabled metering table. A disabled metering table does not trigger metering tasks for the next metering cycle but does not affect existing tasks.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** state.

**Limits**

Only custom-type metering tables can be disabled.

**Usage notes**

> **Important**
>
> After a metering table is disabled, if it is later enabled again, some metering data may be missing and cannot be replenished.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.

6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to manage and click **Disable** in the **Operations** column.

7. In the dialog box that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-6"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.6. Clone a metering table

By cloning an existing metering table, you can quickly create a new metering table, which significantly improves efficiency and reduces repetitive work.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

Only custom-type metering tables can be cloned.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.

6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to manage and click **Clone** in the **Operations** column.

7. In the **Clone** panel, update the basic information and metering fields of the metering table.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/de18d8d65fc1a1074038cc068e1c7cc3.jpeg)

8. Click **OK**. After the metering table is cloned, it is in the Draft state by default and is displayed in the list on the Draft tab.

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-7"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.7. Delete a metering table

This topic describes how to delete a custom metering table.

**Prerequisites**

- You have logged in to the console as an operations administrator.

- The status of the custom metering table to be deleted is **Draft**.

**Limits**

You can delete only custom metering tables.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Then, click the card of the resource to go to metering configuration details page.

6. On the **Draft** tab of the **Metering Table** page, find the metering table that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Operations** column.

7. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-8"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.8. Create a draft based on an existing metering table

You can create a metering table in the Draft state based on an existing metering table. This creates a new version of the metering table. If the draft is enabled, a new version of the metering table is generated.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

Only custom-type metering tables support creating drafts.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.

6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to manage and click **Create Draft** in the **Operations** column.

7. In the **Create Draft** dialog box, enter a description.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7e87998a5fe764cde2c39e0ef184e1b4.jpeg)

8. Click **OK**. After the draft is created, the new version of the metering table is displayed in the list on the Draft tab.

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-9"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.9. View published version records of a metering table

You can view the published version records of a metering table to understand its historical changes, which helps troubleshoot issues.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

You can view version records only for custom-type metering tables.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.

6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to manage and click **Versions** in the **Operations** column.

7. In the **Published Versions** panel, view the version record information of the metering table. The latest version is displayed at the top.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0cc35d95f3dccdf25314e1a8284037c6.jpeg)

   | Related operations | Description |

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-10"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.10. View metering data push

This topic describes how to view the metering data push in each metering cycle of a cloud service.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select a cloud service resource from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Click the card of the resource to go to the metering configuration details page.

6. Click the **Metering Data Push** tab.

7. View the details of metering data push in each metering cycle.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The total number of abnormal metering cycles to be processed is displayed above the list.
   >
   > - You can configure the **Status** and **Metering Cycle** parameters above the list to find metering data push records.
   >
   >   - For records in the **Uncompleted** state, you can click **View Details**, **Retry**, or **Cancel** in the Actions column.
   >
   >   - For records in the **Processing** state, no operation is supported.
   >
   >   - For records in the **Completed** or **Canceled** state, you can click **View Details** in the Actions column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/073902216147259eb48c061e818362fb.jpeg)

8. Click **View Details** in the **Actions** column of a metering cycle to view the metering data push details.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e2a9ee52f624343659a2c8e32150ba06.jpeg)

   | Section | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Basic Informa tion | The Basic Information section displays the following metering data push information: <strong>Product</strong>, <strong>Resources</strong>, <strong>Status</strong>, <strong>Description</strong>, and <strong>Metering Cycle</strong>. |
   | Meterin g Data Push Progres s | The metering data push progress includes <strong>Obtain Metering Data</strong> and <strong>Audit Metering</strong> <strong>Data</strong>.<br>• <strong>Obtain Metering Data</strong>: If metering data is obtained, click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/dbdba30fda31f4e4a9d89e053764b6e2.png" width="14" alt="">icon to show<br>metering data push details. You can view metering details by <strong>Organization</strong>, <strong>Resource Set</strong>, <strong>Region</strong>, and <strong>Instance ID</strong>.<br>• <strong>Audit Metering Data</strong>: If the metering data audit fails, click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/00ab4d9204042679ee7403d5c406f8cb.png" width="14" alt="">icon to view<br><strong>Affected Data Example</strong>. |

<a id="section-7-1-5-1-11"></a>

##### 7.1.5.1.11. View alert records of metering data

The Alert Records tab displays the alert rules and alert records of cloud service metering data.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration Management**.

4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select a cloud service resource from the **Resources** drop-down list.

5. Click the card of the resource to go to the metering configuration details page.

6. Click the **Alert Records** tab.

7. View alert records. Alert records are displayed in reverse chronological order. The latest alert record is displayed at the top.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/21ef3101b9cd37d709a6aa4676261224.jpeg)

8. Optional. Click **Alert Rules** to view the details of the alert rules.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9acbed1c11621a16b053f0af75fc089e.jpeg)
