<a id="section-7-1-5-2-2"></a>

##### 7.1.5.2.2. View and export usage statistics details

On the Metering Details page, you can view resource usage statistics. The information and metering changes of resource instances are recorded at a granularity of one hour or one second. This topic describes how to view and export the details of resource usage statistics.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Details**.

4. On the Metering Details page, click the **Hourly Details** or **Second-level Details** tab.

   - **Hourly Details**: Resource usage statistics are recorded at a granularity of one hour.

   - **Second-level Details**: Resource usage statistics are recorded at a granularity of one second.

5. On the **Hourly Details** or **Second-level Details** tab, click Advanced Filter, configure filter conditions such as **Cloud Platform**, **Organization**, **Resource Set**, **Resources**, **Metering Table**, **Region**, **Time: (UTC±HH:MM)**, and **Instance ID**, and then click **Search**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The Cloud Platform parameter is displayed in filter conditions and the metering details list only in multi-cloud environments. Based on the cloud platform that you select, the metering details list displays the resource usage statistics of cloud services in Apsara Stack Multi-Enterprise Cloud Edition and the Alibaba Cloud public cloud.
   >
   > - The Metering Table parameter is displayed only on the Hourly Details tab.

6. View the details of resource usage statistics in the list.

   **Hourly Details**

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/df95c78c1d96cd4b6aa00f14b4c68c11.jpeg)

   **Second-level Details**

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7329da443babb0e368f46d7081d30b45.jpeg)

7. Click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ffab809861c8e60470695b10cd14ab4d.png" width="18" alt=""> icon in the upper-right corner to export the resource usage statistics as an

   **.xlsx** file to your computer.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can view or export up to 1,000 entries of resource usage statistics in the console. If you want to view or export more resource usage statistics, you can call the MeteringQuery operation.

<a id="section-7-1-6"></a>

### 7.1.6. Product management

<a id="section-7-1-6-1"></a>

#### 7.1.6.1. Product management

The product management feature supports centralized access to custom services and provides service operations capabilities in internal operations control and resale scenarios.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-1"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.1. Add product category

The top-level product category represents the cloud platform type. It includes system-preset and custom types. System-preset top-level categories include "Apsara Stack" and "Public Cloud". Platform administrators can add custom top-level categories in Configuration > Native Hybrid Cloud > Cloud Platform Type Management. When you add a product category, you can create level 1 and level 2 categories under the top-level category. These correspond to the two-tier menu for products.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager management console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. On the **Product Management** page, click **Add Category**.

5. In the **Add Category** dialog box, configure the product category.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Configuration item</td>
       <td>Description</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Product Parent Class</td>
       <td>You can select a top-level category or a level 1 category as the parent class.<br>• If you select a top-level category as the parent class, the system adds a level 1 category under this category.<br>• If you select a level 1 category as the parent class, the system adds a level 2 category under this category.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Product Category Name</td>
       <td>Enter the name of the product category that you want to add.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b4687e2d3544bb872ea1ae6fbfee7855.jpeg)

6. Click **Confirm**.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-2"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.2. Edit product category

Update the name when a custom product category changes.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is an operations administrator by default.

**Limits**

- You can edit only the names of custom level 1 and level 2 categories.

- You cannot edit preset product categories.

- Top-level categories represent cloud platform types. You cannot edit them on the Product Management page. For more information, see Cloud platform type management.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Operations Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. On the **Product Management** page, move the pointer over the product category name

   and click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1a750db5b1e9ddb5d3b339ac482f3f74.png" width="11" alt=""> .

   > **Note**
   >
   > Enter a category name in the search box above the product category structure to quickly find the category.

5. In the **Edit Category** dialog box, update the product category name.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When you update the name of a level 1 or level 2 category, the parent category information appears and you cannot edit it.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6f2f86e1e695d673d90cddadf80b1f25.jpeg)

6. Click **Confirm**.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-3"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.3. Delete a product category

You can delete a custom product category when it is no longer needed.

**Prerequisites**

- No products exist under the custom product category.

- The current user must be an operations administrator by default.

**Limits**

- You cannot delete preset product categories.

- Top-level categories represent cloud platform types. You cannot edit them on the product management page. For more information, see Cloud platform type management.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. On the **Product Management** page, hover over the name of the custom product category

   and click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2cbd62185a54f8d052b4bd327f74687a.png" width="13" alt=""> .

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Enter a category name in the search box above the category tree to quickly locate the category.
   >
   > - Before you delete a product category, delete its child categories first, then delete the parent category.

5. Click OK.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-4"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.4. Add a product

After you complete adding service categories, you can add services under secondary service categories.

**Prerequisites**

The current user must be an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. On the **Product Management** page, click **Add Products** above the list.

5. In the **Add Products** dialog box, configure the service.

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Product category | Select the category to which the service belongs. You can select <strong>Software</strong> <strong>Products</strong>, <strong>Hardware Products</strong>, or <strong>Offline Products</strong>. |
   | Category | Select the category to which the service belongs.<br>The first column indicates the cloud platform type (that is, the top-level category). The second column indicates the name of the secondary category. |
   | Service provider | Select the service provider to which the service belongs. |
   | Product code (unique code) | Enter a product code. The code must be 2 to 20 characters in length and can contain lowercase letters and hyphens (-). It must start and end with a letter. Do not start your input with "custom-". The system automatically prepends "custom-" after the service is created. |
   | Product display name | Enter a display name for the service. The name must be 2 to 30 characters in length. It must start with a letter and end with a letter or digit. It can contain underscores (_) and hyphens (-). |
   | Product description | Enter a description for the product. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f1da7904222c8d0665bb8fc0f85802cb.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-5"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.5. Edit service

Update the service information when it changes.

**Prerequisites**

- The service is in the **Not put on shelves** state.

- The operating user defaults to an Operations Administrator.

**Constraints**

You cannot edit preset services.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Service Management** > **Service Management**.

4. On the **Service Management** page, click a service category on the left.

5. Under the selected category, click **Edit** in the **Actions** column for the target service.

   > **Note**
   >
   > To quickly find a service, enter its name in the search box above the service list.

6. In the **Edit Product** dialog box, update the service configuration.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You cannot modify the service provider or service code when updating the configuration.

7. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-6"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.6. Publish a service

This topic describes how to publish a service. You can use a service only after it is published.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

The resource type for a service must be published before you publish the service. After the resource type is published, the service is automatically published. For more information about how to publish a resource type, see Publish a resource type.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. Publish a service.

   | Operati on | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Publish a service in the service list. | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service category in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the right side of the page, find the service that you want to manage and click <strong>Shelf</strong> in the <strong>Operation</strong> column.<br>Note<br>You can enter the name of a service in the Cloud Product Name field above the service list to quickly find the service.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Publish a service in the service page. | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the right side of the page, click <strong>Shelf</strong> in the upper-right corner of the <strong>Basic</strong> <strong>Information</strong> section.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-7"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.7. Unpublish a service

When you unpublish a service, all its resource types that have been published are unpublished at the same time. After the service is unpublished, you can no longer use it.

**Prerequisites**

- The service is in the **Put on shelves** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. Unpublish a service.

   | Operati on | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Unpubli sh a service in the service list. | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service category in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the right side of the page, find the service that you want to manage and click <strong>Lower Shelf</strong> in the <strong>Operation</strong> column.<br>Note<br>You can enter the name of a service in the Cloud Product Name field above the service list to quickly find the service.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Unpubli sh a service in the service page. | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the right side of the page, click <strong>Lower Shelf</strong> in the upper-right corner of the <strong>Basic</strong> <strong>Information</strong> section.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-8"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.8. Delete a product

This topic describes how to delete a service. You can delete a service if you no longer need it.

**Prerequisites**

- The service is in the **Removed** or **Not put on shelves** state and has no resource types under it.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. Delete a service.

   | Operatio n | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Delete a service in the service list | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service category in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the right side of the page, find the service that you want to delete and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Operation</strong> column.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Delete a service on the service page | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the right side of the page, click <strong>Delete</strong> in the upper-right corner of the <strong>Basic</strong> <strong>Information</strong> section.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-9"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.9. Edit product tags

Add or remove tags in the product list.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. On the **Product Management** page, click a product category on the left.

5. Under the product category, click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5a25945ce1ac6b46a31b86beb43891a2.png" width="16" alt=""> in the **Tag** column of a product on the right side of the

   page.

6. In the **Edit Tags** dialog box, edit tags for the resource.

   | Operation | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Add a tag | i. Click <strong>Add</strong>.<br>ii. Enter a tag key and a tag value. |
   | Remove a tag | i. Click<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cd7e7b0318e6ba98f8679ba217d8d2b4.png" width="14" alt="">in the tag row. |

7. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-10"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.10. Add a resource type

Add a resource type under a product.

**Prerequisites**

The default user for this operation is the operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top menu, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. On the **Product Management** page, expand the product category on the left and select a product.

5. On the right side of the page, click **Add Resource Type**.

6. On the **Create Resource** page, follow the instructions to complete **Basic configuration**, **Attribute configuration**, **Specification configuration**, **Attribute constraints**, **Lifecycle configuration**, **Quota management**, and **Metering configuration** in sequence.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Resource types that do not support resource lifecycle management only support basic configuration and metering configuration.

**Basic configuration**

On the **Basic Configuration** page, configure the basic information of the resource.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1c3c98af8bd6cc82905476206912d684.jpeg)

Configuration item

Description

Enter a unique identifier for the resource. The identifier must be 2 to 20 characters in length, start and end with a lowercase letter, and can contain only lowercase letters and hyphens (-).

**Unique Identifier**

You cannot start your input with "custom-". The system automatically adds the prefix "custom-" after the resource is created.

**Basic Informati**

Enter a resource name. The name must be 2 to 30 characters in

**Attribute configuration**

On the **Attribute Configuration** page, configure the basic attributes of the resource and reference relevant attributes of other products.

**Manage basic attributes**

1. On the **Basic Attributes** tab, click **Add Attributes**.

2. In the **Property Configuration** panel, configure the basic attributes.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/82de8c0864502e8ba7bd646e56537e32.jpeg)

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Attribute Name | The name of the custom attribute. The attribute name must be unique among all attributes of the resource. |
   | Attribute Field Identifier | Enter the field identifier for the attribute. The field identifier must be unique among all attributes. |
   | Field Type | Select the field type for the attribute, including <strong>Character type</strong>, <strong>Numerical</strong>, <strong>Enumerated type</strong>, and <strong>Boolean</strong>. |

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Attribute recognition location</td>
       <td>This parameter specifies the location of the attribute field within a single instance information (JSONObject).<br>For example, the structure of a single Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) instance information is as follows (simplified version):<br>• Set the attribute recognition location of the VPC name to VpcName.<br>• Set the attribute recognition location of the IPv6 CIDR block to Ipv6CidrBlocks.Ipv6CidrBlock[*].Ipv6Isp.<br>• Set the attribute recognition location of the associated vSwitch to VSwitchIds.VSwitchId.<br><code>{</code><br><code>"VpcName": "test",</code><br><code>"Ipv6CidrBlocks": {</code><br><code>"Ipv6CidrBlock": [</code><br><code>{</code><br><code>"Ipv6Isp": "BGP",</code><br><code>"Ipv6CidrBlock": "****:****:2:48::/61"</code><br><code>}</code><br><code>]</code><br><code>},</code><br><code>"Description": "",</code><br><code>"CidrBlock": "172.*.*.*/12",</code><br><code>"Status": "Available",</code><br><code>"VSwitchIds": {</code><br><code>"VSwitchId": [</code><br><code>"vsw-pb4a3h8dx2q9e4f1r****",</code><br><code>"vsw-pb4g86up0q0f9jcoq****",</code><br><code>"vsw-pb48jvsg77a2cjnyf****"</code><br><code>]</code><br><code>}</code><br><code>}</code></td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Display Control</td>
       <td>Select the display control format for the attribute.<br>• When <strong>Field Type</strong> is set to <strong>Character type</strong>, select <strong>Single line text</strong> or <strong>Multi-</strong><strong>line text</strong> as the display control.<br>• When <strong>Field Type</strong> is set to <strong>Numerical</strong>, select <strong>Single line text</strong> as the display control.<br>• When the <strong>Field Type</strong> is set to <strong>Enumerated type</strong>, select <strong>Multi-select</strong> or <strong>Single-select</strong> as the display control.<br>• When the <strong>Field Type</strong> is set to <strong>Boolean</strong>, select <strong>Switch</strong> as the display control.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Attribute value source</td>
       <td>When <strong>Field Type</strong> is set to <strong>Enumerated type</strong>, you must configure the source of attribute values. You can select <strong>Custom enumeration values</strong>, <strong>Interface</strong>, or <strong>Resource list</strong>.<br>• If you select <strong>Custom enumeration values</strong> for <strong>Attribute value source</strong>, you must set <strong>Data source configuration</strong>, including <strong>Name</strong> and <strong>Value</strong>. You can add entries, delete entries, and adjust the order of entries.<br>• If you select <strong>Interface</strong> for <strong>Attribute value source</strong>, you must set <strong>Interface</strong> <strong>Information</strong>, <strong>Request parameter configuration</strong>, and <strong>Request result</strong> <strong>configuration</strong>.<br>• <strong>Interface Information</strong>: Enter the interface key and the request URL of the interface.<br>• <strong>Request parameter configuration</strong>: Set the names and values of common attributes and custom attributes. You can add or delete parameters.<br>• <strong>Request result configuration</strong>: Enter a conversion function for the request result.<br>Note<br>The function must start with $code: and contain a function body that returns a structure in the format of { success: boolean, data: any }. The built-in params parameter indicates the returned result.<br>• If you select <strong>Resource list</strong> for <strong>Attribute value source</strong>, you must set <strong>Product Category</strong>, <strong>Cloud Product Name</strong>, <strong>Cloud Resource</strong>, and <strong>Resource</strong> <strong>List</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

    <td colspan="2">Interface parameter configuration</td>

<table>
  <tr>
    <td>Quota Item Configuration</td>
    <td>After you enable quota management, configure settings related to quota items. Interface parameter mapping and configuration change parameter mapping are optional. All other items are required.<br>• Resource type allows you to select all resource types under the product of the current operation. Quotas may require cross-resource type validation.<br>• Quota items support all custom resource items and resource items configured in specifications for the selected resource type. The system manages these items as quota items.<br>• Quota unit indicates the unit of a quota item.<br>• Interface parameter mapping indicates the filter condition in the inventory interface response that corresponds to this quota item.<br>• For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the inventory interface returns the following inventory data, where "cpu_type" represents the physical inventory of Cpu, set this item to cpu_type.<br><code>[{"metric":"cpu_type","total":100},</code><br><code>{"metric":"disk","total":1000}]</code><br>• If you select Manual configuration for Inventory Acquisition Rules or the quota item cannot obtain inventory information from the interface, you can directly enter an integer as its physical inventory. You can also leave it blank to indicate no physical inventory limit.<br>• If multiple resources configure this quota item and all configure interface parameter mapping, the system retrieves physical inventory multiple times. The final displayed physical inventory is the cumulative value.<br>• Creation parameter mapping indicates the parameter name of this quota item in the create interface request. For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the create interface request is as follows, where "CpuCost" represents the Cpu cost, set this item to CpuCost.<br><code>{"CpuCost":100, "Description":"test"}</code><br>• Configuration change parameter mapping indicates the parameter name of this quota item after configuration change in the configuration change interface request. For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the configuration change interface request is as follows, where "NewCpuCost" represents the cost of Cpu after the configuration change, configure this item as NewCpuCost.<br><code>{"NewCpuCost":100, "Description":"test"}</code><br>• Deduction parameter mapping indicates the parameter name of this quota item in the list interface response. For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the list interface response is as follows, where "CpuCount" represents the cost of Cpu, configure this item as CpuCount.<br><code>{"CpuCount":100, "Description":"test",</code><br><code>"InstanceId":"xxx"}</code></td>
  </tr>
</table>

##### 7.1.6.1.11. Modify a resource type

This topic describes how to modify a resource type when the resource type changes.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. Modify the resource type.

   | Operati on | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Modify the resourc e type in the resourc e type list | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the <strong>Resource Type</strong> tab, find the resource type that you want to modify and click <strong>Edit</strong> in the <strong>Operation</strong> column.<br>iii. On the <strong>EditResources</strong> page, modify the resource type configuration. For more information about the configuration items, see Add a resource type.<br>iv. Click <strong>Return to List</strong>. |
   | Modify the resourc e type on the resourc e type page | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a resource type in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the right side of the page, click <strong>Edit</strong> in the upper-right corner of the <strong>Basic</strong> <strong>Information</strong> section.<br>iii. On the <strong>EditResources</strong> page, modify the resource type configuration. For more information about the configuration items, see Add a resource type.<br>iv. Click <strong>Return to List</strong>. |

##### 7.1.6.1.12. Publish a resource type

This topic describes how to publish a resource type.

**Prerequisites Prerequisites**

- The resource type is in the **Removed** or **Not put on shelves** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Usage notes**

If the service to which the resource type belongs is in the **Not put on shelves** or **Removed** state, the service is published after the resource type is published.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.

4. Publish a resource type.

   | Operatio n | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Publish a resource type in the resource list | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a service in the left-side section.<br>ii. On the <strong>Resource Type</strong> tab, find the resource type that you want to publish and click <strong>Shelf</strong> in the <strong>Operation</strong> column.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Publish a resource type on the resource page | i. On the <strong>Product Management</strong> page, click a resource in the left-side section.<br>ii. <a id="section-7-1-6-1-17"></a>

##### 7.1.6.1.17. Third-party product management integration

To enable management of external cloud products in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, make sure that the relevant systems and network environment meet the basic conditions. This solution is based on the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and relies on its ability to call the management APIs of external cloud products. At the same time, the external clouds must provide standardized APIs to support cross-cloud resource management. Stable and secure two-way network connectivity must be established between the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and external cloud API gateways to ensure the reliability of service calls and the security of data transmission. As the major caller, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console must maintain continuously available network connections with the external cloud API gateways to ensure the efficient execution of cross-cloud resource management processes.

On this basis, the third-party products must provide complete functional support, including instance management features such as resource creation, deletion, modification and query, status change feedback, and execution result feedback. These capabilities ensure that the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console can efficiently call the APIs of external cloud services, test resource management processes in a multi-cloud environment, and reduce the integration complexity and testing costs of cross-cloud systems.

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-17-1"></a>

###### 7.1.6.1.17.1. Integration solution

The integration solution includes Service Provider Interface (SPI) integration for instance management, instance status update triggering by third-party products, and metering data pushing by third-party products.

Instance management SPI integration This topic describes the interface specifications and integration steps for instance management SPI integration.

**Interface specifications**

Instance management is a core function of cloud service lifecycle management. It covers operations such as creating, querying, modifying, and deleting resources like ECS and RDS instances. To support unified management of instances by the Alibaba Cloud Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, external clouds must provide standardized RESTful API interfaces to enable full lifecycle control over instances. The following table lists the specific operation types, request URLs, methods, and parameter descriptions.

> **Note**
>
> All interfaces require POST requests over HTTPS with Content-Type set to application/json; charset=utf-8.

**CreateInstance**

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| action | true | String | Static field: createInstance. |
| aliUid | true | String | The Alibaba Cloud user ID that triggers the request. |
| params | true | JSONString | The request parameters for the API.The system fills in all declared parameters. |
| token | true | Security Token | A JWT security token for service provider validation. |
| traceId | false | String | The EagleEye ID.<br>Service providers can record this ID for traceability purposes. |
| productCode | false | String | The product code.<br>Service providers can record this code, which is assigned during product integration. |
| resourceTypeCod e | false | String | The resource type.<br>Service providers can record this code, which is assigned during resource integration. |
| organizationId | false | Integer | The organization ID.<br>Service providers can record the organization ID passed during instance creation. |

**Integration steps**

1. Create an instance. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console calls the API to trigger an instance creation request. The SPI returns the generated instance ID and its current status. If the third-party product uses asynchronous API calls, return a taskId so that the cloud service can later query the task progress. After the task completes, return the instanceId. The cloud service retrieves the instance details by calling the GetInstanceDetail API and then stores them in the database.

2. Delete an instance. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console sends a request to trigger the deletion operation. The SPI deletes the instance corresponding to the provided instance ID and updates the instance status. If the third-party product uses asynchronous API calls, return a taskId so that the cloud service can later query the task progress. After the task completes, the cloud service deletes the record from the database.

3. Query an instance. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console retrieves instance details through the API. The SPI returns the detailed information for the instance corresponding to the specified instance ID.

4. Change the specification. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console calls the API to update the instance's specification. The SPI performs the modification and returns the result. If the third-party product uses asynchronous API calls, return a taskId so that the cloud service can later query the task progress. After the task completes, the cloud service retrieves the updated instance details by calling the GetInstanceDetail API and updates the database.

5. Get specifications. If the third-party product needs to support dynamic specification retrieval, configure this API. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console calls this API to obtain the currently supported specifications in real time.

6. Get inventory. If the third-party product needs to support inventory retrieval, configure this API.

Update the status of third-party product instances

If a third-party product instance is managed by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and its status or information changes on the third-party platform, the third-party platform can call the CloudUpdateResource operation to notify the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to query the real-time information about the instance by calling the GetInstanceDetail operation.

CloudUpdateResource information:

**Basic information**

- Operation: CloudUpdateResource

- Version: 2019-05-10

- Request method: POST

- Product: Apsara Uni-manager Management Console

- Supported account: the tenant accounts granted the permission to synchronize resource information

- Call method: POP SDK

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requ ired | Open | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| resourceType | String | true | true | The resource type of the third-party product to be accessed. |
| resourceId | String | true | true | The ID of the resource instance. |

**Response parameters**

If true is returned for the success parameter, the instance status is updated.

```json
{
    "code": "200",
    "success": true,
    "message": ""
}
```

Push metering data of third-party products Third-party products proactively push metering data by calling the PutMeteringData operation.

PutMeteringData information:

**Basic information**

- Operation: PutMeteringData

- Version: 2019-05-10

- Request method: POST

- Product: Apsara Uni-manager Management Console

- Supported account: the tenant accounts granted the permission to upload metering data

- Call method: POP SDK

Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| productCode | String | Yes | The resource type of the third-party product to be accessed. |
| data | String | Yes | The metering data in the JSON format. Take note of the following items:<br>1. The metering data of at most 100 instances can be pushed per request.<br>2. Except for the <code> ResourceGId </code>, <code> ResourceGName </code>, <code> OrgId </code>, <code> OrgName </code>, <code> RegionId </code>, and <code> TableVersion </code> fields, all the other fields in the metering data must be pushed.<br>3. The instance ID in the metering data must be managed in the resource management module.<code> InsId </code> indicates the instance ID in the resource management module.<br>4. The values of StartTime and EndTime in the metering data must be on the hour, and the start time is one hour earlier than the end time. Unit: seconds. In addition, the StartTime and EndTime of all instances in a request must be in the same metering cycle. |

**Sample request**

```json
{
    "productCode": "custom-resourceCode", # The resource type.
    "data": [
        {
            "InsId": "insId-example1",     # The instance ID.
            "StartTime": 1756346400,  # The start time of the metering cycle. The value 
is a UNIX timestamp representing the number of seconds that have elapsed since January 
1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC.
            "EndTime": 1756350000,   # The end time of the metering cycle. The value isa UNIX timestamp representing the number of seconds that have elapsed since January 1, 
1970, 00:00:00 UTC.
            "fieldKey1": "fieldValue1"  # Other metering fields. 
        },
        {
            "InsId": "insId-example2",
            "StartTime": 1756346400,
            "EndTime": 1756350000,
            "fieldKey1": "fieldValue1"
        }
    ]
}
```

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| success | Boolean | Indicates whether the request was successful. |
| message | String | The error message. |

    <td>The user who created the instance.</td>
  </tr>
</table>

**Response Parameter**

If success=true, the update succeeded.

```json
{"code":"200","message":"success"}
```

<a id="section-7-1-6-1-17-2"></a>

###### 7.1.6.1.17.2. Demo code

A JSON Web Key (JWK) can be at most 4,096 characters in length.

You can generate a JWK at https://mkjwk.org/. You can use the information displayed in the left card in the following figure to generate a JWK. The information displayed in the right card is used to generate a public key, which is used to verify JWT tokens. For more information, see the Verify a JWT token section of this topic.

![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/09bce61030c38f8cde357225b556b454.jpeg)

**Declare POM dependencies in Java**

```xml
<dependencies>
    <!-- JJWT API -->
    <dependency>
        <groupId>io.jsonwebtoken</groupId>
        <artifactId>jjwt-api</artifactId>
        <version>0.11.5</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- JJWT implementation -->
    <dependency>
        <groupId>io.jsonwebtoken</groupId>
        <artifactId>jjwt-impl</artifactId>
        <version>0.11.5</version>
        <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
    <!-- JJWT Jackson module (for JSON data processing) -->
    <dependency>
        <groupId>io.jsonwebtoken</groupId>
        <artifactId>jjwt-jackson</artifactId>
        <version>0.11.5</version>
        <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>com.nimbusds</groupId>
        <artifactId>nimbus-jose-jwt</artifactId>
        <version>9.37</version> <!-- Latest stable version -->
    </dependency>
</dependencies>
```

**Generate a JWT token**

```text
/**
     * Generate JWT token
     */
    private String generateJwtToken(JSONObject requestBody, String secret) {
        try {
            PrivateKey privateKey = RSAKey.parse(secret).toPrivateKey();
            // Header
            Map<String, Object> header = new HashMap<>();
            header.put("alg", "RS256");
            header.put("typ", "JWT");

            // Payload
            // exp 15 minutes
            Map<String, Object> claims = new HashMap<>(requestBody);
            // Identify the request source as Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
            claims.put("iss", "ascm");
            claims.put("iat", System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000);
            claims.put("exp", (System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000) + 900);

            return Jwts.builder()
                    .setHeader(header)
                    .setClaims(claims)
                    .signWith(privateKey, SignatureAlgorithm.RS256)
                    .compact();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new CommonException(500, SPI_TOKEN_GENERATE_FAILED);
        }
```

**Verify a JWT token**

```text
// The public key.
private String jwtPublicString = "{\n" +
            "    \"kty\": \"RSA\",\n" +
            "    \"e\": \"AQAB\",\n" +
            "    \"alg\": \"RS256\",\n" +
            "    \"n\": \"sxc***\"\n" +
            "}";

/**
 * Verify the token.
 *
 * @param token
 */
private void validateToken(String token) {
    if (StringUtils.isEmpty(token)) {
        throw new RuntimeException("The token is required.");
    }
    try {
        PublicKey publicKey = RSAKey.parse(jwtPublicString).toPublicKey();
        Jws<Claims> jws = 
Jwts.parserBuilder().setSigningKey(publicKey).build().parseClaimsJws(token);
    } catch (SecurityException | MalformedJwtException e) {
        System.err.println("Invalid JWT signature or format: " + e.getMessage()); // The token is invalid.
    } catch (ExpiredJwtException e) {
        System.err.println("JWT token has expired: " + e.getMessage()); // The token expires.
    } catch (Exception e) {
        System.err.println("Token check file" + e.getMessage());
    }

}
```

**Create an instance**

```text
/**
 * Create a instance.
 *
 * @param map The request parameters in the JSON format.
 * @return The instance information that is returned in the JSON format after the instance is created.
 */
@PostMapping("/create")
public String createInstance(@RequestBody Map<String, Object> map) {
    String token = (String) map.get("token");
    String expiredTimeStr = (String) map.get("expiredTime");
    String params = (String) map.get("params");
    String spec = JSONObject.parseObject(params).getString("spec");


    // Verify the token.
    validateToken(token);
    // Parse the time string.
    Date expiredTime = parseDate(expiredTimeStr);
    // Implement the logic to create the instance.
    return instanceManager.createInstance(spec, expiredTime);
}
```

**Delete an instance**

```text
/**
 * Delete a specific instance.
 *
 * @param map The request parameters in the JSON format.
 * @return If the instance is deleted, true is returned. Otherwise, false is returned.
 */
@PostMapping("/delete")
public String deleteInstance(@RequestBody Map<String, Object> map) {
    String instanceId = (String) map.get("instanceId");
    String token = (String) map.get("token");
    // Verify the token.
    validateToken(token);
    // Implement the logic to delete the instance.
    return instanceManager.deleteInstance(instanceId);
}
```

**Query the details of an instance**

```text
/**
 * Query the details of an instance.
 *
 * @param map The request parameters in the JSON format.
 * @return The instance details that are returned in the JSON format.
 */
@PostMapping("/query")
public String queryInstance(@RequestBody Map<String, Object> map) {
    String instanceId = (String) map.get("instanceId");
    String token = (String) map.get("token");
    validateToken(token);
    // Implement the logic to query the details of the instance.
    return instanceManager.queryInstance(instanceId);
}
```

**Change the specifications of an instance**

```text
/**
 * Change the specifications of a specific instance.
 *
 * @param map The request parameters in the JSON format.
 * @return The instance information that is returned in the JSON format after the specification change.
 */
@PostMapping("/changeSpec")
public String changeSpec(@RequestBody Map<String, Object> map) {
    String instanceId = (String) map.get("instanceId");
    String token = (String) map.get("token");
    String params = (String) map.get("params");
    String newSpec = JSONObject.parseObject(params).getString("newSpec");
    validateToken(token);
    // Implement the logic to change the specifications of the instance.
    return instanceManager.changeSpec(instanceId, newSpec);
}
```

###### 7.1.6.1.17.3. Appendix

This topic describes error codes and provides a POP call example.

**Error codes**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | The request was successful. |
| 400 | The parameter verification failed. |
| 404 | The resource does not exist. |
| 500 | An internal service error has occurred. |

**POP call example**

```java
package org.example;

import com.alibaba.fastjson.JSON;
import com.aliyuncs.CommonRequest;
import com.aliyuncs.CommonResponse;
import com.aliyuncs.DefaultAcsClient;
import com.aliyuncs.IAcsClient;
import com.aliyuncs.http.FormatType;
import com.aliyuncs.http.HttpClientConfig;
import com.aliyuncs.http.MethodType;
import com.aliyuncs.http.ProtocolType;
import com.aliyuncs.profile.DefaultProfile;

import java.util.Map;

/**
 * @author Leke
 * @date 2025/8/7 13:52
 */
public class PopClient {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String region = "cn-wulan-***-d01";
        String ak = "*******";
        String sk = "***************";

        String endpoint = "ascm.api.cn-wulan-***-d01.intra.***.shuguang.com";

        DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile(region, ak, sk);
        HttpClientConfig clientConfig = HttpClientConfig.getDefault();
        clientConfig.setProtocolType(ProtocolType.HTTP);
        profile.setHttpClientConfig(clientConfig);

        IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);

        CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
        Map<String, String> body = request.getSysBodyParameters();

        // Specify a trituple.
        body.put("product", "ascm");
        body.put("version", "2019-05-10");
        body.put("action", "PutMeteringData");

        request.setSysDomain(endpoint);
        request.setSysMethod(MethodType.POST);
        request.setHttpContentType(FormatType.FORM);
        request.putHeadParameter("x-acs-caller-sdk-source","ascm-
metering.metering_server#");
        // To use the AccessKey pair of an operations administrator to call the API, specify the role ID of the operations administrator in the request header. The role ID ofthe operations administrator is 1.
        request.putHeadParameter("x-acs-roleid", "1");

        // Enter the metering code.
        body.put("productCode", "custom-resourceCode");
        // Enter the metering data.
        body.put("data", "[{\n" +
                "\t\"InsId\": \"leke\",\n" +
                "\t\"StartTime\": \"1756346400\",\n" +
                "\t\"EndTime\": \"1756350000\",\n" +
                "\t\"fieldKey\": \"fieldValue\"\n" +
                "}]");

        try {
            CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
            System.out.println(JSON.toJSONString(response));
        } catch (Exception e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        }

    }
}
```

<a id="section-7-1-6-2"></a>

#### 7.1.6.2. Service provider management

The service provider management feature allows you to manage the service providers of custom services in a centralized manner.

<a id="section-7-1-6-2-1"></a>

##### 7.1.6.2.1. Add a service provider

Before you add a custom service, you must add the service provider to which the service belongs.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Service Provider Management**.

4. On the **Service Provider Management** page, click **Add Service Provider**.

5. In the **Add Service Provider** dialog box, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Service Provider Display Name | The display name of the service provider. The display name must be 2 to 30 characters in length and can contain underscores (_) and hyphens (-). It must start with a letter and end with a letter or digit. |
   | Service Provider Description | The description of the service provider. The description can be up to 200 characters in length and can contain common characters and punctuations. |
   | Contact | The contact information of the service provider. The contact information must be 2 to 30 characters in length and must start and end with a letter. |
   | Phone Number | The phone number of the service provider. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6b8d9fbcd61ddda131038f65a577f1e3.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-6-2-2"></a>

##### 7.1.6.2.2. Modify a service provider

This topic describes how to modify a service provider when the service provider information changes.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

The built-in system service providers cannot be modified.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Service Provider Management**.

4. On the **Service Provider Management** page, find the service provider that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the **Operation** column.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can specify the Service Provider Display Name and Source parameters above the service provider list to quickly find a service provider.

5. In the **Edit Service Provider** dialog box, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Service Provider Display Name | The display name of the service provider. |
   | Service Provider Description | The description of the service provider. |
   | Contact | The contact information of the service provider. |
   | Phone Number | The phone number of the service provider. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/86fa979b76ac237cc26b5da642a6b5f9.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-6-2-3"></a>

##### 7.1.6.2.3. Remove a service provider

You can remove a service provider if you no longer need it.

**Prerequisites**

- The service provider has no services.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

The built-in system service providers cannot be removed.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Service Provider Management**.

4. On the **Service Provider Management** page, find the service provider that you want to remove and click **Delete** in the **Operation** column.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can specify the Service Provider Display Name and Source parameters above the service provider list to quickly find a service provider.

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

### 7.1.7. Examples

<a id="section-7-1-7-1"></a>

#### 7.1.7.1. Example: Manage the memory quota of ECS

This topic describes how to manage the memory quota of Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator or organization administrator.

- Quotas are configured for the parent organization.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the main menu, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quotas**.

4. In the left-side organizational structure of the Quotas page, select the organization or resource set whose resources you want to manage.

5. In the upper-right corner of the page, select a region.

6. Click the **Elastic Compute Service** card to view the quota details.

7. In the **Quota Details** panel, view the resource items, quotas, amount and percentage of allocated quotas, and amount and percentage of activated resources.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Quota**: If you do not specify a quota for a resource item, no quota is configured for the resource item. The system does not limit the usage of the corresponding resources.
   >
   > - **Allocated Quota (Percentage/Allocated Amount)**: displays the quotas that are allocated to each resource item in the specified organization and its sub-organizations. You can view the amount and percentage of allocated quotas.
   >
   > - **Activated Resources (Percentage/Activated Amount)**: displays the resources that are activated in the specified organization and its sub-organizations. You can view the amount and percentage of the activated resources.

8. In the lower part of the **Quota Details** panel, click **Create Quotas** or **Modify Quota**.

9. In the **Quota** column of the **Memory Quota(GB)** field, enter the quota that you want to set. Example: 500.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a33588dbe0ba060dedbc20d88b2331c1.jpeg)

0. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-7-1-7-2"></a>

#### 7.1.7.2. Create an alert rule for the memory quota of ECS

This topic describes how to create an alert rule for the memory quota of Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator or organization administrator.

- The memory quota of ECS is configured.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the main menu, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quota Alerts**.

4. On the Quota Alerts page, click **Create Alert**.

5. In the **Create Quota Alert** dialog box, configure the parameters in the Alert Object Information and Alert Information sections.

   In the Alert Object Information section, select an organization or a resource set and a region. Select **Elastic Compute Service** from the Cloud Service Category drop-down list.

   In the Alert Information section, configure the Alert Name, Alarm Standard, and Alert Threshold parameters. For example, you can set the name of the alert rule to ECS_memory, select Used for the Alarm Standard parameter, select Number from the drop-down list in the Threshold column of the Memory Quota(GB) field, and set the threshold to 180. This way, an alert is triggered when the used memory of ECS exceeds 180 GB in size.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1bfefe9e765e8041be9316900ca57566.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-1-7-3"></a>

#### 7.1.7.3. Example: Create and publish a process

This topic provides an example on how to create and publish a process.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Process Management** > **Process Management**.

4. On the **Process Management** page, click **Create Process**.

5. Configure the basic information and click **Next**.

   - **Process Name**: Enter a name for the process. Example: Process for baseservicetest.

   - **Process Description**: Enter a description for the process. Example: The process is used for the baseservicetest organization.

   - **Applicable Personnel**: Select **All Organizations** or **Select Organization**. Example: Select **Select Organization** and select baseservicetest from the **Select Organization** drop-down list.

     > **Note**
     >
     > If you turn off **Bind Sub-organization**, the process cannot be associated with the sub-organizations of the selected organization. If you need to associate sub-organizations with the process, turn on **Bind Sub-organization**.

   - **Select Initiator**: Select **All Users** or **Specified Role**. Example: Select **All Users**.

6. In the **Process Configuration** step, configure the process nodes, including the start, approver, and end information. After the configuration is complete, click **Submit**.

   - **Start**: Click the **Start** card. In the **Initiator Settings** panel, select or clear **Allow Initiator to Add CC Recipient**. Example: Clear **Allow Initiator to Add CC Recipient**. In this case, the initiator is not allowed to add CC recipients.

   - **Approved By**: Click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e9b1630f89e22eb16a3d57160fce281d.png" width="16" alt=""> icon. In the **Approval Node Settings** panel, configure the

     approval node.

     - **Approved By**: specify the approver type. Example: Set the **Type** parameter to **Specific Personnel** and select **admin(admin)** from the **Specific Personnel** drop-down list.

     - **Approval Method**: Select **Parallel Signature(Requires Approval by One)** or **Sequential Signature(Requires Approval by All)** for **When multiple approvers are specified**. You have specified admin as the approver. Keep the default setting. Select or clear **Allow the approver to specify additional signatories**. Only the current approver can add signatories. Multiple signatories can be specified. Example: Select **Allow the approver to specify additional signatories**. In this case, the admin user is allowed to add signatories.

     - **Add CC Recipient**: You can select CC recipients from the **Specific Personnel** drop-down list. Example: Leave the **Specific Personnel** parameter empty.

   - **End**: Click the **End** card. In the **End Node Settings** panel, you can specify the users who are notified of the end of the process. After the process ends, the approval results are automatically sent to the specified users. Example: Leave the **Specific Personnel** parameter empty.

     > **Note**
     >
     > If you need to notify other users, select the users from the **Specific Personnel** drop-down list. The selected users must be visible to the process creator.

7. After the process is created, view the process in the process list.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52e76920d19eddf6719c5d802ec7ea2b.jpeg)

8. Click **Publish** in the **Operations** column of the process. After the process is published, the status of the process changes to **Published**. You can associate a process with a business scenario only when the process is in the **Published** state.

## 7.2. Service operations

<a id="section-7-2-1"></a>

### 7.2.1. Shopping cart

You can add the cloud services for which you want to apply to the shopping cart and apply for multiple cloud services of different types at a time on the Shopping Cart page.

**Background information**

You can add multiple cloud services for which you want to apply to the shopping cart, confirm the information on the Shopping Cart page, and then submit multiple applications at a time. This improves the usage efficiency.

You can add a service to the shopping cart on the service configuration page. After a service is added to the shopping cart, you can remove and modify the configurations of the service on the Shopping Cart page. After an application is submitted, a service order is generated.

**Add a service to the shopping cart**

In this example, Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is used.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Networking** > **Cloud Network** > **Virtual Private Cloud**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Virtual Private Clouds**.

4. On the Virtual Private Clouds page, click **Create VPC**.

5. On the Create VPC page, configure the parameters. For more information, see the user guide of VPC.

6. Click **Add to Cart** in the lower part of the page

**View services in the shopping cart**

1. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu and

   > **Note**
   >
   > - After you add a service to the shopping cart on the service configuration page, you are automatically navigated to the Shopping Cart page.
   >
   > - The number in the upper-right corner of the Shopping Cart icon indicates the number of services added to the shopping cart.

2. On the Shopping Cart page, view the information about the cloud services that are added to the shopping cart in the following columns: **Service**, **Specifications**, **Billing Method**, **Quantity**, **Duration**, and **Fee**.

   > **Note**
   >

**Remove one or more services from the shopping cart**

- **Remove a single service**

  <ol type="i">

  <li>

  On the Shopping Cart page, find the service that you want to remove and click **Remove** in the **Actions** column.

  </li>

  <li>

  In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the service is removed, it is no longer

  </li>

  </ol>

  displayed in the shopping cart.

- **Remove multiple services at a time**

  <ol type="i">

  <li>

  On the Shopping Cart page, select the services that you want to remove.

  </li>

  <li>

  Click **Batch Remove** in the lower part of the page.

  </li>

  <li>

  In the message that appears, click **OK**.

  </li>

  </ol>

**Modify service configurations in the shopping cart**

1. On the Shopping Cart page, find the service whose configurations you want to modify and click **Change Specifications** in the **Actions** column.

2. Modify the configurations based on your business requirements by referring to the user guide of the cloud service.

**Submit service applications**

1. On the Shopping Cart page, select the services for which you want to apply.

2. In the lower part of the page, click **Apply Now**.

3. On the **Confirm Order** page, click **Create Now**.

#### 7.2.1.1. Create a list

The Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ) page displays the configuration information about services in a list by group. You can create multiple lists to manage resources in CPQ by group. You can also select and submit resources across groups. This topic describes how to create a list in CPQ.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu, and

   then click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/88c070391bad8794d9ccd63b81d3ada1.png" width="28" alt=""> icon to go to the CPQ page.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The number in brackets after CPQ indicates the number of services that have been added to CPQ.

3. On the **CPQ** page, click **Create List**.

4. In the **Create List** dialog box, enter a name for the list that you want to create.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The list name must be unique under each Apsara Stack tenant account.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c091617b617ca4a6406f43f63c4aa85a.jpeg)

5. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-2-1-2"></a>

#### 7.2.1.2. Save a list

If you use the Save List feature, you save the default list as a custom list. This topic describes how to save a list in Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ).

**Limits**

Only the default list can be saved.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu, and

   then click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/88c070391bad8794d9ccd63b81d3ada1.png" width="28" alt=""> icon to go to the CPQ page.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The number in brackets after CPQ indicates the number of services that have been added to CPQ.

3. On the **CPQ** page, click **Save List** on the right side of **Default List**.

4. In the **Save List** dialog box, configure the **List Name** parameter.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - If the default list contains a service, the service is also saved to the custom list. After you save the default list as a custom list, the contents of the default list are cleared.
   >
   > - The list name must be unique under each Apsara Stack tenant account.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b5ffe3fab62050c803e2a9e3a7b85f31.jpeg)

5. Click **OK**.

**Procedure**

2. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu, and

   > **Note**

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2be05d22071041b4cdb290902c141ae4.jpeg)

4. Click **OK**.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu, and

#### 7.2.2.2. Service management

The Service Management page displays all services that you can manage. You can create custom services, publish services, and authorize specific users to access services.

**Background information**

The service management feature is used to manage and control specific specifications of specific services that belong to an enterprise or organization. For example, enterprises or organizations require employees to go through an approval process before the employees purchase Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances with high specifications, or authorize only a specific user or users in a specific organization to purchase high-specification ECS instances. In this case, enterprises or organizations can configure the specifications and specify users by using the service management feature. After a service is published, the authorized users or organizations can select only the specifications that they are authorized to access. If they create resources with high specifications, they must go through an approval process. This way, enterprises or organizations can impose limits on resource users and manage specifications in a fine-grained manner.
