#### 7.2.4.10. Cost tags

<a id="section-7-2-4-10-1"></a>

##### 7.2.4.10.1. Add cost tags

Cost tags can be displayed in bills, cost centers, and cost data analysis. You can view and calculate costs based on the added cost tags to accurately understand the costs of applications or systems.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Cost Tag**.

4. On the **Cost Tag** page, click **Add Tag**.

5. In the **Add Tag** dialog box, select the tags that you want to add from the **Available Tags**

   list and click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/af873094bf91e0dca3bcd6e283fbac76.png" width="18" alt=""> icon to add the tags to the **Added Tags** list.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The tags in the Available Tags list are from Tag Management.
   >
   > - To remove a tag from the Added Tags list, select the tag in the Added Tags list and click the
   >
   >   icon.
   >
   >   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/703f2fcb53b0f8b3f2ee0b7c09fcc386.png" width="21" alt="">

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd5d35adf9fff1f42e6b8909aa0db5ea.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-2-4-10-2"></a>

##### 7.2.4.10.2. Delete cost tags

After you delete a cost tag, the cost tag no longer takes effect in bills, cost centers, and cost data analysis. It is no longer displayed and available for filtering.

**Usage notes**

> **Important**
>
> If you delete a cost tag, historical bills, cost centers, and cost data analysis are not affected.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Cost Tag**.

4. On the **Cost Tag** page, find the tag key that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can specify a tag name in the Tag Key field above the list to filter tag keys.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4d0996eaf3be358d490c6735298aff3d.jpeg)

5. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-2-4-11"></a>

#### 7.2.4.11. Import task management

Displays billing import records. View the progress and results of tasks.

**Prerequisites**

- Billing import relies on API-based import. For details, see the interface documentation for “CreateBillingPushTask”, “BatchPushBilling”, “UpdateStatusPushFinished”, and “QueryBillingPushTaskStatus” in the *Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide*.

- The default operating user is the operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operation** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Bills** > **Import Task Management**.

4. On the **Import Task Management** page, set filter conditions in the **Advanced filtering** section, then click **Search**.

5. View imported billing records in the list.

   - **View task**: Click **View Task** in the **Actions** column to view task details.

   - **Delete task**: Click **Delete** in the **Actions** column. Alternatively, select multiple tasks and click **Delete** below the list.

<a id="section-7-2-5"></a>

### 7.2.5. Budget management

<a id="section-7-2-5-1"></a>

#### 7.2.5.1. Configure budget settings

Budget management can be used to limit the available quotas for organizations or cost centers. You can configure budget accounts, budget control settings, and budget alert settings based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role is granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and the permissions to configure global settings and budget alert settings.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. In the upper-right corner of the **Budgets** page, click **Budget settings**.

5. In the **Budget settings** panel, configure global settings and budget alert settings.

   - **Global Settings**

     | Parameter | Description |
     | --- | --- |
     | Budget account creation dimension | Valid values: <strong>By organization</strong> and <strong>By financial unit</strong>.<br>• <strong>By organization</strong>: configures budget accounts based on the organization architecture.<br>• <strong>By financial unit</strong>: configures budget accounts based on the cost center architecture. If you select By financial unit, you must configure cost centers and allocation rules.<br>Note<br>You can configure the Budget account creation dimension parameter only if you enter the Budgets module for the first time and you have not completed the initial setup. You cannot modify this parameter after it is configured. Proceed with caution. |

     <table>
       <tr>
         <td>Insufficient budget control settings</td>
         <td>Valid values: <strong>If the budget is insufficient, you can apply for new</strong> <strong>resources.</strong> and <strong>Insufficient budget does not allow new resource</strong> <strong>applications</strong>.<br>Note<br>• If the budget is insufficient, you can apply for new <strong>resources.</strong>: The system does not limit resource allocation by budget management. The account balance can be deducted to a negative value.<br>• Insufficient budget does not allow new resource <strong>applications</strong>: The system controls resource allocation based on orders.<br>• Subscription services do not accept resource applications if the account balance is less than the order payment.<br>• Pay-as-you-go services do not accept resource applications if the account balance is zero or less than zero.</td>
       </tr>
     </table>

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/69b5bc7b6adb8bd774834c0852d019d6.jpeg)

   - **Budget alert**

     | Parameter | Description |
     | --- | --- |
     | Alarm switch | Specifies whether to enable budget alert. Valid values: <strong>Open</strong> and <strong>Close</strong>. |
     | Alert Threshold | The alert threshold. The system checks the available quotas of the allocation accounts at 09:00 every day. If a quota is lower than the specified threshold, an alert notification is sent. |
     | Alert object | The alert contact. Valid values: <strong>Organization Administrator/financial unit</strong> <strong>authorized user</strong> and <strong>Operations Administrator</strong>. You can select both options. |

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5776048763ad17d4bb3d32b341d0d4a0.jpeg)

6. Click **Save**.

<a id="section-7-2-5-2"></a>

#### 7.2.5.2. View independent accounts

You can view the list of independent accounts on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role is granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and the permissions to view independent accounts.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. On the **Budgets** page, click **Independent account list** in the left-side **Budget Overview** section.

5. View independent accounts. You can filter or search for specific accounts by configuring the **Account name** and **Includes deleted accounts** parameters.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8b4be945506699c92a8ce680b8df30ba.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - An independent account is the master account of a level-1 organization or cost center. You can increase or reduce the budget for an independent account.
   >
   > - An allocation account is used to control the quota of an organization or cost center. The quotas of allocation accounts are allocated from the independent account level by level.
   >
   > - The account list displays only independent accounts. This helps you view the overall quota information about each level-1 organization or cost center.

<a id="section-7-2-5-3"></a>

#### 7.2.5.3. View the income and expenditure details of all accounts

This topic describes how to view the income and expenditure details of all accounts on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to view the income and expenditure details of all accounts and access the Budgets module.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. On the **Budgets** page, click **Income and expenditure details** in the **Budget Overview** section in the left-side pane.

5. In the upper part of the **Budget Account** section, select one or all cloud platforms.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and only if budgets are configured by organization.
   >
   > - If you select **All**, you can view the income and expenditure details of accounts on all cloud platforms.

6. View the income and expenditure details of accounts. In the **Advanced Filter** section above the list of income and expenditure details, configure filter conditions such as **Assign Accounts**, **Independent Account**, **Operator**, **Serial Number**, **Revenue and Expenditure Type**, **Flow Type**, **Account Period**, and **Billing Date** to filter data or search for specific data.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/179c9b3e35015b974a4078ab40ccf53d.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > **Flow Type**: You can select **Quota adjustment**, **Quota Allocation**, **Freeze**, **Freeze release**, or **Deduction**.
   >
   > - **Quota adjustment**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an independent account.
   >
   > - **Quota Allocation**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an allocation account.
   >
   > - **Freeze**: The system suspends the available quota based on the cloud service bill on a daily basis, or suspends the available quota when the system regenerates a bill.
   >
   > - **Freeze release**: The quota suspended in a month is released when the system generates the monthly bill.
   >
   > - **Deduction**: When the system generates a monthly bill, the system deducts the bill amount from the available quota and adds the bill amount to the used quota.

<a id="section-7-2-5-4"></a>

#### 7.2.5.4. View account details of a node

You can view the account details of a node on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and view account details.

**Limits**

- An operations administrator can view all nodes.

- If budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture, you can view only the organization to which you belong and its subordinate organizations.

- If budget accounts are configured based on the cost center architecture, you can view only the cost center for which you are authorized and its subordinate cost centers.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform or All from the cloud platform drop-down list.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node that you want to view.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can select **Show Deleted Accounts** to display the deleted nodes.

6. On the right side of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.

7. View the account details.

   - **Independent account details**

     > **Note**
     >
     > - By default, independent accounts are enabled and cannot be disabled.
     >
     > - An independent account is the master account of a level-1 organization or cost center. You can increase or reduce the quota of an independent account.
     >
     > - In single-cloud environments, select a level-1 node to view the independent account details of the node. In multi-cloud environments, select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, select a level-1 node, and then view the independent account details of the node.

     | Section | Description |
     | --- | --- |
     | Independent account | Displays the total budget quota within the level-1 node. You can adjust the account quota.<br>• Available quota = Total quota - Used quota - Frozen quota<br>• Frozen quota: The amount of the frozen quota is calculated based on the daily bill amount.<br>• Used quota: After a monthly bill is settled, the actual bill amount of the current month is the used quota. The used quota is deducted from the total quota, and the frozen quota is unfrozen. |
     | Budget allocation details | By default, the available budget of the current level-1 node is the quota of the independent account. After budgets are allocated to subordinate nodes, the budget quota of the current node is reduced accordingly.<br>• <strong>Current &amp; Subordinate</strong>: the overall quota information about the current node and its subordinate nodes.<br>• <strong>Current Budget Quota</strong>: The actual available quota for resource allocation at the current node is the sum of its allocation account quota and the quotas of its subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled.<br>• <strong>Current Allocation Account</strong>: the allocation account quota of the current node.<br>• <strong>Subordinate Allocation Account</strong>: the total quotas allocated from the current node to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled.<br>• <strong>The quota is allocated to the subordinate account.</strong>: the quotas allocated to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are enabled. |

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/37ba7a8470d685fed8b5f10f0f824743.jpeg)

   - **Allocation account details**

     > **Note**
     >
     > - In single-cloud environments, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on a specific cloud platform are allocation accounts.
     >
     > - In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

     <table>
       <tr>
         <td>Scenario</td>
         <td>Description</td>
       </tr>
     </table>

     <table>
       <tr>
         <td>Allocation accounts in single-cloud environments or allocation accounts of level-2 and lower nodes if you select <strong>All</strong> from the cloud platform drop-down list in multi-cloud environments</td>
         <td>• If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ecaf226574b9d8fdb49dd5ef74696222.jpeg" alt=""><br>• <strong>Parent Budget Quota</strong>: the quota of the nearest parent node for which quota allocation is enabled.<br>• <strong>Current Allocation Account</strong>: the quota information about the current account.<br>• If quota allocation is enabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account uses the budget quota of the node.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e2baf01b449b0af25155a51c43f21ab3.jpeg" alt=""><br>• <strong>Current &amp; Subordinate</strong>: the overall quota information about the current node and its subordinate nodes.<br>• <strong>Current Budget Quota</strong>: The actual available quota for resource allocation at the current node is the sum of its allocation account quota and the quotas of its subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled.<br>• <strong>Current Allocation Account</strong>: the allocation account quota of the current node.<br>• <strong>Subordinate Allocation Account</strong>: the total quotas allocated from the current node to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled.<br>• The quota is allocated to the subordinate <strong>account.</strong>: the quotas allocated to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are enabled.</td>
       </tr>
       <tr>
         <td>Allocation accounts of the nodes on the cloud platform selected from the cloud platform drop-down list in multi-cloud environments</td>
         <td>• If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node on the cloud platform selected from the cloud platform drop-down list, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9bc88765cc84ca3ed26d023d763e4a4c.jpeg" alt=""><br>• If quota allocation is enabled for the allocation account of a node on the cloud platform selected from the cloud platform drop-down list, the allocation account uses the budget quota of the node.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f8ca4ced2c4c74e6a2ffe17d1a9f1e23.jpeg" alt=""></td>
       </tr>
     </table>

<a id="section-7-2-5-5"></a>

#### 7.2.5.5. View the transaction details of a node

You can view the transaction details of a node on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, organization administrator, or organization resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and view account details.

**Limits**

- An operations administrator can view all nodes.

- If budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture, you can view only the organization to which you belong and its subordinate organizations.

- If budget accounts are configured based on the cost center architecture, you can view only the cost center for which you are authorized and its subordinate cost centers.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node that you want to view.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can select **Show Deleted Accounts** to display the deleted nodes.
   >
   > - In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

6. On the right side of the Budgets page, click the **Income and expenditure details** tab.

7. Click Advanced Filter and configure the following parameters to filter or search for specific transaction details: **Operator**, **Serial Number**, **Revenue and Expenditure Type**, **Flow Type**, **Account Period(UTC+08:00)**, and **Billing Date(UTC+08:00)**.

8. View the transaction details of the node.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d6f979606dffe0c114fd56543a56aa22.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - If the current node is a level-1 node, the transactions within the independent account of the node are displayed. In multi-cloud environments, if you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list and select a level-1 node, the transactions within the allocation account of the node are displayed.
   >
   > - If the current node is a level-2 or lower node, the transactions within the allocation account of the node are displayed. In multi-cloud environments, if you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list and select a node, the transactions within the allocation account of the node are displayed.
   >
   > - Valid values of the **Flow Type** parameter are **Quota adjustment**, **Quota Allocation**, **Freeze**, **Freeze release**, **Deduction**, and **Refund**.
   >
   >   - **Quota adjustment**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an independent account.
   >
   >   - **Quota Allocation**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an allocation account.
   >
   >   - **Freeze**: The system suspends the available quota based on the service bill on a daily basis, or suspends the available quota when the system regenerates a bill.
   >
   >   - **Freeze release**: The quota suspended in the month is released when the system generates the monthly bill.
   >
   >   - **Deduction**: When the system generates a monthly bill, the system deducts the bill amount from the available quota and adds the bill amount to the used quota.
   >
   >   - **Refund**: Refunds may be involved when users enable reversing reconciliation records, change the specifications of subscription resources, and unsubscribe from resources.

<a id="section-7-2-5-6"></a>

#### 7.2.5.6. Enable quota allocation

You can enable quota allocation for allocation accounts. After quota allocation is enabled for the allocation account of a node, you can allocate the quota to the allocation account and use the quota as the separate budget of the node and its subordinate nodes. For more information about how to allocate quotas, see Allocate quotas.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and allocate quotas.

- Quota allocation is disabled for an allocation account.

**Limits**

> **Note**
>
> - By default, quota allocation is disabled for allocation accounts. If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node.
>
> - If you want to manage the budget quota of a subordinate node in a more fine-grained manner, you can enable quota allocation for the node and allocate the available quota to the node.

- You can enable quota allocation only for allocation accounts.

- An operations administrator can enable quota allocation for all allocation accounts.

- Users can enable quota allocation for the subordinate nodes within their organization or their authorized cost center, and then allocate quotas to the subordinate nodes.

- Before you enable quota allocation for the allocation account of a node, you must enable quota allocation for the parent node of the node.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform or All from the cloud platform drop-down list.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node to which the allocation account belongs.

   > **Note**
   >
   > In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

6. On the right-side section of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.

7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Enable** in the upper-right corner of the Assign accounts section.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/07438c55c11f968a62d26fd164b408b1.jpeg)

8. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **Enable**.

<a id="section-7-2-5-7"></a>

#### 7.2.5.7. Disable quota allocation

You can disable quota allocation for allocation accounts. If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and allocate quotas.

- Quota allocation is enabled for an allocation account.

**Limits**

- An operations administrator can disable quota allocation for all allocation accounts.

- Users can disable quota allocation for the subordinate nodes within their organization or their authorized cost center.

- Before you disable quota allocation for a node, you must disable quota allocation for all its subordinate nodes and withdraw the quota allocated to the node. In this case, the total quota of the node is 0.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform or All from the cloud platform drop-down list.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node to which the allocation account belongs.

   > **Note**
   >
   > In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

6. On the right-side section of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.

7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Disable** in the upper-right corner of the Assign accounts section.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8903cbb39e055d96ae9fb796b8551ee0.jpeg)

8. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **Disable**.

<a id="section-7-2-5-8"></a>

#### 7.2.5.8. Adjust quotas

You can adjust quotas for the independent accounts of level-1 nodes based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and adjust quotas.

**Limits**

You can adjust quotas only for independent accounts.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select All from the cloud platform drop-down list.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture. In multi-cloud environments, if you want to adjust the quota for an independent account, select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list.
   >
   > - In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the level-1 node that you want to view.

6. On the right side of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.

7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Adjustment quota** in the upper-right corner.

8. In the **Adjustment quota** dialog box, configure the parameters to adjust the quota.

   | Paramete r | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Adjustm ent type | The adjustment type of the quota. Valid values: <strong>Increase</strong> or <strong>Decrease</strong>. |
   | Quota | The quota that you want to increase or decrease. The quota that you want to decrease cannot be greater than the total quota. |
   | Remarks | The description of the adjustment. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5cc5c27eccda692253308e166fbafa1a.jpeg)

9. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-2-5-9"></a>

#### 7.2.5.9. Allocate quotas

After the quota allocation feature is enabled for the allocation account of a node, you can allocate quotas to the node. This topic describes how to allocate quotas to a node.

**Prerequisites**

- The quota allocation feature is enabled for the allocation account of a node.

- You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to allocate quotas and access the Budgets module.

**Limits**

- When you configure budgets by organization, you can allocate budget quotas only to the subordinate organizations of the organization to which you belong, but not to the organization itself.

- When you configure budgets by cost center, you can allocate budget quotas only to the subordinate cost centers of the cost center that you are authorized to access, but not to the cost center itself.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.

4. On the Budgets page, select a cloud platform in the **Budget Account** section.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You need to select a cloud platform only in multi-cloud environments and when budgets are configured by organization.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node to which the allocation account belongs.

   > **Note**
   >
   > In multi-cloud environments, **all** nodes of level 2 and lower on the central cloud platform are allocation accounts, and all nodes of managed cloud platforms, including level-1 nodes, are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent nodes of the nodes on the managed cloud platforms refer to **all** nodes of the same level on the central cloud platform. If nodes of the same level on the central cloud platform are disabled, nodes of next higher level are used. For example, **all** level-1 nodes A (independent accounts) of the central cloud platform are the parent nodes of level-1 nodes A (allocation accounts) of the managed cloud platforms, and **all** level-2 nodes B (allocation accounts) of the central cloud platform are the parent nodes of level-2 nodes B (allocation accounts) of the managed cloud platforms.

6. On the right-side section of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.

7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Allocation quota** in the upper-right corner.

8. In the **Allocation quota** dialog box, configure the parameters to allocate quotas. The following table describes the parameters.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <th colspan="2">Parameter</th>
       <th>Description</th>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="2">Superior budget</td>
       <td>Superior allocation account</td>
       <td>The allocation account of the parent node.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Superior available quota</td>
       <td>The quota available to the parent node.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="3">Current account status</td>
       <td>Cloud Platform</td>
       <td>The cloud platform to which the allocation account belongs. This parameter is displayed only when the quota is allocated to the allocation account of a node on the managed cloud platform in multi-cloud environments.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Total budget quota at this level</td>
       <td>The total budget quota of the current node.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Available budget quota at this level</td>
       <td>The budget quota available to the current node.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="3">Allocation quota</td>
       <td>Adjustme nt type</td>
       <td>The adjustment type of the quota. Valid values: <strong>Increase</strong> and <strong>Decrease</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Quota</td>
       <td>The quota that you want to increase or decrease. The quota that you want to increase cannot be greater than the quota available to the parent node. The quota that you want to decrease cannot be greater than the total budget quota available to the current node.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Remarks</td>
       <td>The description of the adjustment.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fcf6bd94db009864be7e1c1275dceaaf.jpeg)

9. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-2-6"></a>

### 7.2.6. Alibaba Cloud platform accounts

You can query the quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts on the Public Cloud Account page.

<a id="section-7-2-6-1"></a>

#### 7.2.6.1. View quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts

This topic describes how to view the accounts of Alibaba Cloud platforms added to the central cloud platform and quotas of the Alibaba Cloud platform accounts.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a resource auditor.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Public Cloud Account**.

4. On the **Public Cloud Account** page, view the accounts of Alibaba Cloud platforms added to the central cloud platform.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can perform fuzzy search on the Public Cloud Account page.
   >
   > - The Public Cloud Account page displays all enabled accounts of the added Alibaba Cloud platforms. An account card displays the name, status, and remaining quota of the account.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/eb00eb3b54b3926c17189d600d2bbc11.jpeg)

5. Click the card of the account that you want to view to go to the **Billing Account** page available to the account.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ff4c5e7b3956373e9d3eaae8d5a72912.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-2-6-2"></a>

#### 7.2.6.2. Configure an alert rule for quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts

After you configure an alert rule for quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts, if the available quota of an Alibaba Cloud platform account is less than the specified threshold, an alert notification is sent to the specified contacts. This topic describes how to configure an alert rule for quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Public Cloud Account**.

4. On the **Public Cloud Account** page, click **Alert Settings** in the upper-right corner.

5. In the **Alert Settings** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |

   | Alarm Switch | Specifies whether to enable alerting. Valid values: <strong>Open</strong> and <strong>Close</strong>. |
   | --- | --- |
   | Alert Threshold | The alert threshold. If the available quota of an Alibaba Cloud platform account is less than the specified threshold, an alert notification is sent to the specified contacts. The system checks the available quota of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts at 9:00 every day. |
   | Alert Object | The alert recipient. Valid values: <strong>Organization Administrator/Cost Unit</strong> <strong>Authorized User</strong> and <strong>Operations Administrator</strong>. You can select both options. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3e9565ce70f9a031a38dfd3420974505.jpeg)

6. Click **Save**.

#### 7.2.7.3. Modify a contract

This topic describes how to modify a contract.

- A contract is in the **Disable** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.

This topic describes how to enable a contract in the Disable state.

**Prerequisites**

- A contract is in the **Disable** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.

4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then click **Search** to search for contracts.

#### 7.2.7.5. Disable a contract

This topic describes how to disable a contract that is in the Enable state but remains ineffective.

**Prerequisites**

- A contract is in the **Enable** state and the current date is earlier than the start date of the validity period of the contract.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.

4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then click **Search** to search for contracts.

#### 7.2.7.6. Terminate a contract

This topic describes how to terminate an effective contract in the Enable state.

**Prerequisites**

- A contract is in the **Enable** state and the current date is later than the start date but earlier than the end date of the validity period of the contract.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

You can terminate a contract only once.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.

4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then click **Search** to search for contracts.

5. In the contract list, view the information about the contracts.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/776d5699d6efae4d457bfecfdacf5910.jpeg)

6. Find the contract that you want to terminate, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3347b63b7ae0b9a5e1384ea59f26fb57.png" width="15" alt=""> icon in the

   **Actions** column, and then select **Terminate**.

7. In the **Terminate Contract** dialog box, specify the date when the contract ends.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/34204aa6a2b115fa19d8c31170bad97c.jpeg)

8. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-2-7-7"></a>

#### 7.2.7.7. Delete a contract

This topic describes how to delete a contract that is no longer required.

**Prerequisites**

- A contract is in the **Disable** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.

4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then click **Search** to search for contracts.

5. In the contract list, view the information about the contracts.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/776d5699d6efae4d457bfecfdacf5910.jpeg)

6. Find the contract that you want to delete, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3347b63b7ae0b9a5e1384ea59f26fb57.png" width="15" alt=""> icon in the **Actions**

### 7.2.8. Pricing

<a id="section-7-2-8-1"></a>

#### 7.2.8.1. Pricing

<a id="section-7-2-8-1-1"></a>

##### 7.2.8.1.1. Price calculator

The price calculator calculates the estimated costs based on cloud service configurations in the deployment cloud environment and region, and allows you to add items to a configuration list.

**Prerequisites**

You can enable price inquiry as a platform administrator. To do so, you can perform the following operations: Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Billing Switch**.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu and

   click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/405153070d85adac06eed3b78d73d9ac.png" width="17" alt=""> icon to open the price calculator.

3. On the **Pricing** page, click the **Price Calculator** tab.

4. Select a cloud service from the left-side **Product List** and select configurations in the right-side section. Then, view the estimated fee and billing details.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can enter the name of a cloud service in the search box to quickly find the cloud service.
   >
   > - In multi-cloud environments, you can select different cloud platforms from the cloud platform drop-down list on the right side to view the fee and billing details of cloud services on different cloud platforms.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/399e89ba650be182014a02bdd571dbb8.jpeg)

5. Click **Add to List** in the lower part of the page.

6. In the **Please choose to join the list** dialog box, select a list from the **List to be added** drop-down list.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c35c7ad6ad502189f31725ff08636592.jpeg)

7. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-2-8-1-2"></a>

##### 7.2.8.1.2. Configuration list

The configuration list displays the list that you create and the service configurations that have been added to the list.

**Prerequisites**

You have enabled price inquiry as a platform administrator. To do so, you can perform the following operations: Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Billing Switch**. On the Billing Switch page, turn on the Price Inquiry Switch.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu, and

   then click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/405153070d85adac06eed3b78d73d9ac.png" width="17" alt=""> icon to go to the Pricing page.

3. On the **Pricing** page, click the **Optional list** tab.

4. Select a saved list from the **Current list** drop-down list to view the configuration details of the list.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/94eeafcd40eae780579a74d49d00baef.png" width="11" alt=""> icon before a service name to show the billable items.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/bb2d0620f1a43fa95f5de3a66e497262.jpeg)

5. Perform operations as needed.

   | Operation | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Save a list | i. Select <strong>Default List</strong> from the <strong>Current list</strong> drop-down list.<br>ii. Click <strong>SAVE list</strong> below the list.<br>iii. In the <strong>New List</strong> dialog box, configure the <strong>List name</strong> parameter.<br>iv. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Delete a list | i. Click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d8b9ff5cf97d4d547099e3a54f719b73.png" width="16" alt="">icon on the right side of <strong>Current list</strong>.<br>ii. In the dialog box that appears, select the list that you want to delete.<br>Important<br>• You cannot delete the default list. You can delete only custom lists.<br>• After you delete a custom list, the service configurations in the custom list are automatically moved to the default list.<br>iii. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Add configurati ons to a list | i. Select the list to which you want to add configurations from the <strong>Current list</strong> drop-down list.<br>ii. Click <strong>Add configuration</strong> below the list to go to the <strong>Price Calculator</strong> tab.<br>iii. For more information, see Price calculator. Select the service that you want to configure and add it to the list. |
   | Remove configurati ons from a list | • Remove a single configuration<br>a. Select a list from the <strong>Current list</strong> drop-down list.<br>b. Find the configuration that you want to remove and click <strong>Remove</strong> in the <strong>Operation</strong> column.<br>c. Click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>• Remove multiple configurations at a time<br>a. Select a list from the <strong>Current list</strong> drop-down list.<br>b. In the list, select multiple configurations that you want to remove.<br>c. Click <strong>Batch Remove</strong> below the list.<br>d. Click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Change configurati ons | i. Select a list from the <strong>Current list</strong> drop-down list.<br>ii. In the list, click <strong>Change configuration</strong> in the <strong>Operation</strong> column to go to the <strong>Price Calculator</strong> tab.<br>iii. On the Price Calculator tab, update the service configurations and click <strong>Add to</strong> <strong>List</strong>. |
   | Export a list | i. Select a list from the <strong>Current list</strong> drop-down list.<br>ii. Click <strong>Export List</strong> below the list.<br>iii. After the list export is complete, click <strong>Download link</strong> to download the price calculation list file in the <strong>.xlsx</strong> format to your computer. |

<a id="section-7-2-8-1-3"></a>

##### 7.2.8.1.3. Service pricing

The Service Pricing tab displays the pricing details of services and the pricing information that has been configured for each service in the billing rule.

**Usage notes**

> **Important**
>
> The prices displayed on this page are for reference only. They are not updated in real time and are not associated with discounts. To query the actual prices, go to the buy page of the cloud service that you want to buy.

**Prerequisites**

You enable price inquiry as a platform administrator. To do so, you can perform the following operations: Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Billing Switch**. On the Billing Switch page, turn on the Price Inquiry Switch.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd11b7663a920dbab0ed28bf1fafdbb3.png" width="24" alt=""> icon to show the floating menu, and

   then click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/405153070d85adac06eed3b78d73d9ac.png" width="17" alt=""> icon to go to the Pricing page.

3. On the **Pricing** page, click the **Service Pricing** tab.

4. On the left side of the Service Pricing tab, select a cloud service from the **Product List**. Then, view the service pricing details in the right-side section.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can enter the name of a cloud service in the search box to quickly find the cloud service.
   >
   > - In multi-cloud environments, you can select different cloud platforms from the cloud platform drop-down list on the right side to view the pricing details of cloud services on different cloud platforms.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a15de31c8ff0afa4c85914880af80bf1.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-2-8-2"></a>

#### 7.2.8.2. Billing configuration overview

On the Rule Overview page, you can view the timeline of each billing configuration in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. The timeline displays the validity period of the billing configuration.

**Background information**

On the Rule Overview page, each billing configuration is displayed in a timeline, which displays the validity period of the billing configuration. This helps you trace the historical billing configuration changes. You can also view billing configurations by day, week, month, quarter, and year. This helps enterprises more clearly and efficiently understand their costs and implement fine-grained operations and cost optimization.

**Prerequisites**

Billing configurations are created.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rules**.

4. On the **Rule Overview** page, view the validity period of each billing configuration in the Gantt chart.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/27eb6955ffebde6483f5b377f74aadfd.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > By default, billing configurations are displayed by month. The name of a billing configuration contains the validity period of the billing configuration.

   - **Change the time span of the Gantt chart**: Click **Day View** in the upper-right corner and select **Week View**, **Month View**, **Quarter View**, or **Year View** from the drop-down list.

   - **Search for billing configurations**: In the navigation tree, enter a keyword in the search box above the billing configuration list.

   - **View the details of a billing configuration**: In the navigation tree, find the billing configuration that you want to view and click its name. The **Billing Configuration Detail** page appears On the **Billing Configuration Detail** page, view the details of the billing configuration.

<a id="section-7-2-8-3-2"></a>

##### 7.2.8.3.2. Cloud services that support price inquiries

After you turn on the price inquiry switch, the system displays cost information during service usage when you create (activate), reconfigure (scale up), unsubscribe (delete or release), renew, use the CPQ, or view orders.

**Enable the pricing inquiry switch**

The platform administrator turns on the price inquiry switch in **Configuration** > **Billing Switch**. For detailed operations, see Configure the billing feature on the Billing Switch page.

**Cost description**

- For cloud services that support the pay-as-you-go billing method, the system displays cost information during new purchase, configuration change (if supported), CPQ, and order processing. The displayed cost represents the unit price of the product.

- FFor cloud services that support the subscription billing method, the system displays cost information during new purchase, configuration change (if supported), unsubscription, renewal, CPQ, and order processing. The displayed cost represents the total amount payable for the product.

  - Date calculation rules

    - New purchase: The purchase day is not billed. If you activate and unsubscribe on the same day, no fee applies. For example, if you purchase a one-month subscription on January 1, 2024, the billing cycle runs from 00:00:00 on January 2, 2024 to 00:00:00 on February 2, 2024.

    - Configuration change: On the day of the change, the system bills based on the previous specification. Starting the next day, the system bills based on the new specification.

    - Renewal: The renewal period starts from the day after the instance expires.

    - Unsubscription: The system bills for the day of unsubscription.

  - Use the following formulas to calculate payable amounts during configuration change, unsubscription, and renewal:

    - Payable amount for configuration change or unsubscription (monthly billing) = Unused fee - (Paid fee - Consumed fee)

      > **Note**
      >
      > - Consumed fee: the fee consumed by this instance during the past period
      >
      > - Paid fee: The total fee already paid for this instance during the past period. This includes fees paid during initial purchase, each configuration change, and each renewal.
      >
      > - Unused fee: The fee required for future usage. The future specification may be the new specification or the current specification.

    - Payable amount for renewal (monthly billing) = Number of renewal months x Monthly unit price

**Cloud services that support price inquiry in Enterprise Edition**

In multi-cloud scenarios, Enterprise Edition supports price inquiry for all cloud services available in the corresponding edition (excluding custom services).

**Fee display examples**

> **Note**
>
> - Configuration cost: shows the unit price or payable amount for a resource item.
>
>   If the resource has associated resources, their costs also appear. For example, when you purchase a new ECS instance, the system also displays the cost of its associated disks<strong>.</strong> ECS disk (EBS) cost: shows the unit price of the ECS disk resource item associated with the ECS instance.
>
> - Cost details/View details: Move the pointer over this link to view the original and discounted prices for the resource item. If associated resources exist, their details also appear. For example, under ECS cost details, the system also displays cost details for the associated ECS disk (EBS) resource item.
>
>   - Original price: the sum of the original prices for all billable items
>
>   - Discounted price: the sum of the discounted prices for all billable items
>
>     - Discounted price = Total price × Discount rate
>
>       The system automatically truncates any amount beyond the seventh decimal place and excludes it from the discounted price.
>
>     - Under the discounted price, the system displays each billable item and its corresponding discounted price.
>
>       For example, in the Elasticsearch cost details, items such as "Pricing by primary node CPU", "Pricing by primary node memory", and "Pricing by data node CPU" represent billable items.
>
>     - Coupon: If a coupon is used for a resource, the system also displays the coupon amount.
>
> - When you change the configuration of a service, a price difference may occur.
>
>   - For pay-as-you-go billing, the price difference represents the difference between the unit prices before and after the configuration change.
>
>   - For subscription billing, a positive number indicates the amount the user must pay to cover the difference, while a negative number indicates the amount to refund to the user.
>
> - When you unsubscribe from a service, you may receive a refund. The system automatically truncates any amount beyond the third decimal place in the calculated refund. The used duration is calculated in full days, and any partial day counts as one full day.

##### 7.2.8.3.3. Public cloud product pricing mode description

The billing switch supports usage-based pricing and cost rate. The cost rate applies to all integrated public cloud products. The usage-based pricing applies only to public cloud products that have metering data and billing rules.

> **Note**
>
> - Usage-based pricing: The system prices resources based on billing rules and pricing factors from metering data. It calculates the resale amount for public cloud services by applying billing rules to public cloud metering data.
>
> - Price multiplier pricing: The resale amount for public cloud services equals the cost amount on the public cloud bill multiplied by the price multiplier.
>
> - When you set the pricing mode to usage-based pricing, the system cannot generate bills for cloud services that support only the cost rate.
