<a id="section-7-4-1-2"></a>

#### 7.4.1.2. View sites

On the Sites page, you can view the site list and the details of a site.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. On the Sites page, view all created sites.

   - You can enter a site name in the search box above the site list and click the Search icon to efficiently filter sites by site name.

   - You can click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2b6ed2780079bf05dc6365e30342b59d.png" width="15" alt=""> icon next to the **Status** field to filter sites by status.

   - You can click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b41059c3b680dfe0a79e29fc54a7e009.png" width="14" alt=""> icon next to the **Launch Time** field to sort sites in ascending or

     descending order.

5. Click the name of a site to go to the site details page.

6. On the site details page, view the basic information, navigations, and associated pages of the site.

   - **Site Information**: displays the name, status, URL, description, platform logo, theme color, and browser icon of the site and the status of the footer feature.

   - **Navigation Configuration**: displays the navigation configurations of the site. For more information about how to configure a site navigation, see Configure a site navigation.

   - **Page List**: displays the pages associated with the site. For more information about how to configure a site page, see Configure a site page.

<a id="section-7-4-1-3"></a>

#### 7.4.1.3. Modify the information and homepage of a site

After a site is created, you can modify the site information based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage and click **Edit** in the Operation column.

   Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Edit** in the upper-right corner.

5. In the **Edit Site** dialog box, modify the site information such as basic information, theme color configurations, and brand configurations based on your business requirements. For more information about the parameters, see Create a site.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When you modify a site, you can configure the Home Page parameter in the Basic Information section to select a page as the site homepage based on your business requirements. Before you select a page as the homepage, make sure that the page is created.

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-1-4"></a>

#### 7.4.1.4. Configure a site navigation

After a site is created, you can configure navigations for the site.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage and click **Configure Navigation** in the Operation column.

5. On the **Navigation Configuration** tab of the site details page, click **Add Navigation**.

6. In the **Add Navigation** dialog box, configure the parameters and click **OK**. The following table describes the parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Navigation Name | Enter a name for the navigation. |
   | Parent Navigation | Select the parent navigation to which the navigation belongs. |
   | Sort | Specify the order in which the navigation is displayed. A smaller value indicates a higher priority. |
   | Navigation Type | Select the type of the navigation. Valid values: <strong>Parent Navigation Group</strong>, <strong>Page Navigation</strong>, and <strong>Third-party Link</strong>. |
   | Associated page | Specify the page with which the navigation is associated. This parameter is displayed only if you set the <strong>Navigation Type</strong> parameter to <strong>Page</strong> <strong>Navigation</strong>.<br>If no option is available in the drop-down list, create a page first. |
   | Third-party Link | Enter the URL of the third-party page with which the navigation is associated.This parameter is displayed only if you set the <strong>Navigation Type</strong> parameter to <strong>Third-party Link</strong>. |
   | Open Mode | Select the method for going to the page with which the navigation is associated. This parameter is displayed only if you set the <strong>Navigation Type</strong> parameter to <strong>Page Navigation</strong>.<br>Valid values: <strong>New Window Opens</strong> and <strong>The Current Window Opens</strong>. |
   | Show or Not | Specify whether to display the navigation and its child navigations. If you set the value to No, the navigation and its child navigations are not displayed. |
   | Display time | Valid values: <strong>Instant Display</strong> and <strong>Scheduled Display</strong>.<br>• <strong>Instant Display</strong>: The navigation is displayed on the portal immediately after you submit the configurations.<br>• <strong>Scheduled Display</strong>: The navigation is displayed on the portal at the specified time. |
   | Time setting | This parameter is displayed only if you set the <strong>Display time</strong> parameter to <strong>Scheduled Display</strong>. Select a start time and an end time. The time is accurate to the second.<br>The start time is required. If the start time is earlier than the current time, the system displays the navigation immediately after you submit the configurations.<br>The end time is optional. If you do not specify an end time, the navigation remains displayed. |

7. On the Navigation Configuration tab, manage the navigation based on your business requirements.

   - To modify the site navigation, click **Edit** in the Operation column.

   - To add a child navigation, click **Add Sub-navigation** in the Operation column.

   - To delete the site navigation, click **Delete** in the Operation column.

<a id="section-7-4-1-5"></a>

#### 7.4.1.5. Configure site pages

After you create a site, configure its pages.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Sites**.

4. On the sites list, click the site name to go to the site details page.

5. On the **Pages** tab, click **Create Page**.

6. In the **Create Page** dialog box, configure the page settings and click **Confirm**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b384f5859b87286a02c16db72262dff3.jpeg)

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Page Template | Select a page template. You can quickly create a page based on a template. If you use a template, the system automatically applies the basic page information and layout configuration. |
   | Page Name | Enter a custom page name. The name must be 1 to 30 characters in length and cannot duplicate an existing page name. |
   | ID | Enter an English identifier for the page. The identifier must be 1 to 30 characters in length, start with a lowercase letter, and can contain only lowercase letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-). It cannot duplicate an existing page identifier.<br>Changing the identifier affects the page URL. If other pages reference this URL, update those references accordingly. |
   | Page Type | You can select only <strong>Low code build</strong>. |
   | Site | The system displays the site name by default. |
   | Page Description | Enter a description for the site page. The description must be 1 to 200 characters in length. |

7. After you configure the site page, you can modify, remove, build content for, or preview the page as needed.

   - Click **Edit** in the Actions column to modify the basic page configuration.

   - Click **View Page** in the Actions column to view the published page.

   - Click **Page Building** in the Actions column to create or update the page layout and content.

   - Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt=""> **Version Management** in the Actions column to go to the page history

     versions. You can view and restore historical versions.

   - Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt=""> **Remove** in the Actions column to remove the page from the site. After removal,

     the site becomes empty.

<a id="section-7-4-1-6"></a>

#### 7.4.1.6. Customize the style of a site

If the preset site styles do not meet your business requirements, you can configure custom site styles. Page-level styles take precedence over global site styles. If no conflicts are involved, both the configured site styles and page styles take effect.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. Click the name of a site to go to the site details page.

5. On the site details page, click **Style Settings** in the upper-right corner.

6. In the **Page Style** dialog box, enter the CSS code for configuring the style.

   Example:

   ```text
   body {
   background-color: black;
   }
   ```

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8bf956161daeb4ca645a7a6dff1ece5d.jpeg)

7. Click **OK**. After the site style is saved, it takes effect immediately.

<a id="section-7-4-1-7"></a>

#### 7.4.1.7. Preview a site

After you configure the homepage, navigations, and pages of a site, you can preview the site and check the display effects of the site to ensure that the site works as expected.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage and click **Preview** in the Operation column.

   Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Preview** in the upper-right corner.

5. On the page that appears, view the display effects of the site.

<a id="section-7-4-1-8"></a>

#### 7.4.1.8. Publish a site

Before you publish a site, make sure that all navigations are associated with pages and the associated pages are published. You can preview the display effects of the site to ensure that the site works as expected before it is published.

**Prerequisites**

- Sites are in the **Offline** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt="">

   icon in the Operation column, and then select **Online**.

   Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Online** in the upper-right corner.

5. In the dialog box that appears, enter a description and click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-1-9"></a>

#### 7.4.1.9. Unpublish a site

You can unpublish a site based on your business requirements. After a site is unpublished, users cannot view the site.

**Prerequisites**

- Sites are in the **Online** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt="">

   icon in the Operation column, and then select **Offline**.

   Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Offline** in the upper-right corner.

5. In the dialog box that appears, enter a description and click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-1-10"></a>

#### 7.4.1.10. Delete a site

You can delete a site that you no longer use.

**Prerequisites**

- Sites are in the **Offline** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.

4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt="">

   icon in the Operation column, and then select **Delete**.

   Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Delete** in the upper-right corner.

5. In the message that appears, click **Delete**.

<a id="section-7-4-1-11"></a>

#### 7.4.1.11. How users access a site

This topic describes how users access a site.

After you publish a site, you can obtain its endpoint on the site details page. Users can visit the site by using this endpoint.

The endpoint format is:  `https://${sitekey}.operation.${internet.domain}/coms/protal/${token}` .

> **Note**
>
> - ${sitekey}: The custom identifier that you set when creating the site.
>
> - ${internet.domain}: The root domain of the tenant.
>
> - /coms/portal/${token}: The path to the site homepage. You can view the specific path in the page list. When you disable the **URL Token** feature, the endpoint does not include ${token}.

<a id="section-7-4-2"></a>

### 7.4.2. Page management

<a id="section-7-4-2-1"></a>

#### 7.4.2.1. Pages

During the lifecycle of a site, you can perform operations such as maintaining, updating, and optimizing the content and structure of the site pages based on your business requirements. This ensures the efficiency and accuracy of site information and good user experience.

**Background information**

Pages are the important components of a site. Each page carries specific information or features to provide services. You can specify a page as the homepage of a site or associate a page with a site navigation based on your business requirements.

**Permissions on pages in different states**

> **Note**
>
> Pages may be in the states described in the following table. Different operations can be performed on pages in different states. In the following table, ✓ indicates that the operation is supported, and × indicates that the operation is not supported.

| State/Operation | Mod ify a pag e | Pre vie w a pag e | Buil d a pag e | Save a page (with updates) | Pub lish a pag e | Dele te a page | Revo ke the publ ishin g of a page | View the revie w detai ls of a page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Draft | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |
| To be published as scheduled | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | × |
| Draft (being reviewed for publishing) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | ✓ |
| Draft (review rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Draft (publishing failed) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |
| Published | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | × |
| Published (modifications to be published) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |
| Published (modifications to be published as scheduled) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | × |
| Published (being reviewed for publishing modifications) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published (review for publishing modifications rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Published (failed to publish modifications) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-1"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.1. Create a page

Create a new page and configure its basic information.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is an operations administrator by default.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Page Management** > **Page List**.

4. On the **Page List** page, click **Create Page**.

5. In the **Create Page** dialog box, configure the basic settings for the page.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c5c1b545252100cece892dc788b29aec.jpeg)

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Page Template | Select a page template. You can quickly create a page based on a template. If you use a template, the system automatically imports the basic page information and layout configuration. |
   | Page Name | Enter a custom name for the page. The name must be 1 to 60 characters in length and cannot duplicate an existing page name. |
   | ID | Enter an English identifier for the page. This identifier generates the page path.It must be 1 to 30 characters long, start with a lowercase letter, and contain only lowercase letters, digits, underscores (_), or hyphens (-). It cannot duplicate an existing page identifier.<br>Changing the English identifier affects the page’s URL. If other pages reference this URL, update those references accordingly. |
   | Page Type | You can select only <strong>Low code build</strong>. |
   | Site | Select the site to which the page belongs.<br>If no sites are available, go to the Site Management page to create a new site. |
   | Page Description | Enter a description for the page. The description must be 1 to 200 characters in length. |

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-2"></a>

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Page Management** > **Pages**.

4. Click **Advanced Filter**. Then, configure the following filter conditions as needed and click **Search**: **Page Name**, **Page Path**, **Site**, **Navigation**, **Page Description**, **Release Time**, and **Update Time**.

5. In the page list, view the information about pages.

   > **Note**

   >
   > - You can click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6a06d93fe1b858c97c9dab2d6c25c22b.png" width="14" alt=""> icon next to the **Release Time** field to sort pages in
   >
   >   ascending or descending order.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3b34f69ae99e43355d383395fbccf5ba.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-3"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.3. Edit page

Update the basic information of the page when necessary.

**Prerequisites**

- The page is in one of the following states: **Draft**, **Draft (Publishing approval rejected)**, **Draft (Publishing failed)**, **Published**, **Published (Modification pending publishing)**, **Published (Modification publishing approval rejected)**, or **Published (Modification publishing failed)**.

- The operator must be an Operations Administrator by default.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Page Management** > **Page List**.

4. On the **Page List** page, click **Edit** in the Actions column.

5. In the **Edit page** dialog box, modify the page information as needed. For configuration item descriptions, see Create a page.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5fb0f9421d889ca15b1e8893452f6b1e.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-4"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.4. Page building

Use page building to configure page content and architecture.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Page management** > **Page list**.

4. On the **Page List** page, click **Page Building** in the Actions column.

5. On the **Page Building** page, add components and materials as needed to build the page.

   - Left side: displays the outline, components, and versions.

     - Outline: displays components that you have added to the page. You can manage these components, including moving, cloning, and deleting them.

     - Components: supported component categories include Navigation, Card, Image and text, Display card, Display component, and Others. Add components to the page as needed.

     - Versions: displays historical version information of the page. You can specify a time range to quickly find a version. You can view or restore a historical version as needed.

   - Middle: displays components that you have added. After you select a component, you can move it up, move it down, clone it, or delete it.

   - Right side: provides settings for the page and components.

     - Page settings: include theme style, background color, background material, and footer display settings.

       - Theme style: configure CSS style code for the page. Page styles take precedence over global site styles. If no style conflicts exist, both site and page styles take effect.

       - Background color: enter a color code (such as #d0021b) in the input box or click the color picker to select a color.

       - Background material: supports **Local Upload** or **Material Center**. Format requirements: JPG or PNG. Size requirements: width 3840 pixels, height customizable.

       - Display footer: footer content is displayed based on the footer configuration of the associated site. If the site does not enable the footer, the footer cannot be displayed.

     - Component settings: configuration items vary by component. You can perform personalized configurations as needed. After you select a target component in the middle section, the right section displays component-related configurations. You can configure the component as needed.

6. After you complete page building, click **Save** in the upper-right corner.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Click **Undo** or **Recovery** to quickly adjust the page during page building.
   >
   > - Click **Preview** to preview the display effect of the page during page building.
   >
   > - Click **Publish** to publish the built page.
   >
   > - Click **View Page** to view the content displayed on the published page. This operation is available only for pages in the Published state.

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-5"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.5. Publish page

You can publish a page multiple times. Each publication generates a version that records the current content of the page.

**Prerequisites**

- The page is in one of the following states: **Draft**, **Draft (publishing approval rejected)**, **Draft (publishing failed)**, **Published (modified, pending publication)**, **Published (modified, publishing approval rejected)**, or **Published (modified, publishing failed)**.

- By default, the operating user is an Operations Administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Page Management** > **Page list**.

4. Publish the page.

   - **Publish a single page**: On the **Page list** page, click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt=""> in the Actions column and

     select **Publish**. Alternatively, enter the page builder, complete and save the page content, then click **Publish** in the upper-right corner.

   - **Batch publish pages**: On the **Page list** page, select multiple pages you want to publish, then click **Batch Publish** at the bottom of the list.

5. In the **Page Publishing** dialog box, select a publishing time. You can choose **Publish now** or **Scheduled release**.

   - **Publish now**: The page updates immediately after you confirm publication.

   - **Scheduled release**: After selecting scheduled release, set the time below. The page content will update at the specified time. After scheduling a release, if you need to modify the time, you must first cancel the scheduled release and then republish.

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-6"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.6. Revoke the publishing of a page

You can revoke the publishing of a page on the Page List page.

**Prerequisites**

- Pages are in the **To be published as scheduled**, **Draft (being reviewed for publishing)**, **Published (modifications to be published as scheduled)**, or **Published (being reviewed for publishing modifications)** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Page Management** > **Pages**.

4. On the **Page List** page, find the page that you want to manage, move the pointer over the

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt=""> icon in the Operation column, and then select **Revoke Publishing**.

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-7"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.7. View the review details of a page

After publishing review is enabled, you can view the review details of pages that are in review or pages whose review is rejected.

**Prerequisites**

- Pages are in the **Draft (being reviewed for publishing)**, **Draft (review rejected)**, **Published (being reviewed for publishing modifications)**, or **Published (review for publishing modifications rejected)** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Page Management** > **Pages**.

4. On the **Page List** page, find the page that you want to manage, move the pointer over the

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt=""> icon in the Operation column, and then select **View Approval Details**.

5. On the page that appears, view the review details.

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-8"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.8. View a published page

You can view a page only after the page is published.

**Prerequisites**

- Pages are in the **Published** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Page Management** > **Pages**.

4. On the **Page List** page, find the page that you want to manage and click **View Page** in the Operation column.

   Alternatively, go to the Page Construction page and click **View page** in the upper-right corner.

5. On the page that appears, view the displayed content of the published page.

<a id="section-7-4-2-1-9"></a>

##### 7.4.2.1.9. Manage the versions of a page

Each time a page is published, a version is generated to record the current content of the page. You can view and restore the historical versions of pages.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Page Management** > **Pages**.

4. On the **Page List** page, find the page that you want to manage, move the pointer over the

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt=""> icon in the Operation column, and then select **Version Management**.

5. In the **Page history** panel, view and restore the historical versions of the page as needed.

   - Find the version that you want to view and click **View** in the Operation column.

   - Find a version and click **Recovery** in the Operation column to restore the page to the selected version. After the page is restored, you must publish the page again to make the page take effect.

You can copy a page of a site to quickly add a page of the same content to the site.

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Page Management** > **Pages**.

4. On the **Page List** page, find the page that you want to manage, move the pointer over the

##### 7.4.2.1.11. Delete a page

You can delete a page that you no longer need.

**Prerequisites**

- Pages are disassociated from sites.

- Pages are in the **Draft**, **Draft (review rejected)**, **Draft (publishing failed)**, **Published**, **Published (modifications to be published)**, **Published (review for publishing modifications rejected)**, or **Published (failed to publish modifications)** state.

- You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Page Management** > **Pages**.

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52fdb4e9c9d166b6962797cbcc027abf.png" width="21" alt=""> icon in the Operation column, and then select **Delete**.

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-3"></a>

### 7.4.3. Material center

You can upload, modify, and delete site materials such as images and videos as needed.

**Background information**

The material center manages the material resources required by the site, including images and videos, so that administrators can quickly find and use them when managing the site.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is an operations administrator by default.

**Upload images and videos**

Upload the image and video materials required by the site to the material center.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Material Center**.

4. On the **Material Center** page, click **Upload Material**.

5. In the **Upload Material** dialog box, enter the **Material Name**, select the **Material Type** (image or video), and then click **Upload Material** to add a file.

   > **Important**
   >
   > - Image format and size requirements:
   >
   >   - The system supports gif, png, jpg, jpeg, and GIF formats.
   >
   >   - The image size must not exceed 6 MB.
   >
   > - Video format, resolution, and size requirements:
   >
   >   - The system supports common video formats. We recommend using mp4, mkv, or mov formats.
   >
   >   - The resolution must be 360p (640 pixels × 360 pixels) or higher.
   >
   >   - The video file size must not exceed 5 GB.

6. Click OK.

**Preview materials**

After you upload materials, you can preview the uploaded images and videos.

1. At the top of the **Material Center** page, search for materials by material name, material type (All, Image, or Video), group, or associated page.

2. The material card displays the material type, format, and latest update time. Hover over the material card and click **Preview** to preview the material.

**Modify the material name or update an image**

Update the name or content of an image or video when necessary.

> **Important**
>
> You cannot edit preset materials.

1. Hover over the material card and click **Edit**.

2. In the **Edit material** dialog box, modify the material name or add a file.

3. Click OK.

**Delete materials**

Delete images, videos, and other resources when they are no longer needed.

> **Important**
>
> - You cannot delete preset materials.
>
> - Before you delete a material, make sure that no page references it.

1. Hover over the material card and click **Delete**.

2. In the dialog box, click OK.

<a id="section-7-4-4"></a>

### 7.4.4. Component management

<a id="section-7-4-4-1"></a>

#### 7.4.4.1. Add components

When you build a service portal, if the preset components cannot meet your business requirements, you can use the component management feature to add custom components.

**Background information**

Components are classified into preset components and custom components.

- Preset components are standardized components that are predefined by the system and have common features and styles. When you build a service portal, you can directly use the preset components to improve development efficiency.

- Custom components are components that are designed and developed by users based on business requirements. If the preset components cannot meet the business requirements, developers can add custom components based on the project requirements and component development kit specifications.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.

4. On the **Component Management** page, click **Add components**.

5. In the **Add components** panel, configure the basic information about the component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can click **Download component development kit** to download the component development kit to your computer.
   >
   > - You can click **Custom Component Description** to view the description of the custom component.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Compone nt name | The unique name of the component. The name must be 1 to 30 characters in length. |
   | Compone nt Key | The component key, which indicates the unique identifier of the component. The key must be 1 to 60 characters in length and cannot be the same as an existing component key. |
   | Type | The type of the component. Valid values: <strong>Navigation</strong>, <strong>Card</strong>, <strong>Graphic and text</strong>, <strong>Display Card</strong>, <strong>Display components</strong>, and <strong>Other</strong>. |
   | Grouping | The group to which the component belongs. You can select multiple groups.<br>• <strong>Create a group</strong>: Click <strong>Add Group</strong>, enter a group name in the field, and then click <strong>Save and use</strong>.<br>• <strong>Modify a group</strong>: Move the pointer over the group and click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b824441d351e5c8079225e7b13c9aa1d.png" width="12" alt="">icon next to the<br>group. Change the group name in the field and click <strong>Save</strong>.<br>• <strong>Delete a group</strong>: Move the pointer over the group and click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fc2a13fb21edcc4656cdb84384334bc5.png" width="12" alt="">icon next to the<br>group. In the message that appears, click <strong>Delete</strong>. After you delete a group, all components associated with the group are removed from the group. Proceed with caution. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a2c371211bd011f92b0507577daa8541.jpeg)

6. Click **Submit**.

7. In the **Component added successfully** dialog box, click **Download component development kit** to download the component development kit to your computer.

   You can also click **Upload later**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c06f44e3b7ec94f738bcc427216b8295.png)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - After a component is created, you can customize the component. For more information, see Customize a component and Understand tools and configurations for building custom components.
   >
   > - After you customize a component, you can use the component when you build a page. For more information, see Configure a component and Publish a component.

<a id="section-7-4-4-2"></a>

#### 7.4.4.2. Configure a component

After a component is added or if the component configurations need to be updated, you can configure the component.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- A custom component is developed. For more information, see Customize a component and Understand the tool and configurations for building custom components.

**Limits**

- You cannot configure preset components.

- You cannot configure custom components in the **Verifying** or **Put on shelves** state.

- You can configure custom components in the **To be configured**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, or **Removed** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**

4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a name in the search box or configure the following parameters to search for the component that you want to configure: **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Valid values of the **Type** parameter: **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
   >
   > - Valid values of the **Status** parameter: **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
   >
   > - Valid values of the **Classification** parameter: **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Configuration** in the upper-right corner of the component card.

6. In the **Configure components** panel, following the instructions to complete the **Upload component** and **Verify component** steps.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   **Upload component**: In the Upload component step, configure the parameters that are described in the following table and click **Next Step**.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Component name | The name of the component that you specified when you created the component. You cannot modify the component name. |
   | Component Key | The component key that you specified when you created the component. You cannot modify the component key. |
   | Type | The component type that you specified when you created the component.You cannot modify the component type. |
   | Grouping | The component group that you specified when you created the component.You cannot modify the component group. |
   | Component executable | Click <strong>Upload files</strong> to upload a .js file that meets the JavaScript standard. The file cannot exceed 5 MB in size. |
   | Component style file | Click <strong>Upload files</strong> to upload a .css file that meets the CSS standard. The file cannot exceed 5 MB in size. |
   | Component configuration file | Click <strong>Upload files</strong> to upload a .json file that meets the JSON standard. The file cannot exceed 5 MB in size. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e1452245b89c6e0a1dfa75a0a3e819d5.jpeg)

   </li>

   <li>

   **Verify component**: In the Verify component step, wait until the component is verified and click **Complete**.

   </li>

   </ol>

<a id="section-7-4-4-3"></a>

#### 7.4.4.3. Preview components

This topic describes how to preview preset and custom components on the Component Management page.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

You can preview only components in the **Configured**, **Removed**, or **Put on shelves** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.

4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
   >
   > - **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
   >
   > - **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Preview** in the upper-right corner of the component card.

6. In the **Component preview** dialog box, preview the component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The component preview displays a static preview image of the component instead of a preview rendered in real time.

<a id="section-7-4-4-4"></a>

#### 7.4.4.4. Modify a component

You can modify the basic information about a component when the component is updated. This topic describes how to modify a component.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

- Preset components cannot be modified.

- Component keys cannot be modified.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.

4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
   >
   > - **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
   >
   > - **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Edit** in the upper-right corner of the component card.

6. In the **Edit components** panel, modify the basic information about the component, including the component name, type, and group.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/68bfe3152751feb615ec632e0736151c.jpeg)

7. Click **Submit**.

<a id="section-7-4-4-5"></a>

#### 7.4.4.5. Publish a component

You can publish a component based on your business requirements. After the component is published, you can use the component when you build a page. This topic describes how to publish a component.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

You can publish only components in the **Configured** or **Removed** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.

4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
   >
   > - **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
   >
   > - **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Shelf** in the upper-right corner of the component card.

6. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-4-6"></a>

#### 7.4.4.6. Unpublish a component

You can unpublish a component based on your business requirements. After the component is unpublished, the component becomes unavailable and is no longer displayed on the Component Management page.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

You can unpublish only components in the **Put on shelves** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.

4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
   >
   > - **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
   >
   > - **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Lower shelf** in the upper-right corner of the component card.

6. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-4-7"></a>

#### 7.4.4.7. Add to page

The system supports adding components to a page.

**Prerequisites**

The user performing this operation must be an operations administrator by default.

**Constraints**

Only components in the **Published** state support being added to a page.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Component Management**.

4. On the **Component Management** page, use filters such as component name, **Group**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Category** to quickly locate your target component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - **Type**: Includes **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic And Text**, **Display Card**, **Display Components**, and **Other**.
   >
   > - **Status**: Includes **Pending Configuration**, **Verifying**, **Verification Failed**, **Configured**, **Unpublished**, and **Published**.
   >
   > - **Category**: Includes **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Click **Add to Page** in the upper-right corner of the component card.

6. In the **Add Page** dialog box, select the page where you want to insert the component.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can select up to 50 pages in batch. Pages in the following four states cannot be selected: Published (modification pending scheduled release), Pending scheduled release, Draft (approval pending for publication), and Published (modification approval pending).
   >
   > - After you add the component, it will be inserted at the end of the page. You must publish the page before the component becomes visible externally.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fc368242aec8eda2afcfb10bb2093346.jpeg)

7. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-4-8"></a>

#### 7.4.4.8. Customize a component

This topic describes how to customize a component.

**Prerequisites**

You have the corresponding development knowledge and experience.

**Procedure**

After you download the development kit of a component, perform the following steps to customize the component:

1. Create a **DemoComponent** directory under the **src/component** directory. Under the DemoComponent directory, create **index.jsx** and **index.module.css** files. To simplify operations, the **index.module.css** file is not modified in this example.

   ```text
   ├── README.md
   ├── build
   ├── config-overrides.js
   ├── package-lock.json
   ├── package.json
   ├── public
   │   └── index.html
   ├── src
   │   ├── component
   │   │   └── .... // Other folders and files.
   │   │   └── DemoComponent
   │   │       └── index.jsx
   │   │       └── index.module.css
   │   ├── global.d.ts
   │   ├── index.dev.jsx
   │   ├── index.js
   │   └── property.json
   └── tsconfig.json
   ```

2. Add the following code to the **index.jsx** file in the **DemoComponent** directory:

   ```bash
   import React from "react";
   import style from './index.module.css'
   const DemoComponent = (props) => {
     return (
       <div style={{ width: 1180, margin: "0 auto", backgroundColor: '#eee' }}>
         <div style={{ padding: 20, display: "flex", alignContent: "center"  }}>
           <div style={{ marginRight: 20 }}>External data</div>
           <div>{props.textSetterValue}</div>
         </div>
       </div>
     );
   };

   export default DemoComponent;
   ```

3. Modify the code in the index.js file under the src directory to import and export the component that you created.

   ```bash
   'use strict';
   import DemoComponent from './component/DemoComponent';

   export default DemoComponent;
   ```

4. Run the  `npm install`  command to install dependencies. After the installation is complete, run the  `npm run start`  command to run the code in a local environment.

5. Modify the **property.json** file under the src directory. The following sample code provides an example:

   ```json
   {
     "key": "DemoComponent", // The key that you specified when you created the component.
     "snippets": [
       {
         "label": "Sample component", // The name of the component that is displayed when you configure the component parameters.
         "screenshot": "", // The thumbnail of the component.
         "schema": {
           "componentName": "DemoComponent", // The key that you specified when you created the component.
           "props": {
        "textSetterValue": "Single-line text box" // The name and default value of the parameter to be passed into the component.
       }
         }
       }
     ],
     "configurations": [ // The configurations for configuring the parameter to be passed.
     {
         "name": "textSetterValue", // The name of the parameter to which the 
   configurations are applied.
         "title": "Single-line text box", // The parameter name displayed in the user interface (UI).
         "titleVisible": true, // Specifies whether the parameter name is displayed.
         "tooltip": "", // The description of the parameter. To view the description, move the pointer over the question mark (?) next to the parameter.
         "category": "Input", // Optional. The configuration category.
         "setter": {
           "component": "TextSetter" // The UI element that is used to configure the parameter.
         }
       }
    ]
   }
   ```

6. Run the  `npm run build`  command to compile the component.

7. After the compilation is successful, the custom component can be configured and uploaded. After the component is published, you can use the component when you build a page. For more information, see Configure a component and Publish a component.

<a id="section-7-4-4-9"></a>

#### 7.4.4.9. Understand the tool and configurations for building custom components

This topic describes the tool and configurations for building custom components.

**Procedure of using a scaffolding tool**

> **Important**
>
> - Node.js must be of V14.x or later.
>
> - The project is built by using React. Do not change the major versions of react-dom and react in the scaffolding tool.
>
> - You do not need to use a specific scaffolding kit for component compilation. However, make sure that the output JavaScript code complies with the Universal Module Definition (UMD) standard, and the configuration files and style files meet the platform requirements.
>
> - The scaffolding tool uses react-app-rewired to build a component. For more information, view related component building materials.

1. After you add a component, in the message that appears, click **Download component development kit** to download the scaffolding tool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can also download the scaffolding tool in the **Add components** or **Edit components** panel.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c06f44e3b7ec94f738bcc427216b8295.png)

2. View the directories in the scaffolding tool.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The actual files in the src/component directory shall prevail. The following sample code shows an example.

   ```text
   ├── README.md   // The description file.
   ├── config-overrides.js // The component configuration file.
   ├── package-lock.json  // The dependency lock file.
   ├── package.json // The dependency configuration file.
   ├── public 
   │   └── index.html // The template file used for local development.
   ├── src
   │   ├── component
   │   │   ├── ExampleComponent.module.css // The detailed component style code in a .module.css file.
   │   │   └── MyButton.tsx // The detailed component execution code in a .tsx file.
   │   ├── global.d.ts // The global description file.
   │   ├── index.dev.js // The main execution file in development mode.
   │   ├── index.js // The main execution file
   │   └── property.json // The configuration file of the component.
   └── tsconfig.json // The TypeScript configurations of the scaffolding tool.
   ```

3. Run the project by referring to the README.md file and open the URL returned from the console.

   The following sample code describes the basic configurations of the component:

   ```json
   {
     "key": "DemoComponent", //The key that you specified when you created the component.
     "snippets": [
       {
         "label": "Sample component", // The component name that is displayed on the user interface (UI).
         "screenshot": 
   "https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i2/O1CN01lQ2dKL27Bg1jDE87g_!!6000000007759-0-tps-3840-960.jpg", // The thumbnail of the component.
         "schema": {
           "componentName": "DemoComponent", // The key that you specified when you created the component.
           "props": {}
         }
       }
     ],
     "configurations": []
   }
   ```

- You can view the component key in the Add components, Edit components, and Configure components panels. The following figure shows an example on how to view the component key in the Add components panel.

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/061670fbbb7be030120e3c8929922472.jpeg)

- After the component is published, you can select the component when you build a page and configure the component content. The following figure shows an example on how the component name is displayed on a page.

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5b98c7785e816faa5f787abf799a0829.jpeg)

**Examples of custom component parameter configurations**

> **Note**
>
> The configurations are passed into a component by using the props parameter. The logic for handling parameters is implemented based on the component. The following section shows examples of key configurations. For more information about all the supported configurations, see the Overview of custom component configurations section of this topic.

**Input**

**Text input box**

Sample code:

```json
{
  "key": "DemoComponent",
  "snippets": [
    {
      "label": "Sample component",
      "screenshot": 
"https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i2/O1CN01lQ2dKL27Bg1jDE87g_!!6000000007759-0-tps-3840-960.jpg",
      "schema": {
        "componentName": "DemoComponent",
        "props": {
     "textSetterValue": "Single-line text box", // The name and default value of the parameter to be passed into the component. The general parameter description in this sample code also applies to other sample code in this section.
          "textSetterTextAreaValue": "Multi-line text box\nMulti-line text box\nMulti-line text box"
    }
      }
    }
  ],
  "configurations": [
  {
      "name": "textSetterValue", // The name of the parameter to which the 
configurations are applied.
      "title": "Single-line text box", // The parameter name displayed on the UI. The display name can be modified.
      "titleVisible": true, // Specifies whether the display name of the parameter is visible.
      "tooltip": "", // The description of the parameter. To view the description, movethe pointer over the question mark (?) next to the parameter.
      "category": "Input",// The configuration category.
      "setter": {
        "component": "TextSetter". // Input box. By default, the values are displayed in a single line. You can use props to pass the configurations of the input box. For more information about the configuration parameters, visit 
https://fusion.design/pc/component/input#Input.
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "textSetterTextAreaValue",
      "title": "Multi-line text box",
      "titleVisible": true,
      "tooltip": "",
      "category": "Input",
      "setter": {
        "component": "TextSetter", // Input box.
        "props": {
          "componentType": "textArea" // Specify that the input values are displayed inmultiple lines. For more information about other parameters, visit 
https://fusion.design/pc/component/input#Input%20Text%20Area.
        }
      }
    }
 ]
}
```

```json
 ]
```

```json
      "category": "Selector",
      "setter": {
        "component": "DateSetter",
        "props": { // For more information about the parameters, visit 
https://fusion.design/pc/component/time-picker-2?themeid=2#Time%20Picker.
          "showTime": true,
          "format": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss"
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "dateSetterRangeValue",
      "title": "Time range selector",
      "titleVisible": false,
      "tooltip": "",
      "category": "Selector",
      "setter": {
        "component": "DateSetter",
        "props": { // For more information about the parameters, visit 
https://fusion.design/pc/component/time-picker-2?
themeid=2#Time%20Picker%20Range%20Picker.
          // The componentType parameter is a reserved parameter of this UI element. Bydefault, you do not need to specify this parameter.
          "componentType": "RangePicker",
          "showTime": true,
          "format": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
