<a id="section-7-4-5"></a>

### 7.4.5. Template management

<a id="section-7-4-5-1"></a>

#### 7.4.5.1. Site template

The site template provides preset site templates. You can quickly create a site based on a site template.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operation** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Site Template**.

4. In the site template list, view the preset site templates.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/eeda66d0d9ac48320cf215e69bfa751b.png)

   - Click **Preview** to preview the preset site.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f48e5829e2d6332af81f54ee54c95c4f.jpeg)

   - Click **View Details** to expand the site template details.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/62901a05e626053e652392c9abe9ed4e.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-4-5-2"></a>

#### 7.4.5.2. Page template

The page template displays preset templates. You can quickly create pages and site templates based on these page templates.

<a id="section-7-4-5-2-1"></a>

##### 7.4.5.2.1. View page templates and page content

View preset and custom page templates, and the page content of each template.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Page Template**.

4. In the page template list, view the preset and custom page templates. Use the page name filter at the top of the page to quickly locate a template.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/929fc91e5f7c10dcffb8c1a6315f1867.jpeg)

5. Click **View Page** in the **Actions** column to preview the page content.

<a id="section-7-4-5-2-2"></a>

##### 7.4.5.2.2. Create a page template

Customize a page template based on your business requirements.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Page Template**.

4. Click **Create Page Template**.

5. In the **Create Page Template** dialog box, configure the page template.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6069ef3565ad7702abbc60d7278a443b.png)

   | Configuration item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Select Page | Select an existing page. |
   | Page Template Name | The name must be 1 to 60 characters in length and cannot be the same as any existing page name. |
   | ID | The ID must be 1 to 15 characters in length. It can contain lowercase letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-). The first character must be a lowercase letter. The ID cannot be the same as any existing page ID. Changing the ID affects the page path. |
   | Site Template | Select a site from the associated preset site templates. |
   | Page Template Description | Enter a description for the page template. The description must be 1 to 200 characters in length. |

6. Click OK.

<a id="section-7-4-5-2-3"></a>

##### 7.4.5.2.3. Edit page template

You can modify the configuration when changes are needed for the page template.

**Constraints**

You cannot edit preset page templates.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager management console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Page Template**.

4. In the page template list, click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/82c19d32900646d71837cb6bd8e32eab.jpeg)

5. In the **Edit Page Template** dialog box, modify the page template configuration. For detailed descriptions of configuration items, see Create a page template.

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-4-5-2-4"></a>

##### 7.4.5.2.4. Delete a page template

You can delete a page template when you no longer need it.

**Limits**

The system does not allow you to delete preset page templates.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Template Management** > **Page Template**.

4. In the page template list, click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/82c19d32900646d71837cb6bd8e32eab.jpeg)

5. In the **Note** dialog box, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5"></a>

## 7.5. Service support

<a id="section-7-5-1"></a>

### 7.5.1. Ticket management

<a id="section-7-5-1-1"></a>

#### 7.5.1.1. Ticket list

The ticket list displays the tickets that are available for viewing and processing.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-1"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.1. View tickets

You can view the ticket lists on which you have permissions.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the **Issues** page, click the **All**, **Created by Me**, **Pending Feedback**, **Pending Confirmation**, **Unclaimed**, **Pending Tasks**, **Handled by Me**, and **Transferred by Me** tabs to view tickets in different states.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b6c9739b71c0b4d19920a3e3fc601e64.jpeg)

   | Tab | Displayed ticket | User and permission |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | All | All tickets accessible to the current user. | • An operations administrator can view all tickets in the console.<br>• An administrator of a service group can view all tickets in the service group.<br>• A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets submitted by the user, tickets handled by the user, and tickets to be claimed.<br>• A regular user can view only the tickets submitted by the user. |
   | Created by Me | All tickets submitted by the current user. | All users can view the tickets that they submitted. |
   | Pending Feedback | Tickets that are submitted by the current user and are in the <strong>Pending Feedback</strong> state. | All users can view the tickets that they submitted. |
   | Pending Confirmatio n | Tickets that are submitted by the current user and are in the <strong>To Be</strong> <strong>Confirmed</strong> state. | All users can view the tickets that they submitted. |
   | Unclaimed | Tickets that are in the <strong>Unclaimed</strong> state. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets to be claimed. |
   | Pending Tasks | Tickets that are submitted by the current user and are in the <strong>Handling</strong> or <strong>Suspending</strong> state. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets to be handled by the user. |
   | Handled by Me | Tickets whose owner is the current user and that are in the <strong>Pending</strong> <strong>Feedback</strong>, <strong>To Be Confirmed</strong>, or <strong>Completed</strong> state. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets handled by the user. |
   | Transferred by Me | Tickets that are transferred by the current user. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets transferred by the user. |

5. Click **Advanced Filter** above the ticket list, configure the **Ticket Number**, **Issue Type**, **Update Time**, **Handle By**, **Over Time**, and **Status** parameters, and then click **Search** to quickly filter tickets.

6. Find the ticket that you want to view and click its number or **Details** in the **Actions** column. On the **Ticket details** page, view the ticket details.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/689339ab80bb6961b9eb40cd1c254d71.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-2"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.2. Withdraw tickets

This topic describes how to withdraw a ticket before it is claimed.

**Prerequisites**

- You are the ticket submitter.

- Tickets are in the **Unclaimed** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. Withdraw one or more tickets at a time.

   - **Withdraw a ticket**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to withdraw and click its number or **Details** in the Actions column.

     </li>

     <li>

     In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Withdraw** in the upper-right corner.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a5714570aa17f42f9eec70d1aedc4b7c.jpeg)

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**. After a ticket is withdrawn, the state of the ticket changes to **Withdrawn**.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Withdraw multiple tickets at a time**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to withdraw.

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Withdraw** in the lower part of the page.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the tickets are withdrawn, the state of the tickets changes to **Withdrawn**.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-3"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.3. Add comments to a ticket

You can add comments to a ticket at any time during ticket processing.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter or have the permissions to process tickets.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. On the **Comment** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter comments and upload attachments.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Supported file formats: PNG, JPG, TXT, RAR, DOC, XLS, ZIP, 7Z, and MP4. A single attachment cannot exceed 512 MB in size. A maximum of five attachments can be uploaded.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a5714570aa17f42f9eec70d1aedc4b7c.jpeg)

6. Click **Comment**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-4"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.4. Modify a ticket

This topic describes how to modify a ticket.

**Prerequisites**

- You are the ticket submitter.

- The ticket is in the **Withdrawn** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the **Created by Me** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to modify and click its number or **Details** in the Actions column.

5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Edit** in the upper-right corner.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e43f3412b4328c633b952d4a4a769317.jpeg)

6. On the **Edit a ticket** page, modify the parameters of the ticket. For more information about the parameters, see Submit a ticket.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d27d695dd79ac8cbf045fe7df23b91f9.jpeg)

7. Click **Submit**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-5"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.5. Claim tickets

Users who have the permissions to process tickets can view all tickets that are in the Unclaimed state and claim the tickets for processing.

**Prerequisites**

- You have the permissions to process tickets.

- Tickets are in the **Unclaimed** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. Claim one or more tickets at a time.

   - **Claim a ticket**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to claim and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

     </li>

     <li>

     In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Claim** in the upper-right corner.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fb5a08fe60afeec85da47b44e05a39f8.jpeg)

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**. After a ticket is claimed, the state of the ticket changes to **Handling**.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Claim multiple tickets**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to claim.

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Claim** in the lower part of the page.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**. After a ticket is claimed, the state of the ticket changes to **Handling**.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-6"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.6. Expedite a long-pending ticket

If a ticket remains open for a time after it is submitted, the ticket submitter can request the ticket processer to expedite the progress of the ticket.

**Prerequisites**

- You are the ticket submitter.

- Tickets are in the **Handling** or **Suspending** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the **Created by Me** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Urge** in the upper-right corner.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can expedite a ticket only once per day. If you expedite a ticket multiple times, the system prompts that the operation is repeated.
   >
   > - After you send a request to expedite a ticket, the ticket processer receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket can be processed with higher priority.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/03c5f4dba18c3fb7e000d8d06ef0b9a2.jpeg)

6. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-7"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.7. Submit a withdrawn or pending feedback ticket

A ticket submitter can resubmit withdrawn or pending feedback tickets.

**Prerequisites**

- You are the ticket submitter.

- Tickets are in the **Withdrawn** or **Pending Feedback** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the **Created by Me** or **Pending Feedback** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Submit** in the upper-right corner. For more information about how to submit a newly created ticket, see Submit a ticket.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9ae3200324c97227b44533a87ede558d.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > - After you resubmit a withdrawn ticket, no ticket processer is assigned to the ticket. In this case, the ticket is assigned based on service groups, service engineers, and assignment rules.
   >
   > - After you resubmit a pending feedback ticket, the ticket is assigned to the original ticket processer, and the state of the ticket changes to Handling.
   >
   > - The ticket processer receives the ticket along with a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket can be processed in a timely manner.

6. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-8"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.8. Return an in-progress ticket

If a ticket lacks valid descriptions, the ticket processer can return the ticket to the ticket submitter, who can add the required ticket information.

**Prerequisites**

- You have the permissions to process tickets.

- Tickets are in the **Handling** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the **Pending Tasks** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. On the **Return to Submitter** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter a comment for returning the ticket and upload attachments.

   > **Note**
   >
   > After the ticket is returned to the ticket submitter, the ticket submitter receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket submitter can add the required ticket information in a timely manner.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/64069d6c4dc92ada964f8f07d1d891d9.jpeg)

6. Click **Return to Submitter** in the lower-right corner.

7. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is returned to the ticket submitter, the state of the ticket changes to **Pending Feedback**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-9"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.9. Transfer tickets

If the processer of a ticket cannot process the ticket, the ticket processer can transfer the ticket to another engineer for processing. Operations administrators can transfer all in-progress tickets to other engineers.

**Prerequisites**

- You have the permissions to process tickets.

- Tickets are in the **Handling** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. Transfer one or more tickets at a time.

   - **Transfer a ticket**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to transfer and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

     </li>

     <li>

     On the Transfer tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, specify a service group and an engineer, enter a comment, and then upload attachments.

     > **Note**
     >
     > After the ticket is transferred, the engineer to whom the ticket is transferred receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket can be processed in a timely manner.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0932d816fb7519f0962e2662487770cf.jpeg)

     | Paramete r | Description |
     | --- | --- |
     | Transfer Service Group | Select the service group to which you want to transfer the ticket from the drop-down list. You can select only one service group. |
     | Service Personn el | Select the engineer to whom you want to transfer the ticket. You can select only one engineer. |
     | Commen t Content | Enter a comment to provide relevant information about the transfer. |
     | Upload Attachm ents | Upload the attachments related to the transfer. |

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     Click **Transfer** in the lower-right corner.

     </li>

     <li value="500">

     In the message that appears, click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Transfer multiple tickets**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to transfer.

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Forward** in the lower part of the page.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the **Ticket transfer** dialog box, specify the transfer information and enter a comment. For more information about the parameters, see the Transfer a ticket section of this topic.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c9e21371e781e23c71678e3fe6e0b26d.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li value="500">

     Click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-10"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.10. Reassign tickets

Administrators can reassign tickets in the Handling state to other engineers for handling. After a ticket is reassigned, the service level agreement (SLA) duration of the corresponding node is recalculated.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator.

- Tickets are in the **Handling** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. Reassign one or more tickets at a time.

   - **Reassign a ticket**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to reassign and click its number or **Details** in the Actions column.

     </li>

     <li>

     On the **Reassign** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/043aa5e687021d68f01acb112392fbb2.jpeg)

     | Paramete r | Description |
     | --- | --- |
     | Reassign Service Group | Select the service group to which you want to reassign the ticket from the drop-down list. You can select only one service group. |
     | Service Personn el | Select the engineer to whom you want to reassign the ticket. You can select only one engineer. |
     | Commen t Content | Enter a comment to provide relevant information about the reassignment. |
     | Upload Attachm ents | Upload the attachments related to the reassignment. |

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     Click **Reassign** in the lower-right corner.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Reassign multiple tickets at a time**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to reassign.

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Reassign** in the lower part of the page.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the **Reassign Ticket** dialog box, configure the parameters. For more information about the parameters, see the Reassign a ticket section in this topic.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1f1a6adaa8bbe383b298373291c98eca.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li value="500">

     Click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-11"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.11. Assign tickets

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. Assign one or more tickets at a time.

   - **Assign a ticket**

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-12"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.12. Suspend a ticket

If a ticket that is in progress cannot be processed at the moment, you can suspend the ticket.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator, a service group administrator, or a ticket processer.

- Tickets are in the **Handling** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to suspend and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. On the **Suspend** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter the reason for the suspension.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4e0cdc1bca37e454b79c266821e4963c.jpeg)

6. Click **Suspend** in the lower-right corner.

7. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is suspended, the state of the ticket changes to **Suspending**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-13"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.13. Activate a ticket

You can activate a ticket that is suspended.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator, a service group administrator, or a ticket processer.

- Tickets are in the **Suspending** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to activate and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. On the **Activate** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter a comment for the activation.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ea10b7b4edbeaa8eec1f775d044b6388.jpeg)

6. Click **Activate** in the lower-right corner.

7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-14"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.14. Close a ticket

After a ticket is processed by an engineer, the engineer can close the ticket and transfer it to the ticket submitter for verification.

**Prerequisites**

- You have the permissions to process tickets.

- Tickets are in the **Handling** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to close and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. On the **Close** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter a comment and upload attachments.

   > **Note**
   >
   > After the ticket is closed, the ticket submitter receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. Then, the ticket submitter can verify the results.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9b68f4eb332222581017e421648a878b.jpeg)

6. Click **Close** in the lower-right corner.

7. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is closed, the state of the ticket changes to **To Be Confirmed**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-15"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.15. Verify the results of a pending confirmation ticket

After a ticket is closed by the ticket processer, the ticket is transferred to the ticket submitter for verification. The ticket submitter can verify the results to check whether the issue is resolved.

**Prerequisites**

- You are the ticket submitter.

- Tickets are in the **To Be Confirmed** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, check whether the issue is resolved in the ticket.

   - **If the issue is resolved**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the **Confirm** tab of the **Process Ticket** section, enter a comment and upload attachments.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/29dc50da1bddf242d4ef186bd5f5eea9.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Confirm** in the lower-right corner.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is confirmed, the state of the ticket changes to **Completed**.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **If the issue is not resolved**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the **Unhandled** tab of the **Process Ticket** section, enter a comment and upload attachments.

     > **Note**
     >
     > After you confirm that the issue is not resolved, the ticket processer receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket processer can process the ticket in a timely manner.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a2d53bcc70a2203a6287f596d169876f.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Unhandled** in the lower-right corner.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**. The state of the ticket changes to **Handling**, and the ticket is assigned to the original ticket processer for processing.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-16"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.16. Evaluate a completed ticket

After the submitter of a ticket confirms that the issue is resolved, the submitter can evaluate the ticket.

**Prerequisites**

- You are the ticket submitter.

- Tickets are in the **Completed** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to evaluate and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

5. On the **Evaluate** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, rate the ticket, enter your comment, and then upload attachments as needed.

   > **Note**
   >
   > When you rate a ticket, select at least half a star and at most five stars.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5a62af7943885c4f291e7b73f391a57a.jpeg)

6. Click **Evaluate** in the lower-right corner.

7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-17"></a>

After a ticket is withdrawn by the submitter, the submitter can delete the ticket if it is no longer required.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. Delete one or more tickets at a time.

   - **Delete a ticket**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to delete and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.

     </li>

     <li>

     In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Delete** in the upper-right corner.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e43f3412b4328c633b952d4a4a769317.jpeg)

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Delete multiple tickets**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to delete.

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Delete** in the lower part of the page.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     In the message that appears, click **OK**.

     </li>

     </ol>

<a id="section-7-5-1-1-18"></a>

##### 7.5.1.1.18. Export ticket details

Operations administrators can export ticket details to local machines for storage.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.

4. On the **All** tab, click **Export Ticket Details** above the ticket list to export ticket details as a **.csv** file to your local machine.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c99469e29a7a1b402718afdff97a4fda.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-5-1-2"></a>

#### 7.5.1.2. Submit a ticket

You can submit tickets to request technical support. A ticket includes the issue type, issue description, and attachments.

**Prerequisites**

You are granted the permissions to submit tickets.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Submit Issues**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can also click **Create a Ticket** on the **Ticket List** page to submit a ticket.

4. On the **Create a Ticket** page, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/75fd773eee495e2ed88832dbeb7a14f0.jpeg)

   | Parameter or setting | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Title | The title of the ticket. |
   | Issue Type | The issue type of the ticket. Valid values: <strong>Product usage</strong>, <strong>Business affected</strong>, <strong>Account permission issues</strong>, and <strong>Billing issues</strong>. |
   | Problem Description | The description of the issue in the ticket. |
   | Custom settings | If custom parameters are available for the issue type of the ticket, configure the custom parameters. |

5. Click **Submit**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-3"></a>

#### 7.5.1.3. Service group

<a id="section-7-5-1-3-1"></a>

##### 7.5.1.3.1. Create a service group

A service group defines the team of service personnel responsible for handling issues.

By default, the operating user is the operations administrator.

**Procedure**

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Issues** > **Service Group**.

4. On the **Service Group** page, click **Create a Service Group**.

5. In the **Create a Service Group** dialog box, configure the service group information.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/10a84b83ddf254e18e80e78e61d25cd3.jpeg)

   Configuration item

   Description

   **Service**

   Enter a name for the service group.

   **group name**

   **Description**

   Enter a description for the service group.

   When tickets are assigned to this service group, you can choose

   **Basic**

   how they are distributed to specific personnel: **Assign in sequence**

   **informati**

   or **Prioritize those with fewer tickets in progress**.

   **on**

   - **Assign in sequence**: Assign tickets cyclically by ascending

   **Ticket**

   order of service personnel ID. Skip personnel whose working

   **assignment**

   hours or status do not match.

   **method**

   - **Prioritize those with fewer tickets in progress**: Assign tickets based on the number of tickets currently being handled by eligible personnel (matching working hours and status). If counts are equal, assign to the personnel with the smallest ID.

   - **Add personnel**:

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Click **Add Personnel** above the list.

     </li>

     <li>

     </ol>

   **Service personnel information**

   <ol type="i" start="100">

   <li>

   Click **Confirm**.

   </li>

   </ol>

   - **Enable personnel**: In the service personnel list, click **Enable** in the Actions column. You can enable personnel only if their current status is disabled.

   - **Disable personnel**: In the service personnel list, click **Disable** in the Actions column. You can disable personnel only if their current status is enabled.

   - **Remove personnel**: Remove a user from the personnel list.

     <ol type="a">

     In the service personnel list, click **Remove** in the Actions column.

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Confirm**.

     </li>

   **Timeout**

   **Service group administrat or**

   <ol type="i" start="100">

   - **Disable administrator**: In the administrator list, click **Disable** in the Actions column. You can disable an administrator only if their current status is enabled.

   - **Enable administrator**: In the administrator list, click **Enable** in the Actions column. You can enable an administrator only if their current status is disabled.

   - **Remove administrator**: Remove a user from the administrator list.

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     In the administrator list, click **Remove** in the Actions column.

     </li>

     <li>

     Click **Confirm**.

   >

##### 7.5.1.3.3. Edit a service group

Update the basic information or service personnel information of a service group.

**Prerequisites**

The operator is an operations administrator by default.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operation** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Service Group**.

4. On the **Service Group** page, click **Edit** in the Actions column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4cb8dd055c18aa243ae0cfac76f1b22a.jpeg)

5. In the **Modify Service Group** dialog box, update the basic information, service personnel information, and fallback rules of the service group. For more information about configuration, see Create a service group.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8f8bbd9b94447fe5f577fd8c27085812.jpeg)

6. Click OK.

<a id="section-7-5-1-3-4"></a>

##### 7.5.1.3.4. Delete a service group

This topic describes how to delete service groups.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tickets** > **Service Group**.

4. On the **Service Group** page, find the service group that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4cb8dd055c18aa243ae0cfac76f1b22a.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-4"></a>

#### 7.5.1.4. Issue categorization

<a id="section-7-5-1-4-1"></a>

##### 7.5.1.4.1. Create an issue type

If the preset issue types cannot meet your business requirements, you can create custom issue types. After you create issue types, ticket submitters can select an issue type that you create when they submit tickets.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.

4. On the **Issue Type** page, click **Create a Problem Category**.

5. On the **Create Issue Type** page, configure the parameters in the **Basic Information**, **Form Configuration**, and **SLA Configuration** steps.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Configure the parameters in the Basic Information step and click **Next**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/98365cb69a2968db9366b7dc2010a2b8.jpeg)

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Name | The name of the issue type. |
   | Description | The description of the issue type. |

   </li>

   <li>

   Configure the parameters in the Form Configuration step and click **Next**.

   </li>

   </ol>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2c43e44bbb1bbf91f17e67e2e78a131c.jpeg)

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Component | Available types of components include <strong>Input</strong>, <strong>Select</strong>, <strong>Time</strong>, and <strong>Other</strong>.<br>• <strong>Input</strong>: Available components of this type include <strong>Input Box</strong>, <strong>Number Field</strong>, and <strong>Multi-line Input Box</strong>.<br>• <strong>Select</strong>: Available components of this type include <strong>Select</strong>, <strong>Single-select</strong>, and <strong>Multi-select</strong>.<br>• <strong>Time</strong>: Available components of this type include <strong>Date</strong> and <strong>Time Interval</strong>.<br>• <strong>Other</strong>: Available components of this type include <strong>Attachment</strong>, <strong>Cloud</strong> <strong>Service Type</strong>, <strong>Cascade Selection</strong>, <strong>Organization</strong>, <strong>Resource Set</strong>, and <strong>Cloud</strong> <strong>Service Instance</strong>. |
   | Form Design | Drag components from the left-side Component section to this section.<br>• After you drag components to this section, you can drag them in the current section to adjust the display order, copy components, and remove components.<br>• Click <strong>Preview Complete Form</strong> in the upper-right corner to preview the designed form. |
   | Component Configurati on | In the Form Design section, select a component. Then, configure the component in the Component Configuration section. |

   <ol type="i" start="3">

   <li>

   Configure the parameters in the SLA Configuration step and click **Save**.

   </li>

   </ol>

You cannot modify the preset actions.You can configure notification methods in the Notification Method column. The notification methods include <strong>Short Message Service (SMS)</strong>, <strong>email</strong>, and <strong>DingTalk</strong>. |
   | Custom Actions | You can configure custom actions in this section.<br>• Add a custom action<br>a. Click <strong>Add</strong>.<br>b. In the <strong>Add Custom Action</strong> panel, configure the parameters in the Configuration Call and Pop-up Layer Configuration steps.<br>a. <strong>Configuration Call</strong>: Configure the <strong>Operation Name</strong>, <strong>Operation</strong> <strong>Permission Settings</strong>, <strong>Available Status</strong>, <strong>Interface call key</strong>, and <strong>Interface call URL</strong> parameters.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3533f73478931c7bb399d0ebc0b44d1f.jpeg)<br>b. <strong>Pop-up Layer Configuration</strong>: Design and configure the form. Drag components from the left-side Component section to the Form Design section. In the Form Design section, select a component. Click <strong>Submission</strong>.<br>• Modify a custom action<br>a. Find the custom action that you want to modify and click <strong>Configuration</strong> in the Operation column.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e562676b424c682847316b97d0c54734.jpeg)<br>b. In the <strong>Add Custom Action</strong> panel, modify the configurations of the action.<br>c. Click <strong>Submission</strong>. |

     <ol type="a">

<a id="section-7-5-1-4-2"></a>

##### 7.5.1.4.2. View issue types

This topic describes how to view the preset and custom issue types.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.

4. View the created issue types on the Issue Type page.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - You can enter the name and description of an issue type above the issue type list to quickly find the issue type.
   >
   > - To filter issue types by status, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9d6988b7c15b0ca6a55e01b6f339a6d8.png" width="11" alt=""> icon in the Status column.
   >
   > - The following preset issue types are supported: **Product usage**, **Business affected**, **Account permission issues**, and **Billing issues**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6d80e6c57b81db27db74bcfcc3c1291b.jpeg)

5. Find the issue type that you want to view and click its name to go to the details page of the issue type.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1e0c6a85d2d3a24f0cf0b42cf1659249.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-5-1-4-3"></a>

##### 7.5.1.4.3. Modify an issue type

This topic describes how to modify an issue type.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.

4. On the **Issue Type** page, find the issue type that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6d80e6c57b81db27db74bcfcc3c1291b.jpeg)

5. On the **Modify Issue Type** page, modify the configurations of the issue type. For more information about the parameters, see Create an issue type.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2737f3d80202a0f9b732075349c66149.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-5-1-4-4"></a>

##### 7.5.1.4.4. Enable an issue type

After you enable an issue type, the issue type is displayed in the Issue Type drop-down list. Ticket submitters can select the issue type when they submit tickets.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- Issue types are in the **Deactivate** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.

4. On the **Issue Type** page, find the issue type that you want to enable and click **Enable** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6d80e6c57b81db27db74bcfcc3c1291b.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-4-5"></a>

##### 7.5.1.4.5. Disable an issue type

After an issue type is disabled, the issue type is no longer displayed in the Issue Type drop-down list. Ticket submitters can no longer select the disabled issue type when they submit tickets.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- Issue types are in the **Enable** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.

4. On the **Issue Type** page, find the issue type that you want to disable and click **Deactivate** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6d80e6c57b81db27db74bcfcc3c1291b.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-4-6"></a>

##### 7.5.1.4.6. Copy an issue type

You can copy the configurations of an existing issue type to create another issue type.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.

4. On the **Issue Type** page, find the issue type that you want to copy and click **Copy** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6d80e6c57b81db27db74bcfcc3c1291b.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the operation succeeds, a new issue type is created and named in the format of {Original issue type name}_copy.

<a id="section-7-5-1-4-7"></a>

##### 7.5.1.4.7. Delete an issue type

This topic describes how to delete an issue type.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.

4. On the **Issue Type** page, find the issue type that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6d80e6c57b81db27db74bcfcc3c1291b.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-5"></a>

#### 7.5.1.5. Ticket dispatch rule

<a id="section-7-5-1-5-1"></a>

##### 7.5.1.5.1. Create a ticket dispatch rule

Tickets can be automatically assigned to engineers based on ticket dispatch rules. You can create different ticket dispatch rules for different scenarios.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Allocation Rule**.

4. On the **Allocation Rule** page, click **Create a Rule**.

5. In the **Create a Ticket Assignment Rule** panel, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3db04359c1b6731454bc1b9d9b1239eb.jpeg)

   <table>
     <tr>
       <th colspan="2">Parameter</th>
       <th>Description</th>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="4">Basic Informat ion</td>
       <td>Rule Name</td>
       <td>The name of the rule.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Description</td>
       <td>The description of the rule.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Assign to Service Group</td>
       <td>The service group with which you want to associate the rule. You can select only one service group from the drop-down list. If no service group is available, create a service group on the Service Group page.For more information, see Create a service group.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Priority</td>
       <td>The priority of the rule. A greater value indicates a higher priority.Valid values: 1 to 999. Existing rules and their priorities are displayed in the drop-down list. The priority of each rule must be unique.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td colspan="2">Rule Group</td>
       <td>The conditions based on which tickets are assigned to engineers. You can add conditions and condition groups to a rule group.<br>• <strong>Add a condition or a condition group</strong>:<br>Note<br>The relationship between conditions and condition groups can be <strong>And</strong> or <strong>Or</strong>. <strong>And</strong> indicates that all conditions must be met.<strong>Or</strong> indicates that at least one condition must be met.<br>a. Click <strong>Add Condition</strong> or <strong>Add Group</strong>.<br>b. Configure the condition, condition type, and condition value.<br>• Condition: Select a condition. Supported conditions include organization, service, issue type, description, and ticket content.<br>• Condition type: After you select a condition, select a supported condition type.<br>• Condition value: This item is displayed after you select a condition type. Set the condition value based on the condition and condition type.<br>• <strong>Delete a condition or a condition group</strong>: Click the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/22b85c15599d18ff5709335f7ceb183f.png" width="14" alt="">icon on<br>the right side of the condition or condition group.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-5-2"></a>

##### 7.5.1.5.2. View ticket dispatch rules

This topic describes how to view the created ticket dispatch rules and the service group and rule conditions in a rule.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tickets** > **Allocation Rule**.

4. On the Allocation rules page, view the ticket dispatch rules.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/922528f2f586b75cd0d74d88d4a571c9.jpeg)

5. Click **Advanced Filter** above the rule list, configure the following filter conditions, and then click **Search** to quickly search for ticket dispatch rules: **Rule name**, **Description**, **Assign to Service Group**, and **Status**.

6. Click a rule name. In the **Rule Details** panel, view the rule details.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/43d62e05ffe8d1b5eebbe7763f652bd6.jpeg)

<a id="section-7-5-1-5-3"></a>

##### 7.5.1.5.3. Modify a ticket dispatch rule

This topic describes how to modify the basic information, service group, and match conditions of a ticket dispatch rule.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tickets** > **Allocation Rule**.

4. On the **Allocation rules** page, find the ticket dispatch rule that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/922528f2f586b75cd0d74d88d4a571c9.jpeg)

5. In the **Edit ticket allocation rules** panel, modify the basic information about and conditions of the rule. For more information about rule parameters, see Create a ticket dispatch rule.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7d97801284a58c4fc6947a6030f232d7.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-5-4"></a>

##### 7.5.1.5.4. Enable a ticket dispatch rule

After you enable a ticket dispatch rule, the system automatically dispatches tickets to the service group based on the specified conditions and priorities.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- The ticket dispatch rule is in the **Deactivate** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tickets** > **Allocation Rule**.

4. On the **Allocation rules** page, find the rule that you want to enable and click **Enable** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/922528f2f586b75cd0d74d88d4a571c9.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-5-5"></a>

##### 7.5.1.5.5. Disable a ticket dispatch rule

After you disable a ticket dispatch rule, the system no longer automatically dispatches tickets based on the specified rule conditions.

**Prerequisites**

- You are an operations administrator.

- The ticket dispatch rule is in the **Enable** state.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tickets** > **Allocation Rule**.

4. On the **Allocation rules** page, find the rule that you want to disable and click **Deactivate** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/922528f2f586b75cd0d74d88d4a571c9.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

<a id="section-7-5-1-5-6"></a>

##### 7.5.1.5.6. Delete a ticket dispatch rule

This topic describes how to delete ticket dispatch rules that you no longer use.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tickets** > **Allocation Rule**.

4. On the **Allocation rules** page, find the rule that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the Operation column.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/922528f2f586b75cd0d74d88d4a571c9.jpeg)

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

#### 7.5.1.6. Data insights

The Data Insight page displays the real-time data and historical data of the ticket service.

<a id="section-7-5-1-6-1"></a>

##### 7.5.1.6.1. View the ticket overview

This topic describes how to view an overview of tickets on the Data Insight page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Data Insight**.

4. Click the **Ticket Overview** tab.

5. View the ticket overview.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a8436b0cfb122a823bffb11853f340f1.jpeg)

   | Item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Overall statistics | Displays the total number of tickets in the <strong>Total Tickets</strong> card and the numbers of tickets in different states, including <strong>Unclaimed</strong>, <strong>Withdrawn</strong>, <strong>Handling</strong>, <strong>Pending</strong> <strong>Feedback</strong>, <strong>To Be Confirmed</strong>, <strong>Completed</strong>, and <strong>Suspending</strong>. |
   | Overdue Unprocesse d Ticket Statistics | Displays statistics on overdue tickets in a chart and a table. |
   | SLA Trend | Displays the fulfillment trend of the ticket service level agreement (SLA). You can switch between the <strong>1 Month</strong> and <strong>1 Week</strong> views. |
   | Service Group Personnel | Displays the information about service groups, including <strong>Service Group Name</strong>, <strong>People During Business Hours</strong>, and <strong>Total People in Service Group</strong>. |

<a id="section-7-5-1-6-2"></a>

##### 7.5.1.6.2. View the ticket type analysis

This topic describes how to view the ticket type analysis on the Data Insight page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Data Insight**.

4. Click the **Ticket Type Analysis** tab.

5. View the analysis information.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6d3900230f607a1c23828b3bb499a3bf.jpeg)

   | Item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Data and Percentage of Tickets of Various Types | Displays the number and percentage of tickets of each type. You can switch between <strong>Pie Chart</strong> and <strong>Column Chart</strong>. |
   | New Ticket Trend Analysis | Displays the trend of new tickets. You can switch between the <strong>1 Month</strong> and <strong>1</strong> <strong>Week</strong> views. |
   | Correlation Analysis of Ticket Type and Average Processing Duration | Displays the average amount of time required to resolve tickets of each type in a column chart and a table. |

<a id="section-7-5-1-6-3"></a>

##### 7.5.1.6.3. View the processing efficiency analysis of tickets

This topic describes how to view the processing efficiency analysis of tickets on the Data Insight page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Data Insight**.

4. Click the **Processing Efficiency Analysis** tab.

5. View the analysis information.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0258b40f41acea6707aff39ec20343d4.jpeg)

   | Item | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Maximum Waiting Time | Displays the longest waiting time recorded for tickets to be claimed. |
   | Maximum Timeout Period | Displays the longest timeout period recorded for completed tickets. |
   | Response Duration and Resolution Duration of Service Group | Displays the amount of time required to respond to or resolve a ticket by each service group. |
   | Top 10 Tickets with the Longest Processing Duration | Displays the information about the top 10 tickets by processing duration. You can switch between the <strong>Resolved</strong> and <strong>Unresolved</strong> views.<br>You can also check the detailed processing information of a ticket. To do so, find the ticket that you want to view and click its number or click <strong>Details</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column to go to the ticket details page. |

<a id="section-7-5-1-7"></a>

#### 7.5.1.7. Shift schedule management

<a id="section-7-5-1-7-1"></a>

##### 7.5.1.7.1. Schedule

View and manage shift information. View detailed shift assignments.

<a id="section-7-5-1-7-1-1"></a>

###### 7.5.1.7.1.1. Batch shift schedule

Set up shift schedules in batch.

**Prerequisites**

The default user for this operation is the Operations Administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Issues** > **Scheduling Management** > **Schedule Table**.

4. On the **Schedule Table** page, click **Batch Shift Schedule**.

5. In the **Batch Shift Schedule** dialog box, configure the shift schedule.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Configuration item</td>
       <td>Description</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Service Group</td>
       <td>Select the service group to assign shifts.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Date</td>

<a id="section-7-5-2"></a>

### 7.5.2. Document management

<a id="section-7-5-2-1"></a>

#### 7.5.2.1. Documents

Operations administrators can maintain and update documents such as service manuals and usage specifications to control the query and display of documents.

**Background information**

As an operations administrator, you can update and maintain knowledge documents related to your cloud platform by using the document management feature. This allows you to manage documents in a centralized manner. Users can query and view knowledge documents and obtain relevant information. For example, users can query the usage specifications and process descriptions of a cloud service on the service portal and help center. This helps users obtain the latest knowledge and information at the earliest opportunity.

- Document list: displays all documents on the cloud platform.

- Document Classification: displays document categories, document groups, and document collections at three levels. Document categories are at level 1, document groups are at level 2, and document collections are at level 3.

**Limits**

- You cannot create document groups in, rename, move, or delete a preset document category.

- You can only copy preset document groups. You cannot create document collections in, rename, move, or delete a preset document group.

- You cannot rename, move, or delete a preset document collection.

- You can only copy preset documents.

**Permissions on directories in different states**

> **Note**
>
> Directories may be in the states described in the following table. Different operations can be performed on directories in different states. In the following table, ✓ indicates that the operation is supported, and × indicates that the operation is not supported.

| State/Operation | Delet e a direct ory | Rev oke the publ ishi ng, ena blin g, or disa blin g of a dire ctor y | View the review details of a directory | Ena ble a dire ctor y | Dis abl e a dire ctor y | Mov e a dire ctor y | Rename a directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enabled | × | × | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Enabled (being reviewed for disabling) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | × |
| Enabled (review for disabling rejected) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Enabled (disabling failed) | × | × | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Disabled | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ |

**Permissions on documents in different states**

> **Note**
>
> Documents may be in the states described in the following table. Different operations can be performed on documents in different states. In the following table, ✓ indicates that the operation is supported, and × indicates that the operation is not supported.

**States related to the editing and publishing of documents**

| State/Operat ion | Mo dif y a do cu me nt | Pu bli sh a do cu me nt | Cop y a doc um ent | Del ete a doc um ent | Re vok e the pu blis hin g, ena bli ng, or dis abl ing of a doc um ent | Vie w the revi ew det ails of a doc ume nt | Ena ble a doc um ent | Dis abl e a doc um ent | Mo ve a doc um ent | Ren ame a doc ume nt | Ma nag e ver sio ns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Draft | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Draft (being reviewed for publishing) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Draft (review rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Draft (publishing failed) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published (modifications to be published) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published (being reviewed for publishing modifications) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |

##### 7.5.2.1.1. Create a document category

This topic describes how to create a document category.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Document Management** > **Documents**.

4. In the Document Classification section, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/775869bc5cd1dc67fac93147134ab46e.png" width="13" alt=""> icon.

5. In the **Create** dialog box, enter a name in the **Name** field.

   > **Note**
   >
   > A document category consists of document groups and collections. When you create a document category, a document group and a document collection are created in the document category by default. By default, after a document category is created, it is displayed in the upper part of the Document Classification section.
   >
   > - The default name of a document group is in the Default Group ({Document category name}) format.
   >
   > - The default name of a document collection is in the Default Document Collection ({Document category name}) format.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/31c85bfb8c5d7c447195c18d9bad5073.jpeg)

6. Click **OK**.

In the Document Classification section, find the document category that you want to manage, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/33fa82d8632a57437e492e9d1acda8d5.png" width="16" alt=""> icon to the right of its name, and then select **Create**

   **a child**.

5. In the dialog box that appears, enter a name in the **Name** field.

   > **Note**

   > You do not need to configure the Select Location parameter. This parameter is dimmed by default and indicates the document category to which the document group belongs.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c9338c209a08ae9c27d332052208d22b.jpeg)

##### 7.5.2.1.5. Move a document category, document group, or document collection

This topic describes how to move a document category, document group, or document collection to adjust its location.

**Limits**

In a custom document collection, a level-2 or level-3 document category cannot be moved upwards to be a level-1 document category.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

In the Document Classification section, find the document category, document group, or document collection that you want to move, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/33fa82d8632a57437e492e9d1acda8d5.png" width="16" alt=""> icon to the right

   of its name, and then select **Move**.

5. In the dialog box that appears, select the location at which you want the document category, document group, or document collection to be displayed.

   > **Important**

# 8.Security

<a id="section-8-1"></a>

## 8.1. Overview

The Apsara Uni-manger Management Console uses AccessKey pairs and multi-factor authentication (MFA) to enhance security when you access systems and resources.

| Module | Description |
| --- | --- |
| AccessKey pairs | AccessKey pairs are used to access cloud resources.<br>• You can view the AccessKey pairs of your account.<br>• You can create AccessKey pairs within your account. Each account can have at most two AccessKey pairs.<br>• You can enable or disable an AccessKey pair of your account. However, at least one AccessKey pair must be enabled within your account.<br>• You can delete an AccessKey pair from your account. However, at least one AccessKey pair must be retained within your account. |
| MFA | MFA is an identity authentication method that enhances security by requiring additional verification factors beyond the username and password of an account.<br>• You can check whether the MFA feature is enabled for a user. If the MFA feature is disabled for a user, you can enable the feature for the user.However, you cannot disable the MFA feature after it is enabled.<br>• You can bind or unbind virtual MFA devices.<br>• You can reset MFA keys. |

<a id="section-8-2"></a>

## 8.2. AccessKey pairs of a personal account

An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. AccessKey pairs are used to authenticate the identity of request senders, which can ensure cloud resource security.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and click **User Information** in the menu that appears.

   | Operation | Procedure |
   | --- | --- |
   | View AccessKey pairs | In the AccessKey Pair section, view the AccessKey pairs of your account.<br>Note<br>The AccessKey IDs and AccessKey secrets provide full permissions on cloud resources within your Apsara Stack tenant account. Keep them confidential. |
   | Create an AccessKey pair | You can delete your existing AccessKey pairs and create new ones to implement the rotation of AccessKey pairs.<br>i. In the AccessKey Pair section, click <strong>Create AccessKey Pair</strong>.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>Close</strong>. |
   | Disable an AccessKey pair | Important<br>If you disable an AccessKey pair, errors may occur in the services or applications that depend on the AccessKey pair. Proceed with caution.<br>i. In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair that you want to disable and click <strong>Disabled</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>Disable</strong>. |
   | Enable an AccessKey pair | In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair that you want to enable and click <strong>Enable</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column. |
   | Delete an AccessKey pair | Important<br>If you delete an AccessKey pair, errors may occur in the services or applications that depend on the AccessKey pair. Proceed with caution.<br>i. In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair that you want to delete and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>ii. In the message that appears, click <strong>Delete</strong>. |
   | View the logs of an AccessKey pair | i. In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair whose logs you want to view and click <strong>View AccessKey Pair Logs</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column. The <strong>AccessKey Logs</strong> page appears. For more information about AccessKey pair logs, see AccessKey logs. |

<a id="section-8-3"></a>

## 8.3. MFA

<a id="section-8-3-1"></a>

### 8.3.1. Overview

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is an authentication method. In addition to username and password authentication, MFA provides an extra layer of protection.

**Introduction to MFA**

When MFA is enabled, you must enter your username and password (first security factor) and then a variable verification code (second security factor) from an MFA device when you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Two-factor authentication enhances security for your account.

MFA devices use the Time-based One-time Password (TOTP) algorithm to generate time-dependent 6-digit dynamic verification codes. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console supports software-based virtual MFA devices. You can install software (such as the Alibaba Cloud app) that supports MFA on your mobile device (such as your mobile phone) to act as a virtual MFA device.

**Precautions**

The TOTP algorithm requires that the time of the system clock of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console remain consistent with the standard time on the Internet. Otherwise, discrepancies in time can lead to inconsistent MFA verification codes and you may be unable to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

<a id="section-8-3-2"></a>

### 8.3.2. Manage MFA

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is an authentication method. In addition to username and password authentication, MFA provides an extra layer of protection. You can enable or disable the MFA feature in the console.

**Bind a virtual MFA device**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the upper-right corner of the Home page, click the profile picture and select **User Information** in the menu that appears.

3. In the upper-right corner of the **MFA** section, click **Bind Virtual MFA Device**.

4. On the **Bind Virtual MFA Device** page, bind an MFA device as prompted. After an MFA device is bound, the value of the MFA Status parameter changes to Enabled and the value of the Device Status changes to Bound.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a1377eba283a7b062e985e81f26c9925.jpeg)

   > **Note**
   >
   > After a virtual MFA device is bound, you must enter a 6-digit MFA verification code in addition to your username and password before you can log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Disable a virtual MFA device**

1. In the upper-right corner of the **MFA** section on the **User Information** page, click **Disable Virtual MFA Device**.

2. In the message that appears, click **Disable Virtual MFA Device**.

   After you disable the MFA feature, you need to only enter your username and password next time you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Forcibly enable the MFA feature**

Administrators, including the platform administrator, operations administrator, and organization administrator, can check whether the MFA feature is enabled for their users. If the MFA feature is disabled for the users, the administrators can forcibly enable the MFA feature for the users.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users** > **Users**.

4. On the Users page, click the **System Users** tab.

5. Find the user for which you want to enable the MFA feature, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/096d9e73777d235b023aabd7f41d395d.png" width="15" alt="">

   icon in the **Actions** column, and then click **MFA Settings**.

6. In the MFA Settings dialog box, turn on **MFA Settings** and click **OK**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > The MFA feature can be forcibly enabled for users, but cannot be forcibly disabled.
   >
   > - Before the MFA feature is enabled, the MFA feature of the user is in the **Disabled and Unbound** state.
   >
   > - After the MFA feature is enabled, the MFA feature of the user is in the **Enabled and Unbound** state. After the MFA feature is forcibly enabled for a user, the user must go to the Bind Virtual MFA Device page to bind a virtual MFA device before the user can log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

# 10.Message center

<a id="section-10-1"></a>

## 10.1. Manage all messages

The All Messages page in the Message Center module displays all read and unread messages related to services, operations, process approvals, application O&M, announcements, and alerts that you have received.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2e83f8bac8519378ecfad05568e7323b.png" width="13" alt=""> icon.

3. In the **Message** panel, click **More**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/74e0aefa28bf672e074a2c07568f96b5.jpeg)

4. In the left-side navigation pane, click **All Messages**.

5. On the **All Messages** page, switch to different tabs to view the messages of the corresponding business type.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3e962de2ba70f6ae69395c4e9165fb73.jpeg)

6. In the upper part of a tab, specify the start date and end date to quickly find messages within the specified time range.

7. In the message list, click the message title and view the content of the message on the right side of the page. If the message is unread, the message is marked as read. The <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cf7b5603201c57d911f6e805ea7eea96.png" width="6" alt=""> icon

   indicates that the message is unread.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can select an unread message and click **Mark as Read** to mark the selected message as read.

8. Select a message and click **Delete**.

9. In the message that appears, click **Delete**.

   > **Important**
   >
   > After you delete a message, the message cannot be restored. Proceed with caution.

<a id="section-10-2"></a>

## 10.2. Manage unread messages

The Unread Messages page in the Message Center module displays all unread messages related to services, operations, process approvals, application O&M, announcements, and alerts that you have received.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2e83f8bac8519378ecfad05568e7323b.png" width="13" alt=""> icon.

3. In the **Message** panel, click **More**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/74e0aefa28bf672e074a2c07568f96b5.jpeg)

4. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Unread Messages**.

5. On the **Unread Messages** page, switch to different tabs to view the unread messages of the corresponding business type.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/907e0590a7446ec26518aea921a88bf0.jpeg)

6. In the upper part of a tab, specify the start date and end date to quickly find unread messages within the specified time range.

7. In the message list, click the message title and view the content of the message on the right side of the page. The message is then marked as read. The <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/cf7b5603201c57d911f6e805ea7eea96.png" width="6" alt=""> icon indicates that the

   > **Note**
   >

   > **Important**
