## 10.4. Query records

This topic describes how to query the historical records of message senders and message content.

**Limits**

Only the users within your permission scope are displayed.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/2e83f8bac8519378ecfad05568e7323b.png" width="13" alt=""> icon.

3. In the **Message** panel, click **More**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/74e0aefa28bf672e074a2c07568f96b5.jpeg)

4. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Query Records**.

5. On the **Query Records** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Username**, **Template Name**, **Template Type**, **Error Code**, and **Send At** parameters, and then click **Search**.

6. View the message senders and message content that are displayed.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Click **Preview** in the **Content** column of a record to view the message content in the **Content Preview** panel.
   >
   > - Click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f3319de689afeaf6f9c9a36f9cd8ea64.png" width="12" alt=""> icon next to the **Sending Status** column and select **Sent**,
   >
   >   **Preparing**, **Send failed**, or **Timeout** to filter records by status.
   >
   > - If a record is in the **Send failed** or **Timeout** state, click **Retry** in the **Actions** column to send the message again.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e38f383bbc7e1c1972c74bb2cecf3f7e.jpeg)

# 11.User center

<a id="section-11-1"></a>

## 11.1. User information management

On the User Information page, you can manage the information about your account, such as the basic information, password, multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices, methods to receive system messages, and AccessKey pairs.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the upper-right corner of the page, click the profile picture of the current user.

3. Select **User Information** in the menu that appears.

   | Section or tab | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Basic Information | In the <strong>Basic Information</strong> section, you can view the detailed information about your account. You can also click <strong>Edit</strong> in the upper-right corner of the section to modify the account information, such as the display name, mobile phone number, landline phone number, email address, DingTalk token, and remarks.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/bfdc7666d61d3e50ba4196237b95bafb.jpeg) |
   | MFA | In the <strong>MFA</strong> section, you can enable or disable the MFA feature. For more information about MFA, see Manage MFA.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/77d5083f511cb4d474091e41b63d82a0.jpeg) |
   | Messages | In the <strong>Messages</strong> section, you can select one or more methods for receiving system messages. Make sure that the selected methods are configured. For more information, see Message Gateway.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a1df9af935ddfa213866a5de93b6bb33.jpeg) |
   | AccessKey Pair | In the <strong>AccessKey Pair</strong> section, you can manage your AccessKey pairs. For more information, see AccessKey pairs of a personal account.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/55dbc39fc8b2c0bd6575e29505f3548a.jpeg) |
   | Resource Sets | On the <strong>Resource Sets</strong> tab, you can switch between different roles and view the resource sets to which each role is added.<br>Note<br>If multiple clouds have been bound, you can switch between the cloud tabs to view the corresponding resource sets.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/635c4b5aa6b4e1a68496818157b55641.jpeg) |
   | User Groups | On the <strong>User Groups</strong> tab, you can view the user groups to which the user belongs.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1cdb91c0b47cc723beafd2ba18a553a6.jpeg) |
   | Role Permissions | On the <strong>Role Permissions</strong> tab, you can switch between different roles and view the <strong>management permissions</strong>, <strong>application permissions</strong>, and <strong>menu permissions</strong> of each role.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e9790dee6b6795f0eadb00f5257217d7.jpeg) |
   | Left-side section | ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/ad3ac79e823d78ae2a388e66de85852f.jpeg)<br>Note<br>If the user has been granted a multi-cloud role, multi-cloud identity information is also displayed.<br>• Click <strong>Switch Role</strong>. If the current user has multiple roles, you can switch to another role. In the Switch Role dialog box, you can also set a role as the default role.<br>• Click <strong>Change Password</strong>. In the Change Password dialog box, specify the current password and new password and confirm the password. Click <strong>OK</strong> to change the password.<br>• Click <strong>View Current Role Policy</strong> to view the Resource Access Management (RAM) role, policies, and trusted policies of the level-1 organization to which the current role belongs. |

## 11.2. Enable the proxy mode as a proxy administrator for a proxy user

This topic describes how to enable the proxy mode as a proxy administrator for a proxy user.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the proxy administrator role.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the upper-right corner of a page, click the profile picture to expand the User Center menu.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/40a68d916ed298ac8617b803523406ed.jpeg)

3. In the **Proxy Status** section, select an organization or a resource set and click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/fd200785245d1756320b9003092f4cd6.png" width="30" alt=""> to

   enable the proxy mode.

   <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/73ea5338b51ef604584a48b841c56c1d.png" width="26" alt=""> indicates that the proxy mode is enabled.

   - If you have not previously managed the resources of the proxy user as a proxy administrator, you must reset the initial password of the proxy user account the first time you enable the proxy mode for the proxy user.

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     In the dialog box that appears, click **Modify**.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/18a62295ed1405af442e66fd84758932.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li>

     In the Reset Password dialog box, change the password and click **Confirm**.

     > **Note**
     >
     > To obtain the initial password of a proxy user account, contact the administrator.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/74f08567f4ac8f4786ddc20729d0ca05.jpeg)

     </li>

     </ol>

4. Check whether **Proxy Status** appears in the top navigation bar. If Proxy Status appears in the top navigation bar, the proxy mode is enabled.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f7989701995f665b8e9b68ae0c99e523.jpeg)

<a id="section-12"></a>

# 12.OpenAPI Explorer

<a id="section-12-1"></a>

## 12.1. Overview

This topic describes the permissions and overview of OpenAPI Explorer.

OpenAPI Explorer is an integrated portal that allows external developers to use Apsara Stack capabilities. It provides documentation, debugging tools, SDKs, and sample code of APIs. OpenAPI Explorer provides a series of APIs and shares its core capabilities and services with external developers. This way, external developers can access and use these resources to develop innovative and growth services.

**Permissions**

The following table describes the default permissions in OpenAPI Explorer.

| Permission | Description |
| --- | --- |
| View call statistics | You can view all features in the Call Statistics module. |
| View page integration configurations | You can view all features in Page Integration Configurations. You cannot modify these features. |
| Modify page integration configurations | You can view and modify all feature configurations in Page Integration Configurations. |

Different roles have different permissions in OpenAPI Explorer. The following table describes the default roles and their permissions.

| Role | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| Organization administrator | Views call statistics and page integration configurations. |
| Operations administrator | Views call statistics and views and modifies page integration configurations. |
| Security auditor | Views call statistics and page integration configurations. |

**Overview of OpenAPI Explorer**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, select a service or feature based on your business requirements. The following table describes the services and features.

   | Menu | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Home | • The <strong>API Integration</strong> tab provides API developer guides, API debugging tools, SDK sample code, and API call statistics. To view API call statistics, you must be granted the required permissions. You can search by cloud service or text content. This tab contains the Popular Services and Recent Calls tabs.<br>Note<br>You can click <strong>View Cloud Service Endpoint</strong> to go to the Service Endpoint page and query the endpoints of each cloud service.<br>• On the <strong>Page Integration</strong> tab, you can view the process of page integration configuration. You can click <strong>Page Integration Configuration</strong> to go to the <strong>Overview</strong> page of Page Integration. |
   | API Integrati on | • <strong>API Documentation</strong>: provides the API references of cloud services.<br>• <strong>API Debugging</strong>: allows you to debug API operations.<br>• <strong>API Change History</strong>: records the change history of API operations of cloud services.<br>• <strong>SDK Sample Code</strong>: provides SDK sample code of cloud services.<br>• <strong>Diagnostic Center</strong>: allows you to perform intelligent diagnostics on API error messages.<br>• <strong>MCP Service Management</strong>: allows you to create and manage MCP interface services. The MCP service allows you to convert API operations of cloud services into online MCP interfaces. This allows large language models (LLMs) to call API operations to perform operations on cloud resources. |
   | Call Statistics | You can view data on the <strong>Call Overview</strong>, <strong>Call Statistics</strong>, and <strong>Statistical Reports</strong> pages.<br>• <strong>Call Overview</strong>: displays the call trends and error distribution.<br>• <strong>Call Trend</strong>: You can select a time range and view the total number of calls, the number of errors, and the error rate within the selected period of time. The number of calls to each cloud service is displayed in a column chart. You can move the pointer over the column chart to view the number of successful calls and the number of failed calls.<br>• <strong>Error Distribution</strong>: You can view the distribution of API errors based on filter conditions such as the call date, cloud service, and API version.<br>• <strong>Call Statistics</strong>: You can specify the filter conditions, such as service, API version, API name, and time range, to query the call details of an API operation of a cloud service. You can view the namespace, number of calls each time, average duration per call, and call success rate of an API operation. You can click <strong>Call Source</strong> <strong>Distribution</strong> in the Actions column of an API operation to view the AccessKey ID that is used for calls and identify the source of the operation.<br>• <strong>Statistical Reports</strong>: You can configure the following parameters to create a statistical report task based on your business requirements: Interval, Data Source, Statistical Policy, Keyword, and Custom Aggregation Policy. After a statistical report task is created, you can view the task status and report details at any time. This helps you understand the status of your business. In addition, you can start, stop, or delete statistical report tasks. |
   | Automati on Service Desk | The Automation Service Desk module includes the Template, Task, and Terraform Explorer modules.<br>• Template: includes Template Management and Template Center. Apsara Stack provides a series of templates based on Terraform to manage cloud resources in a standardized manner. You can also upload custom templates and edit templates online.<br>• Task: orchestrates resources based on templates and tracks the status of resources during the orchestration process.<br>• Terraform Explorer: debugs Terraform templates online. |
   | Page Integrati on | You can configure page integration for Apsara Stack pages to directly embed cloud management pages into third-party platforms. You can hide the top navigation bar and adjust the color of a page to ensure that the page adapts to third-party platforms.This minimizes the effort required to integrate pages into third-party platforms. |

## 12.2. API integration

<a id="section-12-2-1"></a>

### 12.2.1. API documentation

This topic describes how to view the API documentation of a cloud service.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **API Documentation** in the top navigation bar.

4. In the upper-left corner, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c0573d48d3e19069190f4a548ff6472c.png" width="26" alt=""> icon to select the cloud service

   whose API references you want to view.

5. In the left-side navigation pane, click Change History or Developer Guide.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3e16e111688d2aeb52fbd59321b989bf.jpeg)

   - On the Change History page, view the change history of API operations. Click the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e71f89d62a5b35427847a4c47fb96f5a.png" width="10" alt=""> icon

     before an API operation to view the change details of the API operation in the JSON format.

   - In the Developer Guide section, view the methods to call API operations and the API references.

<a id="section-12-2-2"></a>

### 12.2.2. API debugging

This topic describes how to debug an API operation.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **API Debugging** in the top navigation bar.

4. In the upper-left corner, move the pointer over the <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c0573d48d3e19069190f4a548ff6472c.png" width="26" alt=""> icon to select the cloud service

   whose API operation you want to debug.

5. Select an API version from the **Version** drop-down list.

6. In the left-side navigation page, enter the name of the API operation that you want to debug in the search box to search for the API operation.

7. Click the API operation, configure the parameters on the **Parameter** and **Request Header** tabs, and then click **Initiate Call**.

   > **Important**
   >
   > - OpenAPI Explorer obtains a temporary AccessKey pair of the current account by using the user login information. If you initiate a call, you may perform operations on resources online within the current account. Proceed with caution.
   >
   > - You can click **Clear** to clear the configured parameters.
   >
   > - On the **Debug Parameters** tab, you can view the information about the request parameters.
   >
   > - On the **SDK Examples** tab, you can view SDK sample code on the Java, Python, and Go tabs. You can also click **Download Project**, **View Dependencies**, and **Copy** in the upper-right corner of the tab.
   >
   > - On the **Call Result** tab, you can view the call result.
   >
   > - On the **API Reference** tab, view the API reference.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/68759fe0b614d02cac0d69804ea70e92.jpeg)

<a id="section-12-2-3"></a>

This topic describes how to view the change history of API operations.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **API Change History** in the top navigation bar.

4. On the API Change Overview page, configure the **Service Category**, **Service Name**, and **Change Type** parameters and click **Search**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > Fuzzy search is supported.

5. View the change history of API operations in the **Change Result** section.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/52ca4ac7f8fcbfe984f10c76941692c7.jpeg)

### 12.2.5. Diagnostics center

The Diagnostic Center module allows you to perform intelligent diagnostics on API error messages.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **Diagnostic Center** in the top navigation bar.

4. On the **Intelligent Diagnostics** page, enter an error message that contains the RequestId or ErrorCode parameter in the field.

   > **Important**
   >
   > The RequestId parameter is used to query the diagnostics solutions of the service that you access. The ErrorCode parameter is used to query the diagnostics solutions of all services. If an error message contains both the RequestId and ErrorCode parameters, the RequestId parameter prevails.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7c59136ab01798b4705c8b808e8a6902.jpeg)

5. Click **Diagnose**.

6. On the **Diagnostic Plan** tab, view the diagnostics information.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f69161046c8e5dec84e7c44f784d763a.jpeg)

<a id="section-12-2-6"></a>

### 12.2.6. MCP service management

This topic describes how to create and manage Model Context Protocol (MCP) services.

**Custom services**

**Procedure**

On the Custom Services tab, create and manage custom MCP services.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **MCP Service Management** in the top navigation bar.

4. On the **MCP Service** page, click the **Custom Services** tab.

5. On the **Custom Services** tab, click **Create MCP Service**.

6. On the **Create MCP Service** page, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Name | The name of the MCP service. |
   | Organization | The organization to which the MCP service belongs. |
   | Resource Set | The resource set to which the MCP service belongs. |
   | Region | The region to which the MCP service belongs. |

   | Document Language | The language of the MCP service document. Valid values: <strong>Chinese</strong> and <strong>English</strong>. |
   | --- | --- |
   | Cloud Products and APIs | Configure API operations for the MCP service.<br>• Add cloud services and API operations<br>a. Click <strong>Add Cloud Product and API</strong>.<br>b. In the <strong>Create</strong> dialog box, select the service, the service version, and API operations to be added.<br>c. Click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>• Add API operations for an added cloud service<br>a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the added cloud service for which you want to add API operations and click <strong>Add</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>b. In the <strong>Add API</strong> dialog box, select the API operations that you want to add.<br>c. Click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>• Modify an API operation of a service<br>a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the API operation of the service that you want to modify and click <strong>Edit</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>b. In the panel that appears, modify the settings in the <strong>API Overview</strong>, <strong>API Request Description</strong>, and <strong>API Parameters</strong> sections.<br>Note<br>• When the answer of the large language model (LLM) that depends on the MCP service is inaccurate, you can modify the API overview, API request description, and API parameters to improve the LLM's understanding of each API operation.<br>• When you modify API parameters, you can also delete some optional parameters. When the LLM transmits parameters to the API operation, these deleted parameters are invisible to the API operation. This reduces the error rate of the LLM and the token consumption.<br>• After you save the modifications, you must disconnect and reconnect the MCP service on the client to make the modifications take effect.<br>c. Click <strong>Save and Submit</strong>.<br>• Remove an API operation<br>a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the API operation that you want to remove and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>b. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>• Remove all API operations of an added cloud service of a version<br>a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the cloud service whose API operations you want to remove and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the <strong>Actions</strong> column.<br>b. In the message that appears, click <strong>OK</strong>. |
   | Description | The description of the MCP service. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a1c043104b6da7d887836ab06a29f82e.jpeg)

7. Click **Create**.

8. In the **Risks** message, read the risk tips and click **I have known the risks and continue the update**.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d08901160f4792bf476f9e7709f0abb5.jpeg)

   - Click **View Configuration Methods** in the **Configuration Information** section. In the **Configuration Method** dialog box, view the details of the configuration method.

<a id="section-12-3"></a>

## 12.3. Call Statistics

This topic describes how to use the Call Statistics module in OpenAPI Explorer.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, click **Call Statistics** in the top navigation bar.

4. Perform the following operations in the **Call Statistics** module:

   - **Call Overview**: In the left-side navigation pane, click **Call Overview**.

     - **Call Trend**: Configure the **Call Date** parameter to select a time range and view the total number of calls, the number of errors, and the error rate within the specified time range. The number of calls to each cloud service is displayed in a column chart. Move the pointer over the column chart to view the numbers of successful and failed calls.

       ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b6b9998b3f933c655a505573b7c5e0ba.jpeg)

     - **Error Distribution**: Configure the **Call Date**, **Cloud Service**, and **API Version** parameters to view the distribution of API errors based on the specified filter conditions.

       ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0123131b393db3c56f044c6c80c0b1b7.jpeg)

   - **Call Statistics**: In the left-side navigation pane, click **Call Statistics**.

     Configure the **Service**, **API Version**, **API Name**, and **Called At** parameters to search for the call details of an API operation of a cloud service. The information is displayed in the following columns: **API Name**, **Service**, **Namespace**, **API Version**, **Calls/Times**, **Average Latency (ms)**, and **Success Rate**.

     > **Note**
     >
     > - The value of the **Called At** parameter must be within seven days.
     >
     > - Click **Call Source Distribution** in the **Actions** column of an API operation to view the **AccessKey** ID and the source service of the API operation.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d07b620eaf767136ac10d0d9bc7bcf3a.jpeg)

   - **Statistical Reports**: In the left-side navigation pane, click **Statistical Reports**.

     - Create a statistical report task: On the Statistical Reports page, click **Create Statistical Report**. In the Create Task dialog box, configure the parameters described in the following table and click **OK**.

       | Parameter | Description |
       | --- | --- |
       | Task Name | The name of the statistical report task. |
       | Interval | The interval at which the statistical report task retrieves statistics. Valid values:<br>• 1 Hour<br>• 6 Hours<br>• 12 Hours<br>• 24 Hours |
       | Data Source | The source of the statistics. Valid value: <strong>pop-sls</strong>. |
       | Statistical Policy | The method used to retrieve statistics. Valid value: <strong>Keyword</strong> <strong>Retrieval</strong>. |
       | Keyword | The keywords used to retrieve statistics. Click <strong>Add Entry</strong> and specify keywords in key-value pairs. |
       | Custom Aggregation Policy | The aggregation policy. Select an aggregation policy from the drop-down list. |

     - View a statistical report task: The created statistical report tasks are displayed in the task list.

       ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d260f6b76d938e5c524888284c409927.jpeg)

       <ol type="a">

       <li>

       Find the statistical report task that you want to view and click **View Reports** in the **Actions** column.

       </li>

       <li>

       The execution history of the statistical report task is displayed. Click **View Details** in the **Actions** column of a report to view the report details in the following sections: **Basic Information**, **Matching Info**, and **Time Distribution**.

       </li>

       </ol>

     - Start a statistical report task: Find the statistical report task that you want to start and click **Start** in the **Actions** column If the task changes to the **Running** state, the task is started.

       > **Note**
       >
       > You can start tasks only in the **Canceled** state.

     - Stop a statistical report task: Find the statistical report task that you want to stop and click **Stop** in the **Actions** column. If the task changes to the **Canceled** state, the task is stopped.

       > **Note**
       >
       > You can stop tasks only in the **Running** state.

     - Delete a statistical report task: Find the statistical report task that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

## 12.4. Automation Service Desk

This topic describes how to use the Automation Service Desk module.

**Manage templates**

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, click **Automation Service Desk** in the top navigation bar.

4. In the upper-left corner, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.

5. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Template** > **Template Management**.

6. On the Template Management tab, click **New Template**. In the New Template panel, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

   | Paramete r | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Organiz ation | The organization to which the template belongs. |
   | Resourc e Set | The resource set to which the template belongs. |
   | Templat e Name | The name of the template. |
   | Templat e Descript ion | The description of the template. |
   | Templat e File | The template file. Click <strong>Upload File</strong> to upload a template file.<br>Note<br>The template file must meet the following requirements:<br>• The file must be a ZIP package.<br>• The file name must be encoded in UTF-8.<br>• The file name is case-sensitive.<br>• The file name must be 1 to 1,023 bytes in length.<br>• The file name cannot contain forward slashes (/) or backslashes (\\).<br>• The file cannot exceed 10 MB in size. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4d453ea5612555e615ad5f5ee4cb7735.jpeg)

7. Click **OK**.

8. Perform operations on the template. The following table describes the supported operations.

   | Operation | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | View a template | i. Find the template that you want to manage and click its ID to go to the template details page.<br>ii. On the template details page, view the template information on the Template Management, Version Management, and Resource Orchestration tabs.<br>• <strong>Template Management</strong>: displays the template information in the <strong>Basic</strong> <strong>Information</strong>, <strong>Version Information</strong>, and <strong>Template Content</strong> sections.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6a27f15f452f052c7e52a4e2ad6a3285.jpeg)<br>• <strong>Basic Information</strong>: displays the <strong>Template ID</strong>, <strong>Creation Time</strong>, <strong>Template</strong> <strong>Name</strong>, <strong>Template Description</strong>, and <strong>Source Path</strong> parameters.<br>• Click <strong>Edit</strong> next to the template name to rename the template.<br>• Click <strong>Edit</strong> next to the template description to modify the template description.<br>• Click <strong>Settings</strong> next to the source path to update the template file.<br>• <strong>Version Information</strong>: displays the latest version of the template. If the template details change, click <strong>Publish New Version</strong> to generate a new version.<br>• <strong>Template Content</strong>: displays template content on the Template Details and Associate Parameter Set tabs.<br>• On the Template Details tab, click <strong>Download Project</strong> to download the template file in the <strong>ZIP</strong> format to your computer for storage.<br>• On the Template Details tab, turn on <strong>Edit Code</strong> to manually modify the template.<br>• On the Associate Parameter Set tab, view the parameter sets that are associated with the template.<br>• Click <strong>Associate Existing Parameter Set</strong>. In the Associate Existing Parameter Set dialog box, select existing parameter sets that you want to associate with the template. You can associate up to five parameter sets with a template.<br>• If you no longer need an associated parameter set, click <strong>Disassociate</strong> in the Actions column to disassociate the parameter set from the template.<br>• If the existing parameter sets do not meet your business requirements, click <strong>Create Parameter Set</strong> to create a custom parameter set.<br>• <strong>Version Management</strong>: displays the version information about the template.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4137be06c85065798a9748574d66e373.jpeg)<br>• Select a version from the <strong>Current Version</strong> drop-down list to view the corresponding version information.<br>• Click <strong>Create Task with Current Version</strong> to create a task based on the current version.<br>• On the Template Details tab, click <strong>Download Project</strong> to download the template file in the <strong>ZIP</strong> format to your computer for storage.<br>• On the Associate Parameter Set tab, click <strong>Associate Existing Parameter</strong> <strong>Set</strong>. In the Associate Existing Parameter Set dialog box, select existing parameter sets that you want to associate with the template. You can associate up to five parameter sets with a template. If the existing parameter sets do not meet your business requirements, click <strong>Create Parameter Set</strong> to create a custom parameter set.<br>• <strong>Resource Orchestration</strong>: displays the tasks that are associated with the template. |
   | Modify a template | Find the template that you want to modify and click <strong>Edit</strong> in the Actions column. In<br>• Click <strong>Create Task</strong> to create a task based on the template. For more the Edit panel, modify the template name and description and click <strong>OK</strong>.information, see the Orchestrate resources section of this topic.<br>• Click the ID of a task to go to the task details page. |
   | Create a task | • Find the task that you want to manage and click <strong>Initiate Job</strong> in the ActionsFind the template that you want to manage and click <strong>Create Task</strong> in the Actions column. In the Initiate Job dialog box, enter a description and click <strong>OK</strong> to startcolumn to create a resource orchestration task based on the template. For more a job.information, see the Orchestrate resources section of this topic. |
   | Share a template | Find the template that you want to share, move the pointer over the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1d674b9ceabc34b800342b44840686e8.png" width="14" alt="">icon in the<br>Actions column, and then select <strong>Share</strong>. In the Shared Template message, click <strong>OK</strong>.After the template is shared, it is displayed on the Shared Template tab of the All Templates page. |
   | Unshare a template | Find the template that you want to unshare, move the pointer over the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1d674b9ceabc34b800342b44840686e8.png" width="14" alt="">icon in the<br>Actions column, and then select <strong>Cancel Sharing</strong>. In the Unshare Template message, click <strong>OK</strong>. After the template is unshared, it is removed from the Shared Template tab of the All Templates page. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/9b29763badd28320296284f696fa70fd.jpeg)

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Delete a template</td>
       <td>Find the template that you want to delete, move the pointer over the<img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1d674b9ceabc34b800342b44840686e8.png" width="14" alt="">icon in the<br>Actions column, and then select <strong>Delete</strong>. In the Delete Template message, click <strong>OK</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

**Manage parameter sets**

**Procedure**

1. In the left-side navigation pane of the **Automation Service Desk** page, choose **Template** > **Template Management**.

2. On the Template Management page, click the **Parameter Set Management** tab.

3. On the Parameter Set Management tab, click **Create Parameter Set**. In the Create Parameter Set panel, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Parameter Set Name | The name of the parameter set.<br>The name must start with a letter and cannot start with http:// or https://. The name must be 2 to 25 characters in length and can contain hyphens (-), underscores (_), letters, and digits. |
   | Parameter Set Description | The description of the parameter set. |
   | Parameter | The parameters in the parameter set. You can create, modify, and delete parameters based on your business requirements.<br>• Create a parameter: Click <strong>Add Parameter</strong>. In the Add Parameter dialog box, configure the Parameter Name, Parameter Type, and Parameter Value parameters, and click <strong>OK</strong>.<br>• Modify a parameter: Find the parameter that you want to modify and click <strong>Edit</strong> in the Actions column. In the Edit dialog box, modify the parameter value and click <strong>OK</strong>. You cannot modify the parameter name or parameter type.<br>• Delete a parameter: Find the parameter that you want to delete and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the Actions column. In the Delete Parameter message, click <strong>OK</strong> to delete the parameter. To delete multiple parameters at a time, select the parameters that you want to delete and click <strong>Batch Delete</strong> in the lower part of the panel. In the Delete Parameters message, click <strong>OK</strong>. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1d7ef982b1fc79788f06b6af78208f00.jpeg)

4. Click **OK**.

5. Perform operations on the parameter set. The following table describes the supported operations.

   | Operation | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | View a parameter set | The created parameter sets are displayed in the parameter set list. Find the parameter set that you want to view and click <strong>Details</strong> in the Actions column. In the Parameter List message, view the parameters in the parameter set. |
   | Modify a parameter set | Find the parameter set that you want to modify and click <strong>Modify</strong> in the Actions column. In the Modifying Parameter Set panel, modify the parameter set name, parameter set description, and parameters based on your business requirements. |
   | Delete a parameter set | Find the parameter set that you want to delete and click <strong>Delete</strong> in the Actions column. In the message that appears, click <strong>Delete</strong>.<br>Important<br>You cannot delete the parameter sets that are associated with tasks or templates. |

**Use the Template Center module**

**Procedure**

1. In the left-side navigation pane of the **Automation Service Desk** page, choose **Template** > **Template Center**.

2. On the Template Center page, click the **Preset Template** or **Shared Template** tab to view preset or shared templates.

   - View details of a template: Move the pointer over a template and click **View Details** to view the basic information and details of the template.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/771844f0c63af85fc634fec0103d2898.jpeg)

     - The template description and template name are displayed in the Basic Information section.

     - The Template Details tab displays the content of the template, including the directory structure and the details of each file.

     - The time displayed in the upper-right corner of the page indicates the estimated amount of time to use the template to call cloud resources. The estimated amount of time is displayed only for preset templates.

   - **Download code**: You can download the template code as a package to your computer for storage. To download code of a template, move the pointer over the template and click **Download Code**. Alternatively, click **Download Code** on the template details page.

   - Reference a template: In the upper-right corner of the template details page, click **Reference Template** to reference the content of the template file to create a template. To reference a shared template, move the pointer over the shared template and click **Reference Template**. Alternatively, click **Reference Template** on the template details page. In the New Template panel, configure the Organization, Resource Set, Template Name, and Template Description parameters, and then click **OK**.

**Orchestrate resources**

**Procedure**

1. In the left-side navigation pane of the **Automation Service Desk** page, choose **Task** > **Resource Orchestration**.

2. On the Resource Orchestration page, click **Create Task**. In the Create Task panel, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Task Name | The name of the task.<br>The task name must start with a letter and cannot start with http:// or https://.The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length and can contain hyphens (-), underscores (_), letters, and digits. |
   | Organization | The organization to which the task belongs. |
   | Resource Set | The resource set to which the task belongs. |
   | Select Template ID/Version | The template based on which you want to create the task and the template version. |
   | Associate Parameter Set | The existing parameter sets that you want to associate with the task. You can select multiple parameter sets.<br>Important<br>You cannot associate a parameter set that is already associated with a template and a template version or an empty parameter set with the task. |
   | Execution Mode | The method used to execute the task. Valid values: <strong>Manually Execute</strong> and <strong>Automatic Execution</strong>.<br>Note<br>If you select Manually Execute, when the preview of the execution plan is complete, and the preview result changes, a manual execution plan enters the pending state, and manual confirmation is required to complete the execution. If you select Automatic Execution, the execution plan skips manual confirmation and is automatically executed. |
   | User Information Configuration | The AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret. |
   | Cloud Resource Ownership Configuration | The organization and resource set to which the cloud resources belong. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/e0049a14ed5d6688266dd0eded8ccad9.jpeg)

3. Click **OK**.

4. Perform operations on the task. The following table describes the supported operations.

   | Operation | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | View a task | • View the information about created tasks in the following columns: <strong>Task</strong> <strong>ID/Name</strong>, <strong>Status</strong>, <strong>Template ID/Name</strong>, <strong>Template Description</strong>, <strong>Template</strong> <strong>Version</strong>, <strong>Organization</strong>, <strong>Resource Set</strong>, and <strong>Creation Time</strong>.<br>• Find the task that you want to manage and click its ID to go to the task details page. On the task details page, view the information on the <strong>Task Details</strong>, <strong>Job</strong> <strong>History</strong>, and <strong>Resources</strong> tabs.<br>• <strong>Task Details</strong>: displays the information in the Basic Information, Current Job, and Template Content sections.<br>Note<br>• You can click <strong>Initiate Job</strong> in the Basic Information section to initiate a new job.<br>• You can click <strong>Modify</strong> in the Basic Information section to modify the task.<br>• You can click <strong>Status Details</strong> in the Current Job section to go to the execution details page to view the task execution details.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/95d1aa2406ff1222fcb65253825de627.jpeg)<br>• <strong>Job History</strong>: displays the information about historical jobs in the <strong>Job ID/Job</strong> <strong>Name</strong>, <strong>Execution Status</strong>, <strong>Executed Version</strong>, and <strong>Creation Time</strong> columns.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/008a58a89bedafdc7c4cfe944c865b60.jpeg)<br>Click the job ID to go to the task execution details page.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0be59464ea7d3c38d17a94a5809f7197.jpeg)<br>• <strong>Resources</strong>: displays the information about resource instances generated by the task in the <strong>Instance ID/Name</strong>, <strong>Cloud Services</strong>, <strong>Organization</strong>, <strong>Resource Set</strong>, and <strong>Creation Time</strong> columns.<br>Note<br>After a resource is created, you can click <strong>Details</strong> to go to the resource details page. |
   | Modify a task | ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/16ae4244856bf4b1a441031d5032e9bc.jpeg)<br>Find the task that you want to modify and click <strong>Modify</strong> in the Actions column. In the Edit Task panel, modify the task information. You cannot modify the organization, resource set, or template ID of the task.<br>• Find the template that you want to manage and click its ID to go to the template |
   | Initiate a job | details page. On the template details page, view the information on the Find the task that you want to manage and click <strong>Initiate Job</strong> in the Actions<strong>Template Management</strong>, <strong>Version management</strong>, and <strong>Resource</strong> column. In the Initiate Job dialog box, enter a description and click <strong>OK</strong>.<strong>Orchestration</strong> tabs. |

## 12.5. Page integration

This topic describes the procedure for page integration.

**Background information**

The Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console provides configuration capabilities for page integration, including customization of page color scheme, language, appearance and theme color, brand logo, and platform version declaration. The console supports hiding original brand information, adjusting layout, and changing page styles to match the style of the customer’s or third-party ISV’s cloud management console, thereby enhancing consistency in user experience.

**Prerequisites**

Before integrating the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console pages into a customer-owned or third-party ISV management console, you must complete SSO authentication through the Cloud Management Platform. You must configure unified identity authentication between the management console application (which will integrate Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console pages) and the private cloud Cloud Management Platform. This means configuring the Cloud Management Platform as the Service Provider (SP) and the customer-owned or third-party ISV management console as the Identity Provider (IdP), ensuring single sign-on (SSO) support when users navigate between platforms.

For specific configuration methods of third-party authentication in the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console, see Third-party authentication.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

2. Click **Product** in the top navigation bar, then select **Development tools** > **APIs and tools** > **Developer Portal**.

3. On the **Developer Portal** page, click **Page Integration** in the menu bar.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/0a8d65788b690806aad4d177d3ab8425.jpeg)

4. On the **Page Integration Overview** page, click **Page open configuration** to complete Embedding target application configuration, Page style configuration, and Embedded page list configuration.

5. After completing the configuration, embed the required cloud service management pages into the management console application that needs to integrate Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console pages.

   On the **Page Integration Overview** page, click **Page URL embedding** to view the operation URLs of the configured cloud service management pages.

**Embedding target application configuration**

Fill in the information of the Management Console application (your own or a third-party ISV Management Console) that needs to integrate pages from the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

To ensure that resource operation buttons (such as Create and Modify) on embedded cloud service management pages correctly redirect to the corresponding resource creation or modification pages in the integrating party's Management Console, you must configure the appropriate resource operation link addresses for these buttons. This achieves seamless integration between Management Console resource management operations and the integrating party's business.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can change the link URL to a third-party operation link address. The domain name of the modified link address must match the root domain name of the embedded page, and the address must be an absolute URL.

# 13.Apsara Stack Skills portal

The Apsara Stack Skills portal is a centralized management portal for open skills in Apsara Stack Enterprise Edition. The portal enables Apsara Stack users to discover, browse, install, and manage skills. Skills are standardized capabilities that AI agents use to call Alibaba Cloud service CLI or MCP and intelligently manage cloud resources on the tenant side.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. Go to the homepage of the Apsara Stack Skills portal.

   - Method 1: Click **Products** in the top menu bar and choose **Development Tools** > **APIs & SDK** > **Apsara Stack Skills Portal**.

   - Method 2: Go to the OpenAPI Explorer.

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Click **Products** in the top menu bar and choose **Development Tools** > **APIs & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**.

     </li>

     <li>

     On the OpenAPI Explorer page, click **Apsara Stack Skills Portal** in the top menu.

     </li>

     </ol>

3. View the information on the portal homepage.

   | Page section | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Portal homepage | This section displays the Skills portal. Click <strong>View All Skills</strong> to go to the <strong>All</strong> <strong>Skills</strong> page.<br>![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/810c385cf76151c6b97a7e63ab773463.jpeg) |

   <table>
     <tr>
       <td>Popular Skills</td>
       <td>This section displays the top six skills cards by popularity. Click <strong>View More</strong> to go to the <strong>All Skills</strong> page.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7e84feb85eb1c92cfd5a19a71003de79.jpeg" alt=""></td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Product Category</td>
       <td>This section displays the number of skills by cloud product category. Click a card to go to the <strong>All Skills</strong> page and view the filtered results for the corresponding category.<br><img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/4560be531ccb0fd7610a8bf8ce8a682d.jpeg" alt=""></td>
     </tr>
   </table>

4. Go to the **All Skills** page and browse skills.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/d5fa4ec14b436b07644d6654ba5140e8.png" width="12" alt=""> on a skill to add the skill to your favorites.
   >
   > - Click <img src="en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/1fed0b35afaa2b125d795ce9a3841847.png" width="14" alt=""> on a skill to download the skill to your local device.
   >
   > - In the upper-right corner of the page, you can sort and display skills by My Favorites, Most Downloaded, Most Favorited, or Default (Latest), and switch between card mode and list mode.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/27400c6de23567d1dbe99e1bf40f3118.jpeg)

5. Click a skill name to go to the skill details page. View the information on the Skill Introduction tab and the Skill Files tab.

<a id="section-14"></a>

# 14.Edge Cloud management

<a id="section-14-1"></a>

## 14.1. View edge entities

The EDGE list page displays the connected edge entities. You can view the connection status of the edge entities and log on to the console of an edge entity.

**Prerequisites**

Edge entities are connected. For more information, see Configure edge entities.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Computing** > **Edge Computing** > **Edge Entity**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Edge Entity**.

4. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.

5. On the **EDGE list** page, view the information about the connected edge entity in the following columns: **Edge Entity ID/Name**, **Organization/Resource Set**, **Region**, **Edge Entity Type**, **Edge Entity Status**, and **Edge Entity Control**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > You can click **Jump Edge Console** in the Edge Entity Console column to go to the console of an edge entity.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/480b3cda2914b047e843b5615e5ca078.jpeg)

6. Find an edge entity and click the ID of the edge entity to go to the **Edge Entity Overview** page.

   - **View the basic information**

     In the **Basic Information** section, view the following information about the edge entity: the edge entity name, edge entity ID, edge entity type, organization, resource set, region, and link to the edge entity console.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/3f4b8341d00d73bd386af215d392dba5.jpeg)

   - **View the overview information**

     On the **Overview** tab, view the CPU capacity, memory capacity, primary storage capacity, alert statistics, and number of activated instances of the edge entity.

     | Item | Description |
     | --- | --- |
     | CPU Capacity | Displays the used CPU capacity, total inventory, and percentage of the used CPU capacity. |
     | Memory | Displays the used memory capacity, total inventory, and percentage of the used memory capacity. |
     | Primary Storage Capacity | Displays the used primary storage capacity, total inventory, and percentage of the used primary storage capacity. |
     | Alert Statistics | Displays the total number of alerts for the edge entity and the number of alerts at the <strong>Urgent</strong>, <strong>Critical</strong>, and <strong>Note</strong> levels. |
     | Activated Instances | Displays the resources that are activated for the edge entity, including the total number of resources of each type, the number of resources in the <strong>Running</strong> state, and the percentage of resources in the <strong>Running</strong> state. |

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/6cd6dc68316416f7587d4c9e7896492b.jpeg)

   - **View the resource information**

     On the **Resource Information** tab, view the detailed resource information of the edge entity. You can configure the **Cloud Services**, **Resource Type**, **Creation Start and End Time**, **Resource Name**, and **Resource ID** parameters to filter resources.

     > **Note**
     >
     > - Click **Create Resource**. In the **Select Resource Type** dialog box, configure the **Organization**, **Resource Set Name**, **Edge Entity**, and **Cloud Services** parameters.
     >
     > - Find a resource and click the resource ID. In the panel that appears, view the basic information of the resource, including the cloud platform, resource name, resource ID, region, organization, resource set, creation time, and state.
     >
     > - Find a resource and click **Manage** in the **Actions** column to go to the cloud service resource management page of the edge site. You can manage the resource on the page.
     >
     > - By default, cloud resource information is automatically updated every hour. Find a resource and click **Update** in the **Actions** column to manually update the information about the cloud resource in real time.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/8f732e28823f7481bba3978bdc088dd5.jpeg)

<a id="section-14-2"></a>

## 14.2. Manage resources

On the Resources page, you can view all edge entity resources that you can manage.

**Limits**

Before you create a resource, make sure that you have created an organization and a resource set, and an edge entity is connected.

**Create a resource**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Computing** > **Edge Computing** > **Edge Entity**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Resources**.

4. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.

5. On the **Resources** page, click **Create Resource**.

6. In the **Create Resource** dialog box, configure the **Organizations**, **Resource Set Name**, **Edge Entity**, and **Cloud Services** parameters.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/13d292cc58927c9cde5af0f006c05504.jpeg)

7. Click **Submit**.

**View resources**

1. On the **Resources** page, configure the **Resource Name**, **Resource ID**, **Edge Entity Name**, **Cloud Services**, **Resource Type**, and **Creation Start and End Time** parameters to filter resources.

2. On the Resources page, view the information about resources in the following columns: **Resource ID/Name**, **Edge Entity Name**, **Cloud Services**, **Resource Type**, **Status**, **Organization/Resource Set**, and **Created At**.

   > **Note**
   >
   > - Find a resource and click **Manage** in the **Actions** column to go to the cloud service resource management page of the edge site. You can manage the resource on the page.
   >
   > - Find a resource and click **Update** in the **Actions** column to manually update the information and state of the resource.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/06d63ec033ab047e775c972973d9f0c8.jpeg)

3. Find a resource and click the resource ID. In the panel that appears, view the basic information of the resource, including the cloud platform, resource name, resource ID, region, organization, resource set, creation time, and state.

<a id="section-14-3"></a>

## 14.3. Configure edge entities

On the Edge Entity Configuration page, you can view the connected edge entities and manage the edge entities that do not belong to an organization or a resource set.

**Limits**

Before you connect to an edge entity, make sure that you have created an organization and a resource set.

**Connect to an edge entity**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Computing** > **Edge Computing** > **Edge Entity**.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Edge Entity Configuration**.

4. On the **Edge Entity Configuration** page, click **Connect Edge Entity**.

5. Configure the parameters in the following steps as prompted:

   > **Note**
   >
   > If you have questions when you connect to an edge entity, contact Apsara Stack technical support.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   **Basic Information**: Select an edge entity type and configure information in the **Basic Configuration**, **Associated Organization Configuration**, and **Advanced Settings** sections for the edge entity.

   <table>
     <tr>
       <th colspan="2">Section and parameter</th>
       <th>Description</th>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="2">Basic Configuratio n</td>
       <td>Name</td>
       <td>The custom name of the edge entity.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Edge Entity Type</td>
       <td>The type of the edge entity. Valid values: <strong>Alibaba Cloud</strong> <strong>ZStack</strong> and <strong>Alibaba Cloud SmartX</strong>.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td rowspan="3">Associated Organizatio n Configuratio n</td>
       <td>Organizati on</td>
       <td>The organization to which the edge entity belongs.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Resource Set</td>
       <td>The resource set to which the edge entity belongs.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Region</td>
       <td>The region in which the edge entity resides.</td>
     </tr>
     <tr>
       <td>Advanced Settings</td>
       <td>Connection Configurati on</td>
       <td>The connection configurations of the edge entity.<br>• For more information about the connection configurations of an Alibaba Cloud ZStack edge entity, see the Configuration template for Alibaba Cloud ZStack section of this topic.<br>• For more information about the connection configurations of an Alibaba Cloud SmartX edge entity, see the Configuration template for Alibaba Cloud SmartX section of this topic.</td>
     </tr>
   </table>

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/37788a2f3570f33ccb13388ea3b01af6.jpeg)

   **Configuration template for Alibaba Cloud ZStack**

   JSON

   ```json
   {
     "endPoint": "http://{ip1}:{port1}/zstack",  
     "properties":{
       "oidcAuthEndpoint":"http://{ip2}:{port2}/zstack",  
       "consoleEndpoint":"http://{ip3}:{port3}"
     }
   }
   ```

   > **Note**
   >
   > - endPoint: the IP address and port that are mapped to the Server Load Balancer (SLB) API in the configurations for virtual private cloud (VPC)-based reverse access.
   >
   > - oidcAuthEndpoint: the IP address and port that are mapped to the API in the SLB configurations.
   >
   > - consoleEndpoint: the IP address and port that are mapped to the portal in the SLB configurations.

   **Configuration template for Alibaba Cloud SmartX**

   JSON

   ```json
   {
    "endPoint": "http://{ip1}:{port1}/api/alpha/proxy/cloudtower-alpha-ali-cmp-service
   ",
    "properties": {
     "consoleEndpoint": "http://{ip2}:{port2}"
    }
   }
   ```

   > **Note**
   >
   > - endPoint: the IP address and port that are mapped to the SLB API in the configurations for VIP-based reverse access.
   >
   > - consoleEndpoint: {ip2} indicates the IP address of the SLB instance. {port2} indicates the listener port of the SLB instance that is used to listen to the specified service.

   </li>

   <li>

   **Account Authorization**: Enter the authorization credentials of the edge entity to grant permissions to the current account and synchronize the role of the account.

   | Parameter | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | AccessKey ID | The AccessKey ID of the edge entity. |
   | AccessKey Secret | The AccessKey secret of the edge entity. |

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/f6e4bcd37bb3c9c36936e5a1dd6f6ca5.jpeg)

   - **Obtain the authorization credentials of an Alibaba Cloud ZStack edge entity**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Log on to the Alibaba Cloud ZStack console<strong>.</strong>

     </li>

     <li>

     On the **Operational Management** tab, click **AccessKey Management** in the left-side navigation pane. On the **AccessKey Management** page, view the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret.

     > **Note**
     >
     > If no AccessKey pair is available, click **Generate AccessKey** to create an AccessKey pair.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - **Obtain the authorization credentials of an Alibaba Cloud SmartX edge entity**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Log on to an Alibaba Cloud SmartX edge entity by using a URL in the following format:  `http://{IP address of the Alibaba Cloud SmartX edge entity}/api/alpha/proxy/cloudtower-alpha-ali-cmp-service/admin/get-access-key` .

     > **Note**
     >
     > {IP address of the Alibaba Cloud SmartX edge entity} indicates the IP address of the portal of the Alibaba Cloud SmartX console. Replace the value based on the actual situation.

     </li>

     <li>

     Enter the root account and password of the Cluster Manager role to obtain the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret.

     > **Note**
     >
     > - access: the AccessKey ID of the edge entity.
     >
     > - secret: the AccessKey secret of the edge entity.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/a64fce40a038b42eabbd129f05aeb8d3.jpeg)

     </li>

     </ol>

   </li>

   <li>

   **Federated Logon Settings**: Complete federated logon settings for third-party cloud management.

   - **Federated logon settings for Alibaba Cloud ZStack**

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     In the **Access configuration** field of the **Federated Logon Settings** step, obtain the values of the **clientId** and **clientSecret** parameters.

     ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/b5b25ce54bb0d8dfb68f5ddd2eca7cd3.jpeg)

     </li>

     <li>

     Log on to the Alibaba Cloud ZStack console. On the **Settings** tab, click **Add 3rd-Party Authentication Server**. On the page that appears, add a third-party server for authentication.

     | Parameter | Description |
     | --- | --- |
     | Name | The custom name of the third-party server. |
     | Description | The description of the third-party server. |
     | Type | The type of the third-party server. Set the value to OIDC. |
     | Client ID | The client ID that is obtained from the access configurations of the federated logon settings. |
     | Client Secret | The client secret that is obtained from the access configurations of the federated logon settings. |
     | Authorization Request URL | The authorization request URL, in the following format: <code>https://{Domain name}/auth/realms/cmp/protocol/openid-</code><code>connect/auth </code>.<br>Note<br>Replace {Domain name} with the domain name of the corresponding environment based on the environment configurations.<br>• Versions earlier than V3.18.2<br>Concatenate a domain name in the following format: mcm.${global:internet-domain}.<br>• V3.18.2 and later<br>Concatenate a domain name in the following format: mcm.console.${global:internet-domain}. |

# 15.AI stack management

AI stack management allows you to add and manage AI stacks all-in-one machines.

**Limits**

- Before you can use the AI stack management feature, the platform administrator needs to display the menu of the **AI Stack service**. To display the AI stack menu, go to the **Configurations** > **Menu Settings** > **Main Menu Configuration** > **Single-cloud Menu** tab.

  ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/806852aedd8fc93d30d641d917d81796.jpeg)

# 17.FAQ

<a id="section-17-1"></a>

## 17.1. Errors when you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console

This topic describes how to troubleshoot the errors when you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Problem description**

The page does not respond or an internal error is returned after you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console with the correct account and password.

**Cause**

Three possible causes:

- Network issues.

- An error is reported when the ascm-auth service calls the ASS service.

- The services in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and the base services (ASS, RAM, Tair, and Ummak) that the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console depends on have not reached the desired state.

**Solution**

1. Check on Apsara Infrastructure Management Framework whether the services in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console cluster have reached the desired state.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Log on to the Apsara Infrastructure Management Framework console.

   </li>

   <li>

   In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operations** > **Cluster Operations**.

   </li>

   <li>

   In the **Cluster** field, enter  `ascm` .

   </li>

   <li>

   Find the cluster and then click **Operations** in the Actions column.

   </li>

   <li>

   Click the **Services** tab and check the current status of services.

   If a service has not reached the desired state, set the service to the desired state. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console again.

   </li>

   </ol>

2. If all services in the cluster have reached the desired state and the logon is still abnormal, you can check network issues in the order of frontend page > Portal dockers > ASAPI dockers > Auth/Manager dockers".

   Troubleshooting procedure: Run the  `curl`  command in each container to connect the endpoint of the next service.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Click the **Machines** tab.

   </li>

   <li>

   In the **Machine** field, enter the name of the docker SR.

   </li>

   <li>

   Find the machine and click **Terminal** in the Actions column.

   </li>

   <li>

   In the left-side machine list, click the machine and run the following command.

   ```text
   bash -c bash
   ```

   </li>

   <li>

   Run the following command to view the ID of the docker:

   ```bash
   docker ps
   ```

   </li>

   <li>

   Run the following command to access the docker:

   ```bash
   sudo docker exec -it <Docker ID> bash 
   ```

   </li>

   <li>

   Run the following command in the docker:

   </li>

   </ol>

   If an endpoint cannot be connected, contact onsite network engineers to solve network issues.

3. If no network issues are found between dockers, you must check logs to discover issues.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Open the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console page, enter the account and password, and then press F12.

   </li>

   <li>

   Click **Log On**.

   </li>

   <li>

   Click the Headers tab and obtain  `eagleeye-traceid` .

   </li>

   <li>

   Perform the operations in step 2 to access the **ascm-portal.Portal#** docker.

   </li>

   <li>

   Run the following command in the docker:

   ```text
   grep <eagleeye-traceid>/root/logs/ascm-portal/ascm-error.log*
   ```

   Find the service that returns errors based on the error logs. Contact onsite O&M engineers to further discover possible causes.

   </li>

   </ol>

4. If the Auth docker is normal, the username and password are correct, and the logon is still abnormal, the possible cause usually is that an error is reported when the AAS service is called.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Run the following command in the Auth docker:

   ```text
   grep {eagleeye-traceid} /logs/ascm-logger/*.log -5
   ```

   </li>

   <li>

   If a return value error is reported in the log, it can be determined that an error is reported

   </li>

   </ol>

   when the AAS service is called. Contact AAS O&M engineers to further discover possible causes.

<a id="section-17-2"></a>

## 17.2. What do I do if a timeout error occurs when I call the API operations of VPC, ECS, SLB, or ApsaraDB RDS in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console?

This topic describes how to troubleshoot a timeout error that occurs when you call the API operations of a cloud service such as Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), Elastic Compute Service (ECS), Server Load Balancer (SLB), or ApsaraDB RDS in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Problem description**

A timeout error occurs when you call the API operations of a cloud service such as VPC, ECS, SLB, or ApsaraDB RDS in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Cause**

The timeout error may be caused by full garbage collection (GC) processes that are frequently run on Portable OpenAPI Proxy (POP).

**Solution**

1. Access the  `webapp-pop.PopAliyunCom#`  container.

   For more information, see *Routine inspection* in *Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Operations and Maintenance Guide*.

2. Run the following command in the container:

   ```text
   tail -f/home/admin/logs/eagleeye/stat-eagleeye-jvm.log | grep gc
   ```

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/5dcf01da066397e43fffa0a333dc63d0.jpeg)

   ConcurrentMarkSweep indicates the logs of the full GC processes. A full GC process is run every one or two minutes.

3. Restart the containers in the following sequence: POP > ASAPI > Manage > ResourceManage > OneConsole.

4. After the containers are restarted, view the full GC processes that are run on POP.

   If the issue persists, contact on-site O&M engineers.

<a id="section-17-3"></a>

## 17.3. What do I do if a timeout error occurs when I create an ACK cluster in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console?

This topic describes how to troubleshoot a timeout error that occurs when you create a Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) cluster in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Problem description**

An error is reported when you create an ACK cluster in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. The error message "java.net.SocketTimeoutException:Read timed out" is returned.

**Cause**

The issue may occur due to the following reasons:

- Network issues occur.

- Performance is degraded due to the high load of the backend service.

**Solution**

1. Find the call logs for Apsara Stack API (ASAPI) and Portable OpenAPI Proxy (POP).

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Press the F12 key. Click **Create** again.

   </li>

   <li>

   Obtain the request ID from the response.

   </li>

   <li>

   Log on to the Apsara Infrastructure Management console and then access the

   </li>

   </ol>

   **asapi.ApiServer#** container.

   <ol type="i" start="4">

   <li>

   Run the following command in the container to query the EagleEye ID:

   ```text
   grep <requestid> /logs/asapi-logger/*
   ```

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/7e261979d3d7095329d9667dba084bd6.png)

   </li>

   <li>

   Run the following command to query the duration on ASAPI based on the EagleEye ID:

   ```text
   grep <EagleEye ID> / logs/asapi-logger/*
   ```

   </li>

   <li>

   Access the **webapp-pop.PopAliyunCom#** container and run the following command to query the logs from POP and the duration on POP:

   ```text
   grep <EagleEye ID> /opt/tianji/alidata/www/logs/java/gateway/logs/trace/*
   ```

   </li>

   </ol>

2. Compare the duration on ASAPI with that on POP.

   - If the duration on POP is slightly longer than that on ASAPI, such as a time difference within 1 second to 2 seconds, contact service engineers to further troubleshoot the timeout error.

   - If the duration on ASAPI is much longer than that on POP, you can check whether full garbage collection (GC) processes are run on POP. For more information, see What do I do if a timeout error occurs when I call the API operations of VPC, ECS, SLB, or ApsaraDB RDS in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console?

<a id="section-17-4"></a>

## 17.4. What do I do if a timeout error occurs when I obtain ACK clusters in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console?

This topic describes how to troubleshoot the timeout error when you obtain Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) clusters in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Problem description**

An error is reported when you obtain ACK clusters in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. The error message "java.net.SocketTimeoutException:Read timed out" is returned.

**Possible cause**

The error may occur due to the following reasons:

- Network issue

- Performance degradation caused by the high load of the backend service

**Solution**

1. Press the F12 key. Refresh the page and obtain the list of ACK clusters again.

   On the **Headers** tab, find the  `_preventCache`  field.

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c1d0691949b5a8c67771cf656dfe2090.jpeg)

2. Access the **asapi.ApiServer#** container.

   <ol type="i">

   <li>

   Run the following command to obtain Manage logs by using _preventCache:

   ```bash
   cat /logs/ascm-logger/main_trace* | grep <_preventCache>
   ```

   </li>

   <li>

   Obtain the EagleEye ID from the Manage logs. Run the following command to find the

   </li>

   </ol>

   logs on API operations called by Manage from ASAPI:

   ```text
   grep /logs/ascm-logger/* | grep <EagleEye ID>
   ```

   <ol type="i" start="3">

   <li>

   Run the following command to obtain the logs on the API operations called by ASAPI

   </li>

   </ol>

   through POP based on the EagleEye ID:

   ```text
   grep <EagleEye ID> / logs/asapi-logger/*
   ```

   Obtain the  `x-acs-signature-nonce`  value.

3. Query POP logs.

   - Method 1

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Enter the VM where the server role PopAliyunCom# is located.

     </li>

     <li>

     Access the **pop-aliyun-com** container. Run the following command to query the logs on Portable OpenAPI Proxy (POP) calls:

     ```text
     grep <EagleEye ID> /opt/tianji/alidata/www/logs/java/gateway/logs/trace/trace.log
     ```

     > **Important**
     >
     > The logs in the container will be refreshed soon. Up to 20 minutes are required to access the POP container and obtain the logs.

     </li>

     </ol>

   - Method 2

     <ol type="a">

     <li>

     Log on to the Simple Log Service console.

     For more information about how to view logs in Simple Log Service, see View logs.

     </li>

     <li>

     Select **ali-pop-log** for Project and **pop_rpc_trace_log** for Logstore.

     </li>

     </ol>

     <ol type="i" start="100">

     <li>

     If you cannot query desired logs by using the EagleEye ID, use  `CS and DescribeClusters`  as the filter condition, and select a small time range for calling the API operation.

     </li>

     </ol>

4. Based on the preceding logs, analyze which module consumes longer time.

## 17.5. Errors when Blink API operations are called

This topic describes how to troubleshoot the errors in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console when Blink API operations are called.

**Problem description**

An error is reported in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console when a Blink API operation is called. The error code is "ascm.manage.EntityNotExist.Instance".

**Solution**

1. Access the **ascm-brm.Manage#** docker. For more information, see Routine inspections.

2. Run the following command in the docker to access the BRM database:

   ```text
   mysql -u${db_user} -h${db_host} -p${db_password} -D${db_name} -P${db_port}
   ```

3. Run the following command in the database to check whether the  `resource_instance.no_show_count`  value is 1 and whether the  `instance_id`  value contains uppercase letters.

   ```sql
   select * from resource_instance where type ='foas_project' and instance_id = '$project_name' ;
   ```

   ![](en-apsara-uni-manager-user-guide-v3.18.6-2607-20260902.assets/c35e3917bf661e666852fdc4fb404e95.png)

   - If the  `instance_id`    value contains uppercase letters, run the following command to back up the table data and then modify the uppercase letters of the  `instance_id`  value to lowercase letters.

     If 10 minutes later the  `no_show_count`  value automatically changes to 0, you can skip subsequent steps.

     ```text
     create tableresource_instance_bak20210204 as select * from resource_instance;
     updateresource_instance set instance_id = lower(instance_id) where type ='foas_project';
     ```

   - If the  `instance_id`  value does not contain uppercase letters and the  `no_show_count` value is 1, run the following command in the **ascm-brm.ResourceMgr#** docker to obtain logs:

     ```text
     cat/logs/ascm-logger/call_trace* |grep foas |grep ListProject |grep ECONNREFUSED |tail -5
     cat/logs/ascm-logger/call_trace* |grep foas |grep ListProject 
     |grepServiceUnavailable | tail -5
     cat/logs/ascm-logger/call_trace* |grep foas |grep ListProject |grep'\"Code\"' | tail -5
     cat/logs/ascm-logger/call_trace* |grep foas |grep ListProject 
     |grepResponseTimeoutError | tail -5
     cat/logs/ascm-logger/call_trace* |grep foas |grep ListProject |grep InternalError| tail -5
     ```

     If no logs are returned, run the following command to obtain logs:

     ```bash
     cat /logs/ascm-logger/call_trace.log|grep foas |grep ListProject| Region for grep$project | AccessKey pair of the organization for grep$project |grep $project_name | tail -5
     cat /logs/ascm-logger/call_trace.log |grep foas |grep ListProject| Region for grep$project | AccessKey pair of the organization for grep$project | tail -5
     ```

4. Provide the collected logs to onsite O&M engineers for the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
